functions.name: can_swapin_thp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: nr_pages is a power of two greater than zero, vmf->orig_pte is the swap PTE that faulted at vmf->address, and ptep points to the first PTE slot of the nr_pages-aligned range containing vmf->address, inside a page table the caller has mapped and locked. Postcondition: returns true only if all four checks pass: (1) the PTE at ptep equals vmf->orig_pte with its swap offset moved back by idx, where idx is the faulting page's index within the aligned range; (2) swap_pte_batch reports that all nr_pages PTEs starting at ptep form one contiguous batch of swap entries; (3) all nr_pages swap entries have the same zeromap state; (4) none of the nr_pages swap entries has a swap-cache (SWAP_HAS_CACHE) entry; if any check fails it returns false, and in every case it takes and releases no lock and acquires no page or folio reference.

functions.name: thp_swap_suitable_orders
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: orders is a bitmask of candidate THP orders whose highest set bit is at most 30, so the int shift 1 << order cannot overflow; swp_offset is the faulting entry's swap offset and addr is the faulting address. Postcondition: if no set order o in orders satisfies (addr >> PAGE_SHIFT) % (1 << o) == swp_offset % (1 << o), it returns 0; otherwise let o_max be the highest set order that satisfies it, and it returns orders with every bit above o_max cleared, so o_max is the highest set bit of the result; because congruence modulo 2^o_max implies congruence modulo every smaller power of two, every set bit of the result satisfies the congruence; the function has no side effects.

functions.name: nft_pipapo_avx2_lookup_4b_32
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller is inside a kernel FPU section with AVX2 register ymm15 zeroed; f is a valid field whose lt lookup table, mt mapping table and bsize describe the bitmaps; map and fill are writable bitmaps of at least f->bsize longs; pkt points to at least 16 readable bytes; offset is non-negative. Postcondition: the function scans each 256-bit block i in [offset, f->bsize / NFT_PIPAPO_LONGS_PER_M256). When first is false and the map block is all zero, it skips the block and leaves it unchanged. When the AND of the 32 nibble buckets (with the map block, if first is false) is zero, it stores zero into the map block. Otherwise it stores the match bitmap into the map block and calls nft_pipapo_avx2_refill on it. If last is false, that call fills fill from the mapping table and clears the matched map bits. If last is true, it neither touches fill nor clears map. The function returns -1 if no block matched, which includes the case where the range is empty. If last is true it returns the bit index (rule index) of the lowest set bit in the highest-indexed matching block. Otherwise it returns the refill result of the first matching block, which is the mapping target of its lowest set bit, divided by XSAVE_YMM_SIZE. Nothing is allocated or freed.

functions.name: xtensa_pmu_cache_event
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: config is any 64-bit perf cache configuration value; its low byte is read as the cache type, its second byte as the cache op and its third byte as the cache result. Postcondition: the function returns -EINVAL (-22) when the type byte is greater than 4 (the table has 5 rows: L1D=0, L1I=1, LL=2, DTLB=3, ITLB=4), the op byte is greater than 2, the result byte is greater than 1, or the selected table entry is zero (type 0 with op 2, types 1, 3 and 4 with an op other than 0, and type 2 with any op); otherwise it returns the positive PMU control word stored in that entry (0x10AF1/0x20AF1 for L1D read, 0x10BF1/0x20BF1 for L1D write, 0x108F1/0x208F1 for L1I read, 0x109F1/0x809F1 for DTLB read, 0x107F1/0x807F1 for ITLB read, access/miss respectively), and it takes no locks and allocates no memory.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the usual process arguments (argv[0] non-NULL) in the drill command-line format. Postcondition: it parses options and arguments, builds a resolver, and performs the requested operation (query, AXFR, trace, secure trace, chase, query-to-file, answer-from-file); the -v and -h options, option errors, a failed WSAStartup, a failed resolver setup, a failed AXFR start and an AXFR with no first record all jump to cleanup. Some errors (the error() macro, a bad -T/-S combination, a missing server name) may terminate the process directly with exit() and skip cleanup. At the exit label it frees the qname, source address, resolvers, key list, command-line rr list, trace start name and the progname/TSIG strings, then returns result. The result is 0 (EXIT_SUCCESS) on normal success. It is EXIT_FAILURE when no packet is received, a chase query fails to produce a packet, or setup fails. Under HAVE_SSL it can also be an ldns status code from DNSSEC verification, secure trace or chase. Where the answer packet is verified against -k keys, a query for type ANY breaks out of the switch early, skipping the answer-file dump and ldns_pkt_free of the packet.

functions.name: ldns_rr_new_frm_str_internal
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: str is a NUL-terminated presentation-format RR string; newrr may be NULL; origin may be NULL; prev may be NULL or point to an owner rdf (or NULL) that this function may free and replace; explicit_ttl may be NULL. Postcondition: returns LDNS_STATUS_OK and, if newrr is non-NULL, stores a newly allocated RR in *newrr (caller owns it), otherwise the parsed RR is freed; returns LDNS_STATUS_SYNTAX_SUPERFLUOUS_TEXT_ERR if rdata text remains unconsumed, or LDNS_STATUS_SYNTAX_MISSING_VALUE_ERR if a non-question RR with a known type has fewer rdata fields than the minimum (and was not in \# format); otherwise on allocation failure returns LDNS_STATUS_MEM_ERR, and on syntax failure returns LDNS_STATUS_SYNTAX_ERR, _TTL_ERR, _CLASS_ERR, _TYPE_ERR, _RDATA_ERR, or a status from ldns_wire2rdf or ldns_dname_cat. On every failure return the temporary buffers and the partial RR are freed and *newrr is not set; *prev (when given) may already have been replaced with the owner name. When the TTL token is not a number it is taken as the class (or type), the default TTL is used and *explicit_ttl is set false, otherwise true.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process arguments with argv[0] non-NULL and argv[argc] NULL. Postcondition: it parses options and exits the process with status 1 (via lafe_errc or usage) on any error, such as an invalid option or blocksize, conflicting modes, a missing mode, a missing -p target directory, or option combinations such as -t without -i, -n without -t, --format without -o, or -l without -p; --help and --version print text and exit 0; in mode -i the mode_in/mode_list call is not expected to return; otherwise it runs mode_out or mode_pass, frees the matching object, the uid/gid caches and overrides, the read-disk archive, destdir and the passphrase buffer, and returns cpio->return_value.

functions.name: Bcj2_Decode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: zip is a valid BCJ2 decoder state whose tmp_stream and sub_stream buffers (indices 0..2) hold at least the remaining byte counts recorded in it, and outBuf is writable for outSize bytes. Postcondition: the function first initialises the range-decoder state if bcj_state is 0, then emits any saved odd_bcj bytes and decodes up to outSize bytes into outBuf; it returns the number of bytes written (0..outSize) and updates tmp_stream_bytes_remaining, sub_stream_bytes_remaining[0..2] and bcj2_outPos accordingly; if outSize is 0 it returns 0 after updating bcj2_outPos only, without updating the remaining-byte counters; it returns SZ_ERROR_DATA immediately, without updating the remaining-byte counters or bcj2_outPos, when a jump target needs 4 bytes but fewer remain in the corresponding sub-stream; no lock or buffer ownership is transferred.

functions.name: find_elf_data_sec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a is a valid archive_read positioned so that the first bytes read ahead are the start of the candidate ELF file. Postcondition: returns the file offset (sh_offset) of the section named ".data" if the ELF header, section table and string table are all readable and consistent and the offset is at most SSIZE_MAX; in every other case (not ELF, bad header values, seek or read failure, no ".data" name, section not found, offset too large) it returns the default SFX_MIN_ADDR; in all cases it finally seeks the stream back to offset 0 (the seek result is ignored).

functions.name: isSVD
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h points to a readable volume descriptor buffer (at least 2048 bytes); iso9660 is unused apart from being passed to isNull. Postcondition: returns 48 if the descriptor type is 2, the three reserved fields are null, the file structure version is 1, the little-endian logical block size is positive, the volume space size is greater than 20 blocks, the L path table location is at least 18 and below the volume size, the M path table location is either 0 or at least 18 and below the volume size, and the root directory record is valid; otherwise returns 0. It modifies nothing.

functions.name: archive_read_format_lha_read_header
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a is a valid archive reader whose format data is a struct lha and entry is a valid archive_entry. Postcondition: it resets per-entry state and returns ARCHIVE_EOF at the end-of-archive marker (a zero first byte, or no more data), or the error from truncated_error if data is truncated; for a leading 'MZ' before the first header it skips the self-extracting stub, passing on any error below ARCHIVE_WARN. It returns ARCHIVE_FATAL (with an error message) for a bad header format, an unsupported header level, a failed pathname conversion or a negative compressed size, and returns truncated_error if a non-directory entry has an empty filename. It returns ARCHIVE_FAILED for an unparsable symlink name, and any error from the level-specific header reader below ARCHIVE_WARN is returned as is. Otherwise it fills the entry (pathname, symlink, mode, uid/gid, names, times, size) and the lha state (entry_bytes_remaining, offsets, end_of_entry for directories or empty content, format name) and returns the header reader's status, ARCHIVE_OK or ARCHIVE_WARN. Temporary path strings are freed on all paths after they are created; the conversion-failure paths also clean conv_buffer.

functions.name: xmllite_read_toc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a is a valid archive_read whose xar reader state is set up so the TOC can be read through a stream adapter. Postcondition: returns ARCHIVE_OK if the XML reader reached EOF with every element, end element and text node handled; otherwise returns the error from xmllite_create_stream_adapter if it was negative, or ARCHIVE_FATAL if CreateXmlReader, SetInput or Read fails, if a name or text value cannot be obtained, or whatever non-OK status xmllite_xmlattr_setup or xml_start returns (the latter may be a non-fatal code); a failed SetInput or Read also sets an archive error message. On every path the XML reader, if created, is released and the stream adapter is freed with free(); temporary name strings and attribute lists are freed, but the text buffer is not freed if the loop is left through the Text case's fall-through (the Text case falls through to the default break, which is harmless).

functions.name: process_extra
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a is a valid archive_read for a zip format, p points to extra_length readable bytes of extra-field data, zip_entry is a valid zip_entry, and entry is either NULL or a valid archive_entry. Postcondition: returns ARCHIVE_OK immediately if extra_length is 0, or if extra_length is under 4 and every byte is zero; if extra_length is under 4 with a nonzero byte it sets ARCHIVE_ERRNO_FILE_FORMAT and returns ARCHIVE_FAILED. Otherwise it walks the (id, size) records. It returns ARCHIVE_FAILED with ARCHIVE_ERRNO_FILE_FORMAT set when a record's data overruns extra_length, when a Zip64 (0x0001) field holds a missing or over-INT64_MAX 64-bit uncompressed size, compressed size or local header offset (each read only if the matching entry value is 0xffffffff), when a 0x5455 time field has zero data size, or when a 0x9901 AES field has data size under 6. Along the way it updates zip_entry fields (flags, sizes, local_header_offset, mtime, atime, ctime, uid, gid, system, mode, aes_extra) from the 0x0001, 0x5455, 0x5855, 0x6c78, 0x7855, 0x7875 and 0x9901 records, truncated sub-fields being skipped silently. A 0x7075 record may set entry's pathname and may set zip->sconv_utf8 as a side effect; conversion errors are ignored. Unknown records are skipped, and it otherwise returns ARCHIVE_OK. No locks or references are transferred to the caller.

functions.name: set_directory_record_rr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bp is either NULL (size-measuring pass) or points to a writable System Use area of dr_len bytes, and isoent and iso9660 are valid; for DIR_REC_PARENT the isoent (or its rr_parent/parent) has a non-NULL file, and isoent->rr_child is non-NULL when its CL entry is written. Postcondition: it builds the Rock Ridge System Use entries for the directory record (SP for the root self record, RR, NM, PX, SL, TF, RE, PL, CL, PN, ZF and CE as selected by the record type and file attributes), splitting long NM and SL entries into continuation entries and moving to extra records via extra_next_record when space runs out; the used size is accounted through extra_tell_used_size even when bp is NULL, nothing is written when bp is NULL, the record is closed with extra_close_record, and it returns ctl.dr_len, the resulting directory record length. It has no error return.

functions.name: archive_write_zip_data
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a is a valid archive_write whose format_data is a zip writer state with an active entry whose compression (and, if flagged encrypted, encryption) stream is initialized, and buff points to at least s readable bytes. Postcondition: s is first clamped to entry_uncompressed_limit and added to entry_uncompressed_written; if the clamped s is 0 it returns 0 without doing anything else; otherwise it lazily initializes traditional or WinZip AES encryption (returning that init function's non-OK code on failure), then stores, or compresses with deflate/zstd/bzip2/lzma/xz, and optionally encrypts the data and writes the output through __archive_write_output (updating entry_compressed_written and written_bytes); on success it decreases entry_uncompressed_limit by s, updates entry_crc32 unless AES AE-2 encryption is active, and returns the clamped s. Errors: ARCHIVE_FAILED with an archive error set if AES-CTR encryption fails; ARCHIVE_FATAL without an error set if deflate returns Z_STREAM_ERROR, ZSTD_isError, BZ2_bzCompress returns other than BZ_RUN_OK, or lzma_code returns LZMA_MEM_ERROR; ARCHIVE_FATAL with an error set for an invalid or unspecified compression type; or the non-OK return of __archive_write_output or encryption init on failure. On any error return, counters and stream state may be partially advanced.

functions.name: test_compat_star_acl_posix1e
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the reference file test_compat_star_acl_posix1e.tar can be extracted into the working directory and read by libarchive as a tar archive containing at least three entries. Postcondition: the test creates a read archive, opens the file, and reads three headers; each of them is asserted to succeed. For the first, second and third entries it asserts 5 ACCESS ACLs (mode 0142), 7 ACCESS ACLs (mode 0543) and 6 DEFAULT ACLs (mode 0142), and that the ACLs match the expected tables. Finally it closes and frees the archive, asserting ARCHIVE_OK for both. It returns nothing, and failed assertions are reported by the test framework.

functions.name: test_read_format_rar_multivolume_uncompressed_files
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the ten reference files test_rar_multivolume_uncompressed_files.part01.rar to part10.rar can be extracted into the working directory and libarchive's RAR reader is available. Postcondition: the test opens all ten volumes as one archive and checks the first through sixteenth entries in order: pathname, timestamps, size, mode, encryption flags, symlink targets, and for the file entries seek and read results via archive_seek_data with SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR and SEEK_END and the volume-boundary helper. It then checks that the next header returns ARCHIVE_EOF, that archive_file_count is 16, and that archive_read_close and archive_read_free return ARCHIVE_OK. The function returns nothing, and any mismatch is recorded as a test failure through the assertion macros. It does not return an error code.

functions.name: test_read_format_zip_zstd_one_file_blockread
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test harness is running and the reference file test_read_format_zip_zstd.zipx can be extracted into the working directory. Postcondition: returns nothing; creates a read archive, and if the zstd filter is unsupported it reports a skip, closes and frees the archive and returns early; otherwise it opens the zip with a 37-byte block size and asserts that the first entry is "vimrc" in format "ZIP 2.0 (zstd)", that its data read in blocks (extract_one_using_blocks with block size 13) has CRC 0xBA8E3BAA, that the next header returns ARCHIVE_EOF, and that closing and freeing the archive return ARCHIVE_OK; failed assertions are recorded by the test framework.

functions.name: test_sparse_basic
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as a libarchive test case with a writable current directory, and the helpers test_sparse_whole_file_data, verify_sparse_file and verify_sparse_file2 are available. Postcondition: it first runs test_sparse_whole_file_data, then returns early with no further checks if the SKIP_TEST_SPARSE environment variable is set (reporting a skip), if getcwd fails (the failed assertion is recorded), or if the current directory's filesystem does not report holes (it frees cwd and reports a skip); otherwise it checks the sparse-entry counts for file0..file3 (4, 3, 20, 0) and for file4 (2) only when off_t is wider than 4 bytes, using one reader. It then checks file0 through archive_read_disk_entry_from_file with expected count 5 for both flag values, and with ARCHIVE_READDISK_NO_SPARSE expects 0 sparse entries for every file. Every archive handle it creates is freed with archive_read_free, the cwd string is freed on every path after getcwd succeeds, and nothing is returned.

functions.name: test_write_disk_perms
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test runs in a writable scratch directory; on Windows (non-Cygwin) it only reports a skip. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it writes entries through an archive_write_disk object, checking that each header and finish_entry call returns the expected code (ARCHIVE_OK, 0 or ARCHIVE_WARN, with the WARN cases only when not root or when a bad gid is available). It then frees the archive and entry, and stats the created files, asserting the expected modes (SUID/SGID kept only when the owner or group could be restored, otherwise dropped) and that file_bad_owner keeps the caller's uid when not root. Failed assertions are recorded by the test harness; nothing is returned.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process command-line arguments, with argv[0] a valid program name. Postcondition: the function parses all options into a local struct bsdtar (flags, extract/readdisk flags, filters, matching patterns), and exits the process via lafe_errc, usage(), long_help() or version() on invalid options, a missing mode, conflicting compressions or mode-restricted options, or allocation failure. Otherwise it runs the single selected mode (tar_mode_c, tar_mode_r, tar_mode_t, tar_mode_u or tar_mode_x), frees the match object, substitutions, cset and passphrase buffer, warns if a delayed error was recorded, and returns bsdtar->return_value, which is 0 if no error was recorded.

functions.name: list_item_verbose

Postcondition: one 'ls -l'-style line has been written to out (mode, link count, user name or uid, group name or gid, size or device numbers, mtime, pathname, and ' link to X' or ' -> X' for a hard link or symlink), the bsdtar u_width and gs_width fields are initialised or widened as needed, the static 'now' is set on first call, and the time field is '-- -- ----' if localtime fails or strftime yields 0; nothing is returned and no line terminator is written.

functions.name: cbor_stream_decode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: callbacks points to a callbacks table whose handlers are all non-NULL, and source points to at least source_size readable bytes (source_size may be 0). Postcondition: if source_size is 0 the function returns a result with status CBOR_DECODER_NOT_ENOUGH_DATA (as set by claim_bytes) and calls no callback; otherwise it decodes only the first data item header, and for a reserved or unassigned initial byte (0x1C-0x1F, 0x3C-0x3F, 0x5C-0x5E, 0x7C-0x7E, 0x9C-0x9E, 0xBC-0xBE, 0xDC-0xDF, 0xE0-0xF3, 0xF8, 0xFC-0xFE) it returns a result with status CBOR_DECODER_ERROR and calls no callback. For a valid initial byte it invokes exactly one matching callback with the decoded value (embedded values, length, tag, simple value or float, or a start/break marker), but only if claim_bytes confirms the needed argument bytes are available (for strings, the string bytes too, via the claim macros). If the needed bytes are missing it calls no callback and returns the non-FINISHED status set by claim_bytes. Otherwise it returns the result with status CBOR_DECODER_FINISHED, with the claimed byte count recorded by claim_bytes. The function does not allocate memory or take locks, and it does not retain the source buffer.

functions.name: test_serialize_indefinite_string
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global test buffer holds at least 512 bytes and memory allocation succeeds; the function takes an unused cmocka state pointer. Postcondition: it builds an indefinite string with one 12-byte definite chunk 'Hello world!' (the chunk is moved into the item), asserts that the chunk count is 1, that cbor_serialize into the 512-byte buffer returns 15 with bytes 0x7F 0x6C 'Hello world!' 0xFF, and that cbor_serialized_size is 15; it then releases the item with cbor_decref, which also frees the chunk and its data, and returns nothing. A failed assertion aborts the test.

functions.name: diff_algo_myers
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: algo_config and state are valid, with state->left and state->right holding initialized atom lists, and state->kd_buf/kd_buf_size describing either no buffer or a buffer allocated with realloc-compatible memory. Postcondition: if the required Myers state ((2*max+1)^2 ints, max = left+right atom count) overflows size_t or exceeds algo_config->permitted_state_size, it returns DIFF_RC_USE_DIFF_ALGO_FALLBACK without changes; if growing state->kd_buf fails it returns ENOMEM; otherwise it computes the shortest edit path with Myers' forward pass (the buffer is grown and stored in state->kd_buf/kd_buf_size if needed and overwritten), backtracks, and adds the minus/plus/snake chunks to state via diff_state_add_chunk, returning DIFF_RC_OK; it returns the non-zero error from diff_atom_same if a comparison fails, ENOMEM if diff_state_add_chunk fails, and DIFF_RC_USE_DIFF_ALGO_FALLBACK if the section lengths are inconsistent, in which case chunks may already have been added to state.

functions.name: re_update_line
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: el is a valid EditLine, old and new are writable NUL-terminated wide-character line buffers (new is also modified in place) and i is the screen line number of the line. Postcondition: it returns nothing; trailing blanks are stripped by writing NUL at the end of both buffers, and if there is no difference it returns at once. Otherwise it moves the terminal cursor to line i, applies the minimal inserts, deletes, overwrites and clear-to-end-of-line needed to make the screen show the new line, and copies the changed text into old (re__strncopy and re_insert/re_delete). It returns early after the first-difference step when there is nothing to keep at the end of the line, and otherwise carries on through the second-difference and late-insert steps.

functions.name: terminal_echotc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: el is a valid EditLine and argv is NULL or a NULL-terminated vector of wide strings (command name first, then an optional -v/-s flag, then the capability name and its arguments). Postcondition: returns -1 if argv is NULL or has no argument after the command name, if the capability is not found or empty, or if a required numeric argument is missing, is not a non-negative integer, or an extra argument is present (printing a diagnostic to el_errfile unless silent); returns 0 when no capability name is given after the optional flag, after printing one of the special values tabs, meta, xn, am, baud, rows/lines or cols to el_outfile, or after sending the capability string (with the parsed cols/rows substituted via tgoto when it needs arguments) through terminal_tputs.

functions.name: name##_RB_INSERT
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: head points to a valid red-black tree and elm points to a node not currently linked in it, with a key that cmp can compare. Postcondition: if a node comparing equal to elm already exists it is returned and the tree and elm are unchanged; otherwise elm is linked in as a leaf (or as root if the tree was empty) with its parent/child links set, augmented, and rebalanced via the INSERT_COLOR function, and NULL is returned.

functions.name: name##_RB_FIND
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: head points to a valid red-black tree and elm points to a node holding a key that cmp can compare. Postcondition: returns the node in the tree whose cmp against elm is zero, or NULL if there is none; the tree is not modified.

functions.name: name##_RB_NEXT
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: elm is a non-NULL node linked in a valid red-black tree. Postcondition: returns the in-order successor of elm (the leftmost node of its right subtree, or the nearest ancestor of which elm is in the left subtree), or NULL if elm is the maximum; nothing is modified.

functions.name: name##_RB_MINMAX
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: head points to a valid red-black tree. Postcondition: if val is negative returns the leftmost (minimum) node, otherwise the rightmost (maximum) node, or NULL if the tree is empty; the tree is not modified.

functions.name: name##_HT_INIT(struct name *head)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_INIT(head). Precondition: head points to a writable hash-table head. Postcondition: the head is reset to empty (table NULL, length 0, entry count 0, load limit 0, prime index -1); any previous table is not freed.

functions.name: name##_HT_FIND_P_(struct name *head, struct type *elm)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_FIND_P_(head, elm). Precondition: head is valid; elm is valid with its hash already set (when hashes are cached); table length is nonzero if the table is non-NULL. Postcondition: returns NULL if head->hth_table is NULL; otherwise returns the address of the link in elm's bucket chain that points to the first element for which eqfn(*p, elm) is true, or the address of the chain's terminating NULL link if no match exists. The table is not modified.

functions.name: name##_HT_FIND(const struct name *head, struct type *elm)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_FIND(head, elm). Precondition: head and elm are valid. Postcondition: stores the hash into elm (when hashes are cached) and returns the element in the table matching elm per eqfn, or NULL if the table is absent or has no match; the table is not modified.

functions.name: name##_HT_INSERT(struct name *head, struct type *elm)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_INSERT(head, elm). Precondition: head and elm are valid and the table contains no element matching elm. Postcondition: the table is grown first if absent or at its load limit (the GROW result is ignored, so a failed growth leaves the old table and may crash on an absent table); the entry count is incremented, elm's hash is set when cached, and elm is linked at the front of its bucket chain. Returns nothing.

functions.name: name##_HT_REPLACE(struct name *head, struct type *elm)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_REPLACE(head, elm). Precondition: head and elm are valid. Postcondition: grows the table if absent or at its load limit, sets elm's hash, and stores elm in the slot found by FIND_P_. If a different matching element r existed, elm takes over r's chain successor, r's next is cleared, the count is unchanged, and r is returned. Otherwise (no match, or the match is elm itself) the entry count is incremented and NULL is returned.

functions.name: name##_HT_REMOVE(struct name *head, struct type *elm)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_REMOVE(head, elm). Precondition: head and elm are valid. Postcondition: sets elm's hash; if the table is absent or no element matches, returns NULL and changes nothing else; otherwise unlinks the matching element, clears its next pointer, decrements the entry count and returns that element.

functions.name: name##_HT_FOREACH_FN(struct name *head, int (*fn)(struct type *, void *), void *data)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_FOREACH_FN(head, fn, data). Precondition: head is valid and fn is a callable callback. Postcondition: if the table is absent it returns immediately; otherwise fn(elem, data) is called once on every element, and each element for which fn returns nonzero is unlinked from its chain (its next pointer is not cleared) and the entry count is decremented. Returns nothing.

functions.name: name##_HT_START(struct name *head)
functions.prose_contract: Generated by HT_PROTOTYPE as name##_HT_START(head). Precondition: head is valid (table pointer valid for hth_table_length slots). Postcondition: it calls mountkernfs, opens /kern read-only, reads directory entries with getdents into an 8192-byte buffer, and fails the test (via atf_tc_fail_errno) if open or getdents returns -1; it requires (ATF_REQUIRE_STREQ) that the first three entries are named ".", ".." and "boottime" in that order, otherwise the test fails; it returns nothing and does not close the directory fd.

Any failed syscall or mismatch fails the test; it returns nothing and does not close the fd.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(attach4, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Test body for attach4: requires a working ptrace/ATF environment where msg_open and atf_utils_fork succeed. It forks a tracer child that waits for a message, PT_ATTACHes to its parent (the test process), waits for the parent's SIGSTOP stop, PT_DETACHes, signals the parent and exits with 5; the parent then reaps the tracer, checks it exited with status 5, and checks that a further wait on it fails with ECHILD. It closes the pipe pair, returns nothing, and any failed requirement aborts the test.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(attach5, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Test body for attach5 (compiled only when TWAIT_HAVE_PID): requires a working ptrace/ATF environment where both msg_open calls and atf_utils_fork succeed. A tracee child records its parent pid, reports ready, waits to be told to exit, asserts getppid() is unchanged, and exits with 5. A tracer child attaches to the tracee, waits for the SIGSTOP stop, continues it, and signals readiness. The parent then lets the tracee exit and waits until it is a zombie. A WNOHANG wait on the tracee returns 0 because the tracer must see it first. The parent releases the tracer, which reaps the tracee with status 5 and exits with 10. The parent reaps the tracer (status 10) and then the tracee (status 5), closes both pipe pairs, and returns nothing. Any failed requirement aborts the test.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(attach6, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Test body for attach6 (compiled only when TWAIT_HAVE_PID): requires a working ptrace/ATF environment where both msg_open calls and atf_utils_fork succeed. It forks a tracee that records getppid(), reports to the parent, waits for a message, and then builds a sysctl name for CTL_KERN, KERN_PROC2, KERN_PROC_PID with its own pid to query its kinfo_proc2 and check its parent relationship while traced. A tracer child attaches to the tracee as in attach5, and the parent coordinates and reaps the children. It returns nothing, and any failed requirement aborts the test. The slice is cut off after the name array is filled, so the rest of the behaviour is not visible.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_set_start_hint, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the ATF framework runs the test case; the body calls setup() itself. Postcondition: it mallocs a page array (never freed), loads one segment and initializes it with uvm_physseg_init_seg. It checks that uvm_physseg_set_start_hint(upm, atop(128)) returns true and that uvm_physseg_get_start_hint then returns atop(128). It returns nothing, and a failed check is reported by ATF.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_get_pg, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the ATF framework runs the test case; the body calls setup() itself. Postcondition: it mallocs a page array (never freed), loads one segment and checks that there is 1 entry and uvmexp.npages is 0. After uvm_physseg_init_seg it checks that uvmexp.npages equals PAGE_COUNT_1M, then checks that uvm_physseg_get_pg(upm, 5)->phys_addr equals 5*PAGE_SIZE and that uvm_physseg_get_pg(upm, 113)->phys_addr equals 113*PAGE_SIZE. It returns nothing, and a failed check is reported by ATF.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_get_pmseg, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the ATF framework runs the test case with __HAVE_PMAP_PHYSSEG defined; the body calls setup() itself. Postcondition: it mallocs a page array (never freed), loads one segment, checks that there is 1 entry and uvmexp.npages is 0, then initializes the segment and checks that uvmexp.npages equals PAGE_COUNT_1M. It gets the pmseg with uvm_physseg_get_pmseg and checks it is non-NULL. It copies the local pmseg.dummy_variable into the extracted pmseg's dummy_variable, then sets the local one to false. The slice is cut off, so any later checks are not shown. It returns nothing, and a failed check is reported by ATF.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_unplug, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the body calls setup() itself and mallocs a vm_page slab of npages1+npages2+npages3 entries without checking for failure. Postcondition: it plugs a 1MB segment, unplugs the middle 512KB (leaving a gap and two entries), unplugs the tail fragment (invalidating its handle, one entry left), unplugs from the back and front, and checks the entry count and uvmexp.npages after each step; any failed ATF_REQUIRE aborts the test. The final unplug of the last fragment is expected to raise SIGABRT. The function returns nothing and does not free the slab.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_page_physload_preload, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the body calls setup() itself. Postcondition: it calls uvm_page_physload for segment 1 and, if VM_PHYSSEG_MAX > 1, for segment 2, requiring each handle valid, uvmexp.npages equal to 0, and the entry count to be 1 and then 2; failed requirements abort the test. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_page_physload_postboot, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the body calls setup() itself and mallocs a slab of npages1+npages2 vm_pages without checking it. Postcondition: it physloads segment 1 (checking a valid handle, npages 0, one entry), calls uvm_page_init_fake, expects SIGABRT, then physloads segment 2 post boot, which is expected to abort so the later checks are normally not reached. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_handle_immutable, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the body calls setup() itself. Postcondition: it physloads segment 2, requiring npages 0, one entry, and get_prev returning UVM_PHYSSEG_TYPE_INVALID_EMPTY. If VM_PHYSSEG_MAX > 1 it then loads segment 1 (two entries), takes get_prev of the original handle, and checks it is not INVALID_EMPTY and that its start and end equal VALID_START_PFN_1 and VALID_END_PFN_1, expecting failure for the static array implementation when UVM_HOTPLUG is undefined. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_seg_chomp_slab, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body; it calls setup() itself and needs malloc and the uvm_physseg allocator to work. Postcondition: it chomps a slab of 2*UVM_PHYSSEG_BOOT_UNPLUG_MAX pages into the segment extent and checks that extent_alloc returns 0, then that extent_free returns ENOMEM when VM_PHYSSEG_MAX==1, otherwise 0 in a loop of npages alloc/free pairs. It then sets uvm.page_init_done=true, chomps again, and requires npages further alloc/free pairs to succeed. Any failed requirement fails the test; it returns nothing, and the slab is never freed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_alloc_from_slab, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body; it calls setup() itself and needs malloc and the uvm_physseg allocator to work. Postcondition: it chomps a slab of 2*npages pages into the segment and requires uvm_physseg_seg_alloc_from_slab to return non-NULL for npages. After setting uvm.page_init_done=true it requires a second non-NULL allocation when VM_PHYSSEG_MAX>1. It then calls atf_tc_expect_fail("alloc beyond extent") and requires one more non-NULL allocation, which is expected to fail. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_init_seg, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body; it calls setup() itself, so uvmexp.npages starts at 0, and it needs malloc and the uvm_physseg allocator to work. Postcondition: it chomps a slab, allocates npages pages from it, and requires uvmexp.npages to still be 0. It sets seg start=0, end=npages, avail_start=0, avail_end=npages, calls uvm_physseg_init_seg and requires uvmexp.npages to equal npages. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_get_start, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body; it calls setup() itself to fake early boot. Postcondition: it loads a segment with uvm_page_physload and requires uvmexp.npages==0, one physseg entry, and uvm_physseg_get_start(upm)==VALID_START_PFN_1. When VM_PHYSSEG_MAX>1 it loads a second segment and requires two entries, npages still 0, and the start of the new handle to equal VALID_START_PFN_2. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_get_start_invalid, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body; it calls setup() itself. Postcondition: it loads one segment, sets uvm.page_init_done=true, and requires uvmexp.npages==0, one entry and page_init_done true. It then checks that uvm_physseg_get_start(UVM_PHYSSEG_TYPE_INVALID) returns (paddr_t)-1. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_1MB, t)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body (only built with UVM_HOTPLUG); the slab malloc result is not checked. Postcondition: after setup(), plugs segment 1, fakes the page init over the slab, plugs segment 2, unplugs random-sized chunks across segment 2 in PF_STEP strides, then performs 10,000,000 random PHYS_TO_VM_PAGE lookups with results ignored. The ATF_REQUIRE_EQ checks abort the test if a plug fails or the entry count is not 1 then 2; otherwise it ends with a trivially true check. Returns nothing, and the slab is never freed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_64MB, t)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body (only built with UVM_HOTPLUG); the slab malloc result is not checked. Postcondition: after setup(), plugs segment 1, fakes the page init over the slab, plugs segment 3, unplugs random-sized chunks across segment 3 in PF_STEP strides, then performs 10,000,000 random PHYS_TO_VM_PAGE lookups with results ignored. The ATF_REQUIRE_EQ checks abort the test if a plug fails or the entry count is not 1 then 2; otherwise it ends with a trivially true check. Returns nothing, and the slab is never freed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_128MB, t)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body (only built with UVM_HOTPLUG); the slab malloc result is not checked. Postcondition: after setup(), plugs segment 1, fakes the page init, plugs a segment at VALID_START_PFN_2 with npages2 computed from the PFN_4 range, unplugs random-sized chunks over the PFN_4 range in PF_STEP strides, then performs 10,000,000 random PHYS_TO_VM_PAGE lookups with results ignored. The ATF_REQUIRE_EQ checks abort the test if a plug fails or the entry count is not 1 then 2; otherwise it ends with a trivially true check. Returns nothing, and the slab is never freed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uvm_physseg_256MB, t)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body (only built with UVM_HOTPLUG); the slab malloc result is not checked. Postcondition: after setup(), plugs segment 1, fakes the page init, plugs a segment at VALID_START_PFN_2 with npages2 computed from the PFN_5 range, unplugs random-sized chunks over the PFN_5 range in PF_STEP strides, then performs 10,000,000 random PHYS_TO_VM_PAGE lookups with results ignored. The lookup loop adds ctob(VALID_START_PFN_5) when pa < ctob(VALID_END_PFN_5), which is almost always. The ATF_REQUIRE_EQ checks abort the test if a plug fails or the entry count is not 1 then 2; otherwise it ends with a trivially true check. Returns nothing, and the slab is never freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv is a valid NULL-terminated array of argc argument strings, as passed by the C runtime. Postcondition: the function never returns; it always ends the process via exit(). The exit status is 1 on a usage or option error (errx, err or usage(1)), 1 in connect mode if no connection succeeded or a UDP test failed on the last port tried, 1 in unix-socket connect mode if unix_connect fails or -z is given, and otherwise 0 (listen mode finished, or the last connection succeeded). On normal exit it closes the last socket s if nonzero and the tun device if open, and in unix connect mode it unlinks the temporary datagram socket when -u is set. It leaks the strdup'd proxy string and holds no locks.

functions.name: socks_connect
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: host, port, proxyhost and proxyhints are valid, proxyport and proxyuser may be NULL (proxyport defaults to the HTTP or SOCKS port), and socksv is 5, 4 or -1 (HTTP CONNECT). Postcondition: it connects to the proxy via remote_connect and returns -1 if that connection fails, otherwise performs the handshake and returns the connected proxy socket descriptor; on a 407 reply with proxyuser set it closes the socket and retries (reconnecting, sending Basic auth from getproxypass on retries), and it terminates the process via err/errx on an unknown port, more than 4 attempts, any I/O failure, protocol error, invalid or too long hostname, too many headers or unknown protocol.

functions.name: chufilter
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: chuc points to a valid chucode with NCHUCHARS code characters and timestamps, and rtime points to a valid receive timestamp. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it prints the code and returns early without further effect (after printing a message) if the two halves differ, the first nibble is not 6, the day/hour/minute/second fail the sanity check (second must be 31..39), or the date is hopelessly off (not within CLOCK_WAYTOOBIG of the receive time in the current, previous or next year); otherwise it may update the static yearstart and lastcode, computes per-character offsets, averages them by multiplying the sum by 0.1, adds offset_fudge to the mean, finds the min and max offsets and adds offset_fudge to those two entries, and prints a line with mean, min and max. No lock or reference is taken or released and no value is returned.

functions.name: isc_log_doit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: lctx is NULL or a valid log context; category, module and format are non-NULL, category->id and module->id are within the context's counts, level is not ISC_LOG_DYNAMIC, args is a valid va_list for the format, and the caller does not hold lctx->lock. Postcondition: returns nothing; if lctx is NULL or isc_log_wouldlog says the level would not be logged it returns immediately without locking; otherwise it takes lctx->lock and, for each matching channel of the category (falling back to the default category, then the internal default channel) whose debug/level filters pass, formats the message once into lctx->buffer, and with write_once prunes expired history entries and returns early (unlocking) if the text duplicates a recent message, else appends a copy to the history if allocation succeeds. It writes the message to each channel according to its type (file with rolling, reopening and max-size tracking, file descriptor, syslog, or null), and releases lctx->lock on every path before returning.

functions.name: isc_md5_final
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx points to a valid, initialized isc_md5_t state (possibly updated with data) and digest points to at least 16 writable bytes. Postcondition: the MD5 padding (0x80, zeros, and the 64-bit bit-length) is applied, with an extra block processed if padding does not fit; the 16-byte digest of all data hashed is written to digest in little-endian byte order, the whole ctx structure is then zeroed, and nothing is returned.

functions.name: isc_interfaceiter_destroy
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: iterp is non-NULL and *iterp is a valid interface iterator (magic valid), use_GAA_determined is true, and if use_GAA is set then iter->buf4 is NULL (the check is written twice on buf4, buf6 is never checked), otherwise iter->ipaa is NULL. Postcondition: returns nothing; in GAA mode ipaa (if non-NULL) is freed to the iterator's memory context, otherwise buf4 and buf6 (each if non-NULL) are freed; the iterator's magic is cleared, the iterator itself is freed to its memory context, and *iterp is set to NULL.

functions.name: do_nodename
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ai points to a writable struct addrinfo (with ai_family set when nodename is NULL), nodename is NULL or a NUL-terminated string, and hints is NULL or points to a valid addrinfo. Postcondition: it first callocs ai->ai_addr (a sockaddr_storage-sized zeroed buffer, owned by the caller afterwards and not freed on error paths) and returns EAI_MEMORY if that fails; a NULL nodename gets the wildcard address (INADDR_ANY if ai_family is AF_INET, otherwise an all-zero IPv6 address) and returns 0; a numeric IPv6 string (containing ':') or numeric IPv4 string is converted, sets ai_family/ai_addrlen and returns 0; otherwise, if hints has AI_NUMERICHOST it returns EAI_NONAME; otherwise it calls DNSlookup_name for AF_INET, and if no host is found returns EAI_AGAIN for TRY_AGAIN/EAI_AGAIN or else the lookup error (retrying numeric IPv4 parsing first on EAI_NONAME, returning 0 if that succeeds); if a host is found it copies the first address into ai_addr, sets ai_family, ai_addrlen and sa_family, sets ai_canonname to an estrdup of the host name when hints has AI_CANONNAME, and returns 0.

functions.name: rpl_vsnprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: format points to a NUL-terminated string, args matches the conversions in format, and str is either NULL or points to a writable buffer of at least size bytes (a NULL str with nonzero size is treated as size 0). Postcondition: at most size characters including the terminating NUL are written to str; when size > 0 and str is non-NULL the output is always NUL-terminated (truncated if needed), and nothing is written if size is 0; %n conversions store the count of characters produced so far through the caller's pointer; the function returns the full untruncated output length as an int, or returns -1 with errno set to EOVERFLOW if a width/precision accumulation or float formatting overflowed, or to ERANGE if the length is at least INT_MAX.

functions.name: config_tos
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ptree points to a valid config_tree whose orphan_cmds FIFO is well-formed (a possibly empty list of attr_val nodes). Postcondition: returns nothing; in a first pass it clamps the stored value.d of T_Bcpollbstep to [0,4], T_Floor and T_Ceiling to [0,STRATUM_UNSPEC-1], T_Minclock and T_Maxclock to at least 1, and T_Minsane to at least 0, logging a warning for the bcpollbstep, floor and ceiling clamps; other attributes are left unchanged. It then logs an error, without stopping, if minsane<minclock<=maxclock does not hold or if floor>ceiling, using the tracked values (starting from the sys_* globals). In a second pass it calls proto_config with the matching PROTO_* item and tos->value.d for every option except T_Basedate, which is skipped; any attribute not handled there (including T_Cohort-less unknown tokens) goes to fatal_error, which is not expected to return.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: yyparse takes no arguments; the lexer (yylex), the parser tables and the global configuration state (cfgt, lexer include stack) must be set up, because the semantic actions append to cfgt and call lex_* functions. Postcondition: it runs the LALR parse loop, reading tokens with yylex and executing the grammar actions, and returns 0 on YYACCEPT (input fully parsed), 1 on YYABORT (unrecoverable syntax error at end of input, an error-recovery stack that cannot be popped further, or the stack still full after growth), or 2 on memory exhaustion (stack size already at YYMAXDEPTH or allocation failure), in which case yyerror("memory exhausted") is called; syntax errors call yyerror("syntax error") and increment yynerrs. On every return it destroys the discarded lookahead and the symbols on the parser stack and frees the stack if it was heap-allocated; no other resources are handed to the caller beyond what the actions stored in cfgt.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the lexer yylex and the configuration globals (cfgt, old_config_style, lexer file stack) are usable and the input token stream is available; no arguments. Postcondition: runs the LALR parse loop, executing the grammar actions that append parsed configuration nodes to cfgt and may call yyerror/msyslog and free strings; on error it recovers via the error token, and it returns 0 if the input was accepted (YYACCEPT), 1 if parsing was aborted (YYABORT, e.g. unrecoverable syntax error or end of input during recovery), or 2 on parser stack exhaustion (after yyerror("memory exhausted")); on return it discards the lookahead and pops and destroys all remaining stack symbols and frees the heap-allocated stacks if they were grown.

functions.name: jjy_receive_telephone
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: rbufp->recv_peer is a valid peer whose procptr and unitptr point to a valid jjyunit, and the line buffer for the current discipline holds the received data. Postcondition: always returns JJY_RECEIVE_WAIT. If the clock state is IDLE, DAILOUT or BYE, the data goes to modem_receive, and if the modem state changed to disconnect or connect, a DISCONNECT or CONNECT event is run through teljjy_control. Otherwise the silent timer is reset, the event is set to LOGIN (text is exactly "Name ? "), PROMPT (text is exactly ">"), ERROR (text starts with "?", length at least 1) or DATA, and teljjy_control is called once.

functions.name: nextvar
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: datalen, datap, vname and vvalue are valid pointers, and *datap points to a buffer of *datalen readable bytes holding comma-separated name[=value] items, where values may contain quoted parts. Postcondition: it parses the next item, skipping silently any item with an empty name and, after reporting an error, any item whose stripped name or value does not fit the static name/value buffers. For the first acceptable item it copies the name and value into static NUL-terminated buffers, sets *vname and *vvalue to them, sets *datap past the item, sets *datalen to the bytes remaining up to the end, and returns TRUE. When no further item can be started (no name character after the separators), or a quoted value has no closing quote, it sets *datap to the end of the data, sets *datalen to 0 and returns FALSE, leaving *vname and *vvalue unchanged.

functions.name: evbuffer_read
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: buf is a valid evbuffer and fd is a socket or file descriptor to read from; the function takes the buffer lock itself and releases it before returning. Postcondition: returns -1 if the buffer's end is frozen, if space cannot be allocated, or if the read fails (read, readv or recv returns -1), with the buffer unchanged; returns 0 if the read returned 0 (EOF, or a connection abort on Windows), with the buffer unchanged; otherwise reads at most min(howmuch, readable bytes, EVBUFFER_MAX_READ) bytes (the whole cap if howmuch is negative), appends them to the buffer's chains, increases total_len and n_add_for_cb by n, invokes the buffer callbacks, and returns n, the number of bytes read (greater than 0).

functions.name: optionSetMembers
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: if opts is not one of the special OPTPROC_* sentinel values, opts and od must be valid pointers, nm_list must hold nm_ct member names, and od's option argument is read as a member-set string. Postcondition: returns nothing; for OPTPROC_EMIT_USAGE it calls enum_err, for OPTPROC_EMIT_SHELL it calls set_memb_shell, for OPTPROC_RETURN_VALNAME it calls set_memb_names, and in each case it returns without touching optCookie; otherwise if od->fOptState has OPTST_RESET set it returns unchanged; otherwise it parses the argument into a bitmask (starting from check_membership_start, handling commas, +/|/-/! prefixes, 'all', 'none', numeric values and member names, then inverting if requested and masking to nm_ct bits when nm_ct is less than the bit width of uintptr_t) and stores it in od->optCookie; if the argument is NULL, a stray ',' or '|' follows a comma, or a name is unknown (find_member_bit returns 0), od->optCookie is set to 0.

functions.name: gen_mvkey
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: id and evpars are valid, evpars has room for nkeys+3 pointers, the global nkeys is positive and at most MVMAX-1 (arrays are indexed 0..nkeys), and modulus2/nkeys is a usable prime bit size. Postcondition: it generates the MV parameters p, q, g, the polynomial coefficients, the group key b and the server and client keys; if the self-check prod(gs[i]^(a[i] x[j]^i)) = 1 fails for any j it returns NULL early, leaking all BIGNUMs, the DSA object and the BN_CTX and having written nothing to evpars or any file; otherwise it writes the trusted-authority key, the server key and nkeys client keys as PEM to the file opened by fheader, stores the trusted-authority EVP_PKEY, the server EVP_PKEY and nkeys client EVP_PKEYs in evpars followed by a NULL terminator, closes the file, frees a[i], gs[i], x[j], xbar[j], xhat[j] and s1[j], and returns the trusted-authority EVP_PKEY (evpars[0]); the other BIGNUMs and the BN_CTX are not freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the program's arguments have already been parsed into the globals and locals used here (encode, utc, Year/Month/DayOfMonth or the offset, SecondsToSend, leap-second and DST settings, SetSampleRate and so on), and the system clock is readable. Postcondition: this part of main reads the system time and sets the starting Year, DayOfYear, Hour, Minute, Second and StraightBinarySeconds, either from the given UTC date or from the clock plus offset after delaying to align with the next second. It then prints the WWV or IRIG starting point and builds the WWV code string. After that it loops SecondsToSend times (forever if zero), printing headers, setting the rate correction, stepping the leap-second state machine (deleting or inserting a second) and advancing Second, Minute and Hour with DST-switch handling. If LeapState holds an invalid value it prints a message and calls exit(-1). The slice is cut off in the middle of the DST handling, so the rest of main (output and return) is not visible here.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the command-line options (getopt style) for the tg2 time-code generator, with option arguments in the formats sscanf expects. Postcondition: the remaining options in the slice (l, o, q, r, s, t, u, v, x, y, z) set offset, quality, sample rate, leap, tone, DUT1, level, verbosity, initial date/time and debug variables; an unknown option prints a message and calls exit(-1). After option parsing, Verbose is forced on if Debug is set, leap-second and DST-switch day-of-year and pending-warning times are computed when requested, and the format character selects IRIG or WWV encoding (an unknown format prints a message and calls exit(-1)). The audio device is then opened write-only; if open returns <= 0 the program exits with status 1. With the soundcard API it sets mu-law, mono and the sample rate, exiting with -1 on any ioctl failure, wrong format or channel setting, or a rate more than 0.1% from the request; otherwise it reads the audio info and exits with 0 if that fails, then sets port, gain, rate, mono, 8-bit mu-law and applies it. On success the device is open and configured and the function continues past this slice.

functions.name: v_sentenceb
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp is a valid editor screen and vp is an initialized motion command whose m_start holds the starting cursor position and whose count is used as the repeat count if VC_C1SET is set (otherwise 1). Postcondition: if the start is line 1, column 0 it returns 0 immediately without changing anything; otherwise it moves backward to the start of the cnt-th previous sentence (stopping at start of file if there are fewer), sets vp->m_stop and vp->m_final to that position, and for motion commands adjusts vp->m_start (either to the last character of the previous line with VM_LMODE set, or by decrementing its column) and returns 0; it returns 1 if cs_init, cs_prev, cs_next, cs_bblank, cs_fblank or db_get fails, in which case it may already have partly modified vp. No locks, references or memory are acquired or released.

functions.name: v_txt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: this slice is the middle of the key-dispatch switch inside the main input loop of v_txt (nvi vi text input), so sp, tp (the current TEXT with lb, cno, offset, ai, owrite), evp (the current event), the flags and is_flags are valid and a key has been read. Postcondition: for K_VWERASE the cursor moves back over trailing blanks and then one word (rules depend on TXT_TTYWERASE/TXT_ALTWERASE), stopping at the autoindent column or the offset, bumping owrite for each character erased and blanking them if an incremental search is running (then IS_RESTART is set), or it bells (unless TXT_REPLAY) when already at the offset. For K_VKILL it first tries txt_backup to the previous line when cno is 0 (goto err if that fails), then kills back to the autoindent or offset the same way. For K_CNTRLT it adds autoindent via txt_dent or inserts the char as normal when TXT_CNTRLT is unset. For K_VLNEXT it sets the quote flags and inserts a '^' placeholder. K_HEXCHAR starts hex collection. K_TAB expands to spaces when expandtab applies. Otherwise the character is checked for showmatch, illegal control characters (message, then goto done on replay, else break), abbreviation expansion (goto err on failure, goto resolve if one was expanded) and unmap handling, then inserted with txt_insch (goto err on failure) and hex-decoded via txt_hex after the third hex digit (goto err on failure). The function is not a standalone function here; the slice belongs to v_txt and falls through to later code of that function.

functions.name: v_txt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp is a valid screen, tp is the current TEXT line on sp->tiq, and the caller passes flags (TXT_RECORD, TXT_REPLAY, TXT_CR, TXT_AUTOINDENT, etc.) describing the input mode. Postcondition: this part of the text-input loop handles one event: it may replay recorded input (jumping to done if nothing was recorded), set TERM_CEDIT for the cedit character, run filename completion, expand and limit abbreviations, record or replay the event, insert quoted characters, convert hex sequences, and on CR/NL either set TERM_CR/TERM_SEARCH and finish, or save line lengths, update the old line, and append a new TEXT (made by text_init, with insert/owrite/lno set and autoindent carried over) to the tail of sp->tiq. Any failure in completion, hex, abbreviation, screen update, text allocation or autoindent jumps to the err path, and the other exits are the done, resolve and k_escape paths.

functions.name: bword
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp and vp are valid, vp->m_start holds the cursor position, and vp->count is used only if VC_C1SET is set (otherwise the count is 1); type selects BIGWORD or small-word motion. Postcondition: it moves backward over cnt words from m_start and returns 0 after setting vp->m_stop and vp->m_final to the resulting position, decrementing vp->m_start.cno by one if ISMOTION(vp); it returns 1 without setting m_stop or m_final if cs_init, cs_prev, cs_next or cs_bblank fails, or if the position did not move from m_start (at start of file), in which case v_sof is first called on m_start.

functions.name: vs_colpos
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp is a valid screen and lno names a line of the file being edited (the function reads it with db_get); cno is a screen column, possibly beyond the first screen row. Postcondition: returns 0 if the line is missing or empty; otherwise it skips cno / sp->cols screen rows and returns llen - 1 if the line ends before that row is reached, else steps through characters and, on reaching a character whose end column scno is >= cno % sp->cols, returns the offset of the next character (or llen - 1 if it is the last) when scno equals the column, or the offset of the character that overruns the column otherwise; if no such character is found it returns llen - 1. It takes no locks and gives the caller no references or memory.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command line, whose first non-option argument is a destination (lid or other portid string), and the IB device and a mirroring-capable switch (device id 0x1b3) are reachable. Postcondition: it parses options (usage is shown if no destination is given), opens the MAD port, resolves the destination and reads the vendor general info, and calls IBEXIT (terminating with an error) if opening the port, resolving the destination, the vendor call, the device-id check, the lossy firmware check (FW < 7.4.0 when lossy is set), or the set-mode validation (no dport and dlid, or no Rx and Tx ports) fails; otherwise it prints the FW version and, in debug mode, the configuration, then runs mirror_config and, if lossy_set, lossy_config for the Clear, Read or Set operation, closes the port and exits with status 0. It never returns normally.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds a destination (lid, guid or direct route), a port number and optional operation words (enable, disable, on, off, reset, down, arm, active, query, or speed, espeed, fdr10, width, vls, mtu, lid, smlid, lmc, mkey, mkeylease, mkeyprot with a value), and the local IB port can be opened. Postcondition: the function never returns; it prints the port's PortInfo (and Mellanox extended info if supported), then if an operation or value was given it writes the modified PortInfo to the port (for op ON it instead prints 'Port is already in enable state' and skips the write if the physical state is not Disabled), otherwise for a query of a switch port with non-zero number in Active state it reads and prints the peer port's info and validates link width and speed, warning on mismatches; it then closes the MAD port and calls exit(0). Bad arguments, failure to open or resolve ports, setting M_Key fields on a non-zero switch port, too many hops, or failure to resolve self end the process through IBEXIT, or show usage when fewer than two arguments are given.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the command line of the RC pingpong program (options -p -d -i -s -m -r -n -l -e -g -o -t and at most one server name) and an RDMA device is reachable. Postcondition: it parses options, opens the device, creates the context, exchanges addresses with the peer and runs the ping-pong loop until iters sends and receives have completed; it then prints the throughput statistics (plus timestamp statistics with -t), acks the CQ events, closes the context, frees the device list and the remote destination and returns 0. It returns 1 on a bad option, a bad extra argument, or any setup, exchange, connect, post, poll, time or close failure; in timestamp mode a nonzero ret from ibv_start_poll (other than retried ENOENT) or from parse_single_wc, or a non-ENOENT failure from ibv_next_poll, is returned as that value; on these error paths resources are not released.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the usual program arguments (options -a, -I, -P, -p, -C, -S, -t, -s, -c, -v, -V, -d are parsed with getopt). Postcondition: allocates and initializes a control block; returns -ENOMEM if the allocation fails; on an address error from get_addr, an invalid size or count (EINVAL), an unknown option (usage printed, EINVAL), or neither -s nor -c given (usage printed, EINVAL) it frees the block and returns that error; if event channel creation fails it returns errno; if rdma_create_id or pthread_create fails it destroys the event channel, frees the block and returns that error code; otherwise it runs the persistent server, the server or the client, destroys the cm_id and the event channel, frees the block and returns the run's result (0 on success). The cb block is always freed before return, except in the -ENOMEM case where nothing was allocated. After a successful pthread_create the cm thread is not joined.

functions.name: link_mgr_set_physp_pi
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sm is an initialized SM with valid subnet options, p_physp is a physical port with a valid node pointer and cached PortInfo, and port_state is a requested IB link state (or IB_LINK_NO_CHANGE). Postcondition: builds a new PortInfo (and, when FDR10 needs changing, a Mellanox extended PortInfo) from the cached values and subnet options; sends a PortInfo Set via osm_req_set only if something changed (or on a switch external port during the first master sweep), and sends the extended PortInfo Set if needed; updates the guid2mkey map if the M_Key changed; returns 0 normally, including when base switch port 0 needs no update and is skipped, or when no switch is found for port 0 (error logged, nothing sent); returns -1 if any osm_req_set call fails. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: osm_mcast_tbl_get_block
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_tbl and p_block are non-null, and p_block has room for IB_MCAST_BLOCK_SIZE (and at least IB_SMP_DATA_SIZE bytes) entries; if block_num <= p_tbl->max_block_in_use and position <= p_tbl->max_position then block_num * IB_MCAST_BLOCK_SIZE <= p_tbl->mft_depth (asserted). Postcondition: returns FALSE and leaves p_block untouched if block_num > p_tbl->max_block_in_use; otherwise returns TRUE, and if position > p_tbl->max_position it zero-fills IB_SMP_DATA_SIZE bytes of p_block, else it copies the IB_MCAST_BLOCK_SIZE mask-table entries (*p_tbl->p_mask_tbl)[block_num*IB_MCAST_BLOCK_SIZE + i][position] into p_block[i] for i in [0, IB_MCAST_BLOCK_SIZE).

functions.name: osm_prtn_config_parse_file
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_log and p_subn are valid OpenSM log and subnet objects and file_name is a valid C string path. Postcondition: returns -1 if the file cannot be opened (logging a verbose message, nothing to close); otherwise reads the file line by line, strips '#' comments, splits statements on ';' and parses each via parse_part_conf (flushing and resetting the partition config at each ';'), then closes the file and returns 0 if the last status was success (is_parse_success == 1, meaning the last processed non-empty statement parsed without error), or 1 if no statement was parsed (empty file), a parse error occurred (parse_part_conf returned negative), or creating the partition config failed (an error is logged and printed to stderr). A partially built config not terminated by ';' is not flushed here.

functions.name: osm_sa_db_file_load
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_osm points to a valid initialized OpenSM instance. Postcondition: returns 0 without touching anything if this is not the first master sweep or no sa_db_file name is configured; returns -1 if the file cannot be opened; otherwise reads the file line by line and loads the MC Group, mcm_port, Service, InformInfo and GUIDInfo records into the SA database (parse failures inside PARSE_AHEAD jump to _error, which closes the file and returns ret). Multicast groups are kept or deleted via sa_db_file_load_handle_mgrp once their member records are parsed, mlids_init_max is raised to the largest mlid seen, and no_clients_rereg is set to FALSE if any record failed to load. On full success the sa dirty flag is cleared, the file is closed and ret (0 in the code shown) is returned. The file is always closed once it was opened.

functions.name: osm_mftr_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is a valid osm_sa_t pointer and data a valid osm_madw_t pointer holding an SA MAD with attribute MFTRecord, and the caller does not hold sa->p_lock. Postcondition: if the method is neither SubnAdmGet nor SubnAdmGetTable, an error reply with status IB_MAD_STATUS_UNSUP_METHOD_ATTR is sent via osm_sa_send_error and nothing else is done; otherwise the function takes sa->p_lock, and if the requester physical port cannot be found it releases the lock, logs an error and sends no response; otherwise it builds a list of matching MFT records by applying mftr_rcv_by_comp_mask over the switch GUID table, releases the lock, and sends the response with osm_sa_respond (record size sizeof(ib_mft_record_t), passing the list). The lock is released on every path where it was taken, nothing is returned, and the function logs entry and exit.

functions.name: mpr_rcv_get_path_parms
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sa, p_mpr, p_src_alias_guid, p_dest_alias_guid and the output parameter pointer are valid, the subnet's switches have LID routing tables, and the caller keeps ownership of everything (no locks taken, no memory transferred). Postcondition: the function walks the route from the source port to the destination port for the destination LID, lowering the MTU and rate to the minimum over the ports on the route and clearing from the valid SL mask every SL that maps to the drop VL on some switch when QoS is enabled. It returns IB_NOT_FOUND when the source switch has no route to the destination LID (ERR 4515), when the path needs more than MAX_HOPS hops (ERR 4520), when all SLs lead to VL15 on some hop, when a matching QoS level requires an SL that is not valid, or when the MTU or rate selector in p_mpr cannot be satisfied. It returns IB_ERROR for a missing remote physical port (ERR 4505), a non-switch node mid-path (ERR 4503), a dead-end route on a switch (ERR 4516), or an invalid MTU or rate selector value. Otherwise it continues past the end of this slice to produce the result, which is not shown here. On failure the caller loses nothing.

functions.name: pr_rcv_get_path_parms
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sa, the path record request, both alias GUID entries and the source/destination physical ports are valid, and the subnet routing tables are populated. Postcondition: the function walks the route hop by hop from the source port to the destination port, lowering mtu and rate to the path minimum and, when QoS is enabled, clearing SLs that map to VL15 in valid_sl_mask. It returns IB_NOT_FOUND if the destination switch has no route to the destination LID, if all SLs lead to VL15, if the hop count exceeds MAX_HOPS, if the QoS-selected SL is not valid, or if the requested MTU selector cannot be met. It returns IB_ERROR if a remote physical port is missing, a non-switch node is reached before the destination, or a switch has no route to the destination LID. Otherwise it continues with QoS adjustment, the packet lifetime (0 for a loopback path) and the MTU selector checks, all of which jump to Exit on failure. The slice is cut off in the middle of the MTU selector switch, so the later code and the final success return are not shown.

functions.name: osm_pir_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is a valid osm_sa_t and data a valid osm_madw_t carrying a PortInfoRecord SA MAD; the caller does not hold sa->p_lock, since the function acquires it itself. Postcondition: if the method is neither Get nor GetTable it sends an IB_MAD_STATUS_UNSUP_METHOD_ATTR error and returns without taking the lock; if the requester physical port cannot be found it releases the lock, logs an error and returns without responding; otherwise it builds a list of matching PortInfoRecords (only for the port with the requested LID if LID or BaseLID is in the component mask, logging an error if no such port exists, else for all nodes), releases sa->p_lock, zeroes the m_key of each record when the MAD sm_key is zero, and calls osm_sa_respond with the list. It returns nothing.

functions.name: osm_smir_rcv_process
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is a valid osm_sa_t and data is an osm_madw_t carrying an SA MAD for an SMInfoRecord request; the caller does not hold sa->p_lock (the function acquires it). Postcondition: if the method is neither Get nor GetTable it sends an IB_MAD_STATUS_UNSUP_METHOD_ATTR error and returns without taking the lock; otherwise it takes sa->p_lock and, if the requester physical port, the local SM port or (for the local SM) the pkey sharing check cannot be satisfied, it releases the lock, logs an error and returns without sending any response; if a LID was given but no port matches, it adds no records; otherwise it adds the matching local and/or remote SMInfo records to a list. On all non-error paths it releases the lock and calls osm_sa_respond with the (possibly empty) list; nothing is returned.

functions.name: do_sweep
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sm points to a valid, initialized osm_sm_t with its subnet, log, lock and managers set up, and the caller is the state-manager sweep context. Postcondition: returns nothing; it returns early without doing a sweep if the SM state is neither MASTER nor DISCOVERING, and otherwise performs a light sweep, a reroute-only pass, or a full heavy sweep (repeating discovery while a new heavy sweep is requested), resetting the sweep flags and reporting events. It returns early on any failed or pending step: sweep_hop_0/1 failure, pending transactions, reroute failure, SM port down (drop manager run, move to DISCOVERING), a higher or master SM found (standby/handover/wait-for-handover/polling-timeout signals), or a unicast routing failure. On full success it configures LIDs, routing, multicast, GUIDs and links, clears coming_out_of_standby and first_time_master_sweep, signals subnet_up_event, stores the databases and reports SUBNET_UP. The write lock is held only briefly while setting polling_sm_guid and is released.

functions.name: osm_switch_recommend_path
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_sw and p_port are valid, lid_ho is a positive host-order LID, and the switch's hop-count tables and port profiles are populated (with p_port->priv pointing to remote-guid counts when routing_for_lmc and dor are used). Postcondition: returns 0 if the target port is on this same switch; returns the remote switch's port number if the target is an end port whose remote switch is p_sw; returns OSM_NO_PATH if the target has no remote switch, the switch has no known hops to its base LID, or no healthy, linked least-hop port exists; otherwise returns an existing LFT port for lid_ho if it is healthy, linked and has least hops (unless ignore_existing), else a healthy, linked, least-hop output port chosen by lowest path count, with LMC remote-guid, DOR, scatter and port-shifting adjustments (the code after the shown part is not visible, so this last selection is described from the visible logic only). The function only reads switch state apart from local scratch arrays.

functions.name: auditd_expire_trails
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global directory queue dir_q holds the audit trail directories to scan, and warn_expired is either NULL or a callable function pointer. Postcondition: returns ADE_PARSE if getacexpire fails, ADE_NOERR with no work if neither an expire age nor an expire size is configured, and ADE_READLINK if the current-trail link cannot be read. Otherwise it scans each directory for regular trail files (skipping the current trail), sorts them by timestamp oldest first, and for each file meeting the size/age condition (AND or OR per the configuration) calls warn_expired if set and unlinks it. It returns ADE_NOMEM if an allocation failed during the scan, and ADE_EXPIRE if an unlink failed (the last of these to be set wins; otherwise ADE_NOERR). All list nodes and path strings it allocates are freed before return, though a scan interrupted by an allocation failure still goes on to expire the files collected so far.

functions.name: TrcPktProcEtmV4I::BuildIPacketTable
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: m_config holds the trace configuration and m_i_table has 256 entries. Postcondition: returns nothing; all 256 m_i_table entries are first set to ETM4_PKT_I_RESERVED with the iPktReserved handler, then each header byte with a defined packet gets its pkt_type and handler (extension, trace info, timestamp, trace on, exceptions, cycle counts, data-sync markers, speculation resolution, conditional, event, context, address, Q and atom packets). Several entries depend on the configuration: ETE (MajVersion>=5) turns on the ETE packets and makes exception-return (0x07) invalid-config, the ITE packet needs MinVersion>=3, data-trace and conditional-trace packets use iPktInvalidCfg when their feature is disabled, the 0x70 ignore, 0x88 timestamp marker and 0xB0-0xB9 ETE source-address packets need FullVersion>=0x43, >=0x46 and >=0x50 respectively, the 0x05 function-return handler is set only for a v8 Cortex-M with FullVersion>=0x42, and Q packets are enabled only when hasQElem() and are not reserved codes.

functions.name: T_FUNC(final_percent, "template ends with %")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function t_final_percent_func(desc, arg); both parameters are unused and may be anything. It calls openpam_subst(NULL, buf, &bufsize, template) on a local buffer holding "Squeamish Ossifrage" and the template "test%" (followed by a hidden NUL and "deadbeef").
