It returns nonzero (true) only if openpam_subst returned PAM_SUCCESS, bufsize equals sizeof("test%") (6) and buf compares equal to "test%"; otherwise it returns 0. It acquires no locks and transfers no memory to the caller.

functions.name: pamk5_authenticate
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: args is a valid pam_args with a config and a usable PAM handle. Postcondition: returns a PAM status code. PAM_USER_UNKNOWN is returned if the user is ignored; any error from context creation, password authentication, authorization or the forced password change is returned (PAM_AUTH_ERR if fail_pwchange is set and the password was expired); PAM_SERVICE_ERR is returned if storing the context as PAM data fails; otherwise PAM_SUCCESS is returned, or the result of pamk5_cache_init_random when a ccache is created. With defer_pwchange an expired account sets ctx->expired and succeeds. On success the context is stored as PAM data "pam_krb5" (PAM then owns it) and args->ctx is set to NULL. The obtained credentials are always freed. On failure, if the context was stored the PAM data is cleared, otherwise the context is freed with pamk5_context_free.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(crit,   LOG_CRIT)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_crit(pargs, fmt, ...) (the same invocation also generates putil_crit_pam). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: logs the formatted message at LOG_CRIT through log_vplain, prefixed with the user when pargs->user is set, or via plain syslog with LOG_AUTHPRIV when pargs is NULL; if formatting fails it logs a vasprintf failure and logs nothing else; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(err,    LOG_ERR)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_err(pargs, fmt, ...) (the same invocation also generates putil_err_pam). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: logs the formatted message at LOG_ERR through log_vplain, prefixed with the user when pargs->user is set, or via plain syslog with LOG_AUTHPRIV when pargs is NULL; if formatting fails it logs a vasprintf failure and logs nothing else; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(notice, LOG_NOTICE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_notice(pargs, fmt, ...) (the same invocation also generates putil_notice_pam). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: logs the formatted message at LOG_NOTICE through log_vplain, prefixed with the user when pargs->user is set, or via plain syslog with LOG_AUTHPRIV when pargs is NULL; if formatting fails it logs a vasprintf failure and logs nothing else; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(debug,  LOG_DEBUG)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_debug(pargs, fmt, ...) (the same invocation also generates putil_debug_pam). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: does nothing unless pargs is non-NULL and pargs->debug is set; otherwise logs the formatted message at LOG_DEBUG, prefixed with the user when pargs->user is set; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(crit,   LOG_CRIT)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_crit_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: formats the message and logs it at LOG_CRIT via log_plain; when pargs is non-NULL and status is not PAM_SUCCESS it appends ": " and pam_strerror(status); if formatting fails nothing is logged beyond the vasprintf failure message; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(err,    LOG_ERR)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_err_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: formats the message and logs it at LOG_ERR via log_plain; when pargs is non-NULL and status is not PAM_SUCCESS it appends ": " and pam_strerror(status); if formatting fails nothing is logged beyond the vasprintf failure message; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(notice, LOG_NOTICE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_notice_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: formats the message and logs it at LOG_NOTICE via log_plain; when pargs is non-NULL and status is not PAM_SUCCESS it appends ": " and pam_strerror(status); if formatting fails nothing is logged beyond the vasprintf failure message; returns nothing.

functions.name: LOG_FUNCTION(debug,  LOG_DEBUG)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function putil_debug_pam(pargs, status, fmt, ...). Precondition: fmt is a valid printf format matching the arguments; pargs may be NULL. Postcondition: does nothing unless pargs is non-NULL and pargs->debug is set; otherwise formats the message and logs it at LOG_DEBUG via log_plain, appending ": " and pam_strerror(status) when status is not PAM_SUCCESS; returns nothing.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the program name followed by options (-C cfile, -f, -q, -u, -x, -N) and then exactly typename, mapname, keyname (plus a value for -u), with exactly one of -q, -u, -x given. Postcondition: the function never returns normally; it terminates the process via exit(). A usage error calls usage(). With HASFCHOWN, an unopenable sendmail.cf exits with EX_NOINPUT. A failure to open the map exits with EX_CANTCREAT, with a recompile hint if the type is unsupported. Otherwise it syncs the database, optionally sets the owner to TrustedUid when running as root, and performs the query, update or delete. It then closes and frees the database and exits with EX_OK, or EX_UNAVAILABLE if a query key is not found, or EX_IOERR if the update fails, the delete fails for any reason other than not-found, or the close fails. A delete of a missing key leaves the status unchanged.

functions.name: mi_milteropen
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: conn is a writable NUL-terminated string of the form [protocol:]filename or [protocol:]port@host (it is temporarily modified but restored), name is a NUL-terminated string used in log messages, backlog is the listen backlog and rmsocket says whether an existing UNIX socket file may be removed. Postcondition: on success it returns a listening, close-on-exec stream socket bound to the parsed address, sets L_family (and L_socksize while parsing), and for a UNIX socket allocates and sets the global sockpath with the socket path; on any failure (NULL or empty conn, unknown socket type, UNIX path too long, bad or unknown port, bad numeric host, unknown host or protocol, socket/fcntl/setsockopt/stat/unlink/bind/listen failure, non-socket file at the path, malloc failure for sockpath) it logs an error and returns INVALID_SOCKET, closing the created socket if one existed.

functions.name: sm_vfscanf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid open SM_FILE_T stream, fmt0 is a NUL-terminated scanf-style format string, and ap supplies pointer arguments matching each non-suppressed conversion (the stream's buffer is addressable). Postcondition: reads and consumes input from fp according to the format, storing converted values through the pointers from ap; returns the number of successfully assigned conversions when the format ends or on a match failure (a literal mismatch or an empty/invalid %[ or numeric/float field); returns SM_IO_EOF (with errno set to EAGAIN) if timeout is SM_TIME_IMMEDIATE, or if the timeout expires via longjmp; returns SM_IO_EOF if the format ends with a lone '%' (NUL conversion character); on input failure (refill fails before a conversion could read data) returns the number assigned so far, or -1 if none were assigned; any timeout event it set up is cleared on every return except the timeout-expiry path, and no locks or references are transferred.

functions.name: sm_vfscanf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid open SM_FILE_T, fmt0 is a NUL-terminated format string, and ap supplies a pointer argument of the proper type for every non-suppressed conversion in the format. Postcondition: if the timeout is SM_TIME_IMMEDIATE (after defaulting from fp->f_timeout), or the timeout fires, it sets errno to EAGAIN and returns SM_IO_EOF; otherwise it scans input per the format, storing converted values through the va_list pointers and consuming input from fp. It returns the number of assigned fields when the format ends or on a match failure (a literal mismatch, an empty %[ set, or a number with no digits, where a lone sign or 'x' is pushed back). It returns SM_IO_EOF when the format has a stray '%' followed by NUL. On input failure (EOF before the first character of a conversion) it returns the number assigned if that is nonzero, else -1. Any timeout event it created is cleared on every return except the setjmp timeout path.

functions.name: smndbm_open
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: db_name, mode, sff, user_info and the database output pointer are valid for use, and type is the db type string. Postcondition: *database is set to NULL first; if type is NULL it returns SMDBE_UNKNOWN_DB_TYPE, and if smdb_setup_file for the .dir or .pag file, or smdb_lock_file for the .dir file (or for the .pag file when the files are being created, in which case lock_fd is closed first), fails it returns that error; otherwise it allocates handles, opens the ndbm database (O_TRUNC added and O_CREAT|O_EXCL cleared if the lock files were just created), and rejects allocation failure (SMDBE_MALLOC), open failure (SMDBE_BAD_OPEN or errno), a GDBM-style database whose dir and pag descriptors are equal (SMDBE_GDBM_IS_BAD) and changed files (the smdb_filechanged error). On success it stores the handle with all method pointers set in *database, keeps the lock fd held, and returns SMDBE_OK; on failure after locking it closes the dbm if open, unlocks the lock fd, frees both structs, leaves *database NULL and returns the error (note the cleanup dereferences db even if its allocation failed).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the makemap command line (options, then exactly two operands: type and map name) and the sendmail globals and I/O streams are usable. Postcondition: it never returns normally and ends via exit(): it exits EX_OK after -l, -L or -x, calls usage() on a bad option or when the operand count is not 2, exits EX_DATAERR if the type resolves to the empty string from the config file with no fallback, EX_CANTCREAT if the database cannot be opened, and EX_SOFTWARE if a cursor cannot be made in -u mode; otherwise it either dumps every key/value pair to stdout (-u) or inserts each valid stdin line into the database (skipping comment and empty lines, and reporting too-long lines, leading-space lines and lines with no RHS and setting EX_DATAERR). Finally it closes and frees the database and exits with EX_OK, EX_DATAERR, or EX_IOERR if the close failed.

functions.name: load_if_names
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none beyond sendmail's runtime state (it takes no arguments). Postcondition: it returns nothing; it queries the kernel for the interface list (SIOCGLIFCONF with IPv6, otherwise SIOCGIFCONF), and for each AF_INET or AF_INET6 interface that is UP and has a specified address, it adds the bracketed IP address to class 'w' if absent. Unless DontProbeInterfaces is DPI_SKIPLOOPBACK and the interface is loopback, it also calls add_hostnames on the address. It returns early without work if socket creation fails or the interface count is not positive. On an ioctl failure it closes the socket and, in the IPv6 variant, frees the buffer, but the IPv4 variant leaks the buffer on ioctl failure. If socket recreation fails inside the IPv6 loop it frees the buffer and returns. On a normal finish it frees the buffer and closes the socket.

functions.name: hostnamebyanyaddr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sap points to a valid SOCKADDR whose family field is set. Postcondition: temporarily shortens the resolver retry count (when NAMED_BIND) and restores it, then performs a reverse lookup by address family (AF_UNIX gives no lookup). If the lookup yields a host name that does not start with '[' and is not a literal IPv6 or IPv4 address, it returns that name sanitized by denlstring (copied to a static buffer when denlstring returned the original string under NETINET6) and frees the hostent where NETINET6 is defined. Otherwise it frees the hostent and returns "localhost" for an AF_UNIX address with an empty path, else a static buffer holding "[<numeric address>]" from anynet_ntoa. It never returns NULL, and the result may be a static buffer overwritten by later calls and must not be freed by the caller.

functions.name: deliver
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: e is a valid envelope and firstto is a non-NULL address whose q_mailer is set; e->e_from.q_mailer is non-NULL. Postcondition: if firstto's state is not OK it returns 0 at once; otherwise it builds the recipient chain for the same mailer and signature, and delivers it by LPC, IPC/SMTP/LMTP or by forking the mailer. Each chained recipient is marked sent (QS_SENT) on success, or marked failed or queued via markfailure, and any other recipients are failed or discarded individually (too large, check_compat, discard, [FILE] mailer). Failed connections fall over to the next MX host. A non-cached SMTP connection is closed via smtpquit, and a cached one stays open. The function returns 0 when there is nothing to send, -1 on too many parameters before $u, and otherwise the final EX_* status code (EX_OK, EX_TEMPFAIL, EX_CONFIG, EX_OSERR, EX_SOFTWARE, EX_DATAERR, EX_UNAVAILABLE and so on). For LMTP the returned code is reset to EX_OK after per-recipient status handling. State is restored in the cleanup block and any exception from the SM_TRY block is rethrown.

functions.name: logdelivery
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: e is a valid envelope; m, mci, to, ctladdr, status, dsn, rcode, xstart and now are the values supplied by the delivery code (m, mci, to, ctladdr and dsn may be NULL where the code checks for it), and status is a non-NULL string. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and writes only syslog entries for the envelope id; when SYSLOG_BUFSIZE >= 256 it builds a single stat line (delay, xdelay, mailer, relay, pri, size, ntries, stage, reply, truncated if too long, stat=status) and logs the to= list, split into several "[more]" lines at commas when too long, each followed by that line, and it also logs an ERROR line if the reply code is inconsistent with the expected type; when SYSLOG_BUFSIZE < 256 it logs separate lines for to=, ctladdr (if any), delay/xdelay/mailer, relay or quarantine info (if any) and stat=. The envelope is not modified.

functions.name: sm_errstring
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: errnum is an error number (system errno, E_DNSBASE+resolver code, E_LDAPBASE-based code or an E_SM_* code); CurHostName and SmtpPhase, when non-NULL, are valid NUL-terminated strings. Postcondition: returns a message string and never NULL (except that strerror or ldap_err2string results are passed through as given): for ETIMEDOUT/ECONNRESET it formats the system message in the static buffer, adding " with " or "Connection reset by " plus the shortened host name when CurHostName is set, and " during <SmtpPhase>" when SmtpPhase is set; for EHOSTDOWN or ECONNREFUSED with a host name it returns a static buffer "Host X is down" or "Connection refused by X"; for EPERM and the E_SM_* codes it returns a constant string; for DNS codes it returns the static buffer "Name server: [host: ]msg"; for LDAP codes (when LDAPMAP) it returns ldap_err2string's result; otherwise it returns strerror's string, or a static buffer "Error N" if strerror returns NULL or (without strerror) errnum is outside 1..sys_nerr-1. The static buffer is overwritten on later calls and is not thread-safe; the caller acquires no ownership.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called once at process start with the usual argc/argv/envp (a second entry aborts after syserr). Postcondition: it parses options, reads the configuration and initialises queues and the operation mode, then runs the selected mode; most paths end in finis() with an exit status (EX_OK, EX_USAGE, EX_CONFIG, EX_NOPERM, EX_OSERR or ExitStat) and do not return. Some early paths return EX_OK for -bt-less show-config (-bS) or EX_USAGE for an invalid mode, a frozen-config request or a missing -L argument. Test mode loops forever reading addresses. A one-shot queue run waits for children with sm_wait, stopping when CurChildren is 0 or on ECHILD, then calls finis. Daemon or queue-interval mode forks into the background unless run in the foreground, runs the queue, and either keeps monitoring persistent queue runners or pauses in a loop; otherwise it goes on to serve requests through getrequests. The caller loses nothing; the function owns all allocated memory and signal setup.

functions.name: dns_map_parseargs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: map points to a valid MAP and args is a writable NUL-terminated option string (options of the form -X, separated by whitespace). Postcondition: allocates a struct dns_map (xalloc), parses the options, setting map flags, map_app, map_tapp, map_file (base domain), timeout, retry, column delimiter, size limit, and the DNS record type and DNSSEC option; the option text is modified in place by NUL-terminating each option. Bad options (nsportip failure, unknown -R type, missing -R type) are reported through syserr, not by return value. The map_app and map_tapp strings are copied with newstr, map->map_db1 is set to the new dns_map, and the function always returns true.

functions.name: get_tls_se_features
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ssl is non-NULL (SM_REQUIRE) and e, tlsi_ctx are valid; srv selects server or client mode. Postcondition: it runs the ruleset tls_srv_features or tls_clt_features via rscheck (with error suppression and QuickAbort off, both restored afterwards), and if that fails, returns no option string, or returns a string shorter than 2 characters, it returns the rscheck status rv (EX_OK when the string was empty or missing). Otherwise it optionally strips surrounding double quotes (a quoted string of length <= 2 after stripping returns EX_OK without applying anything), then parses ';'-separated opt=val pairs, modifying the option string in place. It applies options (SSL options, cipherlist, ciphersuites if TLSv1.3, flags bits into tlsi_ctx, keyfile/certfile, and with _FFR_MTA_STS servername/sts, which may replace STS_SNI with a newly allocated copy), and loads the cert/key pair if both are given. It returns rv (EX_OK) on success, and EX_CONFIG on invalid syntax, an unknown option, an option value that fails to apply, an invalid servername value, or only one of keyfile/certfile given.

functions.name: setoption
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: opt is an option code (or ' ' for a full-word option name, in which case val is a writable string "name[.subopt]=value"), val is a writable NUL-terminated string, e is a valid envelope, and the global option table and state are initialised. Postcondition: returns nothing; it resolves the option (reporting syserr and returning early for a null, unknown or ambiguous name, and returning silently if the option is sticky and not itself sticky-set); it may drop privileges if the option is unsafe for an unprivileged caller; it then stores the parsed value in the global setting for that option (for example aliases file, hop count, delivery mode, error mode, uid/gid, queue sort order, TLS/SASL settings), modifying val in place and allocating copies with newstr; invalid values produce syserr or warnings; invalid delivery mode, or an unknown 8-bit mode, call finis(false,true,EX_USAGE); unknown options are ignored; and finally, if sticky is set and the option has no suboptions, it marks the option sticky.

functions.name: smtp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: nullserver is NULL or a reply string, d_flags is the daemon flag set, and e is a valid envelope; the process has SMTP input and output channels (InChannel and OutChannel) open. Postcondition: the function sends the greeting and then runs the SMTP command loop, reading one command line at a time and replying through message()/usrerr(). Each command (HELO/EHLO, MAIL, RCPT, DATA, AUTH, STARTTLS, VRFY, ETRN and so on) is dispatched on its code. A MAIL command is rejected with a 503 or 530 error, or silently ignored if the "from" keyword is missing, when HELO is required but not given, when a mail transaction is already open, when authentication is required, or when the connection is tempfailed. Otherwise the MAIL command sets the sender, macros and ESMTP arguments, and runs check_mail, the size check, the disk space check and the milter check. On success it sends "250 2.1.0 Sender ok" and sets sm_gotmail. On any error or QuickAbort exception it clears EF_PM_NOTIFY from e_flags and leaves the command without setting sm_gotmail. The loop ends through the doquit path (QUIT, lost input, too many bad commands, open proxy, milter shutdown or similar), where the connection state is torn down; the function returns void.

functions.name: readauth
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: filename is a writable NUL-terminated string (a leading '|' means a program command, only when !_FFR_ALLOW_SASLINFO, and it is tokenized in place by strtok), sai points to an array of string slots with at least SASL_MECHLIST+1 entries, and rpool is a valid resource pool. Postcondition: returns EX_UNAVAILABLE if filename is NULL or empty, without touching anything else; returns EX_TEMPFAIL if the file or program cannot be opened (logging if LogLevel > 5), or if fewer than SASL_PASSWORD lines were read (logging if LogLevel > 8); otherwise returns EX_OK. After opening, it reads non-comment lines (those not starting with '#') into (*sai)[0..lc-1], up to SASL_MECHLIST+1 lines, each a copy allocated in rpool with the trailing newline removed. The file is closed and any program child is waited for before returning, whether the result is EX_OK or EX_TEMPFAIL after reading.

functions.name: xconnect
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: inchannel is the SMTP connection stream; the globals RealHostName, RealHostAddr, InChannel, OutChannel and BlankEnvelope are initialised, and the x_connect ruleset can be consulted. Postcondition: returns 0 without reading input if rscap returns EX_UNAVAILABLE or any other non-EX_OK status (the latter is logged), or if the ruleset result starts with CANONNET ($#, no x-connect). Otherwise it reads one line from InChannel (with the to_nextcommand timeout) and returns -1 if the line is NULL, lacks the required prefix ("PROXY " when the ruleset result is "haproxy1", otherwise "X-CONNECT "), is a haproxy line that is neither UNKNOWN nor TCP4/TCP6, or its address is not a valid IPv4 or IPv6 address; returns -2 for a haproxy "UNKNOWN" line. On a valid address it stores it in RealHostAddr. In haproxy mode it also stores the port taken from the field after the source address (when present), frees RealHostName (set to NULL via SM_FREE) and returns D_XCNCT. In plain x-connect mode it returns D_XCNCT if there is no hostname parameter, otherwise it frees RealHostName, sets it to a newly allocated copy of the hostname (truncated to MAXNAME characters), and returns D_XCNCT_M if the next parameter begins with 'M', else D_XCNCT. The input line buffer is modified (NULs written at the address end and hostname end, the hostname delimiter is restored, and a CR/LF may be cut when debugging).

functions.name: Jim_DictCoreCommand
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: interp is a valid interpreter and argv holds argc valid objects. Postcondition: Jim_ParseSubCmd resolves argv[1] against the dict subcommand table; if it fails (unknown subcommand or wrong argument count) the function returns JIM_ERR. If the entry has a handler function, that function's return value is returned. Otherwise the subcommand is run inline: get, getdef/getwithdefault, set, exists, unset, keys, values, size, merge, create, info and with return JIM_OK or JIM_ERR and set the result or variable as appropriate, and getdef/getwithdefault set the default value as the result when the key is missing. Append, lappend, incr, remove, for, replace and update (and any other unhandled entry) return the result of Jim_EvalEnsemble for "dict" with the subcommand name. For update with fewer than 6 arguments or an odd argc, the ensemble call is made with no extra arguments. The function takes no ownership of the arguments.

functions.name: Jim_execInit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: interp is a valid Jim interpreter. Postcondition: calls Jim_PackageProvideCheck for "exec", allocates a wait-info table, registers the commands "exec" and "wait" (both sharing that table, whose refcount is incremented once so each command holds a reference and JimFreeWaitInfoTable is the delete proc) and registers "pid" with no private data; always returns JIM_OK.

functions.name: do_meta_command
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: zLine is a writable, nul-terminated dot-command line (zLine[0] is the leading '.') and p points to a valid ShellState. Postcondition: the line is tokenized in place into at most 51 arguments, the dot-command named by the first token is executed (output goes to p->out or stderr, state in p may change), and an int status is returned: 0 for success or an empty line, 1 for a usage or command error (also for help listings and error paths), 2 for .exit or a failed .check, or the exit code of the shell's helper command (such as arDotCommand, intckDatabaseCmd, shell_dbinfo_command). Commands such as .exit with a nonzero code, a failed .nonce check or failIfSafeMode errors terminate the process instead of returning. Heap memory allocated for the command (such as the result strings of the .tables listing) is freed before return, and the safe-mode reset at the end runs on the normal exit path.

functions.name: do_meta_command
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: zLine is a writable, NUL-terminated dot-command line whose first character is the leading '.', and p points to a valid ShellState. Postcondition: the line is tokenized in place (at most 51 tokens) and the matching meta-command is run, with its output going to p->out or stderr and p's state updated. The return value is 0 when there are no tokens, when .nonce succeeds, when .import finds a table with no columns, and in most successful cases. It is 1 for usage and other command errors, 2 for .exit and a failed or usage-error .check, or the status from the command helper (e.g. rc from arDotCommand, intckDatabaseCmd). For .exit with a nonzero numeric argument the process exits with that code, and a bad .nonce exits with status 1. Within the .testctrl branch shown here, the selected control is dispatched on its argument count and sqlite3_test_control is called. The result is printed in decimal if isOk==1, in 0x%08x form if isOk==2, and not printed if isOk==3. If no case accepted the arguments (isOk==0 and the control is known), a usage line is printed and rc=1. For fault_install, an unrecognized argument sets rc=1 and shows help. For the FAULT_INSTALL case, the faultsim state is modified and the help text is printed if no arguments or a help option is given.

functions.name: wmain
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc>=1 and argv[0] is non-NULL (asserted); on Windows (when SQLITE_SHELL_IS_UTF8 is false) wargv holds argc wide-character arguments, otherwise this is the shell's ordinary main with argv in UTF-8. Postcondition: the first pass over the arguments performs the sqlite3_config() settings and records the database filename, the -vfs value, the -init file and any non-option arguments as SQL or dot-commands, then sqlite3_initialize() is called; an unknown -vfs name exits the process with status 1. The database is opened only if the file already exists, the init file is processed, and a second pass applies the display and open-mode options. An unknown option returns 1; -version prints the version and returns 0; -help calls usage(1); an -A archive command mix with SQL returns 1; with -bail a failing -cmd returns early (rc 2 becomes 0). If no command arguments were given, commands are read from stdin through process_input, interactively with a history file when stdin is interactive; otherwise each command argument is run in order and the first failure stops with its rc, where 2 becomes 0 and a failed SQL statement gives at least 1. On exit via the normal path it frees azCmd, closes all databases and sessions, resets output, frees the argument copies and zNonce, clears the state, and returns rc, which is the last command or input processing status (0 on success). Under SQLITE_OMIT_MEMORYDB with no database filename it returns 1.

functions.name: OP_FkCounter
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: this is a case body inside sqlite3VdbeExec, with db, p and pOp valid. Postcondition: if P1 is non-zero, db->nDeferredCons is increased by P2; otherwise, if db->flags has SQLITE_DeferFKs, db->nDeferredImmCons is increased by P2; otherwise p->nFkConstraint is increased by P2; the other counters are unchanged and execution continues with the next opcode.

functions.name: OP_FkIfZero
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: this is a case body inside sqlite3VdbeExec, with db, p and pOp valid. Postcondition: if P1 is non-zero, control jumps to P2 when both db->nDeferredCons and db->nDeferredImmCons are zero; if P1 is zero, it jumps to P2 when both p->nFkConstraint and db->nDeferredImmCons are zero; otherwise it falls through; no counters are modified.

functions.name: OP_IfPos
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: register P1 holds an integer (MEM_Int). Postcondition: if its value is greater than zero, P3 is subtracted from it and control jumps to P2; otherwise the value is unchanged and execution falls through to the next opcode.

functions.name: OP_OffsetLimit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: registers P1 (limit) and P3 (offset) hold integers. Postcondition: the output register P2 is prepared as an integer and set to limit + max(0,offset) if limit is positive and the sum does not overflow i64, otherwise to -1; execution then falls through.

functions.name: OP_IfNotZero
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: register P1 holds an integer (MEM_Int). Postcondition: if the value is non-zero, it is decremented by one when positive (negative values are unchanged) and control jumps to P2; if it is zero it is unchanged and execution falls through.

functions.name: OP_DecrJumpZero
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: register P1 holds an integer (MEM_Int). Postcondition: the value is decremented by one unless it is already the smallest i64, and control jumps to P2 exactly when the resulting value is zero; otherwise execution falls through.

functions.name: OP_AggStep
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: P4 is a P4_FUNCDEF and P2/P3 satisfy the asserted register bounds. Postcondition: it allocates a context with a trailing 8-byte-aligned output Mem initialised to NULL, fills the context from the FuncDef, opcode index, Vdbe and encoding with argc=P5, stores it in P4 and sets p4type to P4_FUNCCTX; if allocation fails, control goes to no_mem. This slice ends before the rest of the case body, so later behaviour is not covered.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Fragment of sqlite3VdbeExec, case OP_AggStep1 (reached also by fall-through from OP_AggStep/OP_AggInverse). Precondition: P4 is a P4_FUNCCTX sqlite3_context, aMem[P3] is the accumulator, and pOut is MEM_Null with isError==0 and skipFlag==0. Postcondition: the context's pMem and argv are re-pointed to aMem[P3] and aMem[P2+i] if pMem differed, pMem->n is incremented, and xInverse (if P1 is nonzero) or xSFunc is called; if the callback set isError, a positive isError is copied into rc with an error message taken from pOut, skipFlag (if set) sets register pOp[-1].p1 to integer 1 when that is nonzero and is cleared, pOut is released and reset to MEM_Null, isError is cleared, and execution jumps to abort_due_to_error if rc is nonzero; otherwise (no error, or a negative isError) execution proceeds to the next opcode.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Fragment of sqlite3VdbeExec, cases OP_AggValue and OP_AggFinal. Precondition: aMem[P1] holds only MEM_Null/MEM_Agg flags, and P3 is nonzero only for OP_AggValue. Postcondition: if P3 is nonzero, xValue is invoked via sqlite3VdbeMemAggValue with the result stored in aMem[P3], else sqlite3VdbeMemFinalize finalizes aMem[P1] in place; if that returns nonzero rc, an error message from the result register is set and execution jumps to abort_due_to_error; otherwise the result register is converted to the database encoding and execution continues to the next opcode.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Fragment of sqlite3VdbeExec, case OP_Checkpoint (only when WAL is not omitted). Precondition: the statement is not read-only and P2 is one of the checkpoint modes PASSIVE, FULL, RESTART, TRUNCATE. Postcondition: sqlite3Checkpoint is run on database P1; any error other than SQLITE_BUSY jumps to abort_due_to_error with rc set; SQLITE_BUSY is turned into rc=SQLITE_OK with busy flag 1; on success or busy, integer registers P3, P3+1, P3+2 are set to the busy flag (0 or 1), the WAL size and the checkpointed page count (both -1 if the checkpoint reported nothing, e.g. on busy), and execution continues.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Fragment of sqlite3VdbeExec, case OP_JournalMode (slice ends mid-case, before the result is written). Precondition: P3 is a valid PAGER_JOURNALMODE value, P1 is a valid database index, and the statement is not read-only. Postcondition: out2 register P2 is prepared; the effective new mode is the old mode if P3 is QUERY, if the pager cannot change mode, or if WAL is requested for a temp database or a VFS without shared memory; a change into or out of WAL when not in autocommit or with more than one active reader sets rc=SQLITE_ERROR with a message and jumps to abort_due_to_error; otherwise leaving WAL closes the WAL and sets the mode on success, leaving MEMORY sets mode OFF, and the btree version is set to 2 for WAL or 1 otherwise if rc is still OK. The remainder of the case lies beyond this slice.

functions.name: lookupName
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pParse, pNC, pExpr and pRight are valid, pRight->u.zToken is the non-NULL column name, pExpr is a TK_ID-style node that is not token-only or reduced, zDb is NULL whenever zTab is NULL, and pNC is a chain of name contexts. Postcondition: the name is searched from pNC outward through each context's FROM list, trigger NEW/OLD/RETURNING/upsert excluded references, rowid, and result-set aliases; if exactly one match is found (cnt==1), pExpr is rewritten (to TK_COLUMN, TK_REGISTER or TK_TRIGGER, TK_NULL for an ambiguous rowid in a view when enabled, a coalesce() TK_FUNCTION for a FULL JOIN USING, or a copy of an aliased result-set expression), the matching source item's colUsed or rowidUsed is updated, nRef is incremented on every name context from the top one up to the matched one, and WRC_Prune is returned. A bare double-quoted identifier with no match (when double-quoted strings are enabled) becomes TK_STRING and WRC_Prune is returned, and a bare identifier recognized as true/false also returns WRC_Prune. If a no-match or ambiguous-name error occurs, an error message is recorded, the error count of the top name context is incremented, pExpr becomes TK_NULL and WRC_Abort is returned; misuse of an aliased aggregate or window function, or a row-value alias, also records an error and returns WRC_Abort. Temporary FULL JOIN match lists are freed on all paths, and the function may free the substructure (children) of pExpr.

functions.name: sqlite3ExprCodeIN
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pParse is a code-generating context with a valid pVdbe, and pExpr is an IN expression (with a left-hand side, possibly a vector, and a list or subquery right-hand side); destIfFalse and destIfNull are jump labels or addresses. Postcondition: returns nothing; it emits VDBE code that evaluates the LHS and the RHS, via the IN_INDEX_NOOP comparison sequence, a rowid seek, or an index/ephemeral table search, so that at runtime control jumps to destIfFalse if the LHS is not in the RHS and to destIfNull if the result is unknown because of NULLs, and otherwise falls through as true. If sqlite3ExprCheckIN reports an error it returns immediately without emitting code, and the aiMap and zAff buffers are not freed on that early path. In every other case it frees aiMap and zAff, including on malloc failure or a parse error found in step 2, and it releases the temporary LHS register range if the LHS was reordered, except on the step-2 error path, which skips that release.

functions.name: sqlite3Insert
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pParse is a valid parser context with pParse->db set and no malloc failure pending, pTabList is a one-entry source list naming the target table, and the caller transfers ownership of pTabList, pSelect, pColumn and pUpsert to this function (any of pSelect, pColumn and pUpsert may be NULL). Postcondition: nothing is returned; on success VDBE code is appended to the parse's statement that inserts the rows (from a single-row VALUES list, a coroutine SELECT, a temp table, or the xfer optimization) into the table or view, running triggers, constraint checks, foreign-key checks, upsert handling, autoincrement update and optional row count; on any error (existing pParse->nErr, unknown table, authorization failure, read-only table, unknown or generated column in the IDLIST, column-count mismatch, an upsert on a virtual table or view, SELECT failure, or out-of-memory) an error message is left in pParse (where applicable) and no insert code is completed; in every case, including the early exits, pTabList, the VALUES expression list, pUpsert, pSelect, pColumn, and the internal aTabColMap and aRegIdx arrays are freed.

functions.name: sqlite3WhereCodeOneLoopStart
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pParse, v, pWInfo and pLevel are valid, pLevel is pWInfo->a[iLevel] with a chosen WhereLoop, and notReady is the bitmask of tables not yet coded. Postcondition: emits VDBE code that opens the loop for this level (co-routine, virtual table, rowid, index, multi-OR or full-scan case), then emits tests for the WHERE terms, transitive constraints, RIGHT JOIN match recording and LEFT JOIN hit flag, and marks the coded terms TERM_CODED; it returns pLevel->notReady (notReady minus this table's cursor mask), or returns notReady unchanged if the OR-case allocation of the SrcList fails (out of memory), in which case no further code is generated; the function takes no locks and transfers no references to the caller.

functions.name: sqlite3WhereEnd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pWInfo is a WhereInfo produced by sqlite3WhereBegin for the current parse, with its pParse, pVdbe and pTabList valid, and the loop-body code of the WHERE clause has been emitted. Postcondition: it emits the loop termination code for every level (innermost first), including RIGHT JOIN return subroutines, IN-loop ends, skip-scan, LIKE repeat and LEFT JOIN null-row code. It then, for each level, either generates the RIGHT JOIN unmatched-row loop, or for a co-routine rewrites column references to copies, or for an index-using level (when malloc has not failed) rewrites OP_Column/OP_Rowid/OP_IfNullRow opcodes on the table cursor to use the index cursor, disables matching pParse->pIdxEpr entries, and when a column is missing from a covering index either sets an 'internal query planner error' with rc=SQLITE_INTERNAL (WHERE_IDX_ONLY) or clears WHERE_EXPRIDX and rewrites the explain text. Finally it resolves the break label, restores pParse->nQueryLoop, frees pWInfo (the caller loses it), subtracts the number of RIGHT JOIN levels from pParse->withinRJSubrtn, and returns nothing.

functions.name: sqlite3_config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: op is an SQLITE_CONFIG_* code and the variadic arguments match the types that option expects; if the library is already initialized (sqlite3GlobalConfig.isInit), only SQLITE_CONFIG_LOG and SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE_HDRSZ are permitted. Postcondition: if the library is initialized and op is any other option (including op<0 or op>63), it changes nothing and returns SQLITE_MISUSE; otherwise it reads the option's arguments, updates the corresponding sqlite3GlobalConfig fields or writes results through the caller's pointer arguments (for example GETMUTEX, GETMALLOC, GETPCACHE2, PCACHE_HDRSZ, ROWID_IN_VIEW), and returns SQLITE_OK. SQLITE_CONFIG_GETPCACHE and any unrecognised or compiled-out option return SQLITE_ERROR. SQLITE_CONFIG_PCACHE is a no-op returning SQLITE_OK. The caller gains no references and no locks are taken.

functions.name: openDatabase
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ppDb points to writable storage; zFilename may be NULL (treated as ":memory:") or a UTF-8 filename/URI, zVfs may be NULL or a VFS name, and flags is the open flag word. Postcondition: *ppDb is set to 0 at entry and finally to the new handle, or to 0 if the final error code has low byte SQLITE_NOMEM (in which case the handle is closed); returns SQLITE_OK on success, or the error code from sqlite3_initialize, SQLITE_MISUSE if the READONLY/READWRITE/CREATE bits are not one of the valid combinations, or the error from URI parsing, btree open, built-in/automatic extension loading or a malloc failure (the code is the db's error code, taken after the mutex is released). If a non-NOMEM error occurs after the handle was allocated, the handle is still returned in *ppDb with state SQLITE_STATE_SICK, and the caller must close it. On the NOMEM-before-allocation path *ppDb is 0. The temporary filename from URI parsing and the error message are always freed, and the connection mutex is released before return.

functions.name: fts5MultiIterNew
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a valid Fts5Index, pStruct a valid structure, ppOut is writable, and either iLevel>=0 or pTerm==0 && nTerm==0 (when iLevel>=0, nSegment limits the segments used from that level). Postcondition: returns nothing; *ppOut is always written: it is set to the newly allocated iterator from fts5MultiIterAlloc, and if p->rc was already an error on entry the iterator is still allocated (with nSeg=0 if rc was not OK before sizing) and no segment iterators are initialized or finished; if allocation fails *ppOut is NULL and p->rc is an error; if p->rc==SQLITE_OK after initialization the segment iterators (including the hash-table iterator when iLevel<0, p->pHash is set and SKIPHASH is not requested) are initialized and fts5MultiIterFinishSetup is applied, otherwise the new iterator is freed with fts5MultiIterFree and *ppOut is set to NULL. On return either *ppOut is non-NULL or p->rc is not SQLITE_OK; errors are reported only through p->rc.

functions.name: fts5DoSecureDelete
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p and pSeg are valid and pSeg->pLeaf is a loaded leaf page whose iterator (iLeafOffset, iTermLeafPgno, iTermLeafOffset, nPos, bDel, iEndofDoclist) points at the doclist entry to remove. Postcondition: it returns nothing; it copies the page footer into a temporary buffer, and if that allocation fails (p->rc nonzero) it returns at once without changing the page. Otherwise it removes the entry's rowid/position-list bytes from the leaf, or, when pSeg->bDel is set, replaces them with the rowid delta and a 0x01 byte. It may also delete overflow pages, merge the next entry's delta into the following rowid, remove or replace the term and its footer entry, rewrite the term page, and remove an index entry. If corrupt data is detected it sets p->rc to FTS5_CORRUPT and skips the final page edit. If p->rc is SQLITE_OK at the end, it rewrites the footer and writes the modified leaf page back with fts5DataWrite. The temporary buffer is always freed except on the early allocation-failure return, where it is not freed.

functions.name: sqlite3_str_vappendf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pAccum is a valid sqlite3_str (if its nChar is 0 it does not own a malloc'ed buffer), fmt is a NUL-terminated printf-style format string, and ap supplies arguments matching the conversions in fmt (or a PrintfArguments* first when SQLITE_PRINTF_SQLFUNC is set). Postcondition: returns nothing; the formatted text for each literal run and conversion (padded to width, with %z, %q, %Q, %w, %T and %S handled specially) is appended to pAccum, and any temporary buffer made for a conversion is freed with sqlite3DbFree after that conversion. It stops early, without appending the current conversion, when a temporary buffer allocation fails, when an unknown conversion character is met, or when %T or %S is used without SQLITE_PRINTF_INTERNAL. It also stops at the end of the format string, which includes a lone trailing '%' (appended as a literal '%'). In the %z mprintf optimization the argument string is adopted as pAccum's buffer.

functions.name: sqlite3PagerOpen
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pVfs is a valid VFS, ppPager is a writable output pointer, and zFilename is NULL, empty (temporary or in-memory database) or a database path; nExtra, flags and vfsFlags are valid. Postcondition: the code shown allocates one zeroed block holding the Pager, its PCache, the db, sub-journal and journal file handles and the db, journal and WAL names, and frees the temporary full pathname; if the allocation fails it returns SQLITE_NOMEM_BKPT. Otherwise it opens the database file if a non-empty name was given, picks a default page size and sets the pager's lock, state, readonly and journal fields. It then sets the page size and opens the page cache. If any step fails it closes the file, frees the temp space and the Pager and returns that error code. If all steps succeed it initializes the remaining Pager fields and continues past this slice, which ends before the Pager is stored in *ppPager and SQLITE_OK is returned. The caller owns the returned Pager on success.

functions.name: walTryBeginRead
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pWal->readLock is negative (no read lock held), pCnt points to the retry counter, and useWal is nonzero only for a read/write connection. Postcondition: it increments *pCnt (sleeping after more than 5 retries) and returns SQLITE_PROTOCOL once the retry count exceeds WAL_RETRY_PROTOCOL_LIMIT. Otherwise, if useWal is 0, it reads the wal-index header; a BUSY there becomes WAL_RETRY (shm not mapped, or the recovery lock is free) or SQLITE_BUSY_RECOVERY (recovery lock busy), and any other error is returned, as is the result of walBeginShmUnreliable when the shm is unreliable. It then either takes shared READ_LOCK(0) when the WAL is fully backfilled (returning WAL_RETRY after releasing it if the header changed, else setting pWal->readLock=0 and returning SQLITE_OK), or picks or creates a read mark, returning WAL_RETRY on BUSY, SQLITE_READONLY_CANTINIT if no mark can be used on a read-only shm, or another lock error. It takes a shared lock on READ_LOCK(mxI), sets pWal->minFrame, and if the read mark or the wal-index header changed it releases the lock and returns WAL_RETRY. On SQLITE_OK it holds the shared read lock on slot mxI with pWal->readLock set to that slot; on any other return it holds no read lock.

functions.name: sqlite3BtreeOpen
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pVfs and db are non-NULL, the db mutex is held, flags fit in 8 bits, ppBtree is writable, and zFilename may be NULL or empty for a temp database. Postcondition: on SQLITE_OK, *ppBtree is a new Btree attached to a BtShared (an existing shared one with nRef incremented, or a newly created one) and the pager cache size and PDB file hint are set; on failure from the pager, header read, set-pagesize or a mutex/BtShared allocation, the pager is closed, the allocations are freed, *ppBtree is set to 0 and the error code (e.g. SQLITE_NOMEM) is returned; on the early returns (Btree allocation failure, full-pathname allocation failure, sqlite3OsFullPathname error other than SQLITE_OK_SYMLINK, or SQLITE_CONSTRAINT when this connection already has that shared BtShared attached) the new Btree is freed, *ppBtree is not written, and the code is returned; the static open mutex is released before returning if it was taken.

functions.name: sqlite3_enable_shared_cache
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the argument is any int, and nonzero is treated as true. Postcondition: stores the argument in the global configuration field sharedCacheEnabled, so it affects connections opened afterwards, and always returns SQLITE_OK (0); this implementation never returns an error code.

functions.name: fillInCell
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the BtShared mutex; pPage is a valid b-tree leaf page (intKey) or index page, pCell points to a buffer large enough for the cell, pX describes the payload (nData/nZero/pData/nKey for intKey tables, or pKey/nKey for index keys), and pnSize is writable. Postcondition: builds the complete cell in pCell (header varints, local payload, zero padding for missing source bytes or nZero, and for a payload larger than maxLocal a 4-byte first-overflow-page number), stores the local cell size in *pnSize (at least 4 when no overflow is needed), and returns SQLITE_OK; when overflow is needed it allocates a chain of overflow pages via allocateBtreePage, writing the remaining payload and next-page links into them (plus pointer-map entries under autovacuum), releasing each overflow page reference before returning SQLITE_OK; if page allocation or ptrmapPut fails it releases the held overflow page and returns that error code (*pnSize is already set, and the cell and earlier overflow pages are left partially written).

functions.name: sqlite3_backup_step
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a valid sqlite3_backup object (non-NULL, since the NULL check exists only under SQLITE_ENABLE_API_ARMOR, where it returns SQLITE_MISUSE_BKPT); the function itself takes the source connection mutex, the source btree lock and the destination connection mutex (if p->pDestDb is set), so the caller must not hold them in a conflicting way. Postcondition: if p->rc is already a fatal error (anything other than SQLITE_OK, SQLITE_BUSY or SQLITE_LOCKED) nothing is copied and that code is returned; otherwise it returns SQLITE_BUSY if the source is in a write transaction while a destination connection is set, SQLITE_NOMEM or other errors from opening transactions, SQLITE_READONLY if the destination is WAL or in-memory and the page sizes differ, errors from copying pages or committing (SQLITE_IOERR_NOMEM is mapped to SQLITE_NOMEM), SQLITE_OK if up to nPage pages (all if nPage<0) were copied and more remain, or SQLITE_DONE after copying all pages and committing the destination. The status is stored in p->rc, progress fields (iNext, nPagecount, nRemaining) are updated, any source read transaction it opened is closed, and all mutexes and the btree lock it took are released before returning.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a Vdbe in the run state with valid program and register arrays. Postcondition: it executes opcodes starting at p->pc until a halt, result row, error or interrupt, and returns SQLITE_ROW when a result row is ready (p->pc saved), SQLITE_DONE or SQLITE_ERROR after OP_Halt (or SQLITE_BUSY if halting is busy), or an error code from the error paths (no_mem, too_big, interrupt, abort_due_to_error); the OP_Concat case in it sets r[P3] to NULL if either input is NULL, otherwise to the concatenation r[P2]||r[P1] as a string, or fails with NOMEM or TOOBIG.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a Vdbe in the run state with valid program and register arrays. Postcondition: it executes opcodes starting at p->pc until a halt, result row, error or interrupt, and returns SQLITE_ROW when a result row is ready (p->pc saved), SQLITE_DONE or SQLITE_ERROR after OP_Halt (or SQLITE_BUSY if halting is busy), or an error code from the error paths; the arithmetic cases (Add, Subtract, Multiply, Divide, Remainder) store an integer or real result in r[P3], or NULL if an operand is NULL, the divisor is zero, or the real result is NaN.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a Vdbe in the run state with valid program and register arrays. Postcondition: it executes opcodes starting at p->pc until a halt, result row, error or interrupt, and returns SQLITE_ROW when a result row is ready (p->pc saved), SQLITE_DONE or SQLITE_ERROR after OP_Halt (or SQLITE_BUSY if halting is busy), or an error code from the error paths; the BitAnd, BitOr, ShiftLeft and ShiftRight cases store an integer result in r[P3], or NULL if either operand is NULL.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a Vdbe in the run state with a valid program, and the caller holds the database connection. Postcondition: the program is executed from p->pc until it halts, produces a row, or fails; the result is SQLITE_ROW (after OP_ResultRow, with p->pc advanced), SQLITE_DONE or SQLITE_ERROR (OP_Halt, depending on p->rc), SQLITE_BUSY, or another error code (e.g. SQLITE_NOMEM, SQLITE_TOOBIG, SQLITE_INTERRUPT) from the error exits. The OP_MakeRecord case writes the header-size varint, one serial-type varint per column, then the column bodies into pOut->z, so that header bytes equal nHdr and total bytes equal nByte; it then breaks to the next opcode.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a Vdbe in the run state with a valid program, and the caller holds the database connection. Postcondition: the program is executed from p->pc until it halts, produces a row, or fails; the result is SQLITE_ROW, SQLITE_DONE, SQLITE_ERROR, SQLITE_BUSY, or another error code from the error exits. The OP_Count case stores the btree row count into register P2 (an estimate if P3 is nonzero, an exact count otherwise) and then checks for interrupt; if the exact count fails, rc is set and it aborts with that error.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a Vdbe in the run state with a valid program, and the caller holds the database connection. Postcondition: the program is executed from p->pc until it halts, produces a row, or fails; the result is SQLITE_ROW, SQLITE_DONE, SQLITE_ERROR, SQLITE_BUSY, or another error code from the error exits. The OP_Savepoint case opens a savepoint (allocating one, or returning SQLITE_BUSY if write statements are active), or releases or rolls back the named one. A missing name gives SQLITE_ERROR, and a release with active writers gives SQLITE_BUSY. Releasing the outermost transaction savepoint commits the transaction. Inner savepoints are freed, and failures from vtab, btree or foreign-key checks abort with that rc.

functions.name: sqlite3VdbeExec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a VDBE in VDBE_RUN_STATE with a valid program and register array. Postcondition: it executes opcodes starting at p->pc and returns when one produces a result: SQLITE_ROW for a result row (p->pc saved), SQLITE_DONE or SQLITE_ERROR or SQLITE_BUSY from Halt, or an error code such as SQLITE_NOMEM, SQLITE_INTERRUPT, SQLITE_TOOBIG or a btree error from an opcode failure. The listed slice is the shared body of OP_SeekLT/OP_SeekLE/OP_SeekGE/OP_SeekGT, one case inside the function's opcode switch. That case repositions btree cursor P1 on the key (rowid converted from P3 for tables, an unpacked key of P4 registers for indexes). It lands on the largest entry <(LT) or <=(LE) the key, or the smallest entry >=(GE) or >(GT) it. It jumps to P2 if no such entry exists (or, for an index with SEEK_EQ hint, if no equal entry exists). On a seek or step error it goes to abort_due_to_error with rc set. For a SEEK_EQ cursor it skips the following IdxLT/IdxGT when the seek succeeds.

functions.name: DbObjCmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cd is a valid SqliteDb* for an open connection, interp is a valid Tcl interpreter, and objv holds objc>=0 valid Tcl objects. Postcondition: if objc<2 or the subcommand name in objv[1] is not one of the known options, it sets an error result and returns TCL_ERROR. Otherwise it dispatches on the subcommand. Most subcommands return TCL_ERROR with a message in the interpreter result on a wrong argument count or a failure, and otherwise return rc (TCL_OK unless set by the subcommand). commit_hook with no argument appends the current hook script to the result. With one argument it frees the old script, stores a copy of the new one (or null if empty), and installs DbCommitHandler or clears the hook. complete returns a boolean result for the SQL text (when not compiled out). config lists all options with values, or sets and returns one option's integer value, and returns TCL_ERROR on an unknown option or a bad boolean. copy requires 5 to 7 args and a nonempty separator. It requires a valid conflict algorithm and a readable table and file. It imports the lines in one transaction. On success it sets the result to the line count and returns TCL_OK. On a column-count mismatch or SQL error it rolls back, appends the failing line, and returns TCL_ERROR. The copy path finalizes statements and frees its buffers on all paths after allocation. The function returns rc, and for eval, transaction and the like the result is delegated to helper routines.

functions.name: ieee802_15_4_std_frames
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect_options pointer, p points to the start of an IEEE 802.15.4 frame (MAC header) and the caller has verified that at least the frame control field is available, caplen is the number of captured bytes, and fc is the already-decoded 16-bit frame control field. Postcondition: the function strips a 4- or 2-octet FCS if the CRC matches, prints the version, flags, sequence number, PAN IDs and addresses, auxiliary security header, header and payload IEs, MIC and FCS (depending on verbosity), then prints the payload by frame type (beacon, data, ack, MAC command) and returns 1; it returns 0 after printing an error or truncation message when the sequence number field is truncated, the source or destination address mode is invalid, the capture is truncated before the destination PAN, destination address, source PAN, source address or MIC, or the aux security header, header IE list or payload IE list parse fails (negative length). Errors in beacon or command payload parsing only stop printing of that payload and still return 1. It allocates no memory and acquires or releases no locks or references.

functions.name: rfc1048_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect_options and bp points to the start of an RFC 1048 vendor-extension area (the 4-byte magic cookie followed by options) within the captured packet. Postcondition: returns nothing; it prints the magic cookie and then each option (tag, length and decoded data, or an invalid/length-error note) until a TAG_END is seen (when vflag < 3), or the data ends, or an option's data extends past the captured data; in that truncation case it calls nd_print_trunc and returns. Truncating reads of the packet bytes can also take that path. It acquires no locks and keeps no references.

functions.name: cfm_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect context and pptr points to a captured CFM packet of length bytes (reads are bounds-checked against the snapshot end). Postcondition: returns nothing; it prints the CFM header summary and, when verbose, the opcode-specific fields, then walks the TLVs, printing each and hexdumping where needed. It prints a 'not supported' message for a version other than CFM_VERSION and stops, and prints only the one-line summary when not verbose. It stops early with a diagnostic on a header shorter than the common header, a first TLV offset larger than the remaining length, a too-small or truncated opcode body, too-long MD/MA names, a CFM_TLV_END TLV, a too-short TLV header or body, a too-short Port Status, Interface Status or Private TLV, or a Sender ID management address longer than its TLV. Truncation (the ND_TCHECK bounds checks) prints a truncation message. Other malformed Sender ID fields skip to the next TLV. It acquires no locks or references and allocates and frees nothing.

functions.name: domain_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid dissector context and bp points to a DNS message of the given length (including the 2-byte length prefix when over_tcp is nonzero), of which only bytes up to ndo->ndo_snapend are readable. Postcondition: returns nothing; if over_tcp and length < 2, or the TCP length prefix differs from length-2, or length is less than the DNS header size, it prints an error note and invalid marker and returns without further output. Otherwise it prints the id, opcode, rcode/flags, the question count and counts, and the question, answer and (with -vv) authority/additional records for a response, or the request flags, odd counts, questions and (with -vv) remaining sections for a request. If any section is truncated or fails to parse it prints the truncation marker and returns, otherwise it ends by printing " (length)". It takes no locks and does not retain references or memory.

functions.name: icmp_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect_options, bp points to an ICMP message of plen bytes (possibly truncated by the capture snapend), bp2 points to the enclosing IP header, and fragmented says whether the packet is a fragment. Postcondition: returns nothing; prints "ICMP <description>, length <plen>" with a description chosen from the ICMP type and code; if vflag is set and the packet is not fragmented and all plen bytes are captured, it checks the ICMP checksum and prints a warning when it is wrong; for ICMP error types with vflag >= 1 it prints the embedded IP packet via ip_print, temporarily lowering ndo_snapend and then restoring it; it then sets ndo_protocol to "icmp" and, with vflag >= 1, plen > ICMP_EXTD_MINLEN and a multipart-capable type, decodes the RFC 4884 extension header and objects, returning early on a bad checksum when the length field is 0, on an unsupported version, or on an object with class 0 or too small a length. If any bounds check (ND_TCHECK*) fails because the data is truncated, it jumps to trunc and prints a truncation message. It acquires and releases no locks or references and allocates no memory; all output goes through ndo.

functions.name: ip6_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect_options and bp points to the start of a packet of length bytes, of which the captured part (up to ndo_snapend) may be shorter; no lock or reference is held by the caller. Postcondition: returns nothing; it prints the IPv6 header (and the extension-header chain). If length < 40 or the version is not 6, it prints an invalid marker and returns before pushing any snaplen. If the header is not fully captured, it prints a truncation marker and returns. If the snaplen cannot be pushed, it calls ndo->ndo_error, which does not return. Otherwise it walks the extension headers (hop-by-hop, destination options, fragment, mobility, routing) and, on reaching a non-extension next header, calls ip_demux_print on the remaining payload and then pops the pushed snaplen. It also pops the snaplen when an extension-header handler returns a negative advance, after a mobility header, when the fragment header ends the captured data, or when the loop ends because the snapshot end was reached. A duplicate or misplaced hop-by-hop header, or a hop-by-hop header with zero payload length and no jumbo option, prints an invalid marker and returns without popping. Truncation exits (len smaller than the advance, a jumbo length shorter than the bytes processed, or a zero payload length after an extension header) print a truncation marker and return without popping, leaving the pushed snaplen for the caller to pop.

functions.name: isis_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect_options and p points to length bytes of captured IS-IS PDU data. Postcondition: prints a description of the PDU to ndo and returns 1 or 0; it allocates no memory and takes or releases no locks or references. It returns 0 after printing an error for an unsupported version, system ID length, PDU version or max-area value (255), for a fixed header length smaller than the common header or larger than length, for a non-6-byte system ID length, or for a bogus fixed header length for the PDU type. It also returns 0 for an unknown PDU type when vflag is not 0 (after hexdumping it), and when print_unknown_data fails during verbose or TLV hexdumps. It returns 1 in non-verbose mode after printing a one-line summary for a known PDU type, and for an unknown PDU type when vflag is 0 (after printing the length). In verbose mode it returns 1 after decoding all TLVs and printing any straggler bytes. When the packet is truncated (a failed bounds check, a short header, or a TLV longer than the remaining data), it prints a truncation notice and returns 1. It also returns 1 when isis_print_tlv_ip_reach fails.

functions.name: l2tp_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect context and dat points to a captured packet buffer of which length bytes are the on-wire L2TP data; reads beyond the captured data trigger the bounds-check mechanism (truncation). Postcondition: returns nothing; it prints the version (returns after printing for L2F or for an unknown version), then the flag letters, tunnel/session IDs, Ns/Nr if S is set, and skips the offset padding if O is set, jumping to nd_print_trunc if that padding is not in the captured buffer. It then returns after printing an error if the L flag is set and the length field exceeds length, or if the effective length is smaller than the header size. For a control message (T flag) it prints ' No length' and returns if L is unset, prints ' ZLB' if there is no payload, and otherwise walks AVPs with l2tp_avp_print until the payload is consumed or an AVP call returns 0 (truncated). For a data message (no T flag) it prints ' {', passes the remaining payload to ppp_print, then prints '}'.

functions.name: lisp_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid printer context and bp points to a LISP packet of the given length, of which only the bytes up to ndo_snapend are readable. Postcondition: returns nothing and takes or releases no lock, reference or memory; it prints the message type (and flags in verbose mode), and if the header is not fully captured it prints truncation output and returns. For types other than Map-Register or Map-Notify it returns after printing the type. Otherwise it prints the record count and authentication data (verbose mode prints the key id too), and if the record count is zero it prints invalid output and returns. It then prints each EID record and its locators while the offset is below length and records remain, returning silently when an EID AFI is neither IPv4 nor IPv6, and printing truncation output and returning when a record or locator is not fully captured. Afterwards, if the xTR-ID-present bit is set, it prints the xTR-ID and Site-ID, or invalid output when fewer than 24 bytes are captured. If the bit is not set, it prints any remaining captured bytes as hex data.

functions.name: lspping_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pptr points to a packet of len bytes of an LSP-ping message, and ndo is a valid netdissect_options. Postcondition: returns nothing and prints a decoded form of the packet. If len is shorter than the common header, it prints "packet is too short". With a version other than LSPPING_VERSION it prints an unsupported-version message and returns. With vflag below 1 it prints a one-line summary and returns. Otherwise it prints the header fields and walks the TLVs. Each TLV with nonzero length is bounds-checked against the remaining length and decoded, with sub-TLVs for the target FEC stack and the downstream mapping, BFD discriminator and vendor TLVs. Hex dumps are printed when vflag > 1 or when a TLV or sub-TLV is malformed, truncated or not fully decoded. Lengths are padded to a 4-byte boundary. A TLV or its padding that runs past the packet, or a missing TLV header, prints "packet is too short". A sub-TLV whose padding passes the TLV end prints "TLV is too short" and returns early. Reading beyond the captured data is stopped by the ND_TCHECK macros, which leave the function early. The function takes no locks and allocates or frees nothing.

functions.name: pgm_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect_options, bp points to a PGM packet of which only the captured bytes may be read (reads are bounds-checked), length is the PGM length to print, and bp2 points to the enclosing IPv4 or IPv6 header. Postcondition: returns nothing and prints a one-line description: addresses and ports, then if verbose the PGM type, global source id, type-specific fields and decoded options, then " [length]" and, for PT_PGM_ZMTP1 ODATA/RDATA packets, the ZMTP1 datagram payload; if the ports cannot be read, the packet header is truncated, or an unknown address family is met, it prints a truncation marker and returns; without -v it returns after the PGM length; bad first option, bad OPT_LENGTH, bad total option length, option lengths too short or inconsistent print a diagnostic and return early; an option with length below the minimum only ends option decoding (the trailing length/payload is still printed); the packet is never modified.

functions.name: resp_get_length
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bp points to at least len readable bytes of a RESP packet and endp is a valid pointer to store into. Postcondition: it parses an optional '-' and decimal digits followed by CRLF, always sets *endp to the position reached (just past the CRLF on success or the failure point otherwise), and returns the non-negative length on success, -1 for the null length "-1", -2 if the data is truncated (including len == 0), -3 if the number is too large for an int, -4 if a negative number is not exactly -1 (or is too large), and -5 if the data is invalid (no digit, or missing '\r' or '\n').

functions.name: rsvp_obj_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect context, tptr points to tlen bytes of RSVP objects (pptr/plen is the whole RSVP packet and rsvp_com_header its common header, used for integrity signature checks), and indent is a valid string. Postcondition: it walks the objects while tlen is at least the object header size, printing each header and decoded body (or a hexdump for unknown or undecoded types, or when ndo_vflag > 1), and returns 0 if all objects were processed. It returns -1 after printing an error, in these cases: the object length is not a multiple of 4, the object length is shorter than the header, the object length is larger than the remaining tlen, an object or sub-object is too short, the data is invalid (e.g. bad ERO subobject length or prefix length, bad GENERALIZED_UNI sub-object lengths), a property TLV is shorter than 2, or the captured data is truncated.

functions.name: rsvp_obj_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid netdissect context, tptr points to tlen bytes of RSVP objects inside a packet of which pptr/plen is the whole RSVP message, and rsvp_com_header is the parsed common header (used only for signature verification). Postcondition: walks the objects while at least an object header remains, printing each object's class, class-type and length and decoding its body by class and C-type (or printing unknown data or a hexdump for unknown types, when ndo_vflag > 1, or when the decoder asks for it), and returns 0 after all objects are consumed; it prints an error and returns -1 if an object length is not a multiple of 4, is smaller than the header, or exceeds the remaining length, if a body or sub-object is too short ("object is too short" / "sub-object is too short"), if a property TLV is shorter than 2 bytes, on invalid ERO/RRO or GENERALIZED_UNI sub-object lengths (invalid), or when the captured data is truncated (trunc). It acquires no locks or references and allocates no memory.

functions.name: rsvp_intserv_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ndo is a valid print context and tptr points to an intserv parameter header of which obj_tlen bytes are logically available (captured bytes are checked via the ND_TCHECK macros and GET_* accessors). Postcondition: returns 0 without decoding the body if obj_tlen < 4 or obj_tlen < parameter_length+4, where parameter_length is 4 times the 16-bit word count at tptr+2; otherwise prints the parameter header and, depending on parameter ID (4, 6, 8, 10, 127, 130, 133-136) and only if the length matches the expected size (4, 4, 4, 4, 20, 8, 4), prints its value fields, while for unknown IDs it hex-dumps the body if ndo_vflag <= 1; it then returns parameter_length+4. If a truncation check fails for ID 127 or 130 it prints a truncation notice and returns 0. It takes no locks and does not retain memory.

functions.name: nbt_udp138_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: data points to length bytes of packet data (only the bytes up to ndo_snapend are read) and ndo is a valid dissector state. Postcondition: returns nothing and takes or frees no lock, reference or memory; it sets ndo_protocol, clamps the end to ndo_snapend and returns silently if no captured bytes remain; with ndo_vflag < 2 it only prints "NBT UDP PACKET(138)"; otherwise it prints the header fields via smb_fdata, and if that did not return NULL, at least 4 bytes remain before the end (data+3 < maxbuf) and they equal "\377SMB", it also calls print_smb on that data; in every other case it returns without further output.

functions.name: tcp_print

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the lexer (yylex) is ready to deliver tokens, and cfg_parser with its cfg is initialized because the grammar actions use them. Postcondition: the whole input is parsed as an LALR(1) bison parser. Each reduced option rule validates its string argument; on success it stores the value in cfg_parser->cfg or inserts it into a config list, and on a bad value it calls yyerror and leaves the field unchanged. It frees or transfers ownership of each STRING_ARG token. Out-of-memory conditions in list insertion are fatal (fatal_exit) or reported via yyerror, depending on the rule. It returns 0 when the input is accepted, 1 when parsing is aborted by a syntax error that cannot be recovered or by YYABORT, and 2 when the parser stack is exhausted (memory exhausted). Any stack it grew on the heap is freed before it returns.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global cfg_parser (with cfg, and the stub/forward/view/auth list heads where those rules apply) is set up and yylex supplies tokens, with STRING_ARG tokens carrying malloc'd strings owned by the parser. Postcondition: it parses the whole token stream by LALR shift/reduce, running each rule's action to store validated values into cfg_parser->cfg (taking ownership of or freeing each STRING_ARG string, calling yyerror for bad values or out-of-memory, or fatal_exit for edns-client-string allocation failure), and returns 0 on accepting the input, 1 on abort (syntax error that cannot be recovered, or YYABORT), or 2 when the parser stack memory is exhausted.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the lexer and the global cfg_parser (with its cfg) are initialised, and each STRING_ARG token carries a heap string owned by the parser. Postcondition: yyparse runs the LALR parse loop and returns 0 when the input is accepted, 1 when the parse is aborted by an unrecoverable syntax error or YYABORT, and 2 on memory exhaustion of the parser stacks. While reducing rules (including the slice's view, remote-control and dnstap options) each action either stores or frees its string token and updates cfg_parser->cfg: yes/no options are validated and set; invalid values call yyerror; list options insert or append into config lists; and out-of-memory in cfg_strlist_insert for view local-data calls fatal_exit. If a parser stack was heap-allocated it is freed before returning.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global cfg_parser and its config are set up and the lexer yylex can supply tokens; the function takes no arguments. Postcondition: runs the LALR parse, whose semantic actions write parsed options into cfg_parser->cfg (calling yyerror on bad values, freeing or storing the token strings), and returns 0 when the input is accepted (YYACCEPT), 1 when parsing is aborted (YYABORT at an unrecoverable syntax error, at end of input during error recovery, or when the stack cannot be extended), and 2 after calling yyerror("memory exhausted") when stack memory is exhausted. On every return path it discards the lookahead and any remaining stack symbols and frees the heap-allocated stack if it was reallocated.

functions.name: fe_mul121666
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h points to writable storage for an fe and f points to a valid fe_loose whose limbs are within loose bounds. Postcondition: h holds f multiplied by 121666 modulo 2^255-19 with carried (tight) limbs; nothing is returned and f is unchanged.

functions.name: hostapd_config_fill
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: conf and bss point to valid hostapd configuration structures (conf->bss[0] and bss->radius are used), buf is the NUL-terminated keyword, pos is the NUL-terminated value string, and line is the source line number used in log messages. Postcondition: the keyword in buf is matched against the known parameters, and the matching field of conf or bss is updated, with old heap strings freed and replaced by duplicates and lists or files read where the keyword requires it. It returns 0 on success, including for deprecated or ignored keywords and when a ctrl_interface_group name resolves to a group. It returns 1 for an invalid value, a failed parse, a failed read, or an allocation failure, and -1 if acs_chan_bias is invalid. If an error occurs after a field was already written, such as a numeric value that is out of range, that field may keep the new value. A final fallthrough branch (not in the visible slice) handles keywords that match nothing.

functions.name: hostapd_config_fill
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: conf and bss are valid, initialised hostapd configuration objects (bss normally being one of conf->bss, and bss->radius non-NULL when RADIUS is compiled in), buf is the NUL-terminated keyword, pos is the NUL-terminated value string, and line is the config line number used in log messages. Postcondition: the function dispatches on buf through a long if/else chain and stores the value parsed from pos into the matching field of conf or bss. Many handlers free the previous string or buffer and replace it with a copy (os_strdup, os_malloc, os_readfile), and some handlers allocate or append to lists. It returns 0 when the keyword was handled successfully, when it was deprecated or ignored, and also when the ctrl_interface_group lookup succeeds by group name.
