Otherwise, for in_seq in 0xFF800000..0xFFFFFFFF it returns true on an exact match when the expected number is also in that range or HEIMDAL_SEQ is not set; else it returns true and sets KRB5_AUTH_CONN_HEIMDAL_SEQ if chk_heimdal_seqnum accepts the pair; else it returns false. For other in_seq, an exact match returns true and also sets KRB5_AUTH_CONN_SANE_SEQ if the expected number lies in one of the ambiguous Heimdal ranges (0x80..0xFF, 0x8000..0xFFFF, 0x800000..0xFFFFFF, i.e. matching the three masks). If the expected number is 0, HEIMDAL_SEQ is not set and in_seq is 0x100, 0x10000 or 0x1000000, it sets KRB5_AUTH_CONN_HEIMDAL_SEQ and returns true; the assignment to the local exp_seq has no effect on ac->remote_seq_number. All other cases return false.

functions.name: strptime
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: buf and fmt point to valid NUL-terminated strings and tm points to a writable struct tm. Postcondition: parses buf according to fmt, storing the converted fields into *tm (tm_min, tm_mon, tm_hour, tm_sec, tm_wday, tm_year, tm_mday, tm_yday), and returns a pointer into buf just past the last consumed character when the whole format is processed; returns NULL (0) on any failure: a literal mismatch, an unknown conversion, a failed name or number match (number out of range or not starting with a digit), an invalid E/O modifier (via LEGAL_ALT), or a %p mismatch or %p with tm_hour > 11. Whitespace in fmt matches any amount of whitespace in buf, and tm may be partially modified even when NULL is returned. No locks, references or memory are acquired or released.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the program is run with the file's static test data (saved_pac, s4u_pacs, fuzz1, fuzz2, keyblocks, user names) available and the krb5/Heimdal PAC library usable; argc and argv are ignored. Postcondition: it initializes a krb5 context, runs the ticket-signature test, the saved-PAC and S4U2Self PAC checks, the fuzzed-PAC parse-failure checks, and the PAC add/get buffer, sign, parse, verify and get_types round-trips, including the enterprise, nt-ms and with-realm variants with their expected failures. Any unexpected result makes it call err(), which reports the error and does not return. If every step behaves as expected it frees the PAC, principal and context and returns 0, and no other return value is produced.

functions.name: sendto_kdc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller has a valid context, a built connection list, a selector state and a message to send, and reply points to writable storage; server_used, remoteaddr and remoteaddrlen may be NULL. Postcondition: on success it returns 0, *reply holds the winning server's response (ownership of that buffer moves to the caller and the winner's buffer pointer is nulled), *server_used is set if non-NULL, and the peer address is filled in via getpeername when remoteaddr is non-NULL and *remoteaddrlen is greater than 0; if no connections remain, or no winner was found within MAX_PASS passes, it returns KRB5_KDC_UNREACH. In every case it closes all open sockets, frees every connection (and its input buffer unless it is the shared udpbuf), calls the callback cleanup on each connection if callback_info is set, and frees sel_state and the udpbuf (unless that is the reply's data). Any error returned before this slice's code is not covered here.

functions.name: __rec_iput
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: t is a valid open recno BTREE, data points to a valid DBT, nrec is a record number and flags is 0 or R_IAFTER or R_IBEFORE (other values are treated like a plain insert at nrec). Postcondition: if data is larger than t->bt_ovflsize it is first stored on overflow pages via __ovfl_put and a small overflow reference is stored instead; the function returns RET_ERROR if __ovfl_put fails, if __rec_search returns NULL, or if deleting the existing leaf via __rec_dleaf fails (in that last case the pinned page is first released with mpool_put and no flags); if the page lacks room it calls __bt_split, which inserts the record and unpins the page, increments t->bt_nrecs only when the split returns RET_SUCCESS, and returns the split status; otherwise it shifts the line pointers, writes the record at index idx, increments t->bt_nrecs, sets B_MODIFIED, releases the page to the mpool marked dirty (the caller must not use it afterwards) and returns RET_SUCCESS.

functions.name: cms_signeddata_create
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: context, the crypto contexts, oid and data/data_len are valid and signed_data and signed_data_len are writable output pointers. Postcondition: on success returns 0 and sets *signed_data to a malloc'd buffer holding the DER-encoded PKCS7 SignedData (signature over the SHA-256 digest of data, with messageDigest and contentType signed attributes, and the content attached) with its length in *signed_data_len; on failure returns a nonzero error (ENOMEM if the output malloc fails, an error from pkinit_sign_data, or from oerr when the DER encoding fails; a failure after a bare goto, such as a NULL digest context, OBJ_dup, ASN1_item_i2d or PKCS7_add_signer, returns whatever retval already held). The function frees the PKCS7 object and the signature buffer it allocated itself, and frees the X509_ALGOR only if p7si is set and alg is non-NULL. The caller owns *signed_data on success.

functions.name: x25519_sc_reduce
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s points to a readable and writable buffer of 64 bytes holding a little-endian 512-bit integer. Postcondition: the low 32 bytes of s are overwritten with the little-endian encoding of that integer reduced modulo l = 2^252 + 27742317777372353535851937790883648493; bytes 32..63 are left unchanged (they are only read); nothing is returned and no other memory is modified.

functions.name: AuthenticateProc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called as a Win32 dialog procedure with a valid dialog handle; for WM_INITDIALOG lParam must point to an LSH_DLGINFO_EX structure. Postcondition: WM_INITDIALOG returns FALSE after showing an error message box if the structure size or dialog type is invalid, otherwise it initialises the controls from the defaults or the passed settings, sets the window position and focus, and falls through to return FALSE. WM_HSCROLL updates the slider value text and returns FALSE. WM_COMMAND handles the following commands: IDC_BUTTON_OPTIONS adjusts the options area and keeps the dialog on screen, IDC_BUTTON_CLEAR_HISTORY clears the principal history, IDC_CHECK_RENEWABLE enables or disables the renew slider, ID_HELP opens help, and IDCANCEL calls CloseMe(FALSE). ID_CLOSEME cleans up the sliders, wipes the password buffer, removes the help property, destroys the autocomplete object if one exists, ends the dialog with lParam and returns TRUE. IDOK returns TRUE after a message box if the principal or the password is blank. Otherwise IDOK calls Leash_int_kinit_ex and, on a nonzero error, sets lsh_errno, selects and focuses the offending field and returns TRUE. On success it optionally saves the default settings, optionally adds the principal to the history, calls CloseMe(TRUE) and returns FALSE. WM_MOVE records the window position. Every other message and every path that falls through returns FALSE.

functions.name: NewPasswordProc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called as the dialog procedure of the change-password dialog with a window handle, message and parameters; on WM_INITDIALOG lParam must point to a valid LSH_DLGINFO_EX structure. Postcondition: WM_INITDIALOG returns FALSE if the structure size or dlgtype is invalid (after showing an error box), otherwise fills in the dialog, clears the output fields, sets the title, creates the principal autocomplete and positions the window, then returns FALSE. ID_CLOSEME wipes the password buffers, removes the help property, ends the dialog with lParam, destroys the autocomplete and returns TRUE. IDOK reads the fields and returns TRUE after a message box when the principal or any password is blank, when password2 has a non-printable character (then password2 and password3 are cleared), or when password2 and password3 differ. Otherwise it calls Leash_int_changepwd and, if that fails, returns TRUE (for any error code). On success it adds the principal, shows a success box and calls CloseMe(TRUE), then falls through to return FALSE. IDCANCEL calls CloseMe(FALSE). ID_HELP opens help. WM_MOVE saves the window position. All these other paths return FALSE.

functions.name: ProcessTimeSync
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hostname is a valid NUL-terminated string and tmpstr points to a writable buffer large enough for the message text (hostname, the fixed text and the ctime string). Postcondition: it returns LSH_BADTIMESERV if the host lookup fails (no socket is opened), LSH_NOSOCKET if socket creation fails, LSH_NOCONNECT if setting non-blocking mode or connect fails, LSH_GETTIMEOFDAY if gettimeofday fails, LSH_RECVTIME if no data arrives in 4 recv attempts (500 ms sleeps between failed attempts), LSH_RECVBYTES if the datagram is not exactly 4 bytes, and LSH_SETTIMEOFDAY if settimeofday fails. In each of these cases after socket creation the socket is closed. On success it sets the system time to ntohl(received value) - TM_OFFSET, writes a synchronization message with the hostname and new time into tmpstr, closes the socket and returns 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the standard program arguments; at most one argument (a test file path, or "-info") is expected, otherwise stdin is read. Postcondition: returns 0 after all test lines are read and a pass summary is printed (closing fd if nonzero and freeing the input buffer), or 0 immediately for "-info" after printing WORDSIZE and NN_MAX_BASE; returns -1 on too many arguments, malloc failure, SIGINT handler setup failure, a malformed line (missing record 1, 2 or 3), or a non-NULL 'p' pointer record; the 'n' overflow and the p_normalized mismatch also return -1 directly. The 'c' and 'f' record errors, unknown record types, init failures and nn import failures jump to err, which prints an error message, closes fd if nonzero, frees the buffer and returns -1. Direct -1 returns do not close fd or free the buffer.

functions.name: GENERIC_TEST(
functions.prose_contract: Generated function test_<test_name>(op, params, test_num), defined by the GENERIC_TEST macro invocation (the slice ends partway through the body, so the tail is not visible). Precondition: op equals the operation name string, params is an array of pointers whose types and I/O roles match the declared parameter strings, and global_parameters is set. Postcondition in the visible part: it returns -1 if the types in global_parameters differ from the declared parameter types, and returns 0 if the sanity check fails (bad type or I/O characters, mismatched 'O' typing, or more than one function output). Otherwise it picks up the common length n_len and the fp context from the parameters, declares and initializes the nn and fp outputs, jumps to err if ret is nonzero, and calls the tested function, recording its return value and whether there is a function output. The remaining return values and cleanup occur after the slice and cannot be stated from this code.

functions.name: GENERIC_TEST(
functions.prose_contract: Generated function test_<test_name>(op, params, test_num) (the macro is the real definition, so the name is the macro invocation form). Precondition: op equals the operation string (checked by assert), params holds the test-file values for the declared parameter types and I/O roles, and the global parameter string matches the declared types. Postcondition: returns -1 at once if the declared types differ from the global_parameters; otherwise it runs the tested function and compares every parameter marked 'o' (via fp_cmp, nn_cmp, or direct word/int comparison) and the return value marked 'O' against the expected values, stopping at the first mismatch and printing it. It then frees the temporary nn/fp outputs and returns 1 if all matched and 0 on a mismatch. If initialization fails (ret nonzero) it prints an error and calls exit(-1).

functions.name: md4
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: output points to MD4_DIGEST_SIZE writable bytes, and input points to ilen readable bytes (input may be NULL only if the sub-calls accept it for ilen == 0). Postcondition: runs md4_init, md4_update and md4_final on a local context in sequence, stopping at the first one that returns nonzero, and returns that value; it returns 0 when all three succeed, in which case output holds the MD4 digest of the input. After an earlier failure, md4_final is not called and output is not written by this function; the local context is not returned to the caller.

functions.name: __bign_determinitic_nonce
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: k is a writable nn, q and x are initialized nn values, adata (with adata_len) holds the OID and t data parsed by bign_get_oid_from_adata and bign_get_t_from_adata, h points to hlen readable bytes with hlen <= sizeof(r), and q_bit_len is the bit length of q. Postcondition: returns 0 with k set to a nonzero value strictly less than q, derived deterministically from the hash, the private key x and adata through belt-hash and belt-block iterations; otherwise returns a nonzero error (NULL adata or h, uninitialized q or x, adata parsing failure, hlen too large, any helper failure, r_bar length over 0xffff, or the 32-bit counter i wrapping to 0). In all cases the local theta and FE2OS_D buffers (which hold sensitive data) are zeroed before return.

functions.name: _eddsa_verify_batch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s, pub_keys, m, adata and scratch_pad_area_len are non-NULL, and s, s_len, pub_keys, m, m_len, adata and adata_len each have num valid entries; when scratch_pad_area is non-NULL it is writable for at least *scratch_pad_area_len bytes. Postcondition: if num <= 1 and scratch_pad_area is NULL, it sets *scratch_pad_area_len to 0 and returns 0; if num <= 1 otherwise, it returns the result of _eddsa_verify_batch_no_memory. For num >= 2 with scratch_pad_area NULL, it sets *scratch_pad_area_len to ((2*num)+1)*sizeof(verify_batch_scratch_pad) and returns 0, or returns nonzero if that size is not below 0xffffffff. Otherwise it needs *scratch_pad_area_len to be at least that size, then checks every key and signature (same parameters, key_type == sig_type, hash type, signature length, canonical R, S < q, non-small-order key) and runs the Bos-Coster batch check. It returns 0 if the combined sum is the point at infinity, -1 if it is not, and the result of the no-memory fallback if Bos-Coster returns -2 (time out). Any other failure of a check or of an internal call returns a nonzero error code. On every exit it zeroes the scratch pad (when non-NULL) for *scratch_pad_area_len bytes and uninitializes its local curve, points and numbers. It allocates and frees no memory, and the caller keeps ownership of all buffers.

functions.name: verify_bin_file
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ec_name, ec_sig_name, hash_algorithm, in_fname and in_key_fname are non-NULL strings; in_sig_fname and adata may be NULL, and adata_len is the length of adata. Postcondition: returns 0 only if the public key was imported from in_key_fname and the signature was verified over the content of in_fname; the signature is read either from the structured trailer of in_fname, after checking header magic, lengths, signature type, hash type and curve name, or from the raw file in_sig_fname, and verification uses streaming init/update/finalize or a heap buffer with ec_verify depending on algorithm support. On any failure it returns -1, or the nonzero error code from the helpers string_to_params, check_ancillary_data, import_params, dump_hdr_info, are_str_equal, is_verify_streaming_mode_supported and the MUST_HAVE checks. All opened files are closed and the heap buffer is freed on every path, and a failing fclose turns the result into -1.

functions.name: addr_netmatch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: host and net point to valid struct xaddr objects and masklen is a prefix length. Postcondition: returns -1 if the address families of host and net differ, or if addr_netmask or addr_and fails (for example an unsupported family or masklen too large); otherwise returns the result of addr_cmp on the masked host address and net, which is 0 when the masked host equals net and nonzero otherwise (addr_cmp may itself return a negative value for ordering or an error); nothing is allocated, locked or retained and the inputs are not modified.

functions.name: auth_rhosts2
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pw points to a valid passwd entry (pw_name, pw_dir, pw_uid) and client_user, hostname and ipaddr are valid NUL-terminated strings; the process can switch uid with temporarily_use_uid/restore_uid. Postcondition: returns 1 if, for a non-root user, /etc/hosts.equiv or the ssh shosts.equiv file accepts the host/user pair, or if the home directory is stat-able and passes the strict_modes ownership/mode check and some user ~/.shosts or ~/.rhosts file passes the strict_modes check, is not ignored by the ignore_rhosts setting, and accepts the pair; otherwise returns 0 (no hosts files exist at all, home directory cannot be stat'd, home directory has bad ownership or modes under strict_modes, or no user file accepts). The temporary uid switch is always undone before returning, and each allocated path string is freed; nothing is held by the caller afterwards.

functions.name: kex_exchange_identification
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ssh and ssh->kex are valid with initialised client_version and server_version buffers, and the connection descriptors are usable; timeout_ms > 0 enables a wait before each read, and version_addendum may be NULL or empty. Postcondition: it sends our SSH-2.0 banner, reads the peer's identification (skipping up to SSH_MAX_PRE_BANNER_LINES-1 non-SSH lines when acting as a client), and returns 0 on success; otherwise it returns a negative SSH_ERR_* code (SSH_ERR_SYSTEM_ERROR with errno restored, CONN_CLOSED, CONN_TIMEOUT, ALLOC_FAIL, INVALID_FORMAT, NO_PROTOCOL_VERSION, or a sshbuf error), sending an error message to the peer in some failure cases; it always frees its temporary strings, and it calls fatal if duplicating the peer version string fails.

functions.name: mm_answer_keyallowed
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: m holds a request with a u32 key type (MM_USERKEY or MM_HOSTKEY), a client user string, a client host string, a public key and a u32 pubkey_auth_attempt flag, and authctxt is initialised. Postcondition: it decides whether the key is allowed (only if the key is non-NULL, the user is valid, the option is enabled, the key was not already used and its algorithm matches); it records the key, resets the saved key state and, if allowed, saves the key blob, type, auth options and the cuser/chost strings (ownership passes to the global state), otherwise logs the failed attempt, frees cuser/chost and the options; it frees the key, sends MONITOR_ANS_KEYALLOWED on sock with the allowed flag (plus serialised options when present) and returns 0 always; it calls fatal and does not return on a parse, unknown key type, blob or serialisation error.

functions.name: muxclient
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path is a NUL-terminated ControlPath string and the global options and muxclient_command are initialised. Postcondition: if control_master is not NO/AUTO/AUTO_ASK it returns -1 immediately; if path does not fit in sun_path, socket() fails, or connect fails for a command other than OPEN/STDIO_FWD, it calls fatal (no return); if connect fails for OPEN/STDIO_FWD it logs, unlinks the path when the socket is stale (ECONNREFUSED and control_master not NO), closes the socket and returns -1; if the hello exchange fails it closes the socket and returns -1; otherwise it runs the command: ALIVE_CHECK, TERMINATE, FORWARD, STDIO_FWD, STOP and CANCEL_FWD end with exit(0) (or fatal on failure for ALIVE_CHECK and FORWARD); OPEN returns -1 after the forwards fail or after the session request finishes; PROXY returns the connected socket descriptor (left open); an unknown command calls fatal. The socket is not closed on the return -1 after the session or on proxy return.

functions.name: process_config_line_depth
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: options, filename and line are valid, line is a writable NUL-terminated string, and activep is either NULL (command-line directive, treated as always active) or points to the current active flag; pw, host, original_host and remote_command are as needed by Match and Include. Postcondition: returns 0 for an empty line, comment or blank line, and after a successfully parsed directive; returns -1 on a missing argument, bad quoting, bad option, invalid value, Host/Match/Include on the command line, a failed Include, too many entries, or extra trailing arguments (errors are logged via error()). Some malformed list directives call fatal() instead of returning. A successful Include may instead return -1 if an included file could not be read with ENOENT, and Host and Match update *activep. Option fields are set only when the line is active and only if not already set (first value wins), except SendEnv, which appends. Temporary canonical-name, string-array and argument vectors are always freed, and strings or arrays stored in options are owned by options.

functions.name: process_config_line_depth
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: options, filename, line (a writable, NUL-terminated config line) and the other pointers are valid; activep may be NULL (command-line directive, treated as always active), and depth is the current Include nesting depth. Postcondition: returns 0 for an empty, comment or keyword-only blank line and for a successfully parsed directive, in which case the matching option is set only if the directive is active and the option was still unset (-1/NULL); returns the Include value (-1 when an included file could not be read) if Include sets ret nonzero; returns -1 after logging an error for a missing argument, bad quotes, a bad or unsupported value, extra trailing arguments, an unimplemented opcode, or a Host/Match/Include directive on the command line; some malformed arguments (for example a missing CanonicalDomains, SetEnv, PermitRemoteOpen or ChannelTimeout value) call fatal and do not return. On every exit past argument splitting it frees the temporary canonical-name list, string array and split argument vector; for Host, Match and Include it may change *activep.

functions.name: dump_client_config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: o points to a fully initialized Options structure (defaults filled in, string fields valid or NULL where allowed, arrays consistent with their counts) and host is a valid string; the Options hostkeyalgorithms field may be NULL or a valid allocated string. Postcondition: the host key algorithm list in o->hostkeyalgorithms is expanded via kex_assemble_names (the process terminates via fatal_fr if that fails), and the full client configuration (user, host, port, flag, integer, string, forward and array options, plus the special-case options such as tunneldevice, canonicalizepermittedcnames, escapechar, ipqos, rekeylimit, streamlocalbindmask, syslogfacility and proxyjump/proxycommand) is printed to stdout; the function returns nothing and otherwise leaves the options unchanged.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process command-line arguments and the file-level option variables (family, lflag, uflag, etc.) are in their initial state. Postcondition: main never returns; it ignores SIGPIPE, parses options with getopt, and exits via usage(1), errx(1,...) or err(1,...) on any invalid option or flag combination (missing or extra arguments, -s/-p/-z with -l, -k without -l, proxy with UDP/listen/unix/IPv6/-s, bad numeric values, mktemp failure) or on a failed local_listen, recvfrom, connect or accept. In listen mode it sets ret=0, listens (unix_bind/unix_listen or local_listen), handles one connection per loop iteration (looping only with -k), closes sockets and exits 0. In the AF_UNIX client mode it calls unix_connect, runs readwrite and closes the socket if the connect returned >0 and no -z, otherwise ret=1; it unlinks the temporary socket path if -u, then exits with ret. In the TCP/UDP client mode it tries each port in portlist, closing the previous socket if nonzero, connecting directly or via socks_connect, skipping failed connects, reporting success with -v/-z, running fdpass (-F) or readwrite (unless -z), setting ret=1 if udptest fails, then closes s if nonzero and exits with ret (0 if the last attempted connect succeeded, otherwise as last set, initial value 1).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called as the ssh-agent program entry point with argc/argv holding the command-line options and an optional command to run. Postcondition: main never returns normally. With -k it signals the agent named by SSH_AGENT_PID with SIGTERM, prints unset commands and exits 0, or exits 1 on a missing or bad PID or a failed kill. Bad options or flag combinations call usage(), and fatal errors (such as a too-low file descriptor limit or a failed pledge) call fatal(). If the agent socket cannot be set up (mkdtemp or unix_listener failure) or fork fails it exits 1 (via exit or cleanup_exit). Without -d/-D it forks. The parent closes the socket and, with no command, prints the environment-setting lines and exits 0; with a command it sets SSH_AUTH_SOCK and SSH_AGENT_PID and calls execvp, exiting 1 if setenv or execvp fails. The child (or the process itself in -d/-D mode, which prints the socket info and skips forking) sets up logging, signal handlers and the socket, then loops forever in ppoll serving requests. It exits via cleanup_exit(1) if setsid or setrlimit fails, cleanup_exit(2) when a termination signal was received, or fatal() on a poll error other than EINTR. A SIGUSR1 removes all identities and the loop continues.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the ssh-keygen command line and the process has a valid passwd entry for the current uid. Postcondition: options are parsed with getopt (invalid values call fatal, unknown options call usage); with -Y it returns the result of sig_find_principals, sig_match_principals, sig_sign or sig_verify (or exits 1 on missing arguments, or errors and calls usage for an unsupported operation); otherwise it validates argument combinations (usage on error), returns 0 after -k (gen_krl), -Q (check_krl), -M generate/screen, -A, and returns do_download_sk's result for -K; other single-purpose modes (CA signing, show cert, known hosts, PKCS11 download, fingerprint, passphrase/comment change, conversion, print public, resource record printing) run in sequence, with resource record printing ending in exit(0) or fatal when no key found; with none of those it generates a new key pair (for security-key types enrolling via sshsk_enroll with up to 3 PIN retries), saves private and public key files and optional attestation, prints fingerprint unless quiet, and exits 0, or exits 1 if overwrite is declined or saving the private key fails, or calls fatal on other errors.

functions.name: load_identity_file
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: id points to a valid Identity whose filename is a NUL-terminated path. Postcondition: returns NULL if stat() of the file fails (logging 'no such identity'); otherwise it tries to load the private key, first with an empty passphrase and then, up to options.number_of_password_prompts times, with passphrases read from the user (stopping on an empty passphrase), and returns the loaded key, which the caller owns and must free. It returns NULL if the load fails fatally (non-ENOENT system error or other error, ENOENT, or a wrong passphrase in batch mode), if the key is an authenticator-hosted key with no sk_provider (the key is freed), if the RSA key length check fails (the key is freed), or if the prompts are exhausted. A key loaded without a quit condition and not already in the agent may be added to the agent via maybe_add_key_to_agent. Typed passphrases are zeroed and freed, and the comment is freed on each iteration.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ac/av are the sshd command line (av[0] is the program path, which must be absolute unless -t/-T/-i/-G is given), and the process is the sshd listener. Postcondition: main parses options and the config, loads host keys and certificates into sensitive_data, and exits the process with status 1 or via fatal() on any error, with status 0 for -V or after a -t/-T config test. Otherwise it daemonizes if needed, listens or uses inetd, accepts a connection in a forked child, sets up stdin/stdout and the config pass fd, and execv()s sshd-session. It never returns normally; if execv fails it calls fatal().

functions.name: certify
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller supplies a certificate request, the CA key and optional CA certificate, a policy list, a serial number and a database; the request subject name has already been built. Postcondition: the function applies the 'policy' rules (optional, supplied, match) to build the new subject name, and prints a message and jumps to the shared 'end' cleanup if a policy entry is unknown, invalid, missing or mismatched, or if allocation fails. It then creates a new X509, sets its serial number, issuer, validity times, subject and public key, and adds extensions from the extfile or config section and from the request. It strips email entries from the subject unless email_dn is set and records the subject one-line string in row[DB_name]. Any failing step also jumps to 'end' with the result left at its failure value. The return code and the final signing, database update and cleanup lie outside this slice.

functions.name: ca_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the command-line arguments of the openssl 'ca' subcommand, and the global OpenSSL application state (bio_err, bio_out, default_config_file) is initialised. Postcondition: it parses the options, loads the configuration, CA key, CA certificate and index database, and then performs the requested operations: serial status report, database update for expired certificates, certification of requests (writing new certificate files, then updating the serial and index files), CRL generation and certificate revocation or validation. It returns 0 on success, on -help, and when the user cancels certification at the commit prompt (including an I/O error reading the answer). It returns 1 on any other error, such as an option, configuration, key, certificate, database, certify, file or memory failure, and in that case prints the queued OpenSSL errors to bio_err. On every path it frees everything it allocated (BIOs, certificate stack, passphrase if it allocated it, serial and CRL number, index, option stacks, key, CA certificate, CRL, configs, engine).

functions.name: cmp_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the command-line arguments of the openssl cmp application, and the global option variables (opt_*, bio_err, default_config_file) are in their initial state. Postcondition: the function parses the options and config file, creates the CMP context, and then either acts as an HTTP CMP server (with -port) or runs the selected CMP command opt_repeat times as a client, saving the resulting certificates, chains and keys. In every case, including all error paths, it then cleanses the password/secret option strings, prints the CMP error queue if the result was not 1, frees the CMP context, mock server, TLS info, verify params, engine and config, and closes the CMP log. It returns EXIT_FAILURE if the final internal result is 0 (failure, or -1 after a bad option or -help usage) and EXIT_SUCCESS otherwise (all rounds succeeded, the server returned 1, or -reqout_only completed).

functions.name: cms_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command-line arguments of the `openssl cms` command. Postcondition: it parses options, loads the inputs, performs the one requested CMS operation (encrypt, decrypt, sign, verify, resign, receipts, digest, compress, data, etc.) and writes the output. It returns 0 on success and 1 on early failure or an option error (0 for -help). It returns 2 for failures while loading certificates, keys or files, 3 when creating the CMS structure fails, and 4 when the operation itself fails. It returns 5 when saving certs or signers fails and 6 when writing output fails, or verify_err+32 on a verification failure with -verify_retcode. On every path it prints queued errors if ret is nonzero and frees all resources it owns at the end label: stacks, certificates, keys, ciphers, CMS structures, BIOs, buffers, engine and config. secret_key and secret_keyid are not freed if the recipient-key call absorbed them (they are set to NULL).

functions.name: ec_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv form a valid command-line argument vector for the `ec` app (argv[0] is the program name, with options as described by ec_options). Postcondition: returns 0 if help was requested or if the key was loaded, optionally printed, checked (a failed key check only prints "EC Key Invalid!" and does not change the result), and written (or noout set) successfully; returns 1 on any other failure (option error, cipher or password error, key load failure, output open failure, setting point format, encoding or public-key parameter failure, print failure, check context creation failure, or encoder write failure), in which case the OpenSSL error queue is printed to bio_err. On every path it frees the output BIO, key, cipher, encoder, decoder and key contexts, releases the engine, and securely clears and frees passin and passout if set.

functions.name: enc_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv form a valid command line whose argv[0] is the command name (enc, base64, zlib, brotli, zstd or a cipher name), and the OpenSSL application environment (bio_err, bio_out, option tables) is initialised. Postcondition: it parses options, optionally reads a password or key, and encrypts, decrypts or encodes the input to the output, printing the key, salt and IV if requested; it returns 0 on success (including -help, -list, and -P after printing the key), and returns 1 on any error (bad option, unreadable or empty key file, out of memory, unknown cipher or digest, bad hex salt, key or IV, I/O failure, cipher init failure, empty prompted password, flush failure), after printing a diagnostic. On every path after option parsing it frees the allocated strbuf, buff, BIOs, digest, cipher, skey objects, engine and password, and cleanses the password it used, but it never frees the string pointers taken from argv.

functions.name: list_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command-line arguments for the 'list' subcommand and the option and BIO subsystems (bio_out, bio_err) are usable. Postcondition: returns 0 after printing the requested listings (separated by blank lines) when at least one option was processed, no extra arguments remain, and no -help error occurred; -help prints the help and returns 0 immediately; it returns 1 after printing 'Use -help for summary.' to bio_err on an option error (OPT_ERR), on leftover non-option arguments, or when no option was given at all, and returns 1 without that message if opt_provider fails; it sets the global verbose and select_name according to the options.

functions.name: ocsp_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are a valid command-line argument vector for the openssl ocsp app (argv[0] is the program name). Postcondition: parses options and, depending on them, builds, reads, signs or writes an OCSP request, acts as a responder (single response or a loop over accepted connections), sends the request to a host, or reads a response file, then prints and verifies the response; it returns 0 on success (including -help, responder mode finishing its accept count or index mode, and the no-operation case where no host, response or index is given after the request is written) and 1 on any error (bad option, load/parse/IO failure, index problem, response error status without -ignore_err, nonce mismatch, verify failure, or print_ocsp_summary failure); on every exit path it prints queued errors and frees all certificates, keys, stores, BIOs, stacks, index database, request, response and URL strings it owns.

functions.name: pkcs8_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the command-line arguments of the pkcs8 subcommand (argv[0] is the program name), and the OpenSSL app globals such as bio_err are initialised. Postcondition: returns 0 after the help text is printed or after a key was read, converted (PKCS#8 encrypted, unencrypted or plain private key) and written to the output file or stdout in PEM or DER; returns 1 on any error (bad option, password, key, format, PBE or I/O failure). On every path the X509_SIG, PKCS8 key info, EVP_PKEY, cipher, engine, output and input BIOs and the passin and passout strings are released at the end label.

functions.name: set_keygen_ctx
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pkeytype and pkeylen point to writable storage; if gstr is NULL then *pkeylen is read as the default RSA key length; gstr, if non-NULL, is a NUL-terminated string of the form keytype, keylen, keytype:keylen, or param:file / keytype:file; keygen_engine may be NULL. Postcondition: on success returns a newly allocated EVP_PKEY_CTX that has been initialised for key generation (with the BITS parameter set when a key length was given, or defaulted from *pkeylen for RSA/RSA-PSS), sets *pkeytype to a newly allocated string the caller must free, and may update *pkeylen (to the parameter key's bit size when a parameter file is used). It returns NULL after printing an error to bio_err when: "param" is given with no path, the parameter file cannot be opened or read, the key type cannot be determined, memory allocation fails, the key type does not match the parameters, context allocation fails, keygen init fails, or setting the key size fails. On those paths the parameter key, the file BIO and any created context are freed, but a *pkeytype already allocated is not freed and stays set.

functions.name: req_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv form a valid command line for the openssl 'req' application, and the OpenSSL app globals (bio_err, bio_out, default_config_file, section, batch, req_conf, addext_conf) are usable. Postcondition: it parses the options, loads the configuration, loads or generates the private key, and creates or loads a certificate request. It then optionally builds and signs a self-signed or CA-signed X.509 certificate with -x509 or -CA, or signs the request, optionally modifies the subject and verifies the request, and writes the key, public key, text, subject, modulus, request or certificate to the output. It returns 0 on success, including -help and -noout with no other output requested, and returns 1 on any option, config, key, signing, verification or I/O error, after printing an error message (and the OpenSSL error queue when ret is non-zero). On every path it frees the config objects, BIOs, keys, key-generation context, stacks, hash tables, engines, request, certificates, serial and the non-config-owned passwords.

functions.name: req_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command-line arguments of the openssl req application, with the application's global state (bio_err, bio_out, the config helpers) initialised. Postcondition: it parses the options, loads configuration and keys, optionally generates a key, writes the private key, creates or loads a certificate request, optionally creates a self-signed or CA-signed X.509 certificate (-x509/-CA), optionally modifies the subject, verifies the request and writes the requested outputs (public key, text, subject, modulus, request or certificate). It returns 0 on success, on -help, and when -noout is given with no other output requested; it returns 1 on any error (option, config, key, signing, verification or write failure). Note that with -text the return value is first set to the result of the print call, and nonzero means success. On the failure path it prints the pending OpenSSL errors to bio_err. On every path it frees all objects it allocated (configs, BIOs, keys, key context, option stacks, hash table, engines, request, subject name, certificates, serial, and the passwords unless they came from the config).

functions.name: rsautl_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the command-line arguments of the rsautl application (program name first), and the global bio_err is usable. Postcondition: returns 0 when -help was requested, or when the selected RSA verify-recover, sign, encrypt or decrypt operation succeeded and its output was written (raw, hex dump, or ASN.1 parse dump) to the output BIO; an ASN.1 dump failure only prints the error stack and still returns 0. It returns 1 on option errors, a failed random load, a failed password fetch, a non-private key used for sign or decrypt, input read errors, context creation failure, or a failed RSA operation, printing messages to bio_err. When the key cannot be loaded (pkey is NULL) it returns 1 immediately without freeing passin, the engine or any other resource. On every other path it frees the EVP_PKEY_CTX, EVP_PKEY, engine, both BIOs and the rsa_in, rsa_out and passin buffers before returning.

functions.name: s_client_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv describe the command line of the openssl s_client command (argv[0] is the program name, argv has argc valid strings), and the application globals such as bio_err are initialised. Postcondition: the function parses the options, sets up the SSL context and connection, runs the interactive client session, and returns ret, which is 0 for the -help path or after a clean session end and 1 for option errors, allocation or file-load failures, connect failures, STARTTLS failures, or other session errors. On every exit it frees all buffers, BIO, SSL, SSL_CTX, key, certificate, string and engine objects that it allocated, so the caller keeps no references and has nothing to free.

functions.name: s_client_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv describe a valid command-line argument vector (argv[0] is the program name) for the s_client command, and the OpenSSL app globals such as bio_err are initialised. Postcondition: the function parses the options, loads keys, certificates and CRLs, builds the SSL_CTX, connects to the target, runs the interactive client loop and then frees every resource it allocated, closing the socket on the exit path. It returns 0 after -help or a clean session, and otherwise 1 (for example on an option, parse, load, connect or SSL setup error, after printing a message to bio_err); it also returns whatever value ret holds at the end label if a later code path sets it to something else.

functions.name: s_server_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv describe the command line of the openssl s_server application, with argv[0] the program name. Postcondition: it parses options, loads certificates, keys, CRLs and DH parameters, builds the SSL_CTX (and a second one when a servername and second certificate are given), runs do_server with the chosen callback (rev_body, www_body or sv_body), prints stats and returns 0; -help also returns 0 after printing help. Any option, loading or configuration failure jumps to the end label and returns 1. On every path it frees all objects it owns (contexts, keys, certificates, stacks, strings, session, BIOs, engine) and resets bio_s_out and bio_s_msg to NULL.

functions.name: smime_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command-line arguments of the smime app, and the OpenSSL app globals (bio_err, option parser) are initialised. Postcondition: it parses options and performs the one requested S/MIME operation (encrypt, decrypt, sign, resign, verify or pk7out), returning 0 on success and 1 if the verify parameter object cannot be allocated. For all other errors it returns the stage code reached: 0 for -help, and also 0 for an option-parsing or validation failure before the exit status is set (usage errors, missing operation or signer or recipient, option or allocation failures), 2 for failures while loading passwords, certificates, keys or input and output files, 3 for failures while creating the PKCS7 structure or writing output, 4 for decrypt or verify failures, and 5 if the signer certificates cannot be saved after a successful verify. On every path after the verify parameter is allocated it prints queued OpenSSL errors when the return value is nonzero, and frees all certificates, keys, stacks, stores, BIOs, ciphers, the digest, the engine, the password and the config that it allocated.

functions.name: smime_main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the command line of the openssl smime command and the OpenSSL application state (bio_err, option parser, library context) is initialised. Postcondition: returns 0 on success (including -help); returns 1 if the X509_VERIFY_PARAM cannot be allocated; returns 0 if option parsing or setup fails before the 'ret = 2' assignment (for example bad option, missing operation, or password failure, since ret is still 0 there); returns 2 for failures while loading certificates, keys or input/output files or setting up the verify store; 3 for failures creating the PKCS7 structure or writing the output; 4 for decrypt, verify or output-format errors; and 5 if writing the signer certificates fails after successful verification. On every path after the initial allocation it prints queued errors when the result is nonzero and frees all stacks, certs, keys, BIOs, the PKCS7 object, the store, the verify params, the engine, the passphrase and the config.

functions.name: get_dsa
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dsa_bits should be 512, 1024 or 2048 and the OpenSSL default library context must be usable. Postcondition: returns NULL if dsa_bits is not one of those values, or if the DSA EVP_PKEY_CTX, any BIGNUM, the parameter builder or the OSSL_PARAM array cannot be created, or if EVP_PKEY_fromdata_init or EVP_PKEY_fromdata fails; otherwise returns a newly allocated EVP_PKEY holding the built-in test DSA key pair for that size, which the caller must free. All temporaries (params, builder, BIGNUMs, context) are freed on every path after the context is created.

functions.name: print_x509v3_exts
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bio is a valid BIO, x is a valid X509 certificate, and ext_names is a non-NULL NUL-terminated comma-separated list of extension short names. Postcondition: returns 1 (after printing "No extensions in certificate" to bio_err) if the certificate has no extensions; returns 0 if duplicating ext_names fails, if no names can be parsed (after printing "Invalid extension names" to bio), or if allocating the names array or the new stack, or pushing onto it, fails; returns 1 (after printing "No extensions matched" to bio) if no extension matched; otherwise returns the result of X509V3_extensions_print for the matched extensions. On every path the temporary stack (not the extensions themselves), the names array and the duplicated name string are freed, and the caller keeps no allocations.

functions.name: AES_bi_ige_encrypt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: in, out, key and ivec are non-null (ivec points to at least 64 bytes), enc is AES_ENCRYPT or AES_DECRYPT, length is a multiple of AES_BLOCK_SIZE, in and out each point to length bytes, and key/key2 are valid expanded AES keys; these are checked with OPENSSL_assert, which aborts on violation. Postcondition: returns nothing; it writes length bytes to out with a bidirectional IGE transform: when encrypting, a forward IGE pass runs over the data followed by a backward pass in place on out using the second IV pair (ivec+32, ivec+48); when decrypting, a backward pass runs from the end using IV pair (ivec+32, ivec+48) and then a forward pass over out using (ivec, ivec+16). Both calls use AES_encrypt or AES_decrypt with key only; key2 is never used. Input is not modified, except where in and out overlap.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS(ASN1_OCTET_STRING)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ASN1_OCTET_STRING_new(void). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns the result of ASN1_STRING_type_new(V_ASN1_OCTET_STRING), i.e. a newly allocated ASN1_STRING of that type owned by the caller, or NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS(ASN1_OCTET_STRING)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ASN1_OCTET_STRING_free(x). Precondition: x is NULL or an ASN1_STRING obtained from the allocator that has not been freed. Postcondition: calls ASN1_STRING_free(x), releasing the string and its data (a no-op for NULL); x must not be used afterwards.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS(ASN1_INTEGER)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ASN1_INTEGER_new(void). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns the result of ASN1_STRING_type_new(V_ASN1_INTEGER), i.e. a newly allocated ASN1_STRING of that type owned by the caller, or NULL on allocation failure.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_STRING_FUNCTIONS(ASN1_INTEGER)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ASN1_INTEGER_free(x). Precondition: x is NULL or an ASN1_STRING obtained from the allocator that has not been freed. Postcondition: calls ASN1_STRING_free(x), releasing the string and its data (a no-op for NULL); x must not be used afterwards.

functions.name: ossl_asn1_do_adb
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: val points to a valid ASN1 structure and tt to a valid template; if tt has an ADB flag, its item is a valid ASN1_ADB whose offset locates the selector field in val and whose table has tblcount valid entries. Postcondition: if tt has no ADB flag bits it returns tt unchanged; otherwise if the selector field is NULL it returns adb->null_tt, or if that is NULL goes to the error path; else it computes the selector (OID nid or integer value), and if an adb_cb callback exists and returns 0 it raises ASN1_R_UNSUPPORTED_ANY_DEFINED_BY_TYPE and returns NULL; else it returns the template of the first table entry whose value equals the selector, otherwise adb->default_tt if non-NULL, otherwise takes the error path. The error path raises ASN1_R_UNSUPPORTED_ANY_DEFINED_BY_TYPE only if nullerr is nonzero and returns NULL. No ownership is transferred; the returned pointer refers to existing template data.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKAC)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function NETSCAPE_SPKAC_new(void). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns a newly allocated NETSCAPE_SPKAC built by ASN1_item_new from the template (pubkey and challenge fields initialized), or NULL on allocation failure; the caller owns the result.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKAC)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function NETSCAPE_SPKAC_free(a). Precondition: a is NULL or a NETSCAPE_SPKAC obtained from this library's allocation or parsing functions. Postcondition: calls ASN1_item_free, which frees the structure and its sub-objects (nothing if a is NULL); a must not be used afterwards.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKAC)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function d2i_NETSCAPE_SPKAC(a, in, len). Precondition: in points to a pointer to at least len readable bytes; a is NULL or points to a NETSCAPE_SPKAC pointer. Postcondition: on success returns the parsed NETSCAPE_SPKAC (also stored in *a if a is non-NULL) and advances *in past the consumed bytes; on parse failure returns NULL.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKAC)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function i2d_NETSCAPE_SPKAC(a, out). Precondition: a points to a valid NETSCAPE_SPKAC; out is NULL or points to a pointer to a buffer large enough for the encoding. Postcondition: returns the DER encoding length (negative on error); if out is non-NULL the encoding is written and *out advanced past it, otherwise only the length is computed.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKI)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function NETSCAPE_SPKI_new(void). Precondition: none. Postcondition: returns a newly allocated NETSCAPE_SPKI built from the template (spkac, sig_algor and signature initialized), or NULL on allocation failure; the caller owns the result.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKI)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function NETSCAPE_SPKI_free(a). Precondition: a is NULL or a NETSCAPE_SPKI obtained from this library's allocation or parsing functions. Postcondition: the structure and its sub-objects are freed (nothing if a is NULL); a must not be used afterwards.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKI)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function d2i_NETSCAPE_SPKI(a, in, len). Precondition: in points to a pointer to at least len readable bytes; a is NULL or points to a NETSCAPE_SPKI pointer. Postcondition: on success returns the parsed NETSCAPE_SPKI (also stored in *a if a is non-NULL) and advances *in past the consumed bytes; on parse failure returns NULL.

functions.name: IMPLEMENT_ASN1_FUNCTIONS(NETSCAPE_SPKI)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function i2d_NETSCAPE_SPKI(a, out). Precondition: a points to a valid NETSCAPE_SPKI; out is NULL or points to a pointer to a buffer large enough for the encoding. Postcondition: returns the DER encoding length (negative on error); if out is non-NULL the encoding is written and *out advanced past it, otherwise only the length is computed.

functions.name: BIO_nread
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bio is a valid non-NULL BIO and buf points to a writable char* (as BIO_ctrl requires). Postcondition: if bio->init is zero, it raises BIO_R_UNINITIALIZED on the error queue and returns -2 without calling BIO_ctrl; otherwise it returns (int)BIO_ctrl(bio, BIO_C_NREAD, num, buf), and if that result is positive it also adds it to bio->num_read.

functions.name: BIO_dgram_non_fatal_error
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: err is any integer error code (an errno value or, on Windows, a WSA error code). Postcondition: returns 1 if err equals one of the platform-defined non-fatal codes (WSAEWOULDBLOCK on Windows, EWOULDBLOCK, EINTR, EAGAIN, EPROTO, EINPROGRESS, EALREADY, each only if defined), and returns 0 otherwise; it has no side effects.

functions.name: dgram_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: b is a valid datagram BIO whose ptr field points to a bio_dgram_data, and ptr satisfies the requirement of the particular cmd (for example, non-NULL and correctly typed and sized for the SET/GET timeout, GET_PEER, DETECT_PEER_ADDR, SET_NEXT_TIMEOUT, SET_CONNECTED (may be NULL), GET_LOCAL_ADDR_ENABLE and poll descriptor commands). Postcondition: it dispatches on cmd, performs the command's action on the BIO state or socket (reset, set fd, connect, MTU query/set, peer get/set, nonblocking, timeouts, timer-expiry flags, don't-fragment, peek mode, local address, capability queries, poll descriptors) and returns the command-specific long result (for example 1, 0, a size, an fd, an MTU, or bytes copied); unknown commands return 0; BIO_CTRL_DGRAM_GET_MTU returns data->mtu directly; any other negative result is normalized to -1 before return.

functions.name: BIO_fd_non_fatal_error
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; err is any integer error code (typically an errno value). Postcondition: returns 1 if err equals one of the platform-defined transient error codes (EWOULDBLOCK, ENOTCONN, EINTR, EAGAIN, EPROTO, EINPROGRESS, EALREADY, each only if defined at compile time), otherwise returns 0; no state is modified.

functions.name: mem_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: b is a memory BIO whose ptr is a valid BIO_BUF_MEM with non-NULL buf and readp pointing to valid BUF_MEM structures; ptr must be valid for the commands that use it (BIO_CTRL_INFO and BIO_C_GET_BUF_MEM_PTR accept NULL, BIO_C_SET_BUF_MEM needs the new BUF_MEM). Postcondition: performs the requested control command and returns a long: BIO_CTRL_RESET resets the buffer (clearing it unless read-only or NONCLEAR_RST) and returns 1; BIO_C_FILE_SEEK returns -1 without change if num is negative or beyond the current buffer, otherwise repositions the read pointer to offset num and returns num; BIO_C_FILE_TELL returns the current offset; BIO_CTRL_EOF returns 1 if no data remains else 0; BIO_CTRL_INFO returns the remaining length and stores the data pointer through ptr if non-NULL; BIO_C_SET_BUF_MEM frees the old buffer, sets shutdown to num and installs ptr as the buffer, returning 1; BIO_C_GET_BUF_MEM_PTR stores the BUF_MEM pointer (syncing first unless read-only) into *ptr if non-NULL and returns 1; BIO_CTRL_GET_CLOSE returns shutdown; BIO_CTRL_SET_CLOSE and BIO_C_SET_BUF_MEM_EOF_RETURN store num into shutdown or b->num and return 1; BIO_CTRL_WPENDING returns 0; BIO_CTRL_PENDING returns the remaining length; BIO_CTRL_DUP and BIO_CTRL_FLUSH return 1; BIO_CTRL_PUSH, BIO_CTRL_POP and unknown commands return 0.

functions.name: ossl_cmp_asn1_octet_string_set1
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tgt is either NULL or points to a slot holding a valid (or NULL) ASN1_OCTET_STRING pointer, and src is NULL or a valid ASN1_OCTET_STRING. Postcondition: returns 0 with a CMP_R_NULL_ARGUMENT error raised if tgt is NULL; returns 1 without change if *tgt == src (self-assignment, including both NULL); otherwise duplicates src (or uses NULL if src is NULL), and on duplication failure returns 0 leaving *tgt unchanged; on success frees the old *tgt, stores the new copy (or NULL) in *tgt and returns 1.

functions.name: sc_muladd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s points to 32 writable bytes and a, b, c each point to 32 readable bytes (s may alias a, b or c since all inputs are fully loaded before any output byte is written). functions.name: TXT_DB_insert
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: db is a valid initialized TXT_DB with db->index and db->qual arrays of db->num_fields entries, and row is a row array of field pointers. Postcondition: the function first checks each non-NULL index whose qualifier is NULL or accepts row for an existing equal entry; if one exists it sets db->error to DB_ERROR_INDEX_CLASH, db->arg1 to that field index, db->arg_row to the existing row, changes nothing else and returns 0. Otherwise it inserts row into each such index and then pushes it onto db->data, and returns 1 on success, with row stored in db->data and those indexes. If an index insert (detected by retrieve returning NULL) or the push fails, it sets db->error to DB_ERROR_MALLOC, deletes row from the indexes it was inserted into earlier (those whose qualifier accepts it) and returns 0. The function never frees row.

functions.name: ossl_serial_number_print
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: out is a valid BIO, bs is a non-NULL ASN1_INTEGER whose data points to bs->length readable bytes, and indent is suitable as a printf field width. Postcondition: writes a representation of the serial number to out and returns 0 on success: " (Empty)" if length is 0; if the value fits in int64_t, " <decimal> (0x<hex>)" with a '-' sign before both numbers when the type is negative; otherwise a newline, indent spaces, " (Negative)" if negative, then the bytes as colon-separated two-digit hex. Returns -1 as soon as any BIO_puts/BIO_printf call returns <= 0. The error queue is restored to its prior state by ERR_set_mark/ERR_pop_to_mark around the int64 conversion, so conversion failure leaves no error entry.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds argc valid strings and the program is invoked as quic-client-block [-6] hostname port, so at least 3 arguments (4 with -6) are present. Postcondition: the function makes a QUIC connection to hostname:port, sends an HTTP/1.0 GET request, prints the response to stdout, and shuts the connection down. It returns EXIT_SUCCESS only if SSL_shutdown eventually returns 1. It returns EXIT_FAILURE on a usage error, any setup, connect or write failure, a negative SSL_shutdown result, or when the read side reports a closed connection (SSL_STREAM_STATE_CONN_CLOSED). A remote stream reset, an unknown stream failure or another read error only prints a message and still proceeds to shutdown. When the result is EXIT_FAILURE the OpenSSL error stack is dumped to stderr. Before returning, the ssl object (which owns the BIO), ctx and peer_addr are freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds argc valid NUL-terminated strings; the program expects `[-6] hostname port` and needs argc >= 3 (argc >= 4 when argv[1] is "-6"). Postcondition: it creates a QUIC client connection, opens one bidirectional and one unidirectional stream, sends an HTTP GET on each, reads stream 1 and a server-initiated stream 3 to the end while printing the data to stdout, then calls SSL_shutdown until it returns 1; it returns EXIT_SUCCESS only if that whole sequence completes, and returns EXIT_FAILURE on a usage error, any setup, connect, stream creation, write or accept failure, an SSL_shutdown result below 0, or a connection-closed read state. On every path past the argument check it frees ssl, the three streams, ctx and peer_addr (all NULL-safe), and if the result is EXIT_FAILURE it first prints the OpenSSL error stack to stderr. The BIO is not freed separately once owned by ssl.

functions.name: FuzzerTestOneInput
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: FuzzerInit has run so fuzzer_table and prediction_table (USHRT_MAX entries) are valid, and buf points to at least len readable bytes. Postcondition: returns -1 if len < 11 (counting a skipped value) or if the operation code is not one of insert, delete, lookup, flush, foreach or filter; returns 0 for a handled operation after running it on the table and asserting the result matches the prediction table; an OP_FLUSH that is not the rare flush turn (flushes % 100000 != 1) only counts a skip, increments flushes and returns 0. On insert, if the table fails to grow (rc == -1) the code breaks and returns 0 while still holding the write lock, without marking the entry allocated; otherwise it marks the entry allocated and unlocks. Delete, insert, lookup, flush and foreach/filter update their counters; the filter result list is freed.

functions.name: s390x_ecd_keygen448
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: gctx points to a valid generation context (libctx, propq, selection) usable for fetching SHAKE256 and generating random bytes. Postcondition: allocates a new Ed448 ECX_KEY; if allocation fails it raises an error and returns NULL; if the selection lacks OSSL_KEYMGMT_SELECT_KEYPAIR it returns the blank key with no key material; otherwise it allocates the private key, generates 57 random private bytes, hashes them with SHAKE256 into 114 bytes, clamps the first 57 bytes, computes the public key via s390x_ed448_mul, sets the sign bit in pubkey[56], sets haspubkey to 1, frees the hash context and digest and returns the key; if any step fails (private key allocation, SHAKE256 fetch, random generation, digest context or digest operations, point multiplication) it frees the key, the hash context and the digest and returns NULL.

functions.name: rsa_set_ctx_params
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vprsactx is a PROV_RSA_CTX pointer (NULL is tolerated) and params is an OSSL_PARAM array (NULL or empty is tolerated); when padding or saltlen parameters are supplied the context's rsa, operation and (if PSS-restricted) md fields must be valid. Postcondition: returns 0 if vprsactx is NULL; returns 1 without changes if params is empty; otherwise it first applies the four FIPS indicator parameters (returning 0 if any fails), then parses digest, properties, pad mode, PSS saltlen, MGF1 digest and MGF1 properties into local state, returning 0 (usually with an error raised) on any invalid value: wrong data type, a bad or disallowed padding mode (OAEP, PSS without sign/verify operation, PKCS1/none/X9.31 unless the key is a plain RSA key, plus the FIPS-only X9.31 key-size and permission checks), saltlen given without PSS padding, saltlen below RSA_PSS_SALTLEN_AUTO_DIGEST_MAX, restricted-key violations (autodetected saltlen on non-verify, saltlen below min_saltlen), or MGF1 digest given without PSS padding. Only after all parsing succeeds does it store pad_mode and saltlen into the context; if no md is set, no digest was given and padding is PSS it defaults the digest name to RSA_DEFAULT_DIGEST_NAME; it then sets up the MGF1 digest if given and the digest (or, if no digest name, checks padding against the current mdnid), returning 0 if any of these fails, else 1. On a late failure pad_mode and saltlen have already been updated, and FIPS indicator settings may have been changed by earlier steps. The caller keeps ownership of everything it passed in.

functions.name: port_default_packet_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is a valid QUIC_PORT whose demux owns the received datagram buffer e, and dcid is the destination connection ID parsed from e (possibly NULL). Postcondition: returns nothing; if the port is not running, the datagram is a stateless reset, or the port rejects it, e is released to the demux and nothing else happens; if dcid matches an existing channel in the port's lcidm, e is handed to that channel via ossl_quic_channel_inject and is NOT released here (early return); otherwise, if incoming connections are allowed and the datagram is a valid Initial packet (dcid non-NULL, length at least QUIC_MIN_INITIAL_DGRAM_LEN, header decodes, version 1, type Initial, QRX creation, initial secret derivation and validation succeed, and any retry/token checks pass), a new channel is bound via port_bind_channel, a NEW_TOKEN may be generated, and either the QRX is handed to the channel or its validated packets are injected into the channel; on every other path (NULL dcid, too short datagram, header decode failure, unsupported version possibly after sending a version negotiation packet if at least 1200 bytes, non-Initial packet, QRX or validation failure, a Retry sent, or no channel created) the packet is dropped. On all paths except the existing-channel one, any QRX still owned (qrx and qrx_src) is freed and e is released to the demux.

functions.name: qrx_process_pkt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: qrx, urxe, pkt and first_dcid are valid, pkt points into the datagram buffer of urxe at packet index pkt_idx, and datagram_len is the length of the datagram (first_dcid is written when pkt_idx == 0 and read otherwise). Postcondition: returns 0 after either committing the packet (a decrypted packet, or an unencrypted Version Negotiation/Retry packet, is filled in from the URXE and moved from qrx->rx_free to the tail of qrx->rx_pending, the packet is marked processed, and largest_pn is updated for decrypted packets) or treating it as malformed or already processed or failing allocation (the packet is marked processed in urxe and pkt is advanced past just this packet if its header was decoded, otherwise past the rest of the datagram, with no RXE queued); returns 1 if the packet is deferred because keys for its encryption level are not yet available (or 1-RTT is not yet allowed), in which case pkt is advanced past this packet and it is not marked processed.

functions.name: dtls1_read_bytes
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s must be a DTLS SSL object; type must be 0, SSL3_RT_APPLICATION_DATA or SSL3_RT_HANDSHAKE (peek is only allowed with application data); buf must have room for len bytes and readbytes must be writable when data may be returned. Postcondition: returns 1 with *readbytes set to the number of bytes copied from the current record into buf (the record is consumed by that amount, or released if empty when peeking); returns 0 when len is 0, when the peer has shut down (a received close_notify or fatal alert sets SSL_RECEIVED_SHUTDOWN, the fatal alert also removes the session), or when we already sent shutdown, with the offending record released; returns -1 on error (invalid arguments, record read or release failure, invalid, unknown, too many or no_renegotiation alerts, unexpected records, app data during first handshake, buffering failure), usually after SSLfatal; returns -1 with rwstate SSL_READING and retry flags set on the read BIO when a read must be retried (after a retransmitted Finished or a handshake triggered without SSL_MODE_AUTO_RETRY), or -1 with in_read_app_data set to 2; otherwise returns the handshake_func result when it is <0 (and -1 when it is 0). Stale, buffered, CCS and warning-alert records are consumed internally and reading restarts.

functions.name: ssl3_read_bytes
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ssl is a valid SSL connection, type is 0, SSL3_RT_APPLICATION_DATA or SSL3_RT_HANDSHAKE (and APPLICATION_DATA if peek is set), buf has room for len bytes, and readbytes is writable. Postcondition: returns 1 with *readbytes set to the number of bytes copied (from the stored handshake fragment or from one or more records, which are consumed unless peek is set, and *recvd_type is set when non-NULL); returns 0 for a zero-length read, or when a close_notify or fatal alert was received or the peer had already shut down (SSL_RECEIVED_SHUTDOWN); returns -1 after SSLfatal on protocol errors (bad type, invalid alert, unexpected or early CCS, unexpected record, SSLv2 record, too many warning alerts, release failure), or -1 with a retry flag set (rwstate SSL_READING, or in_read_app_data=2) when a retry is needed; it returns the handshake function's negative result or the record-layer read result if those are <= 0; ignored records (warning alerts, skipped early data, empty records) loop back to read more records.

functions.name: ssl_cipher_get_evp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx and s are valid, and any non-NULL out-pointers (enc, md, mac_pkey_type, mac_secret_size, comp) are writable. Postcondition: returns 0 if s->cipher is NULL; if comp is non-NULL it first sets *comp to the matching SSL_COMP from the compression methods list (NULL if none), and returns 1 at once if enc and md are both NULL. Otherwise it returns 0 if enc or md is NULL, or if fetching the cipher fails, or if fetching the MD/MAC fails (in which case the fetched *enc is freed). It returns 0 if the fetched combination is unusable: *enc is NULL, or *md is NULL and the cipher is not AEAD, or the MAC is not AEAD and mac_pkey_type is non-NULL with *mac_pkey_type == NID_undef. Otherwise it returns 1 with *enc and *md set to fetched objects the caller owns. If use_etm is false and the session version is TLS 1.x, and the cipher/MAC pair is RC4-MD5, AES128/256-SHA1 or AES128/256-SHA256, it tries to fetch the matching combined cipher+HMAC implementation. If that fetch succeeds it frees the original *enc and *md, sets *enc to the combined cipher and *md to NULL.

Postcondition: returns 1 after writing the 2-byte (or as defined by put_cipher_by_char) codes of the non-disabled ciphers from sk, stopping once the written length reaches the limit (0xfffe, or the TLS1.2 cap if defined, minus 2 for each reserved SCSV), then appending the renegotiation SCSV if applicable and the fallback SCSV if SSL_MODE_SEND_FALLBACK_SCSV is set; returns 0 after raising a fatal SSL error if ssl_set_client_disabled fails (SSL_R_NO_PROTOCOLS_AVAILABLE), sk is NULL, any put_cipher_by_char call fails (ERR_R_INTERNAL_ERROR), or no cipher was written or none of the written ciphers covers the maximum version (SSL_R_NO_CIPHERS_AVAILABLE).

functions.name: tls13_change_cipher_state
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s is a valid TLS 1.3 SSL_CONNECTION whose needed secrets, hashes and (for non-early states) s->s3.tmp.new_sym_enc, new_hash and new_mac_pkey_type are already set, and which is a combination of SSL3_CC_* flags (CLIENT/SERVER, READ/WRITE, and EARLY, HANDSHAKE or application). Postcondition: returns 1 if the traffic secret, key and IV for the selected direction and level were derived, logged, and installed in a new record layer via ssl_set_new_record_layer; any failing step (bad handshake buffer length, missing session cipher, digest or HKDF failure, null cipher assertion, logging failure, finished-key derivation, record layer setup) returns 0, mostly with SSLfatal already raised. Side effects: it stores the early exporter, resumption master, exporter master and the client/server application traffic secrets and finished keys into s as applicable, and sets plain-alerts on the write layer, enabled only for a client sending early data. On every exit the key and secret buffers are cleansed, a heap-allocated IV is freed, and for early-data states the cipher (and the MAC digest if the cipher is not AEAD) references taken are released.

functions.name: DEFINE_SET_GET_BASE_TEST(PREFIX, SETN, GETN, DUP, FIELD, TYPE, ERR,
functions.prose_contract: Generated function execute_CTX_<SETN>_<GETN>_<FIELD>(fixture). Precondition: fixture is non-NULL with a valid ctx and the error queue should be empty. Postcondition: it checks that the error queue starts empty, that an exported setter (PREFIX == 1) fails with a queued error on a NULL ctx, that the getter returns ERR with a queued error on a NULL ctx, that the fresh value is the default, that two successive set calls and the following gets behave as expected (match or dup semantics depending on SETN, GETN, DUP), and that the error queue is empty at the end. It frees the values it allocated (and the gotten copies when GETN == 1), and returns TEST_true(res), i.e. 1 if all checks passed and 0 otherwise. It does not free the ctx.

functions.name: test_EVP_DigestSignInit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tst is a test index (values 15 and above select re-initialisation of the signing context and are reduced by 15) and the global nullprov is normally NULL. Postcondition: if nullprov is not NULL it returns the result of TEST_skip without doing anything else; otherwise it returns 1 when every sign step and, for non-HMAC keys, every verify step succeeds (also returning 1 early for the DSA cases when DSA is disabled, and after the short-buffer EVP_DigestSign failure check for tst 9..11), and returns 0 on any failed step; in all non-skip cases all BIOs, contexts, keys, buffers and the fetched digest are freed before returning.

functions.name: mempacket_move_packet
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bio is a mempacket test BIO whose data context holds a packet stack, and d is a valid insertion index (d >= 0 for the stack insert to succeed). Postcondition: returns 0 with no change if d >= s, if the stack has s or fewer packets, or if the packet at s is NULL; returns 0 if the delete does not return that packet, or if the re-insert at d fails (in the insert-failure case the packet has already been removed from the stack and its num already reduced by s-d, so the stack is NOT unchanged); otherwise it moves the packet from index s to index d, reduces its num by (s-d), increments num of each packet now at indices d+1..s, and returns 1.

functions.name: test_hpke_oddcalls
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global library context testctx is set up and the HPKE provider is available; the function takes no arguments. Postcondition: it exercises HPKE APIs with NULL contexts, bad suites, bad modes and bad lengths and expects each to fail, then runs a good keygen, encap, seal, decap and open sequence (with a PSK-mode context lacking a PSK failing and several interspersed failing calls) and checks that the opened plaintext equals the original; it returns 1 only if every expected failure and success happened and the plaintext matched, otherwise 0 at the first unexpected result, and on every path it frees ctx, rctx and the generated private key privp.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds argc valid NUL-terminated strings (argv[0] is the program name), and the test's global option variables are available. Postcondition: it parses the command-line options, builds client and server SSL_CTX objects and SSL objects, runs the requested number of handshakes through the selected BIO type (memory, pair, IPv4 or IPv6), and checks the expected negotiated version and session reuse. Session files and timing output are handled as requested. It returns EXIT_SUCCESS only if all handshakes and checks pass, or if it exits early with success because of -F, a compiled-out protocol, or a PSK key given without PSK support. It returns EXIT_FAILURE for a bad or unknown option, a missing option argument, conflicting protocol options, a setup failure, or a handshake or check failure. On every exit path it frees the SSL objects, SSL_CTXs, SSL_CONF contexts, the conf_args stack, the stdout BIO, the sessions, the providers and the library context, and it closes the test streams.

functions.name: test_tls13_record_padding
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: idx is the test index; 0-5 select a padding configuration (0: client-context padding callback, 1: client-connection padding callback, 2: context block padding, 3: connection block padding, 4: context block padding for handshake only, 5: connection handshake-only padding on client and server), and other values run with no padding configuration; the global libctx, cert and privkey are set up. Postcondition: returns 1 if the TLS 1.3 context pair and connection are created, the padding setters behave as expected (oversized block sizes are rejected), four write/read round trips of "Hello World" from client to server succeed with matching data, and for idx 0 or 1 the padding callback was called exactly 4 times; returns 0 on any failed check; in every case the server and client SSL objects and both SSL_CTX objects are freed.
