functions.name: _wrap_SBCompileUnit_FindLineEntryIndex
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: L is a valid Lua state whose stack holds the arguments of a call to SBCompileUnit.FindLineEntryIndex. Postcondition: with 2 arguments (SBCompileUnit pointer, non-null SBLineEntry userdata) it returns the result of the _SWIG_1 wrapper; with 3 arguments (SBCompileUnit pointer, non-null SBLineEntry, boolean) it returns the result of _SWIG_0; with 4 arguments (SBCompileUnit pointer, number, number, SBFileSpec pointer) it returns the result of _SWIG_2; with 5 arguments (the same plus a boolean) it returns the result of _SWIG_3. In each case the value returned is the number of Lua results pushed. If no overload matches, it pushes a 'Wrong arguments for overloaded function' error string listing the four prototypes and calls lua_error, which does not return normally; the trailing return 0 is not reached in practice.

functions.name: _wrap_SBFrame_EvaluateExpression
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: L is a valid Lua state whose stack holds the call arguments (SBFrame pointer, expression string or nil, and optionally a number, a boolean or an SBExpressionOptions userdata). Postcondition: it dispatches on argument count and types: 2 args (frame, string/nil) call overload _0; 3 args with an SBExpressionOptions userdata third call _3; 3 args with a numeric third call _1; 4 args (frame, string/nil, number, boolean) call overload _2; in each case it returns that wrapper's result count. If no overload matches it pushes a 'Wrong arguments for overloaded function' error string and calls lua_error, which does not return normally (the trailing return 0 is not reached in practice).

functions.name: gpart_issue
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: req is a valid gctl request whose "nargs" parameter is an integer. Postcondition: never returns; if nargs != 1 it calls errx(EXIT_FAILURE) before freeing req. Otherwise it deletes "nargs" and autofills parameters; on autofill failure it warns and exits EXIT_FAILURE. Else it adds a 4096-byte writable ASCII "output" parameter and issues the request; if the result is NULL or empty it prints any non-empty output buffer and exits EXIT_SUCCESS, otherwise it prints the error via gpart_print_error and exits EXIT_FAILURE. On the autofill-failure, success and error paths req is freed with gctl_free before exit.

functions.name: fts_build
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp is a valid FTS handle whose fts_cur points to the current directory node, and type is BREAD, BNAMES or BCHILD. Postcondition: it returns the head of a newly allocated list of child FTSENT nodes in directory order (sorted by fts_compar if set and more than one item), or NULL. It returns NULL, with no list, when: (1) the directory cannot be opened, in which case for BREAD it sets cur->fts_info=FTS_DNR and cur->fts_errno=errno; (2) allocating a node or growing the path fails, in which case it frees the partial list and the node, closes the directory, sets cur->fts_info=FTS_ERR, sets FTS_STOP and restores errno; (3) the directory was empty or had only skipped entries, in which case for BREAD, if cur->fts_info is neither FTS_DNR nor FTS_ERR, it is set to FTS_DP; (4) the chdir back (when it descended and type is BCHILD or nothing was found) fails, in which case it frees the list, sets cur->fts_info=FTS_ERR and sets FTS_STOP. The directory stream is always closed after reading. A readdir error sets cur->fts_errno and sets cur->fts_info to FTS_ERR if items were read, else FTS_DNR. A failed chdir into the directory sets FTS_DONTCHDIR on cur and marks entries FTS_NS (or FTS_NSOK if no stat needed). With FTS_NOCHDIR the path is reset to cur's original path, and it may realloc the path and adjust the node pointers. The caller owns the returned list.

functions.name: _FUNCNAME
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: nptr points to a NUL-terminated string, endptr is NULL or points to writable storage, and base is 0 or in [2,36]; in kernel/standalone builds an invalid base panics, in userspace builds it sets errno=EINVAL, stores nptr in *endptr (if endptr is non-NULL) and returns 0. Postcondition: it skips leading whitespace, accepts an optional sign and, for base 0/16 a 0x prefix (followed by a hex digit) or for base 0/2 a 0b prefix (followed by a binary digit), then returns the accumulated value of the digits valid in the base. On overflow it returns __INT_MAX (positive) or __INT_MIN (negative); in userspace it keeps consuming digits and sets errno=ERANGE, while in kernel/standalone it stops at the overflowing digit and sets *endptr to nptr (since any=0). If no digits were consumed it returns 0 and *endptr (if non-NULL) is set to nptr; otherwise *endptr points just past the last consumed digit. Nothing is allocated or locked, and errno is only written for EINVAL and ERANGE in userspace.

functions.name: _CITRUS_PROP_READ_UINT_COMMON(num, uint64_t, UINT64_MAX)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function _citrus_prop_read_num_common(ms, result, base, neg). Precondition: ms is a valid memstream, result is writable, base is in 2..16 and neg is 0 or 1. Postcondition: reads characters from ms while they are valid digits in the given base and the accumulated uint64_t value would not exceed UINT64_MAX, then pushes back the first unconsumed character (the one read last), stores the accumulated value (negated modulo 2^64 if neg is nonzero) in *result and always returns 0.

functions.name: comp_dst
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 and arg2 point to valid struct ai_order entries whose aio_ai and its ai_addr pointers are valid and whose source/destination scope, policy, flag, matchlen and initial-sequence fields are initialised. Postcondition: returns -1 if the first destination sorts before the second and 1 if it sorts after, applying RFC 3484 rules 1-3 and 5-6 (rule 5 and 6 only when INET6 is defined), then rule 8 (smaller destination scope), rule 9 (longer matching prefix, only for equal non-AF_INET families), and finally the original sequence, returning 1 if dst2's initial sequence is smaller than dst1's and -1 otherwise. It never returns 0, modifies nothing, and holds no locks or references.

functions.name: getifaddrs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pif is a valid pointer to a struct ifaddrs pointer. Postcondition: returns -1 (leaving *pif untouched) if a sysctl fails (a failed second sysctl is retried only on ENOMEM, up to MAX_SYSCTL_TRY times), or if malloc fails; otherwise returns 0 after freeing the temporary sysctl buffer, and sets *pif to NULL when the routing data yields no interfaces or addresses, or else to a single malloc'd block holding a NULL-terminated linked list of ifaddrs entries (with names, addresses and data stored in the same block) which the caller releases with freeifaddrs. It calls abort() if an RTM_NEWADDR message's index differs from the preceding interface's index.

functions.name: _ht_getnetbyaddr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ap supplies, in order, a uint32_t net, an int type, a struct netent *result, a char *buffer, a size_t buflen, an int *errnop and an int *h_errnop (both writable), and rval points to writable storage for a struct netent *. Postcondition: if the per-thread netent data cannot be initialized, it sets h_errno to NETDB_INTERNAL, stores it in *h_errnop and returns NS_UNAVAIL. Otherwise it rewinds the hosts-style networks file, scans entries for one whose address type equals type and whose network number equals net, and closes the file if stayopen is not set. If no entry matches it stores the resolver h_errno in *h_errnop and returns NS_NOTFOUND. If a match is found but copying it into nptr/buffer fails, it sets *errnop to errno, sets h_errno to NETDB_INTERNAL, stores it in *h_errnop and returns NS_RETURN. Otherwise it sets *(struct netent **)rval = nptr and returns NS_SUCCESS.

functions.name: link_ntoa_r
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sdl and buflen are non-NULL; obuf may be NULL, and if non-NULL it points to a writable buffer of at least *buflen bytes. Postcondition: the text form of the link-layer address (the interface name of at most IFNAMSIZ bytes, a ':' if the address is non-empty, then the address bytes as lowercase hex separated by '.') is written to obuf as far as it fits while leaving room for the trailing NUL, and obuf is NUL-terminated when obuf is non-NULL and the initial *buflen is nonzero; *buflen is set to the full length needed including the NUL (saturating at SIZE_MAX), and the function returns 0 if the whole string fit (the buffer was non-NULL and never ran out of room), otherwise -1.

functions.name: load_msgcat
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path and name are non-NULL valid strings, lang is NULL or a valid string. Postcondition: if the cache already holds an entry with the same path (found under the read lock), its refcount is incremented and its catd is returned; otherwise the file is opened, mapped read-only, checked for size, the NLS magic and a valid header, and a new refcount-1 cache entry with copied name, path and lang is inserted at the head of the cache and its new catd is returned; on any failure (open/fstat/mmap errno, ENOENT for a too-small or oversized file or bad magic, EINVAL for an invalid header, ENOMEM for allocation failure or failure to take the write lock) the file descriptor, mapping and any allocations are released and the error is returned via NLRETERR, with SAVEFAIL recorded for every failure except the write-lock failure and the initial cache-lock failure.

functions.name: _nfs4_acl_to_text_np
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: aclp points to a valid acl_t whose entries can be iterated with acl_get_entry, and flags is acceptable to format_entry. Postcondition: if the ACL has zero entries it returns strdup("") (NULL if allocation fails) and leaves *len_p untouched; otherwise it mallocs a buffer of acl_cnt*MAX_ENTRY_LENGTH bytes and returns NULL if that fails; if format_entry fails for any entry it frees the buffer, sets errno to EINVAL and returns NULL; on success it returns the malloc'd NUL-terminated text of all entries, which the caller must free, and if len_p is non-NULL sets *len_p to the string length (excluding the NUL).

functions.name: __rpc_get_time_offset
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td points to a writable struct timeval, uaddr points to a char* that is either NULL or a valid universal-address string, netid is used only when uaddr is NULL and srv is NULL, and at most one of srv and thost may be non-NULL when *uaddr is NULL. Postcondition: td is first zeroed; returns 1 if the remote time was obtained (via an RPCB_GETTIME call, or else via the port-37 time service over TCP or UDP), in which case td->tv_sec holds the signed difference between the remote and local time rounded to the second, td->tv_usec is 0, and if *uaddr was NULL it is set to a strdup'd copy of the address used (caller owns it); returns 0 with td left zeroed when both srv and thost are given with *uaddr NULL, server data cannot be built, no TCP or UDP endpoint exists, the uaddr cannot be converted to a sockaddr, the rpcbind client handle cannot be created, or the time cannot be fetched. The function closes its socket, destroys its client handle, cancels the alarm and restores the old SIGALRM handler, and frees the temporary endpoints it allocated.

functions.name: _get_next_token
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: npp is a valid NUL-terminated writable string. Postcondition: returns NULL if token does not occur in npp (string unchanged); otherwise, if the first token occurrence is preceded by a single escaping backslash (cp > npp+1, cp[-2] != '\\'), it removes that backslash by shifting the rest down and returns the result of recursing on the remainder from cp; else it overwrites the found token char with NUL, strips backslash escapes from the leading part in place (a doubled backslash becomes one, a single backslash is deleted), and returns a pointer to the character after the token, the rest of the string.

functions.name: _fseeko
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid open stdio stream, whence is SEEK_SET, SEEK_CUR or SEEK_END, and ltest is nonzero if the resulting position must fit in a long. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, with the stream positioned at the new offset (via the buffer-adjusting fast paths or the flush-and-seek 'dumb' path), the EOF flag cleared, any ungetc data discarded and the multibyte state reset; returns -1 with errno set to ESPIPE if the stream has no seek function, EINVAL for a bad whence or negative resulting offset, or EOVERFLOW for offset overflow or (when ltest) a position beyond LONG_MAX; in the dumb path it also returns -1 if __sflush or _sseek fails (errno set by them), and on a result above LONG_MAX with ltest it sets __SERR and errno=EOVERFLOW, but __SERR is not set for the other failures listed here.

functions.name: __vfprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid FILE stream, fmt0 is a NUL-terminated format string, ap matches the conversions in it, and serrno is the errno value used by %m. Postcondition: if __use_xprintf > 0 it returns __xvprintf(fp, fmt0, ap); if the stream cannot be prepared for writing it sets errno to EBADF and returns EOF without touching the argument list; otherwise it formats the output to fp and returns the number of bytes written, or EOF if the output count would exceed INT_MAX (errno = EOVERFLOW, also for an INT_MIN '*' width or a width/precision overflowing int), if __find_arguments fails, if a multibyte or wide-string conversion fails (__SERR set on the stream), if an I/O step fails, or if the stream's error flag is set at exit; on every path after setup it calls va_end on the copied list and frees dtoaresult, convbuf and any heap-allocated argtable. On non-error exit it restores the saved __SERR flag into fp->_flags.

functions.name: __vfprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a writable stream, fmt0 points to a NUL-terminated format string, and the variable arguments match the conversions it requests. Postcondition: the formatted output is written to the stream and the number of characters output is returned on success; on failure it returns EOF, with errno set to EOVERFLOW when a width, precision, or `*` width of INT_MIN cannot be honoured, and with the stream error flag set (__SERR) when a wide-character conversion fails; it also returns EOF if argument scanning for `n$` fails. The dispatcher frees any dtoa result and conversion buffer it allocated on the way out.

functions.name: __svfscanf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a readable FILE, locale is a valid locale, fmt0 is a NUL-terminated format string, and ap is a va_list whose arguments match the format's conversions (pointers of the types the flags select, unless assignment is suppressed with '*'). Postcondition: it parses fmt0 against input from fp, storing converted values through the va_list pointers and advancing the stream; it returns the number of assigned fields when the format ends normally (NUL at top level) or on a match failure (literal mismatch, unknown conversion, bad %w width, empty %[ class or empty numeric/float field); it returns nassigned on input failure (EOF/read error) if at least one conversion completed, otherwise EOF; it returns EOF if the format ends with NUL right after a '%' and its flags or width; the caller keeps ownership of fp and ap, and ap is consumed.

functions.name: __vfwprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid stream, fmt0 is a NUL-terminated wide format string, and ap supplies arguments matching the conversions in fmt0. Postcondition: if the stream cannot be prepared for writing, it sets errno to EBADF and returns EOF without touching the stream flags; otherwise it formats the output to fp and returns the number of wide characters written. It returns EOF instead (errno EOVERFLOW if the count, a width or a precision would exceed INT_MAX or width is INT_MIN; the argument-table failure from __find_warguments returns EOF without setting errno here; a failed multibyte conversion for %s sets the stream error flag), or if an output call fails, or if the stream error flag is set at exit. On exit it frees any conversion buffer and any heap-allocated argument table and calls va_end on the copied argument list. If no stream error is set, the saved previous error flag is restored.

functions.name: __vfwprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid FILE stream, locale is a valid locale, fmt0 is a NUL-terminated wide format string, and ap supplies arguments matching its conversions. Postcondition: if the stream cannot be written (prepwrite fails) it sets errno to EBADF and returns EOF without output; otherwise it formats the output to fp and returns the number of wide characters written, or EOF if the stream has an error, if the output count, a width or a precision would exceed INT_MAX (errno EOVERFLOW), if a '*' width is INT_MIN (errno EOVERFLOW), if positional-argument table building fails, or if a multibyte-to-wide conversion for %s fails (which also sets __SERR on fp); on exit it frees any internal conversion buffer and a heap-allocated argument table, ends the copied va_list, and on non-error restores the previously saved __SERR flag. %n stores the running count through the argument pointer.

functions.name: __printf_render_float
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: io is a valid output sink, pi describes a floating-point conversion (spec among a, A, e, E, f, F, g, G; other specs hit an assert on spec=='f' and then are treated as an f conversion), and arg[0] points to a double (or a long double if pi->is_long_double). Postcondition: formats the value into io with the requested sign, 0x/0X prefix for a/A, padding, zero fill, digit grouping (if the alt flag is set and the locale supplies grouping), decimal point and exponent, or prints inf/nan (INF/NAN for uppercase specs), then flushes io, frees the dtoa buffer if one was allocated, and returns the sum of the values returned by the __printf_pad and __printf_puts calls (the number of characters emitted); there is no error return.

functions.name: __ssp_real(recvfrom)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none enforced by this wrapper; for the call to succeed, s must be an open socket descriptor, buf must be writable for len bytes, and from and fromlen must each be NULL or point to writable storage. Postcondition: it forwards all arguments unchanged through the interposing table (INTERPOS_SYS) to the recvfrom system call and returns its result, which is the number of bytes received, or -1 with errno set on failure.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(dbm_open_missing_test, tc)

Precondition: tc is the ATF test case context supplied by the ATF framework, and the database file "tmp.db" does not yet exist. Postcondition: the test checks that dbm_open("tmp", O_RDONLY, 0755) returns NULL and does not create tmp.db (ATF_REQUIRE, aborts the test otherwise), that dbm_open with O_RDONLY|O_CREAT returns non-NULL and creates tmp.db (ATF_REQUIRE), and that dbm_open with O_RDONLY|O_CREAT|O_EXCL on the now existing file returns NULL; ATF_CHECK failures are recorded and the test continues, and nothing is returned. The returned DBM handle from the successful open is never closed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fts_blocks_test, tc)

Postcondition: it creates directories bar and foo with three files each, opens an FTS stream over them with a block comparator that sorts names in reverse order, and checks that fts_read yields the names z y x foo c b a bar in that order and then NULL. It then closes the stream. A failed ATF_REQUIRE (mkdir, creat, close, fts_open_b, fts_close) aborts the test; ATF_CHECK failures are recorded but the test continues. It returns nothing and leaves the created files and directories in place.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(opendir_fifo, tc)

Postcondition: creates a FIFO 'fifo' (mode 0644) and closes the descriptor that mkfifo's return value is assigned to, requires opendir("fifo") to return NULL, and checks that errno is ENOTDIR; a failed REQUIRE aborts the test.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(sig2str_heap_after_end, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called by the ATF framework as the body of test case sig2str_heap_after_end, with the test case pointer tc, on a system where fork() works. Postcondition: the test forks a child that disables core dumps, mallocs a buffer of SIG2STR_MAX - 1 bytes (one byte too small) and calls sig2str(1, buf), then exits with EX_SOFTWARE if that returns. The parent waits for the child, retrying on EINTR, and fails the test if the fork fails (ATF_REQUIRE). The parent fails the test with a message if the child exits normally (EX_SOFTWARE: FORTIFY_SOURCE failed to abort; EX_OSERR: setrlimit failed; any other status: unexpected exit status). If the child was killed by a signal, the parent requires it to be SIGABRT. The function returns nothing, and the child's malloc'd buffer is never freed.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(getpeername_heap_after_end, tc)

Postcondition: the child allocates a one-sockaddr heap buffer, creates a socket pair and calls getpeername with a length one byte larger than the buffer, then exits EX_SOFTWARE if it was not aborted; the parent waits for the child (retrying on EINTR) and fails the test if the child exited normally (EX_SOFTWARE: no abort, EX_OSERR: setrlimit failed, any other status), and requires that a signalled child died with SIGABRT. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(getsockname_before_end, tc)

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(getsockname_end, tc)

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fgets_heap_after_end, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as an ATF test body, where fork, malloc, new_fp, and fgets are available. Postcondition: it forks a child that disables coredumps, mallocs 42 bytes, creates a FILE with new_fp(43), and calls fgets with length 43, which FORTIFY_SOURCE should abort. If fork fails the test requirement fails and nothing else runs. The parent waits for the child, retrying on EINTR, and records a test failure if the child exits normally (EX_SOFTWARE: no abort; EX_OSERR: setrlimit failed; any other status). A child killed by a signal must have received SIGABRT, otherwise the requirement fails. The body returns nothing. The child buffer is never freed, but the child ends by _exit or abort.

If fork fails the test requirement fails and nothing else runs. The parent waits for the child, retrying on EINTR, and records a test failure if the child exits normally (EX_SOFTWARE: no abort; EX_OSERR: setrlimit failed; any other status). functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(strcpy_heap_after_end, tc)

Postcondition: forks a child (requiring fork success); the child disables coredumps, mallocs 42 bytes, and strcpy()s a 43-byte string (42 'A's plus NUL) into it, expecting FORTIFY_SOURCE to abort, else it _exit(EX_SOFTWARE); the parent waits for the child (requiring errno EINTR on retried waits) and fails the test if the child exited normally (with EX_SOFTWARE, EX_OSERR or another status), and requires SIGABRT if it was killed by a signal; returns nothing.

If both enabled (first byte '1') and disabled (first byte '1') are true, res is set to INVALID and RES_FAIL is returned. Postcondition: it never returns; it exits with status 1 if ttyname fails, the tty cannot be opened, modem init or answer chat fails, tcsetattr fails, the login timeout fires, an auto-login name is invalid, or exec of login/ppplogin fails; it exits with status 0 if the answer-wait select times out (recycle for init) or reading stdin hits EOF/error in getname; on a valid login name or PPP request it execs login or ppplogin with the CPU limit lifted; otherwise (autobaud, port selector, empty or '-' name, invalid name without auto-login, or interrupted/failed name read) it loops again, switching to the NX gettytab entry when set.

functions.name: set_flags
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: omode and the capability values (NP, AP, EP, OP, HC, MB, HW, NL, HT, RW, CE, CK, PE, EC, XC, DX and the C0/I0/L0/O0, C1/I1/L1/O1, C2/I2/L2/O2 values with their 'set' flags) have been initialised; n selects the mode (0, 1, or anything else for the default). Postcondition: returns nothing; if all four preset flag values for the selected mode (n==0 uses 0, n==1 uses 1, any other n uses 2) are set, tmode's c_cflag, c_iflag, c_lflag and c_oflag are copied from them and the function returns at once. Otherwise the flags are derived from omode: parity/char size, HUPCL, MDMBUF, CRTSCTS, ICRNL/ONLCR/OPOST and OXTABS are adjusted. For n==1 the result is raw 8-bit mode if RW (iflag=0, lflag=0, OPOST cleared, CS8, no parity) or else ICANON is cleared. For n==0 nothing more is changed. For other n the echo flags ECHOE, ECHOKE, ECHOPRT, ECHO, ECHOCTL and IXANY are also set or cleared. The four results are stored into tmode; omode is not modified.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv[1] is the server name and argv[2..argc-1] are the paths to fetch (argc >= 2, otherwise usage() is called and the program exits); the environment and network are used to look up and connect to the server. Postcondition: for each path it sends an HTTP request and reads the response, writing the body to a file named after the last path component when the status is 200 (ignoring other statuses, and skipping the body for 204/304), reconnecting and reissuing requests if a connection dies after the first request on it; on success it frees resbuf and the address list res0 and returns 0, while fatal errors (malloc, lookup, connect, open, bad file name, a failure on the first request of a connection, fcntl failure) terminate the process via err/errx with exit status 1.

functions.name: _rtld
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp points to the initial process stack (argc, argv, NULL, envp, NULL, auxv ending in AT_NULL) with AT_BASE present in the auxv, and exit_proc and objp are valid writable pointers; the function runs before rtld itself is relocated. Postcondition: on success it stores the rtld exit procedure in *exit_proc and the main object in *objp, and returns the main program's entry point after loading and relocating the main program, preloads and needed objects, setting up initial TLS, running init functions and enforcing relro, with rtld_bind_lock released; in direct exec mode it also shifts argv, envp and auxv left over the interpreter arguments, decrements argc on the stack, and sets the kernel osrel through sysctl. Any fatal error (tainted process in direct exec, missing binary, fstat failure, no execute permission, map, digest, preload, needed-object, version, relocation or relro failure) calls rtld_die() and does not return. With LD_TRACE_LOADED_OBJECTS set it traces the loaded objects and calls exit(0), and with LD_DUMP_REL_PRE or LD_DUMP_REL_POST it dumps relocations and calls exit(0), so it does not return normally in those cases.

functions.name: rrq_window_rfc7440
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test fixture has a running tftpd and a client socket, and the current directory is writable. Postcondition: the test creates rfc7440.txt holding 13*512-4 bytes of sequential uint32_t values, sends an RRQ with windowsize 4 and receives the matching OACK. It then ACKs 0 and receives blocks 1-4, ACKs 4 and receives blocks 5-8. It ACKs 5 as if 6-8 were lost and receives blocks 6-9, ACKs 9 and receives blocks 10-13 (13 is 508 bytes). It then receives blocks 10-13 again as retransmission after the dropped ACK and finally ACKs 13. The function returns nothing; ATF assertions fail the test if open fails or any received packet differs from what is expected.

functions.name: tftp_receive
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: peer is an open socket, block points to a valid uint16_t holding the last acknowledged block number, ts points to a writable tftp_stats, and firstblock is either NULL or points to a received first DATA packet whose payload has fb_size bytes. Postcondition: sets ts->amount to 0 and then accumulates the bytes written, updates ts->blocks, ts->retries, ts->rollovers and ts->tstop, and advances *block (wrapping to 0 or the rollover option value). Returns 0 when a short (final) block was received, written, closed and acknowledged (for the server, after also draining late packets and re-acking a repeated last block); returns -1 when ACK sending or packet receiving exhausts maxtimeouts, when receive_packet fails with a non-timeout error or an ERROR packet, or when write_file returns <= 0 (an error packet is sent to the peer in that case). On the first-block path an unsuccessful write_file result is not checked. The caller loses no resources and holds no locks.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the options -i or -a (optionally -s), exactly one of -i/-a given, and the process can use the machdep sysctls, gettimeofday, settimeofday, and the clock file check. Postcondition: on a usage error it calls usage() and exits with status 2; it returns 0 immediately if the clock file _PATH_CLOCK does not exist, or if -i was given without sleep mode and the clock is not a wall clock; it returns 1 if daemon(), a sysctl get or set, gettimeofday, settimeofday, or a non-sleep-mode mktime failure (nonexistent local time) fails; in sleep mode a mktime failure logs a warning, sleeps REPORT_PERIOD seconds and restarts; on success it sets the kernel time, timezone, machdep.adjkerntz and machdep.wall_cmos_clock, restores machdep.disable_rtc_set if it changed it, and returns 0, except that in init mode with a wall clock it suspends for a signal and then restarts the whole procedure without returning.

functions.name: scsiattrib
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: device is an opened CAM device, argv/argc and combinedopt are valid getopt arguments, and the remaining parameters are the task attribute, retry count, timeout (0 means 60000), verbose flag and error-recovery flag. Postcondition: allocates a CCB and a 65534-byte buffer, parses the options (-a -c -e -F -p -r -s -T -w -V), sends a READ ATTRIBUTE command when -r was given and prints the attribute values, the attribute list, or the partition/logical volume list to stdout according to the service action; returns 0 on success (including the cases where the reply is too short and a 'No ...' message is printed, and when write_attr is 0 and no read is done after a successful send) and returns 1 on any error (CCB or buffer allocation failure, bad option argument, -w given, neither -r nor -w specified, cam_send_ccb failure, CCB status not CAM_REQ_CMP, sbuf allocation failure, or attribute formatting failure); on every path the CCB (if allocated) is freed with cam_freeccb and the data buffer is freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds argc valid NUL-terminated strings; argv[1], if present, should name a camcontrol subcommand. Postcondition: never returns; it calls exit(1) after printing usage if argc < 2, or if argv[1] is ambiguous or unknown; it calls errx(1, ...) on a bad numeric device spec, a failed device lookup, a negative retry count or timeout, an invalid queue option, a missing device identifier, or a failed device open. Otherwise it dispatches to the subcommand handler and closes any opened cam_dev, then calls exit(error), where error is the handler's return value (0 for modepage and CAM_CMD_USAGE, which do not set it; 1 for an unrecognized command after usage(0)).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the usual program arguments, with argv[1] naming a camcontrol subcommand. Postcondition: the function never returns. It calls exit(1) after printing usage if argc < 2 or if the subcommand is ambiguous or not found, and it calls errx(1, ...) on a bad numeric device spec, an unresolvable device name, a negative retry count or timeout, an invalid or ambiguous -Q value, a missing device identifier, or a failure to open the device. Otherwise it parses the generic options, opens a passthrough device unless the command is rescan, reset, devtree, usage or debug, and runs the handler for the subcommand, with error set to the handler's return value. The modepage, usage(1) and CAM_CMD_NONE cases leave error unchanged at 0. An unknown subcommand prints usage(0) and sets error to 1. It then closes the device if one was opened and calls exit(error).

functions.name: ratecontrol
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: device is an open CAM device and argc/argv/combinedopt are a valid getopt option set for the ratecontrol subcommand. Postcondition: it allocates a CCB itself (returning 1 if allocation fails), parses the options, queries path inquiry and transport settings, optionally applies requested settings, optionally sends a Test Unit Ready, and optionally prints the new parameters. It always frees the CCB before returning, except in the allocation-failure case where there is none. It returns 1 for a bad option argument, an HBA that lacks a requested capability, an invalid rate or bus width, or a failed CCB send or status. It returns nonzero from get_cpi, get_print_cts or testunitready when those fail, and otherwise returns 0, or the result of the final get_print_cts call when it runs. If no setting was actually changed it skips the set step and returns the current retval.

functions.name: mmcsdcmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: device is an open CAM device and argc/argv/combinedopt are a getopt-parsable option set (options 4,1,S,I,F,c,a,f,l,W,b). Postcondition: returns 1 if the CCB cannot be allocated (nothing else is done), or 1 after freeing the CCB if an opcode, argument, flags or data-length option is invalid (negative, or non-positive for length). If a bus-width (4/1), frequency or speed option is given, it sends a set-transport-settings CCB, prints the result, frees the CCB and returns the cam_send_ccb return value (negative on send failure, otherwise non-negative even if the CCB status was not CAM_REQ_CMP). If the info option is given, it sends a get-transport-settings CCB and prints the host settings, returning 0; on a send or status failure it returns cam_send_ccb's value without freeing the CCB (a leak). Otherwise it builds and sends the MMC command, allocating and zeroing a data buffer when a length was given (malloc result is not checked), prints errors or the response, frees the CCB and the buffer, and returns 0 even when the command failed.

functions.name: epc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: device is a valid open CAM device, argc/argv/combinedopt describe the getopt option set for the epc subcommand, and retry_count and timeout are valid CAM parameters. Postcondition: allocates a CCB, parses the options, requires an action and an ATA or SATL device (calls errx and exits if the device type cannot be determined), checks that the options needed for the action were given, and runs the status, list or set-features helper; returns 0 on success, 1 on allocation failure, an invalid option value, a missing action, an unsupported device type, a missing required option or an unimplemented action, or otherwise the helper's return value; the CCB is freed on every return path where it was allocated.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the usual program arguments, with argv[0] the program name and the options and one device or interface operand following. Postcondition: main never returns normally; it calls exit(EX_OK) after listing dump devices when -l is given, or after successfully issuing the DIOCSKERNELDUMP ioctl (retrying without compression on EINVAL when -z or -Z was given, and listing devices afterwards if -v). On bad usage (unknown option, an operand count other than one, -z with -Z, -i with -r, a bad -i index or cipher, mismatched server and client options) it calls usage() or errx(EX_USAGE). Other failures exit nonzero: EX_UNAVAILABLE for crypto or public key problems, EX_NOHOST or EX_OSERR for address lookup failure, and EX_OSERR for ioctl failure, including a specific message for ENODEV on netdump. Failure to clear the netdump configuration when disabling exits with status 1. Before exiting the function zeroes the dump argument structure, zeroes and frees the encrypted key buffer, and may open and close the netdump device.

functions.name: checkfilesys
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: filesys names a filesystem device or mount point and the fsck globals (preen, bkgrdflag, bkgrdcheck, ckclean, skipclean, yflag, nflag, debug, etc.) have been set by the caller. Postcondition: it opens and reads the superblock and checks the filesystem. It may call exit() directly with 0, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7 or EEXIT in the -F background-check, gjournal fast-check, journal-recovery and failed background-setup paths. It returns 0 when the filesystem is already clean (setup returned -1 or background setup reported clean). It returns EEXIT when setup fails. Otherwise it runs passes 1-5, prints statistics, and calls ckfini(resolved), which closes the filesystem. It then returns ERESTART if a rerun is needed and a restart is permitted (wantrestart, fewer than 10 restarts, and preen or the user answers RESTART). Otherwise, if chkdoreload reports a reload was needed, it returns 0 when the filesystem was not modified, else it syncs and returns 4. In all remaining cases it returns ERERUN if rerun is set, else 0.

functions.name: checklost
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fat is a valid FAT descriptor whose directories have all been traversed, so the remaining chain heads in its head bitmap are lost chains, and its boot block is readable and writable. Postcondition: each lost chain is checked; a chain of positive length that is not in error is reported and reconnected via reconnect(), and its return flags are ORed into the result. The scan stops early if the accumulated flags include FSFATAL. A chain whose check or reconnect result is FSERROR is cleared, with FSFATMOD set, if the user confirms "Clear". After finishlf(), if the boot block has an FSInfo block, an FSFree that is not 0xffffffff and differs from NumFree is, on confirmation, set to NumFree. An FSNext that is not 0xffffffff and is out of range, or not free when NumFree is nonzero, is, on confirmation, replaced by the first free cluster found from CLUST_FIRST. If either field was changed, the FSInfo block is written with writefsinfo() and its result is ORed into the flags. Returns the accumulated modification flags (FSOK if nothing was done).

functions.name: dbg_dump_ufs2_ino
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sb points to a readable superblock and ino to a readable UFS2 inode; dbg_log may be NULL. Postcondition: if dbg_log is NULL it returns immediately and prints nothing; otherwise it writes to dbg_log a start banner, a header line with indent, the inode address and comment, increments the global indent, prints the inode fields (mode, nlink, uid, gid, blksize, size, blocks, the four times and nanosecond fields, gen, kernflags, flags, extsize), prints di_db[i] for i < MIN(UFS_NDADDR, howmany(di_size, fs_bsize)), then prints di_ib[0], di_ib[1] and di_ib[2] only while the running count of remaining blocks (blocks minus UFS_NDADDR, minus one indirect-block capacity howmany(fs_bsize, sizeof(ufs2_daddr_t)) per level, the last subtracting its square) stays positive, then decrements indent and prints the end banner; it returns nothing and modifies no inode or superblock data.

functions.name: main_loop
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global cfg points to a valid configuration whose control connection is open, every non-NULL listen connection and resource event connection holds a valid descriptor, every resource with a non-NULL hr_event has a non-NULL hr_conn exactly when its role is HAST_ROLE_PRIMARY, and the highest descriptor fits in FD_SETSIZE; pfh is the pidfile handle (possibly NULL). Postcondition: the function never returns; each iteration checks signals, calls select(2) on the control, listen, worker-event and primary-connection descriptors with a REPORT_INTERVAL timeout, and calls hook_check at most once per iteration when REPORT_INTERVAL seconds have passed since the last check. On timeout or EINTR it starts the next iteration. On any other select failure it removes the pidfile (preserving errno) and exits the process via pjdlog_exit with EX_OSERR. Otherwise it checks signals again and services ready descriptors: control_handle for control, listen_accept for listeners, and for each resource event_recv on its event descriptor; if event_recv returns nonzero (worker exited) it closes and clears hr_event and any hr_conn, else for a ready primary connection it calls connection_migrate.

functions.name: Transform
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: buf points to four writable UINT4 words holding the running MD5 state and in points to 16 readable UINT4 words of the input block. Postcondition: the function runs the four MD5 rounds (64 steps) on copies of the state words and the block, then adds the resulting a,b,c,d to buf[0..3] with wraparound; in is not modified and nothing is returned.

functions.name: parseipfexpr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: line is a valid NUL-terminated string and errorptr is either NULL or a writable char * location. Postcondition: the function copies line with strdup and strips whitespace; it requires a non-empty text ending in ';', and parses each ';'-separated 'keyword=args' or 'keyword!=args' operand into a malloc'd int array. On success it frees the temporary copy, sets *errorptr to NULL if errorptr is non-NULL, and returns the heap-allocated oplist (caller must free it) with oplist[0]=asize+2, operands shifted up by one, and oplist[asize+1]=IPF_EXP_END. On any failure (strdup failure, missing final ';', bad '=' position, unknown keyword, too many items, allocation failure, genmask/gethost failure, unknown word, no operands, or getproto/getport failure) it returns NULL, sets *errorptr to the message if errorptr is non-NULL (the getproto/getport failure paths leave error as NULL, so *errorptr is set to NULL there), and frees oplist and temp. The keyword-not-found message is allocated by asprintf and is not freed by this function.

functions.name: printnat
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: np points to a valid, initialized ipnat_t whose in_names string table and offsets (in_ifnames, in_plabel, etc.) are valid, and opts holds option flags such as OPT_DEBUG. Postcondition: a textual description of the NAT rule (map, rdr, bimap, map-block, encap, divert or rewrite form, with interfaces, addresses, ports, protocol, and optional flags such as age, mssclamp, tag, purge) is written to stdout, an 'unknown value for in_redir' message is written to stderr if in_redir is unrecognised, extra debug detail is printed when OPT_DEBUG is set in opts, and nothing is returned; for rules with IPN_NO set in the rdr or map branches it prints the protocol and ";\n" and returns early without the trailing debug output.

functions.name: printstatefield
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sp points to a valid ipstate_t, and for fieldnum -2 the statefields table is terminated by an entry with a NULL w_word. Postcondition: returns nothing; for fieldnum 1..55 except 31 it prints the matching ipstate_t field with PRINTF (pointers and flags in hex, strings, ints, 64-bit packet and byte counters, hostnames and ports converted from network order); for -2 it recursively prints every field with a positive w_value in statefields (indices starting at 1), separated by tabs; for any other value, including 0 and 31, it prints nothing.

functions.name: ipfw_config_pipe
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: av[0] is the command word (skipped), av[1..ac-1] are the remaining arguments starting with a positive decimal pipe/flowset/sched number, and g_co.do_pipe is 1 (pipe), 2 (queue) or 3 (sched). Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it builds a DN_CMD_CONFIG message with the API version and DN_SCH/DN_LINK/DN_FS records (plus a DN_PROFILE record when a profile option is given) according to the mode, parses the options (noerror, plr, queue, buckets, masks, red/gred, ecn, droptail, bw, delay, type, weight, lmax, pri, sched/pipe, profile, burst) into those records, validates delay, queue size and RED parameters, and sends it with do_cmd(IP_DUMMYNET3). It terminates the process via errx on a missing or non-positive number, an unrecognised or misplaced option, or invalid values, and via err(1) if the setsockopt call fails. It returns normally only on success. The buffer allocated with safe_calloc is never freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the command line of mount_nfs: optional flags (including -o option lists), then exactly two operands, the remote spec and the local mountpoint. Postcondition: the function never returns; it exits with status 0 after nmount() succeeds (printing a warning if the mtab update fails for a non-NFSv4 mount), and otherwise exits with status 1 via usage(), err() or errx() on an unknown flag, illegal option value (proto, sec, retrycnt, maxgroups, vers, mountport, -g, -R), mutually exclusive bg and bgnow, an operand count other than 2, an nfscl module that cannot be found or loaded, a getnfsargs failure, a mountpoint that checkpath rejects, or an nmount failure; deprecated flags print a notice, and soft/intr with NFSv4 only warns.

functions.name: mkfs_msdos
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fname names a file or device to open (created and truncated to op->create_size when that is nonzero), dtype is a disk type string or NULL, and op points to a valid msdos_options. Postcondition: returns 0 after validating the options, deriving the BPB (FAT type, sectors per cluster, reserved sectors, FAT size) and, unless no_create is set, writing the boot sector, FSInfo and backup sectors, FATs and root directory area to the file; returns -1 on any failure (conflicting or invalid options, open, ftruncate, fstat, seek, mounted check, geometry lookup, too few clusters, metadata larger than the file system, bootstrap read error, allocation failure, or short write), with a warning printed. In every case the internal buffer is freed and the opened file descriptors are closed. Under MAKEFS, the call exits via errx when create_size is zero.

functions.name: mkfs_msdos
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fname names a device or file the caller may open, dtype is a disk-type string usable by getdiskinfo (it may be NULL), and op points to a valid msdos_options structure (copied locally). Postcondition: returns 0 if the FAT12/16/32 geometry was computed and valid and, unless no_create is set, the boot sector(s), FSInfo and backup sectors, FAT copies and root directory area were all written to the file; returns -1 after printing a warning on any error (conflicting or illegal options, open/ftruncate/fstat/seek/mount-check failures, bad sector size, label or FAT type, too few reserved sectors, too many sectors per FAT, metadata larger than the file system, too few clusters, bootstrap read or seek failure, malloc or sigaction failure, short write). On every path it frees the write buffer and closes the file descriptors it opened (fd and the bootstrap fd1), and it prints the cluster summary and BPB once the geometry is computed.

functions.name: firmware
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: f, argc and argv describe an nvmecontrol firmware command line, and the global option struct opt is filled in by arg_parse. Postcondition: returns void and returns early without doing anything if arg_parse fails. Otherwise it validates the slot and action options (arg_help is called on a bad slot or on no action), opens the controller device (re-opening the namespace's controller device if the nsid is nonzero), and exits with an error via errx if the identify request fails (EX_IOERR), if firmware commands are unsupported, if slot 1 is read-only, if the slot exceeds the controller's slot count, or if activating a slot without valid firmware (all EX_UNAVAILABLE). It reads the image file if one was given, and prompts for confirmation, exiting with EX_DATAERR on 'no'. After a 'yes' it downloads the image if one was given, activates the firmware, and prints the result. It then closes the device and exits with status 0, so it never returns normally after parsing succeeds.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process's command-line arguments (argv NUL-terminated strings, modifiable for the anchor name), and the pf device and netlink are reachable. Postcondition: it parses options and, after validating them (calling usage() or errx(1) and never returning on bad or conflicting options, an empty, reserved or too-long anchor name, a failed open of the pf device, a failed netlink open or a failed allocation), performs the requested show, clear, kill, table, load, enable/disable and debug operations, and never returns normally but terminates by calling exit(exit_val) with 0 or 1; exit_val is 1 if disabling, the table command, showing the running state (non-zero result), loading fingerprints, loading rules or enabling failed. The opened descriptor, the netlink handle and the calloc'd path buffer are not released explicitly.

functions.name: print_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp points to a valid struct pf_osfp_ioctl whose fp_class_nm, fp_version_nm and fp_subtype_nm are NUL-terminated strings. Postcondition: the function rebuilds a static 1024-byte buffer (not reentrant, overwritten on each call) as a colon-separated string: window size (or *, S, T, optionally prefixed with %), ttl, DF flag 0/1, packet size (or *, optionally with %), the TCP option list (or . when there are none; options N, S, T[0], M, W with optional * or %value, comma-separated), class name, version name, subtype name, and finally 'TcpOpts <optcnt> 0x<hex tcpopts>'. Each piece is appended with strlcat, so it is silently truncated if it exceeds the buffer. It always returns a pointer to that static buffer; there are no error returns and the caller gets no ownership.

functions.name: ping6
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the ping6 command line (options followed by an IPv6 target and optional intermediate hops), the process can open raw ICMPv6 sockets, and the program's globals are in their initial state. Postcondition: the function never returns; it parses options, resolves the target, opens and configures the send and receive sockets, drops root privileges, enters capability mode, sends pings and processes replies until interrupted, finished or timed out, prints the summary, frees the packet buffer, and exits with status 0 if any reply was received, 2 if packets were transmitted without a reply and some transmits succeeded, or EX_OSERR otherwise; any usage, resolution or system-call error terminates the process through usage(), err or errx.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the tunefs command line: at least 3 arguments, at least one valid option, and exactly one device name left after option parsing. Postcondition: the function never returns. Bad arguments or a wrong argument count end in usage() or errx(10). An unclean filesystem (without a lone -p) ends in errx(1). Failure to open the disk or to write the superblock ends in errx(11) if disk.d_error is set, otherwise err(12). With -p it prints the superblock via printfs() and exits 0 without changing anything. Otherwise it applies each requested change (volume label, ACLs, maxbpg, avgfilesize, soft-update journaling, gjournal, metadata space, multilabel, minfree, NFSv4 ACLs, soft updates, optimization, avgfpdir, trim) to the in-memory superblock, warning for unchanged or conflicting settings. It then writes the superblock with sbwrite (also to the alternate copies if -A), closes the disk, calls chkdoreload on the mount point, and exits 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the standard process arguments, with argv holding argc valid strings. Postcondition: with argc < 2 or option 'h' it returns veriexec_usage(); option 'i' exits with (state & mask) == 0 after querying the veriexec state; option 'z' sets the veriexec state or debug level via ioctl, prints the debug level or state when relevant, and exits EX_OK; an unknown option prints usage and exits EX_USAGE; the options 'C', 'S', 'v', 'l' (if compiled), 'x' set flags or run checks. A missing device, ioctl failure, bad debug-level argument, trust store init failure, or load failure exits via err/errx with EX_UNAVAILABLE, EX_USAGE, EX_OSFILE or EX_DATAERR respectively. Otherwise it loads each remaining argument as a veriexec file and exits EX_OK. It does not return normally except through the usage return paths.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(snprintf__two_formatters, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called by the ATF framework as the body of test case snprintf__two_formatters with a valid tc. Postcondition: returns nothing; it requires snprintf of "%s, %s!" with "Hello" and "tests" into a 128-byte local buffer to return a value > 0 (otherwise the test is aborted as failed), and records a non-fatal check failure if the buffer is not equal to "Hello, tests!".

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(snprintf__overflow, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called by the ATF framework as the body of test case snprintf__overflow with a valid tc. Postcondition: returns nothing; it calls snprintf into a 10-byte local buffer with "0123456789abcdef" and, if the return value is not 16, calls atf_tc_fail (which ends the test as failed); otherwise it records a non-fatal check failure if the buffer is not "012345678".

functions.name: command_bcache
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv come from the boot loader command interpreter; argv is not used. Postcondition: if argc != 1 it sets command_errmsg to "wrong number of arguments", prints nothing and returns CMD_ERROR; otherwise it prints the cache statistics (total blocks, block size, readahead, unit blocks, cached units, ops, bypasses, hits, misses) to stdout and returns CMD_OK.

functions.name: __elfN(reloc_ptr)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ef points to a valid ELF file descriptor whose rel/relsz and rela/relasz fields describe relocation tables readable via COPYOUT, and p, val and len describe the location to be adjusted. functions.name: scan_tarfile
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pkg is a valid open package whose gzip/tar stream is positioned at pkg->pkg_ofs, and last is either NULL or a tarfile entry of pkg already scanned (the last one in pkg's list when no successor is cached). Postcondition: if the next entry already exists (last->tf_next, or pkg->pkg_first when last is NULL) it is returned unchanged; otherwise the stream is advanced past last's data (via cache_data when the position is still at last's header offset, else by discarding bytes) to the next 512-byte boundary, and header blocks are read, skipping package meta-files whose names start with '+', until a 'ustar' entry is found, which is returned as a newly malloc'd entry with tf_pkg, tf_ofs, tf_size and header set, linked as last->tf_next (or pkg->pkg_first) and stored as pkg->pkg_last; it returns NULL with errno ENOSPC if the aligned offset is before the current position or the header magic is not 'ustar' (end of archive), and NULL on a read, cache_data or malloc failure, in which case any newly allocated entry is freed and nothing is linked.

functions.name: db_disasm
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: loc is the address of a readable x86-64 instruction in kernel memory (the bytes are fetched through get_value_inc), and the decoding tables are valid. For opcodes 0xd8-0xdf the work is delegated to db_disasm_esc, whose returned address is returned after a newline is printed. The function has no error return; unknown opcodes are printed via the bad-instruction entry, and no lock or reference is taken.

functions.name: hammer_time
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called exactly once on the boot CPU, early in amd64 boot, with modulep pointing at the preload metadata and physfree the first free physical address after the loaded kernel and modules; the early page tables and the kernel stack set up by locore must be in place. Before that it has parsed the preload data, loaded microcode, identified the CPU, built the thread0 kstack, per-CPU and dynamic per-CPU areas, loaded the GDT, IDT and TSS, set up fast syscall, fetched the tunables, called getmemsize and init_param2, initialised the console and kdb, the message buffer and the FPU, and set the user segment selectors.

functions.name: cpu_minidumpsys
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: di is a valid dumper device and state supplies a valid msgbuf pointer and dump bitset, with the kernel page tables readable through the direct map. functions.name: vmx_exit_process
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vmx and vcpu are valid, the vCPU is in VMX operation with its VMCS loaded, and vmexit holds the exit reason, qualification and instruction length of the VM exit just taken. Postcondition: the exit is classified and the function returns 1 (handled in the kernel) or 0 (to be processed in userland). It returns 1 early, without advancing RIP, for an MCE during VM-entry, interrupt-window, NMI-window, external-interrupt (including an invalid interrupt info), NMI, machine-check and reflected-exception exits; the reflected exception is injected into the guest. Otherwise, after setting vmexit->exitcode and its fields per exit reason, if the exit was handled it advances vmexit->rip by inst_length, sets inst_length to 0, writes the new RIP to the VMCS and returns 1. If it was not handled and no exitcode was set, the exitcode becomes VM_EXITCODE_VMX with success status and zero instruction type and error, and the function returns 0. If it was not handled and an exitcode was set, that code is kept for userland and the function returns 0. Event-delivery info from the IDT vectoring field is recorded via vm_exit_intinfo, and NMI-blocking state and the VM-entry instruction length are adjusted as needed.

functions.name: vmmdev_machdep_ioctl

Postcondition: the function dispatches on cmd and returns 0 or the errno from the selected handler (for VM_RUN, from vm_run or from a failed copyout or subyte, where a failed subyte gives EFAULT). It returns EINVAL for VM_SET_KERNEMU_DEV or VM_GET_KERNEMU_DEV when gpa lies outside the local APIC, I/O APIC and HPET ranges, and ENOTTY for an unknown cmd. The ISA IRQ commands call the I/O APIC handler only if the first call returned 0 and ioapic_irq != -1. VM_GLA2GPA and VM_GLA2GPA_NOFAULT are asserted to give only 0 or EFAULT. VM_GET_GPA_PMAP, VM_IOAPIC_PINCOUNT and VM_RTC_GETTIME always return 0 and write their results into the data structure. Results of other commands are written back through data. No locks or references are acquired or released here.

functions.name: vmmdev_machdep_ioctl

functions.name: cpu_minidumpsys
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: di is an open dumper device, state supplies a valid dump bitset and msgbuf, and all other CPUs are stopped; the caller is the single running CPU.
