functions.name: systrace_return_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes (descsz > 0 for the copy to be meaningful) and sysnum and ndx are plain integers. Postcondition: if sysnum is one of the listed Linux syscall numbers that carry a description (5-40, 41, 43-59, 61-80, 82-127, 129-212, 214-243, 260-294, 424-439 and 440-441) and ndx is 0 or 1, the string "int" is copied into desc by strlcpy, truncated and NUL-terminated to fit descsz; for every other sysnum (including those that fall through to default, e.g. 42, 60, 81, 128, 213, 442-452) or any other ndx, desc is left unchanged; nothing is returned and no locks or references are taken.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to an array of uint64_t large enough for the syscall's arguments (up to 6 entries), n_args is a writable int pointer, and for a sysnum that has arguments params points to the matching linux_*_args structure for that syscall. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; for a known sysnum it stores each argument in order into uarg[0..n-1] (pointer arguments cast through intptr_t, unsigned types such as uid_t, u_int and uint32_t stored as unsigned values, other integers through the int64_t alias iarg), and sets *n_args to the syscall's argument count (0 for syscalls with no arguments or not traced); for any unknown sysnum it sets *n_args to 0 and writes nothing to uarg. It takes no locks and acquires or releases no references or memory.

functions.name: vm_run
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vcpu points to a valid vcpu of a vm, the vcpu is in the FROZEN state (vcpu_require_state asserts this for the transitions) and the caller can run the guest on it. Postcondition: returns EINVAL without running the guest if the vcpu is not in the vm's active_cpus or is in its suspended_cpus; otherwise it repeatedly enters the guest (saving and restoring FPU state inside a critical section, with state going FROZEN->RUNNING->FROZEN), updates vcpu->nextpc from the exit info, and dispatches the exit to the in-kernel handler. It loops again while the handler returns 0 with retu false. It returns 0 when an exit must be handled by userland (retu true, including unknown exit codes), or returns the nonzero error from vmmops_run or from the exit handler. On return the vcpu is left in the FROZEN state.

functions.name: reset_vm_el2_regs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vcpu points to a valid struct hypctx whose vcpu and hyp pointers are valid and whose pmcr_el0 holds the guest PMCR value. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it sets hcr_el2 (plus HCR_E2H under VHE), hcrx_el2 = 0, mdcr_el2 (including the PMCR_EL0.N field), vmpidr_el2 (from the vcpu id), vpidr_el2, cptr_el2 and tf.tf_spsr; if hyp->feats has HYP_FEAT_FGT it rebuilds hdfgrtr/hdfgwtr, hfgrtr/hfgwtr and hfgitr_el2 from zero by setting the chosen TRAP and NOTRAP bits; if it has HYP_FEAT_FGT2 it zeroes hdfgrtr2, hdfgwtr2, hfgitr2, hfgrtr2 and hfgwtr2; it takes no locks and acquires or frees nothing.

functions.name: adadone
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: periph is a valid CAM periph with an ada_softc, and done_ccb is a completed ATA CCB whose ccb_state type identifies the request kind (buffer I/O, trim, readahead, write cache, log directory, identify directory, supported capabilities, zone info, dump, or other). Postcondition: it returns nothing and dispatches on the CCB type. For BUFFER_IO/TRIM it takes the periph lock, maps the CCB status to a bio error (an ERESTART retry returns early with the lock released and the CCB still in use), releases any frozen devq, updates bio_error/bio_resid/BIO_ERROR, decrements outstanding_cmds and refcount, releases the CCB, reschedules, unlocks and calls biodone on the bio (or on all queued trim bios). For RAHEAD it releases the CCB, sets state WCACHE, schedules and drops the devq freeze (an ERESTART retry only drops the freeze). For WCACHE it drops the freeze, then either releases the CCB and schedules LOGDIR, or calls adaprobedone. For LOGDIR, IDDIR, SUP_CAP and ZONE it parses the returned data into softc flags (or on a non-ERESTART error clears the matching capability flags and releases a frozen devq), frees ataio->data_ptr, and then either releases the CCB and schedules the next probe state or calls adaprobedone; on ERESTART it returns early without freeing the buffer. DUMP is a no-op return. Any other type falls through to xpt_release_ccb(done_ccb).

functions.name: cfiscsi_ioctl_handoff
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ci points to a ctl_iscsi request whose data holds valid handoff parameters (target name, portal group tag, initiator details, socket/offload settings). Postcondition: the function returns nothing and reports the result in ci->status. It sets CTL_ISCSI_ERROR with an error_str if the target is not found (nothing else changed), if cfiscsi_session_new fails (target reference released), or, under ICL_KERNEL_PROXY, if both socket and connection_id are set or the connection id is not found (target reference released). It also sets CTL_ISCSI_ERROR if the target is offline (session handoff cleared and session terminated, target reference released), or if icl_conn_handoff fails (handoff cleared and session terminated; the target reference is not released here). Otherwise it copies the negotiated parameters into the session, binds the session to the target, terminates and waits out any existing session with the same initiator id on that target, registers the initiator with CTL, hands the connection off, clears cs_handoff_in_progress, terminates the session if it was already marked terminating, and sets CTL_ISCSI_OK. No locks are held on return.

functions.name: cdioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dp is a disk whose d_drv1 is a valid cam_periph (with a cd_softc) that the caller has not locked, and addr points to the argument structure the command cmd expects (or may be NULL for commands that take none). Postcondition: it takes the periph lock and a periph hold; if the hold fails it releases the periph reference and returns that error, and if the media is not valid and cmd is a cd-group ioctl other than CDIOCCLOSE/CDIOCEJECT, a failed cdcheckmedia returns its error after unholding. Otherwise it unlocks, dispatches on cmd (play, subchannel, TOC header/entry reads with BCD conversion, copyout of TOC data, patch/volume/mono/stereo/mute/left/right mode-page changes, pause/resume/start/stop/eject/prevent/allow, speed and block size get/set, DVD key and structure commands), freeing every temporary buffer on every path, with EINVAL for bad arguments such as an invalid address format, out-of-range track, oversized length or non-positive block size. CDIOCSETDEBUG, CDIOCCLRDEBUG and CDIOCRESET give ENOTTY, unknown commands go to cam_periph_ioctl, and sub-command errors or a copyout failure become the result. Finally it relocks, unholds, unlocks, prints a message if error and bootverbose, and returns 0 or the error code.

functions.name: dastart
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the periph lock (asserted MA_OWNED) and passes a start_ccb allocated for this periph. Postcondition: depending on softc->state the function either dispatches one command through xpt_action or releases start_ccb. In DA_STATE_NORMAL it takes the next bio and builds a delete, read/write, sync-cache or zone command, queues the ccb on pending_ccbs, takes a refcount, drops the lock around xpt_action, and reschedules. It finishes a bio with EOPNOTSUPP or the zone error and releases the ccb for unsupported commands or zone errors. It issues TEST UNIT READY when only that work is pending, and otherwise releases the ccb when no bio is queued. In the probe states it sends the matching inquiry, mode sense, read capacity or ATA identify/log command with a freshly malloc'd buffer. Some states skip ahead via goto skipstate to another probe state. On a missing buffer or a read-log failure it frees any buffer, calls daprobedone for the ATA states, or just breaks for others, and in the zone VPD case it releases the ccb. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: sagetparams
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: periph is a valid CAM peripheral whose softc is a struct sa_softc, and for every SA_PARAM_* bit set in params_to_get the matching output pointer (blocksize, numblocks, buff_mode, density, write_protect, speed, comp_supported, comp_enabled, comp_algorithm) is non-NULL (comp_supported must also be non-NULL if compression is requested, since it is written when the NOCOMP quirk is set); tcs and prot_page may be NULL. Postcondition: the function gets a CCB and always releases it, and always frees its internally allocated mode buffer and mode10 buffer, on every exit. It returns 0 on success, with each requested parameter stored through its output pointer, compression page copied to tcs if non-NULL, per-density report info and validity lengths stored in softc when SA_PARAM_DENSITY_EXT is requested and SCSI rev is at least SPC (errors from those reports are ignored and give length 0), and when SA_PARAM_LBP is requested and the drive supports protection, softc->prot_info.cur_prot_state is filled and the subpage copied to prot_page if non-NULL. If the compression mode sense fails with EINVAL it retries with the device configuration page, then sets SA_QUIRK_NOCOMP and retries without compression. It returns ENOMEM if the mode buffer (no CCB leak, CCB released) or the mode10 buffer cannot be allocated; EINVAL if the protection mode sense does not complete with CAM_REQ_CMP or returns too little data; or the nonzero error from cam_periph_runccb for the second mode sense or the protection mode sense. If the first mode sense yields a SCSI status error, it prints the sense data and goes to exit returning the error value from that runccb (which may be 0), leaving outputs unmodified.

functions.name: sasetparams
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: periph is a valid sa CAM periph with a softc, and the caller holds the periph lock needed for cam_periph_getccb/cam_periph_runccb. Postcondition: it first reads the current parameters with sagetparams and returns that error if it fails, or ENOMEM if the compression page copy or mode buffer cannot be allocated, freeing what it allocated. Otherwise it builds a MODE SELECT(6) buffer with the requested blocksize, density and (if SA_PARAM_COMPRESSION) the compression setting, and sends it. If the compression page type is unsupported and compression was the only parameter requested, it frees the buffers, releases the CCB and returns ENODEV; if other parameters were also requested, it drops compression and continues with a shorter buffer. If the select fails, it retries without the block descriptor when neither density nor blocksize was requested, or else tries once more with the original blocksize and density (and the original compression page), ignoring the result of that second attempt. It then releases the CCB and frees the buffers. When compression was requested, on error it clears SA_FLAG_COMP_ENABLED, saves the current algorithm in saved_comp_algorithm and sets comp_algorithm to 0; on success it sets SA_FLAG_COMP_ENABLED and comp_algorithm to calg. It returns 0 on success or the error code from the first mode select.

functions.name: GEN_SES_STATUS_DEV_SLOT_ACCESSORS(insert_ready,       INSERT_READY)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ses_status_dev_slot_get_insert_ready(elem). Precondition: elem points to a valid struct ses_status_dev_slot. Postcondition: returns the masked and shifted INSERT_READY field (byte 0, mask 0x08, shift 3), i.e. 0 or 1, and does not modify the element.

functions.name: GEN_SES_STATUS_ARRAY_DEV_SLOT_ACCESSORS(ok,              OK)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ses_status_array_dev_slot_get_ok(elem). Precondition: elem points to a valid struct ses_status_array_dev_slot. Postcondition: returns the masked and shifted OK field (byte 0, mask 0x80, shift 7), i.e. 0 or 1, and does not modify the element.

functions.name: GEN_SES_STATUS_POWER_SUPPLY_ACCESSORS(fail,             FAIL)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ses_status_power_supply_get_fail(elem). Precondition: elem points to a valid struct ses_status_power_supply. Postcondition: returns the masked and shifted FAIL field (byte 2, mask 0x40, shift 6), i.e. 0 or 1, and does not modify the element.

functions.name: GEN_SES_STATUS_COOLING_ACCESSORS(actual_speed_code,    ACTUAL_SPEED_CODE)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ses_status_cooling_get_actual_speed_code(elem). Precondition: elem points to a valid struct ses_status_cooling. Postcondition: returns the ACTUAL_SPEED_CODE field computed from byte 2 with mask 0x07 and shift 2 as the getter defines, and does not modify the element.

functions.name: vdev_raidz_read
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vd is a raidz vdev with a valid top-level vdev, children, spa and parity count, and data points to a buffer of at least bytes bytes that is read at the given offset, with bp describing the expected checksum. Postcondition: returns 0 when data passed checksum verification (directly, after reconstruction from parity, or after rereading all columns and retrying), returns ENOMEM if the raidz map could not be allocated (nothing to free), returns EIO if after reading every column more columns have errors than there are parity columns, and returns ECKSUM if errors are not more than the parity count but combinatorial reconstruction was not attempted (errors equal to parity count) or failed; on every path after the map was allocated it is freed before returning, and data may be overwritten by reconstruction.

functions.name: dtrace_difo_validate
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dp points to a DIF object with a valid instruction buffer and variable table, vstate points to a valid vstate (and vstate->dtvs_state is dereferenced for the kernel-visibility check unless cr is NULL), and nregs is the number of registers available; no lock is taken or released. Postcondition: returns 0 if the DIFO is well-formed, otherwise the nonnegative count of errors accumulated through dtrace_difo_err (instruction operand/register/branch/opcode checks, last instruction must be 'ret', bad return size, variable scope/kind/id/size checks and redefinition mismatches, and out-of-range variable references); it also resets dp->dtdo_destructive and sets it to 1 if copyout/copyoutstr is called, rewrites plain load instructions to their restricted (RLD) forms when cr is NULL or the kernel is not visible to the credentials, and on non-FreeBSD builds increments vstate->dtvs_state->dts_getf for each getf() call when dtvs_state is non-NULL (on FreeBSD getf() is counted as an error). The instruction scan and variable-table scan stop early once an error was found.

functions.name: dtrace_dynvar
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dstate is an initialized dynamic variable state, nkeys is nonzero, key points to nkeys valid keys, and for op DTRACE_DYNVAR_DEALLOC the caller runs on the current CPU with the bucket not locked by itself. Postcondition: it hashes the tuple, and returns NULL immediately if a key's by-reference data cannot be loaded (dtrace_canload fails) or a CPU fault flag is set. Otherwise it looks up the tuple in the hash chain, retrying from the top when the chain changed under it. For ALLOC or NOALLOC it returns the matching dynamic variable if one exists. For DEALLOC it locks the bucket first, unlinks the match, marks it free, pushes it on the per-CPU dirty list, unlocks the bucket and returns NULL. If there is no match, NOALLOC and DEALLOC return NULL (DEALLOC unlocks the bucket). For ALLOC with no match it computes the needed size. If that exceeds the chunk size it increments dtdsc_drops and returns NULL. Otherwise it takes a chunk from the free list, refilling it from the clean list and trying other CPUs as needed. If no space is found it bumps the matching drop counter, sets CPU_DTRACE_DROP and returns NULL. Otherwise it copies the keys and key data into the chunk, publishes it at the head of the hash chain and returns the new dvar. If publishing fails the chunk goes to the dirty list and the whole operation retries.

functions.name: dtrace_dif_subr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called by the DTrace DIF interpreter in probe context with a valid subroutine number, tuple arguments tupregs, destination register rd, and mstate/vstate/state set up; scratch space and CPU fault flags are available. Postcondition: for the STRTOK, SUBSTR, JSON, TOUPPER and TOLOWER subroutines, regs[rd] is set to 0 when a canload/strcanload check fails, when scratch space is insufficient (CPU_DTRACE_NOSCRATCH is then also set), or, for strtok, when the scan reaches the end of the string (the saved strtok pointer and limit are also cleared) or, for json, when dtrace_json returns NULL; otherwise regs[rd] points to a new string in scratch space (strtok token, substring, json result, or case-converted copy), dtms_scratch_ptr is advanced (by size, or by jsonlen+1 for json), and strtok saves its position and limit in mstate. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: dtrace_dif_subr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called from the DIF interpreter with a valid subroutine number subr, tuple arguments tupregs[0..nargs-1], register array regs, and valid mstate, vstate and state; in this slice the cases handled are STRTOLL, LLTOSTR, HTONS/NTOHS, HTONL/NTOHL, HTONLL/NTOHLL, DIRNAME/BASENAME and GETF. Postcondition: it returns nothing and writes the subroutine result to regs[rd]. STRTOLL stores the parsed integer, or INT64_MIN if the string cannot be loaded. For STRTOLL and LLTOSTR, a base argument <=1 or >36 sets CPU_DTRACE_ILLOP in *flags and leaves regs[rd] unchanged. LLTOSTR stores a scratch-allocated (65 bytes) string and advances dtms_scratch_ptr, or stores 0 and sets CPU_DTRACE_NOSCRATCH when scratch is short. The hton/ntoh cases store the 16/32/64-bit value, byte-swapped on little-endian. DIRNAME/BASENAME store a scratch copy of the result (size STRSIZE) and advance the scratch pointer, or store 0 if the source cannot be loaded, or store 0 and set NOSCRATCH if scratch is short. GETF stores 0 if process privilege is lacking; otherwise it stores the file pointer from fget_noref (taken under the shared filedesc lock, which is released, with no reference taken) and records it in mstate->dtms_getf.

functions.name: dtrace_dif_emulate
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: difo holds a validated DIF object (instruction buffer, string and integer tables) and mstate, vstate and state are valid for the current CPU, so register numbers, variable ids, jump labels and tuple depth are in range and the DIF-level checks have been done. Postcondition: it stores difo in mstate->dtms_difo, then interprets instructions from pc 0 until the program ends (RET sets pc to the text length and records the return value) or CPU_DTRACE_FAULT is set in the per-CPU flags. Non-fatal problems (divide by zero, tuple overflow, illegal op, bad address, bad alignment, no scratch) are recorded in the CPU flags and illval rather than trapping. If no fault is set it returns the value of the register given to RET, or 0 if no RET ran. If a fault is set it records the faulting instruction's byte offset in mstate->dtms_fltoffs, sets DTRACE_MSTATE_FLTOFFS in dtms_present, and returns 0. It acquires no locks or references, and it may modify scratch space, variables, dynamic variables and memory it is allowed to store to.

functions.name: dtrace_probe
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called when a probe fires, with a valid probe id and its arguments, in a context where the per-CPU DTrace state and the probe's ECB list are valid. Postcondition: for each enabled ECB whose user-mode/owner conditions, deadman check, buffer reservation and predicate allow it, the record header is written and its actions are executed in order into the per-CPU buffer until a CPU_DTRACE_ERROR flag is set; ECBs that fail a condition, reservation or predicate are skipped, a state past the deadman timeout without full destructive permission is moved to the KILLED activity, and the predicate cache may be updated; the function returns no value.

functions.name: fasttrap_getreg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: rp points to a valid saved register frame (struct reg) and reg is a register constant; on amd64 it must be one of the listed REG_* constants (R15 through GS, DS, ES, FSBASE, GSBASE), on other builds it must be below _NGREG (19). Postcondition: returns the saved value of register reg from rp (for REG_FSBASE and REG_GSBASE it returns the value read from the corresponding MSR via rdmsr); for an unlisted or out-of-range reg it calls panic and does not return; rp is not modified and no ownership changes.

functions.name: dtrace_disx86
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: x points to a dis86_t whose d86_get_byte callback (and d86_data, optional d86_check_func) are set up, and cpu_mode is SIZE16, SIZE32 or SIZE64 (any other value is treated as 64-bit mode). Postcondition: the function decodes one x86 instruction from the byte stream, consuming bytes via d86_get_byte and recording them in x->d86_len and d86_bytes. It fills in x's mode, prefix, operand-size, address-size, memory-size and (with DIS_TEXT) mnemonic and operand fields according to the opcode table entry's addressing mode, and returns 0 on success. If the byte stream ends, the encoding is invalid or unsupported for the mode, or a prefix or operand combination is illegal, it jumps to the error path and returns 1 instead, with the output state only partially filled. It takes and releases no locks or references and allocates no memory.

functions.name: dtrace_disx86
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: x points to a valid dis86_t whose d86_get_byte callback supplies instruction bytes (and d86_check_func is NULL or callable), and cpu_mode is SIZE16, SIZE32 or SIZE64 (any other value is treated as 64-bit mode). Postcondition: the function resets the decode state in x, reads and decodes one instruction (legacy, REX, VEX or EVEX prefixes, opcode tables, ModRM, and per-addressing-mode operands, immediates and displacements), and fills x->d86_len, x->d86_mode, x->d86_opnd_size, x->d86_addr_size and the mnemonic, operands and memory-size fields; it returns 0 on success, or returns 1 via the shared error path if a byte cannot be read, an opcode, prefix or mode/operand combination is invalid, or the decode hits an unsupported encoding. It does not take or release locks or references.

functions.name: fbt_provide_module_function
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: lf, symval and opaque are valid, opaque is the module name string, and the caller may sleep (M_WAITOK allocation). Postcondition: always returns 0. It returns 0 without creating any probe if the symbol is excluded, is "trap_check", or has no recognizable frame-pointer prologue. Otherwise it allocates an entry probe at the prologue, hashes it (chaining via fbtp_tracenext if a probe already exists at that address), and increments lf->fbt_nentries. It then scans the remaining instructions up to the symbol end and stops at the end or at an undecodable instruction. For each return instruction (a ret on amd64; a pop %ebp or leave followed by ret or ret imm16 on i386) not judged to lie within a jump-table pointer, it allocates a return probe, chains it via fbtp_probenext and shares the first return probe's id, inserts it into fbt_probetab, and increments lf->fbt_nentries. The caller gets no references; the allocated probes remain owned by the provider.

functions.name: systrace_return_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes; sysnum and ndx are arbitrary ints. Postcondition: returns nothing; if sysnum is a known syscall number and ndx is 0 or 1, the return-type name for that syscall (for example "int", "ssize_t", "void", "void *", "mode_t" or "off_t") is copied into desc with strlcpy, truncated to descsz; for an unknown sysnum or any other ndx, desc is left unchanged.

functions.name: systrace_return_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes (descsz > 0 if a copy happens); sysnum and ndx may be any ints. Postcondition: if sysnum is a known FreeBSD32 syscall number and ndx is 0 or 1, the return-type name for that syscall ("void", "int", "ssize_t", "mode_t", "off_t" or "void *") is copied into desc with strlcpy, truncated to descsz and NUL-terminated; for any other sysnum or ndx, desc is left unchanged; nothing is returned.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: n_args and uarg are valid writable pointers, uarg has room for the largest argument list (at least 8 entries), and params points to the argument struct matching sysnum (it is only read for syscalls that take arguments). Postcondition: for a known sysnum the function switches on it, stores each argument of that syscall in order into uarg (as uint64_t, with pointers cast through intptr_t) or into the same buffer viewed as int64_t iarg (for signed integer arguments), and sets *n_args to the argument count (0 for syscalls without arguments); for an unlisted sysnum it takes the default path, which is outside the shown slice. It returns nothing, takes no locks and allocates no memory.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: params points to the args structure matching the syscall number sysnum (for syscalls that take arguments), uarg points to a writable array of 64-bit slots large enough for that syscall's arguments, and n_args is writable. Postcondition: for a known sysnum, each argument is stored in order in uarg, as a sign-extended int64 in the same slot for integer-typed arguments or as an unsigned/pointer-cast value for pointer and unsigned arguments (with a pad slot included only if PAD64_REQUIRED is defined), and *n_args is set to the number of arguments (0 for syscalls without arguments); the function returns nothing, and for a sysnum not matched by any case that is visible, uarg and *n_args are left as the code after the switch decides (not shown in this slice).

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to an array large enough for the argument slots of the syscall, n_args is writable, and for any syscall number with a case, params points to the matching freebsd32 argument struct for that number. Postcondition: for a recognized sysnum the function copies each argument from params into uarg in order (iarg is the same buffer viewed as int64_t; integer arguments are stored as signed values, unsigned ones and pointers as unsigned values, with pad fields included only under PAD64_REQUIRED), sets *n_args to the argument count (0 for syscalls with no arguments, in which case params is not read), and returns nothing; for a sysnum not listed in the switch, it leaves the output untouched, except as the default case behaves in the truncated part of the source. It takes no locks and acquires or releases no references or memory.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes; sysnum is a syscall number and ndx an argument index. Postcondition: a local pointer p is set to the type-description string for argument ndx of syscall sysnum when both are listed in the table; it stays NULL for unlisted syscalls, for syscalls with no arguments, and for out-of-range ndx; nothing is returned (void) and no locks or references are taken. The code after the switch (outside the shown part) is what uses p to fill desc.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes, and sysnum and ndx are the syscall number and zero-based argument index. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it looks up the C type string for argument ndx of syscall sysnum in a generated switch, and only if one is found (p is non-NULL) it copies that string into desc, truncated to descsz bytes. For unknown syscall numbers, argument indices out of range, or syscalls with no arguments, p stays NULL and desc is left unchanged. For the preadv/pwritev/pread/pwrite/mmap/lseek/truncate/ftruncate/cpuset_setid cases the index of the 64-bit offset arguments shifts down by one unless PAD64_REQUIRED is defined.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes (descsz > 0 is needed for any copy); sysnum is a freebsd32 syscall number and ndx an argument index, with no range restriction required. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it looks up the static argument type string for (sysnum, ndx) in the generated switch tables and, only if one exists (p != NULL), copies it into desc with strlcpy, truncated to descsz; for unknown syscalls, syscalls with no arguments, or out-of-range ndx, desc is left untouched.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc must point to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes (when descsz is nonzero), and sysnum and ndx are the syscall number and zero-based argument index. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it looks up the argument-type string for that syscall and argument, and the lookup yields no string (p stays NULL) for a syscall with no arguments, an unknown syscall number, or an argument index out of range for that syscall. The visible part of the function ends before the code that uses p, so what is written to desc is not shown here.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes; sysnum is a syscall number and ndx an argument index (any values are accepted). Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it looks up the C type name of argument ndx of the syscall sysnum in the generated tables, and if one exists it copies it into desc with strlcpy (truncated to descsz); for unknown syscall numbers, syscalls with no arguments, or an out-of-range ndx, no type is found and desc is left unchanged (or is cleared if the code after the switch does so for a NULL result).

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes, and sysnum and ndx identify a syscall and one of its argument positions. functions.name: systrace_return_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes; sysnum and ndx are arbitrary ints. Postcondition: returns nothing; if sysnum is a known FreeBSD32 syscall number and ndx is 0 or 1, the return-type name for that syscall (for example "int", "ssize_t", "void *", "void", "mode_t" or "off_t") is copied into desc with strlcpy, truncated to descsz and NUL-terminated; for an unknown sysnum or any other ndx desc is left untouched.

functions.name: mul_u64_u64_div_u64
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: z is nonzero and the exact quotient fits in 64 bits, i.e. the mathematical product x * y is less than 2^64 * z (if z is 0 the division y / z is undefined, and if the quotient does not fit, res wraps modulo 2^64). Postcondition: the function returns floor(x * y / z), computed exactly over the full 128-bit product by shift-and-add with remainder rem < z, so both KASSERTs hold; it has no side effects and touches no memory, locks or references.

functions.name: CK_PR_FENCE(memory, "mfence")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_fence_strict_memory(void). No precondition; executes an mfence instruction with a memory clobber (a full compiler and hardware barrier for loads and stores) and returns nothing.

functions.name: CK_PR_FENCE(load, "lfence")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_fence_strict_load(void). No precondition; executes an lfence instruction with a memory clobber (orders prior loads before later instructions) and returns nothing.

functions.name: CK_PR_FENCE(store, "sfence")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_fence_strict_store(void). No precondition; executes an sfence instruction with a memory clobber (orders prior stores before later stores) and returns nothing.

functions.name: CK_PR_FAS_S(64, uint64_t, "xchgq")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_fas_64(target, v). Precondition: target points to valid, suitably aligned, writable 64-bit memory; postcondition: atomically (xchgq) stores v at *target and returns the previous value of *target.

functions.name: CK_PR_FAS(ptr, void, void *, uint64_t, "xchgq")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_fas_ptr(target, v). Precondition: target points to valid, aligned, writable pointer-sized memory; postcondition: atomically (xchgq) stores pointer v at *target and returns the previous pointer value.

functions.name: CK_PR_LOAD_S(64, uint64_t, "movq")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_md_load_64(target). Precondition: target points to valid, aligned, readable 64-bit memory; postcondition: returns the value read from *target with a single movq load (compiler memory barrier); memory is not modified.

functions.name: CK_PR_STORE_IMM(S, M, T, C, I, K)
CK_PR_CAS_V(double, 2, double)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_cas_double_2(t, c, s), only when CK_PR_DISABLE_DOUBLE is not defined. Precondition: t, c, s point to arrays of 2 doubles (16 bytes), t suitably aligned for cmpxchg16b. Postcondition: atomically compares the 16 bytes at t with those at c and, if equal, stores the 16 bytes at s into t; returns true if the swap happened, false otherwise, by delegating to ck_pr_cas_64_2.

functions.name: CK_PR_CAS_V(char, 16, char)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_cas_char_16_value(t, c, s, v). Precondition: t points to 16 chars (aligned for cmpxchg16b), c and s point to 16-char arrays, v points to writable 16 bytes. Postcondition: atomically compares the 16 bytes at t with c and, if equal, stores s into t; the 16 bytes observed at t (the old value) are written to v; returns true if the swap happened, false otherwise, via ck_pr_cas_64_2_value.

functions.name: CK_PR_GENERATE(bts)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_bts_ptr(target, b) (via CK_PR_BT with a 64-bit bts instruction). Precondition: target points to a valid writable memory word; b is the bit offset, which the bts instruction with a memory operand and register offset may address beyond 64 bits. Postcondition: atomically sets bit b of the memory at target and returns true if that bit was previously set, false otherwise (the carry flag).

functions.name: CK_PR_GENERATE(btr)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_btr_uint(target, b) (via CK_PR_BT with btrl). Precondition: target points to a valid writable unsigned int; b is the bit offset (the instruction with a memory operand and register offset may address bits beyond 32). Postcondition: atomically clears bit b and returns true if that bit was previously set, false otherwise.

functions.name: CK_PR_GENERATE(btc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function ck_pr_btc_64(target, b) (via CK_PR_BT with btcq). Precondition: target points to a valid writable uint64_t; b is the bit offset (a register offset with memory operand may address beyond 64 bits). Postcondition: atomically toggles bit b and returns true if that bit was previously set, false otherwise.

functions.name: MurmurHash64B
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: key points to at least len readable bytes (read as 32-bit words, so ideally 4-byte aligned) and len is non-negative. Postcondition: returns a 64-bit MurmurHash64B of the len bytes at key, seeded by seed, with the high 32 bits from h1 and the low 32 bits from h2; no error values are produced and the input is only read, not modified.

functions.name: AcGetAllTablesFromFile
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Filename names a file and ReturnListHead points to a valid list head (possibly *ReturnListHead == NULL). Postcondition: if the file cannot be opened it returns AE_NOT_EXIST (errno ENOENT) or AE_ERROR; otherwise the file is read and always closed before return. It returns AE_ERROR if the file size is unavailable (UINT32_MAX), AE_BAD_HEADER if the file is smaller than an ACPI table header, AE_TYPE if the file is not binary, AE_OK when reading ends normally (AE_CTRL_TERMINATE) or a table is skipped by AE_TYPE (e.g. non-AML table when only AML is wanted), AE_NO_MEMORY if a descriptor allocation fails (that table is freed), or any other failure status from AcGetOneTableFromFile. On the normal end (end-of-file terminate), the tables read are appended to the end of the list at *ReturnListHead (or become the list if it was empty). On any error return, and on the AE_TYPE skip path, the local list is not attached to *ReturnListHead and its descriptors and tables are leaked (caller does not get them).

functions.name: AcpiDmInspectPossibleArgs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Op is NULL or points to a valid parse object whose Common.Next chain is well-formed (each node has valid opcode info, and for EXECUTE-class nodes a valid Value.Arg list). Postcondition: returns 0 if Op is NULL; otherwise walks the siblings after Op (not Op itself), for at most ACPI_METHOD_NUM_ARGS nodes, and returns the count of nodes accepted as possible method arguments. The walk stops, returning the count so far, at the end of the list, at a STORE or NOTIFY opcode, or at a node of CONTROL, CREATE or NAMED_OBJECT class. An EXECUTE-class node whose argument list has no unnamed-target NAMEPATH argument (and is not REF_OF) also returns the count so far, without counting that node. Otherwise each node is counted. CurrentOpArgCount and TargetCount are unused, and nothing is acquired, released or modified.

functions.name: AcpiDmCreateNewExternal
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ExternalPath and InternalPath are valid NUL-terminated strings (ExternalPath is non-NULL and stays owned by the list if a node is created), and AcpiGbl_ExternalList is a well-formed singly linked list. Postcondition: if an entry with the same Path (case-sensitive strcmp) already exists, no node is created and AE_ALREADY_EXISTS is returned; if that entry has ACPI_EXT_ORIGIN_FROM_OPCODE it is left unchanged, otherwise its Type is upgraded from ACPI_TYPE_ANY to Type when Type is not ANY, its Value is lowered to Value if smaller, Flags gets the new Flags ORed in and ACPI_EXT_INTERNAL_PATH_ALLOCATED cleared; otherwise a zeroed new descriptor is allocated recording the Flags, Value, Type, ExternalPath, InternalPath and the path length, and it is inserted before the first entry whose Path compares greater case-insensitively (or at the tail, or as head if the list is empty), returning AE_OK; if allocation fails AE_NO_MEMORY is returned and the list is unchanged.

functions.name: AcpiDmDumpTable
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Table points to readable memory holding the (sub)table of TableLength total bytes, TableOffset is the offset of Table within the main table, SubtableLength is 0 for a main table or the subtable length, and Info is a field-descriptor array terminated by an entry with a NULL Name (or Info is NULL). Postcondition: it prints each described field as a line of decoded text to the ACPI output, recursing for GAS, HEST notify and IORT memory-access fields, and returns AE_NOT_IMPLEMENTED if Info is NULL (after printing a message); AE_OK when a subtable ends early (an Info->Offset past SubtableLength, or a field overrunning TableLength while SubtableLength is nonzero), when an ACPI_DMT_EXIT descriptor is reached, or when the whole list is dumped successfully; AE_BAD_DATA if a field's offset is at or beyond TableLength, a field overruns TableLength in a main table (SubtableLength zero), or after the list when TableOffset is nonzero and SubtableLength is zero; AE_SUPPORT for an unknown opcode; or any failure status returned by a recursive dump. It allocates nothing and takes no locks or references; it only reads the table and writes the output (and shared message buffer for UUIDs).

functions.name: AcpiDmDumpCedt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Table points to a readable CEDT table whose header Length covers the buffer being walked, with subtable headers following the standard ACPI header. Postcondition: returns nothing; for each subtable it prints a newline, the common header, then the type-specific body (CHBS, CFMWS with the extra interleave targets 1..max-1 where max is 1<<InterleaveWays if InterleaveWays<8 else 3<<(InterleaveWays-8), CXIMS with extra XOR maps 1..NrXormaps-1), or for an unknown type prints an unknown-type message; it then advances by the subtable Length. It returns early, without processing further subtables, on the first AcpiDmDumpTable failure, or after printing 'Invalid zero length subtable' for an unknown-type subtable with zero Length; otherwise it ends when Offset reaches Table->Length. It acquires no locks or references and allocates nothing.

functions.name: AcpiDmDumpHmat
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Table points to a readable ACPI HMAT table of at least Table->Length bytes. Postcondition: returns void after dumping the main HMAT header and then each HMAT structure (header, body, and for locality and cache types the trailing initiator/target domain lists, latency/bandwidth entries or SMBIOS handles) via AcpiDmDumpTable and AcpiOsPrintf. It returns early if the main-table dump, a header or body dump, or a trailing-entry dump fails. It also returns early after printing an error if a structure length is below the header size or the type's body size, or if a trailing count does not fit in the structure length. An unknown structure type prints a message and is skipped using its Length. No memory, locks or references are acquired or released and Table is not modified.

functions.name: AcpiDmDumpIvrs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Table points to a readable ACPI IVRS table whose Length covers the table bytes, so the main header and every subtable and device entry it describes can be read. Postcondition: returns nothing; it prints the main IVRS table, then each subtable in order, and for IVHD subtables (types 10h, 11h, 40h) every device entry, including the HID, CID and UID parts of HID entries. Unknown subtable types are reported and skipped by their Length. It returns early, with the remaining output not printed, if any AcpiDmDumpTable call fails, or if an unknown subtable has zero length (after printing "Invalid zero length subtable"). It acquires no locks or references and allocates no memory.

functions.name: TrCreateConstantLeafOp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ParseOpcode is any UINT32 opcode value; the ASL global state used by TrAllocateOp is initialised. Postcondition: for PARSEOP___LINE__ returns a new PARSEOP_INTEGER op whose integer value is its line number; for PARSEOP___METHOD__ returns a new PARSEOP___METHOD__ op with a NULL string value; for PARSEOP___PATH__ returns a new string-literal op whose string is the op's filename pointer (not copied); for PARSEOP___FILE__ returns a new string-literal op whose string is the simple filename from FlSplitInputPathname, or returns NULL if that call fails (the already allocated op is left unreleased); for PARSEOP___DATE__ returns a new string-literal op whose string is a newly allocated copy of the current ctime text without the trailing newline, or the empty string if ctime returns NULL; for any other opcode returns NULL without allocating an op. On success it prints a debug line and returns the op, which the caller owns.

functions.name: RsDoQwordMemoryDescriptor
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Info points to a valid ASL_RESOURCE_INFO whose DescriptorTypeOp has a (possibly empty) child list of QWordMemory initializer nodes in order. Postcondition: allocates and returns a non-NULL resource node (never an error code) whose buffer holds an Address64 descriptor of type memory range, with flags, specific flags, granularity, min, max, translation offset and length copied from the initializers, an optional ResourceSourceIndex byte and ResourceSource string appended (ResourceLength enlarged accordingly), bit/qword/multibit field tags created, and the resource name attached to the owner; extra initializers or ResSource without a ResSourceIndex raise AslError; RsLargeAddressCheck validates Min/Max/Len/Gran; BufferLength is set to sizeof(AML_RESOURCE_ADDRESS64) + OptionIndex + StringLength; all initializer nodes are completed and consumed.

functions.name: TrDoMethod
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Op is a valid method parse-tree node whose first child has a next sibling (the argument-count node), followed by at least four more siblings in the chain, the fourth being the parameter list node (all non-NULL). Postcondition: the global AslGbl_TempCount is set to 0; if the argument-count node is already PARSEOP_BYTECONST the function returns with no other change; otherwise the argument-count node's Value.Integer is set to the number of parameters (the number of children under a PARSEOP_DEFAULT_ARG parameter node, truncated to the UINT8 counter, or 1 if the parameter node is any other opcode) and its opcode becomes PARSEOP_BYTECONST. Nothing is returned, and no locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: TrWalkParseTree
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Op points to a valid node of a well-formed ASL parse tree (child/next/parent links consistent) and the callbacks needed for the chosen Visitation mode are valid function pointers. Postcondition: if AslGbl_ParseTreeRoot is NULL it returns AE_OK at once without walking; otherwise it walks the subtree rooted at Op in the requested order (downward, upward, twice, or nothing for an unsupported mode) calling the callbacks, and returns AE_OK when the walk completes (a descending callback returning AE_CTRL_DEPTH only skips that op's children), or returns immediately the first failing status (any descending failure other than AE_CTRL_DEPTH, or any ascending failure). If Op is a DEFINITION_BLOCK and ASL_WALK_VISIT_DB_SEPARATELY is set, its Next link is cleared during the walk and restored to the saved value on both the success and error return paths (using the Op current at exit).

functions.name: DtCompileSdev
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: List points to a valid DT_FIELD list cursor (DT_FIELD **) holding the SDEV field list, and the subtable stack is usable. Postcondition: for each SDEV subtable it compiles the header, the type-specific body (namespace device or PCIe endpoint), optional secure component, device id, path and vendor data parts, inserts them under the current parent, fills in offsets, lengths and the header Length, and returns AE_OK when the whole list is consumed. It returns the failing status if any DtCompileTable call fails, and returns AE_ERROR (after DtFatal for an unknown subtable type) for an unknown subtable type or an undefined secure component type; on any error return the output built so far is left partially constructed. In the namespace case, if the device id subtable is absent it skips the rest of that entry (the header Length stays the header size) and still pops the subtable; the header Length is only set to the full size when vendor data is present.

functions.name: AcpiDmCheckForSymbolicOpcode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Op is a valid parse-tree node and Info is the walk info; when C-style disassembly is enabled and Op has an operator-specific shape, its first child exists and for binary/target opcodes the second child exists (and for Divide a third child exists), and Op->Common.Parent is non-NULL for opcodes that take a target. Postcondition: returns FALSE immediately if AcpiGbl_CstyleDisassembly is off, if Op has no first argument, for an unsupported opcode, for Index with a constant source (String/Buffer/Package/VarPackage; sets the CLOSING_PAREN flag), for LNOT whose sub-operand has no child, for Divide with both targets (or any valid remainder target without optimizations; clears the operator symbol and sets LEGACY_ASL_ONLY), when a math op's target is missing, and for Store with ignored optimizations or no target, and for BitNot with no target; otherwise returns TRUE. It records operator symbols in the child nodes, may mark nodes ignored, convert Divide to Mod, promote the target, set compound-assignment/assignment/LNOT flags, and print "!", "~" or "(" via AcpiOsPrintf where needed; no locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: AcpiDsEvaluateNamePath
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: WalkState is a valid walk state whose Op is a valid parse op, with the walk state's operand stack usable. Postcondition: returns AE_OK without doing anything if Op has no parent or its parent is AML_PACKAGE_OP, AML_VARIABLE_PACKAGE_OP or AML_REF_OF_OP; otherwise it creates the operand with AcpiDsCreateOperand and returns that error on failure. If Op has the ACPI_PARSEOP_TARGET flag, the operand itself becomes the result and is pushed. Otherwise it resolves the operand with AcpiExResolveToValue (returning its error on failure). If the original operand type was ACPI_TYPE_INTEGER it removes one reference and copies the object with AcpiUtCopyIobjectToIobject (returning its error on failure, with ResultObj not set); for other types the resolved operand is used directly. It then pops one operand from the stack with AcpiDsObjStackPop; if that fails, ResultObj is set to the new object and the error is returned without pushing. Otherwise WalkState->ResultObj is set to the new object and pushed with AcpiDsResultPush, and the push status is returned. Only when the push succeeds is ACPI_PARSEOP_IN_STACK set in Op->Common.Flags.

functions.name: AcpiExOpcode_1A_0T_1R
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: WalkState is a valid walk state whose Opcode is one of LNot, Decrement, Increment, ObjectType, SizeOf, RefOf or DerefOf, and whose Operands[0] is the already-resolved single operand for that opcode. Postcondition: returns AE_OK and stores the newly created or newly referenced result object in WalkState->ResultObj on success (for DerefOf of a Device or Thermal node the result is the node itself without a new reference; a DerefOf of a RefOf reference to a node with no attached object succeeds with a NULL result); on failure the result object is released via AcpiUtRemoveReference and the error is returned, namely AE_NO_MEMORY, AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE, AE_TYPE, AE_AML_BAD_OPCODE, or a status propagated from the called helpers (resolve, store, field read, namespace lookup, buffer/package argument fetch). The AE_AML_UNINITIALIZED_ELEMENT (NULL package element) and field-read failure paths in DerefOf return directly without going through Cleanup, so they do not release ReturnDesc and do not set ResultObj. DerefOf on a String resolves the named object and finishes through Cleanup. Operand[0] may be replaced and its reference dropped or a reference added during DerefOf.

functions.name: AcpiNsLookup
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the namespace is initialised, ReturnNode is writable, and Path is either NULL (or empty, meaning the starting scope itself) or a well-formed ACPI name path (optional root/parent prefixes, then dual/multi/single name segments) that is resolved relative to ScopeInfo or the current scope; the caller holds the namespace lock. Postcondition: the function walks the path segment by segment, looking up or (depending on Flags/InterpreterMode) creating each node, dereferencing an alias to a scope-opening object when more segments follow, and warning but not failing on a last-segment type mismatch; on success it sets *ReturnNode to the final node, pushes a new scope on WalkState's scope stack if Flags lacks ACPI_NS_DONT_OPEN_SCOPE, WalkState is given and the resulting type opens a scope, and returns AE_OK. On a lookup/search failure it returns that status (e.g. AE_NOT_FOUND, AE_ALREADY_EXISTS), setting *ReturnNode to the node found at the failing segment only in the case where the search returned a status together with a node at the last segment (the not-found and already-exists cases handled at the end of a segment); it returns AE_NOT_EXIST for an alias with no target object and for a missing scope or invalid path, and returns the failure status of the scope stack push if that fails.

functions.name: AcpiNsGetBitmappedType
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ReturnObject is either NULL or a pointer to a valid ACPI operand object whose Common.Type can be read. Postcondition: returns ACPI_RTYPE_NONE if ReturnObject is NULL; otherwise returns ACPI_RTYPE_INTEGER, ACPI_RTYPE_BUFFER, ACPI_RTYPE_STRING, ACPI_RTYPE_PACKAGE or ACPI_RTYPE_REFERENCE for object types INTEGER, BUFFER, STRING, PACKAGE or LOCAL_REFERENCE respectively, and ACPI_RTYPE_ANY for any other type; the object is not modified and no references or locks are taken.

functions.name: AcpiNsSearchOneScope
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Node is a valid parent namespace node, TargetName is a 4-character ACPI name, and ReturnNode is a valid output pointer. Postcondition: if a child named TargetName already exists in Node's scope, it is returned in *ReturnNode with AE_OK (earlier part of the function, not shown); otherwise, if InterpreterMode is ACPI_IMODE_EXECUTE it returns AE_NOT_FOUND and adds nothing; otherwise it creates a new node and, if allocation fails, returns AE_NO_MEMORY with no node added; on success it marks the new node ANOBJ_TEMPORARY if Flags has ACPI_NS_TEMPORARY (and ANOBJ_IS_EXTERNAL in the ASL compiler build for external or scope-op cases), installs it under Node with Type, stores it in *ReturnNode and returns AE_OK.

functions.name: AcpiPsGetNextArg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: WalkState and ParserState point to valid structures with ParserState->Aml/PkgEnd delimiting the AML stream, ReturnArg is writable, and ArgType is an ARGP_* value. Postcondition: depending on ArgType it builds one parse op (simple data, bytelist, namepath for SimpleName/NameOrRef/Target/SuperName, or a linked field list), or sets ParserState->PkgEnd (PKGLENGTH), or sets WalkState->ArgCount (1 for complex term/data/target args or ACPI_VAR_ARGS for non-empty lists, including when a Target/SuperName parses as a method call, in which case the op is freed and the result is NULL); on success it stores the op (or NULL when nothing is returned) in *ReturnArg and returns AE_OK; an unknown ArgType returns AE_AML_OPERAND_TYPE with *ReturnArg set to NULL; on allocation failure (op or field) it returns AE_NO_MEMORY, freeing any partial field list, and on namepath parse failure it frees the new op and returns that error status; on those early error returns *ReturnArg is not written.

functions.name: AcpiRsConvertAmlToResource
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Resource, Aml and the Info conversion table are valid, the table's first entry holds the entry count, and the Aml buffer is large enough for every offset the table reads. Postcondition: returns AE_BAD_PARAMETER if Info is NULL, on an invalid conversion opcode, or on an invalid EXIT_NE sub-opcode; returns AE_AML_INVALID_RESOURCE_TYPE if AcpiRsGetAddressCommon fails for an ACPI_RSC_ADDRESS entry; otherwise processes the table entries in order (stopping early at an EXIT_NE entry whose comparison fails), filling the internal Resource from the AML bytes and growing Resource->Length, and returns AE_OK. On AE_OK the Resource length is rounded up to the native word size unless an ACPI_RSC_FLAGINIT entry was processed. A misaligned Resource pointer only causes a warning. The resource may be partly written when an error is returned.

functions.name: AcpiUtValidateException
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: Status is any ACPI_STATUS value; the global exception name tables must be initialised. Postcondition: the type bits (Status & AE_CODE_MASK) select the environmental, programmer, ACPI-tables, AML or control table and the remaining bits index it; returns a pointer to that table entry if the index is within the table's maximum and the entry's Name is non-NULL, otherwise returns NULL (unknown type, index out of range, or entry without a name); nothing is locked, acquired or modified.

functions.name: ar9300_freebsd_proc_radar_event
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ah is a valid HAL handle, rxs points to a valid RX status, buf holds at least rxs->rs_datalen bytes of the frame, and event points to writable storage. Postcondition: returns AH_FALSE without touching event if the phy error is neither HAL_PHYERR_RADAR nor HAL_PHYERR_FALSE_RADAR_EXT, if ext-channel DFS is supported and rs_datalen < 3 or the trailing pulse_bw_info byte is 0, or if ext-channel DFS is unsupported and both the duration (buf[0], or 0 when datalen is 0) and the RSSI are 0. Otherwise it selects the RSSI (combined or chain 0, negative values clamped to 0, then adjusted by the enhanced or ext-channel rules), fills event->re_full_ts, re_ts, re_rssi, re_dur and re_flags (PRICH, EXTCH, EXTEARLY, ISDC bits as determined) and returns AH_TRUE. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: ar9300_set_interrupts
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ah is a valid initialized AR9300 HAL handle and ints is a HAL_INT bitmask. Postcondition: the function returns omask, the previous interrupt mask captured at entry. Unless the RTC is unavailable (nortc), it adjusts the IER reference count (incrementing it when HAL_INT_GLOBAL is not requested), writes the computed IMR and AR_IMR_S2 (updating the software shadow ah_mask2Reg), stores ints in ah_mask_reg, and, when auto-sleep is unsupported, sets or clears the TIM_TIMER bit in AR_IMR_S5. If HAL_INT_GLOBAL is set and the IER reference count is zero, it re-enables IER (if !nortc) and programs the async enable/mask registers, the MSI registers when MSI is configured, and the sync enable/mask registers. Interrupts were disabled earlier in the function before reprogramming.

functions.name: ath10k_bss_info_changed
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller does not hold ar->conf_mutex, and hw, vif and info are valid (hw->priv is the ath10k device, vif->drv_priv its ath10k_vif); 'changed' is a BSS_CHANGED_* bitmask. Postcondition: the function takes ar->conf_mutex, then for each bit set in 'changed' updates the vif state and issues the matching WMI/firmware operations (IBSS and beaconing control, beacon interval, beacon tx mode and beacon template, mesh SSID, probe response template, DTIM period, AP SSID and hidden_ssid, non-zero BSSID, FTM responder if the service is supported and the value changed, CTS protection and RTS/CTS, slot time, preamble, association (stopping the monitor first if started, then bss_assoc and monitor recalc) or disassociation, txpower, power save, multicast/broadcast rate when the vif has a channel context, management rate recalculation); failures of these calls are only logged as warnings and not propagated; it releases ar->conf_mutex before returning and returns nothing.

functions.name: ath11k_mac_allocate
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ab points to a valid struct ath11k_base whose pdevs array and wmi_ab.wmi array have at least ab->num_radios entries. Postcondition: if ATH11K_FLAG_REGISTERED is set in ab->dev_flags it returns 0 and does nothing; otherwise for each radio i it allocates an ieee80211_hw, initializes the embedded struct ath11k (locks, completions, work items, lists, queues, chainmasks, wmi pointer, lmac id), sets pdevs[i].ar to it and finally returns 0, the caller later releasing them via ath11k_mac_destroy; if any ieee80211_alloc_hw fails it logs a warning, calls ath11k_mac_destroy(ab) to free all hw devices already created (clearing their pdevs[i].ar to NULL) and returns -ENOMEM.

functions.name: ath11k_mac_op_bss_info_changed
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw, vif and info are valid mac80211 objects for an ath11k interface and the caller does not already hold ar->conf_mutex. Postcondition: the function takes ar->conf_mutex and releases it before returning, returns nothing, and for each BSS_CHANGED_* bit set in 'changed' it caches the new value in arvif (beacon interval, DTIM period, SSID, BSSID, txpower, ps, ftm responder, ARP offload) and sends the matching WMI/firmware command or helper update (beacon template, HE/OBSS/BSS-color, TWT, rates, assoc/disassoc, FILS discovery). Failures of individual WMI commands are only logged as warnings and do not stop later bits from being processed.

functions.name: ath11k_qmi_wlanfw_mode_send
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ab points to an initialized ath11k_base whose QMI handle is usable; mode is the firmware mode to request. Postcondition: sends a WLAN mode request over QMI and waits for the response; returns 0 on success, and also returns 0 when mode is ATH11K_FIRMWARE_MODE_OFF and qmi_txn_wait fails with -ENETRESET; otherwise returns the negative errno from qmi_txn_init, qmi_send_request or qmi_txn_wait, or -EINVAL when the response result is not QMI_RESULT_SUCCESS_V01. The transaction is cancelled if the send fails; no memory or lock is returned to the caller.

functions.name: ath12k_core_alloc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is the device to associate with the new object, priv_size is the number of extra private bytes to allocate after struct ath12k_base, and bus is the bus type; the call may sleep (GFP_KERNEL allocations). Postcondition: on success returns a zero-initialized ath12k_base with two single-threaded workqueues (ath12k_wq and ath12k_aux_wq), locks, completions, wait queues, work items and the rx replenish timer initialized, dev and hif.bus set, qmi.num_radios = U8_MAX, single_chip_mlo_support false and device_id 0, owned by the caller; returns NULL if allocating ab or creating the first workqueue fails (nothing leaked), and if creating the aux workqueue fails the first workqueue is destroyed and ab is freed before NULL is returned.

functions.name: ath12k_dbring_buffer_release_event
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ab and ev point to valid objects and ev holds num_buf_release_entry buffer entries and meta entries; it is called in a context where sleeping locks are not required (takes BH spinlocks and the RCU read lock). Postcondition: returns -EINVAL, without touching any buffers, if pdev_id is >= ab->num_radios or if the buffer-entry count differs from the meta-entry count; returns -EINVAL if the pdev is not active under RCU or if module_id is not WMI_DIRECT_BUF_SPECTRAL (the code never assigns a ring, so ring stays NULL and this path is always taken after the module check); the reap loop after that check is thus unreachable in the code as written. In that unreachable path it would look up each released buffer by cookie, remove it from the idr, DMA-unmap it, call the ring handler if set, zero the buffer and replenish it, and return 0. The RCU read lock is released on all paths after being taken.

functions.name: ath12k_dp_tx_htt_tx_filter_setup
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ab is a valid ath12k_base, ring_id indexes a valid entry of ab->hal.srng_list, and htt_tlv_filter points to a valid TX monitor filter description. Postcondition: it allocates an HTC skb and builds an HTT TX ring selection config command in it (message type, pdev id, ring id, swap flags, buffer size, per-type packet filters and TLV masks) and sends it via ath12k_htc_send, returning 0 on success; it returns -ENOMEM if skb allocation fails, and if ath12k_dp_tx_get_ring_id_type or ath12k_htc_send fails it frees the skb with dev_kfree_skb_any and returns that nonzero error code. On success the skb is owned by the HTC layer.

functions.name: ath12k_mac_op_sta_state
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the wiphy lock (lockdep-asserted) and hw, vif and sta are valid mac80211 objects; old_state and new_state describe the state transition being applied to sta. Postcondition: returns 0 on success and stores new_state in ahsta->state; on any failure it returns a negative errno and ahsta->state is not updated. On NOTEXIST->NONE it zeroes ahsta, optionally allocates an ML peer id for an ML sta, creates the DP peer and assigns the default link sta, and on AUTH->ASSOC for an MLD station it selects and activates links. It then moves every link sta in ahsta->links_map through the state change, and on ASSOC->AUTHORIZED for an MLD station it updates the link-active state on each distinct device. On NONE->NOTEXIST it removes the ML station if sta->mlo and deletes the DP peer. Error paths: ML peer id allocation failure, a link-selection error, a link-state error or an assoc-link mismatch jump to exit; the mismatch returns -EINVAL and the ML peer id allocation failure leaves ret as -EINVAL. DP peer creation failure clears the ML peer id (if sta->mlo) and returns its error. Link assignment failure, or a link-state failure on NOTEXIST->NONE, deletes the DP peer, clears the ML peer id (if sta->mlo) and returns the error. The assoc-link mismatch error and the other failures that go straight to exit do not undo the DP peer or ML peer id.

functions.name: ath12k_wifi7_hw_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ab points to a valid ath12k_base whose hw_rev field has been set. Postcondition: if ath12k_wifi7_hw_params contains an entry whose hw_rev equals ab->hw_rev, the function sets ab->hw_params to that entry and ab->ath12k_ops to the Wi-Fi 7 ops, initializes the Wi-Fi 7 HAL, logs the hardware name and returns 0; otherwise it logs an error, leaves ab unchanged and returns -EINVAL.

functions.name: ath12k_pull_reg_chan_list_ext_update_ev
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ab, skb and reg_info are valid, and skb holds a TLV-encoded WMI_REG_CHAN_LIST_CC_EXT_EVENT followed by the rule entries that its counts describe; reg_info is caller-owned and is written. Postcondition: on success it returns 0, reg_info is filled in from the event (counts, alpha2, bandwidths, status code, domain codes, client type), and newly allocated rule arrays are stored in reg_info (reg_rules_2g_ptr and reg_rules_5g_ptr only when their counts are nonzero, plus the 6g ap and client arrays), which the caller must free later; on failure it returns the negative error from TLV parsing (nothing is freed since tb is an error pointer), -EPROTO if the event TLV is missing, -EINVAL if a 2G/5G or 6G rule count exceeds its maximum or the total rule count is zero, or -ENOMEM if any rule-array allocation fails. In every error return after the parse succeeds the temporary TLV array tb is freed, rule arrays already allocated in the call are not freed (leaked), and reg_info may be partially filled; the 5G count is reduced by the number of extra 6 GHz rules that were found in the 5 GHz list.

functions.name: brcmf_cfg80211_start_ap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: wiphy, ndev and settings are valid, ndev belongs to a brcmfmac interface with a vif, and the caller holds whatever locks cfg80211 requires for start_ap. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if no SSID is given and none can be parsed from the beacon head (or its length exceeds the maximum), or, for an mbss vif, if the 11d setting differs from the stored one; otherwise it programs the firmware step by step (regulatory, beacon interval, DTIM, infra, AP or P2P-GO setup, security, SSID, closednet or bss enable) and returns the first negative firmware/security error (closednet or any nonzero error for the closednet iovar), stopping at that step. On success it returns 0 (an unsupported role only triggers WARN_ON and still falls through), updates the beacon management IEs, sets BRCMF_VIF_STATUS_AP_CREATED and turns the carrier on. On any error after the early SSID check, if the vif is not mbss, MPC is re-enabled and ARP/ND offload is restored; the early -EINVAL SSID return skips that cleanup, and the initial value of err is -EPERM but is always overwritten before return. Offloaded PSK/SAE use is recorded in profile->use_fwauth.

functions.name: brcmf_flowring_add_tdls_peer
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: flow points to a valid brcmf_flowring whose tdls_entry list is acyclic and NULL-terminated, and peer points to ETH_ALEN readable bytes; may be called in atomic context. Postcondition: returns nothing; if the GFP_ATOMIC allocation fails, nothing changes; otherwise, if the peer MAC is not already in the list, a new zeroed entry holding it is appended at the tail (or becomes the head of an empty list) and flow->tdls_active is set to true; if the MAC is already present, the new entry is freed, the list is unchanged and tdls_active is left unchanged (not set by this call).

functions.name: brcmf_pcie_download_fw_nvram
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: devinfo has valid chip info (ci), mapped TCM and registers, fw is a valid firmware whose data holds at least 4 bytes and fits in RAM, and nvram is either NULL or a buffer of nvram_len bytes allocated for brcmf_fw_nvram_free. Postcondition: the function halts the ARM, copies the firmware to RAM, and always releases fw; if nvram is non-NULL it copies it to the end of RAM, frees it, and with fwseed also writes a random-seed footer and random bytes before it; it then restarts the ARM and polls up to BRCMF_PCIE_FW_UP_TIMEOUT for the last RAM word to change. It returns the error from brcmf_pcie_enter_download_state if that fails (before fw is released, so fw is not freed then and nvram is not freed), the error from brcmf_pcie_exit_download_state if that fails, -ENODEV if the firmware never changes the shared RAM word or reports an address outside [rambase, rambase+ramsize), and otherwise the result of brcmf_pcie_init_share_ram_info (0 on success).

functions.name: IWL_BIOS_TABLE_LOADER(wrds_table)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function iwl_bios_get_wrds_table(fwrt) (the same pattern generates the other iwl_bios_get_<name> functions, which additionally pass a data pointer through). Precondition: fwrt points to a valid initialized iwl_fw_runtime (and data, where present, is valid for the underlying getter). Postcondition: if fwrt->uefi_tables_lock_status > UEFI_WIFI_GUID_UNLOCKED it first calls the UEFI getter and returns its result when non-negative; otherwise (UEFI skipped, with initial value -ENOENT, or UEFI returned a negative error) it calls the ACPI getter and returns its result, which may be negative or non-negative.

functions.name: iwl_parse_tlv_firmware
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: drv, pieces, capa and usniffer_images are valid pointers, and ucode_raw points to a firmware image whose data and size are readable. Postcondition: returns 0 if the header (minimum length, magic) is valid, every TLV is well formed with no bytes left over, and the usniffer image requirement is met; in that case drv->fw, drv->trans->dbg, capa and pieces are filled from the recognized TLVs, and unknown TLV types are ignored. Otherwise it returns -EINVAL for a short header, bad magic, a TLV length beyond the remaining data, a wrong TLV size, an invalid value (CPU count outside 1..2, paging size too large or not a multiple of FW_PAGING_SIZE, bad calibration, too many stations or links), a duplicate cmd_versions, a missing usniffer image when one was requested without the unified capability, or trailing bytes. It returns -ENOMEM when krealloc, kmemdup or kvmemdup fails. Earlier TLVs may already have been stored, and heap copies (iml, cmd_versions, phy_integration_ver, pc_data, pnvm_data, dbg_mem_tlv) stay owned by drv, capa or pieces even on error.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_load_d3_fw
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the wiphy lock and mvm->mutex, and mvm is a valid iwl_mvm whose hardware is not yet started. Postcondition: the function starts the hardware, loads the WoWLAN ucode and waits for alive, sends the TX antenna config, the PHY DB data and the PHY config command, clears the fw_id_to_mac_id and fw_id_to_link_sta mappings for all stations, and, when the firmware lacks the new station API, adds the aux station MAC_INDEX_AUX, then returns 0. If iwl_trans_start_hw fails it returns its error without stopping the device. If any later step fails (ucode load/alive, TX antenna config, PHY DB send, PHY config command or aux station add) it calls iwl_mvm_stop_device and returns that step's error code, and the station mappings are not initialized unless the failing step was the aux station add.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_mac_setup_register
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mvm is a valid, initialised iwl_mvm whose hw, fw, nvm_data, trans and cfg pointers are set up, and the hardware has not yet been registered with mac80211. Postcondition: fills in the mac80211 hw and wiphy capabilities, features, ciphers, MAC addresses, bands, scan limits and optional WoWLAN support from the firmware capabilities and NVM data. It returns -EINVAL early if the firmware lacks the STA_PM_NOTIF capability but uses the new TX API; it returns the error from iwl_mvm_leds_init if that fails, before TDLS and later setup; otherwise it returns the result of ieee80211_register_hw, calling iwl_mvm_leds_exit first if registration failed, so 0 means success and the hw is registered.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_umac_scan_cfg_channels_v7_6g
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: params, pp and cp are valid, cp->channel_config has room for one entry per accepted channel (up to params->n_channels), and params->channels and params->scan_6ghz_params (when n_6ghz_params > 0) are valid. Postcondition: for each channel in params->channels, except non-PSC channels skipped when params->n_6ghz_params is 0 and params->n_ssids is non-zero, it fills the next cp->channel_config entry (channel number, 6GHz band, iteration count 1, interval 0, flags with the short-SSID/BSSID bitmaps or the force-passive flag, PSC no-listen and unsolicited-probe flags, and psd_20 when version >= 17); it logs a debug message if channels were skipped, and returns the number of channel entries written (ch_cnt), which is at most params->n_channels. It takes no locks and cannot fail with an error code.

functions.name: iwl_mvm_sf_update
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: mvm is a valid initialized iwl_mvm; changed_vif is NULL or a valid vif of mvm, and the caller holds the locking required by iwl_mvm_sf_config and the active-interface iterator. Postcondition: returns 0 without changing anything if the firmware has the SMART_FIFO_OFFLOAD API, or if a HW restart is in progress, or if changed_vif is a P2P device; otherwise it counts active bound interfaces (adding changed_vif when it is non-NULL and not being removed), and chooses new_state: SF_INIT_OFF for 0 macs; for 1 mac, when removing it takes the remaining station vif's state and AP sta from the iteration, otherwise it returns -EINVAL if changed_vif is NULL, else SF_UNINIT for a non-station vif, SF_FULL_ON with sta set to the vif's ap_sta for an associated station with nonzero dtim_period, or SF_INIT_OFF; for 2 or more macs, SF_UNINIT. In all cases except the early returns of 0 or -EINVAL it returns the result of iwl_mvm_sf_config(mvm, sta, new_state), where sta is NULL unless set above.

functions.name: iwl_pcie_irq_msix_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev_id points to the msix_entry of a valid, initialised iwl_trans_pcie device and the function runs in MSI-X interrupt context. Postcondition: it reads and acknowledges the FH and HW cause registers under irq_lock; if both are zero it returns IRQ_NONE without further action. Otherwise it masks the causes, schedules NAPI for rxq 0 or 1 where shared vectors apply, handles the uCode-load/IMR completion, fatal, SW, HW and reset errors, alive, wakeup/Sx, CT-kill and RF-kill causes (waking the relevant waiters and updating stats), clears the IRQ via iwl_pcie_clear_irq only if no NAPI poll was scheduled, releases the sync_cmd lockdep map it acquired, and returns IRQ_HANDLED.

functions.name: mt7615_mac_reset_work
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: work is the reset_work member of a valid mt7615_dev, run in process context with no device mutex held (the function takes it itself). Postcondition: returns void; if MT_MCU_CMD_STOP_PDMA is not set in dev->reset_state it returns immediately without doing anything; otherwise it stops the mac80211 queues of both phys, sets the reset flags, cancels the mac, roc timer and roc work of the phys, disables the tx worker and NAPI, and under the device mutex asks the MCU to stop PDMA, and if the MCU reports reset done it resets DMA, releases tx tokens, reinitialises the token idr, clears the memory range error register and triggers PDMA init and waits for recovery done; it then clears the reset flags, re-enables the tx worker and NAPI and schedules them, wakes the queues, signals reset done and waits for normal state, updates beacons, releases the mutex, and requeues mac_work on the primary phy and on the second phy if present.

functions.name: mt7996_mac_fill_rx
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: skb->data holds a received frame beginning with the hardware RX descriptor (at least the 8 base words, with optional groups 4/1/2/3/5 selected by rxd1), skb->cb holds the mt76_rx_status (its aggr flag is saved as hw_aggr and the area is then zeroed), the phy for the band index in rxd1 exists, and dev, q and info are valid. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, with status filled in (phy_idx, wcid, freq, band, flags, IV, timestamp/ampdu_ref, chains/chain_signal and rate info, amsdu flags, and aggr/qos_ctl/seqno when a wcid exists, the frame is QoS data and hw_aggr is unset), skb->ip_summed possibly set to CHECKSUM_UNNECESSARY, and skb->data pulled past the descriptor and padding so it points to the 802.11 frame (mac header set) or, with header translation, to the 802.3 frame with RX_FLAG_8023 set. It returns -EINVAL if the phy is not running, on an AMSDU error, header translation together with the CM bit, a missing sband channel list, a max-length error, any descriptor group extending past skb->len, a fragment with a non-unicast address, or failure of mt7996_reverse_frag0_hdr_trans. It returns the negative value from mt7996_mac_fill_rx_rate if that fails. On error returns, status, phy->rx_ampdu_ts/ampdu_ref and the mt76 poll list may already have been modified, but skb->data has not yet been pulled, because the only error return after the pull is none. No lock or reference is taken or released, and the caller keeps ownership of skb.

functions.name: mt7996_sta_state
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw, vif and sta are valid mac80211 objects and the caller is in the mac80211 sta_state callback context, with old_state and new_state being the station's previous and requested states. Postcondition: for NOTEXIST->NONE it returns the result of mt7996_mac_sta_add; for NONE->NOTEXIST it calls mt7996_mac_sta_remove and then returns 0 because no event matches; for AUTH->ASSOC it updates the active links and returns the result of mt7996_mac_sta_event with the ASSOC event; for ASSOC->AUTHORIZED it returns the result of mt7996_mac_sta_event with the AUTHORIZE event; for ASSOC->AUTH it returns the result of mt7996_mac_sta_event with the DISASSOC event; any other transition returns 0 without further action.

functions.name: fe25519_scalar_product
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h and f point to arrays of 10 int32_t limbs (f readable, h writable; they may alias since f is fully read before h is written), and n is a uint32_t multiplier.
