Postcondition: h holds the 10 limbs of f multiplied by n modulo 2^255-19, computed by forming 64-bit products f[i]*n, carrying odd limbs 1,3,5,7 and limb 9 (the carry from limb 9 is multiplied by 19 and added to limb 0) with 25-bit rounding, then even limbs 0,2,4,6,8 with 26-bit rounding, and truncating each limb to int32_t; nothing is returned and no memory other than h[0..9] is modified.

functions.name: fe25519_scalar_product
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h points to writable storage for 5 uint64_t limbs, f points to 5 readable limbs (radix 2^51), and n is a 32-bit unsigned multiplier; h may alias f. Postcondition: h holds the 5 limbs of f*n reduced modulo 2^255-19: limbs h[1..4] are masked to 51 bits, and the final carry out of limb 4 is multiplied by 19 and added into h[0], which can therefore slightly exceed 2^51; nothing is returned and no memory is retained.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Takes no arguments and needs the libsodium secretstream and random functions to work. It runs the secretstream xchacha20poly1305 self-test: push and pull round-trips, tag, rekey and counter-overflow checks, failure cases that must return -1, and constant checks. Each check is an assert, so a failed check aborts the program. It frees every buffer it allocated, prints "OK\n" and returns 0.

functions.name: fman_dtsec_get_stat_counter
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: regs points to a valid mapped dTSEC register block that can be read with ioread32be. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit value read from the statistic counter register (TR64 through TDRP) selected by reg_name, converted from big-endian, or 0 without reading any register if reg_name is not one of the handled counters; no locks or references are taken, and the registers are not modified by the function.

functions.name: MatchTableSet
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h_FmPcd, p_CcNode and p_CcNodeParam are valid non-NULL pointers, p_CcNode is a freshly allocated CC node, and p_CcNodeParam describes the extraction, keys and next-engine parameters. Postcondition: it returns E_OK after the node is fully set up (global mask, spinlock, parse code, MURAM key-match, AD and optional stats/FLR/TmpAd tables allocated and filled, node registered in the prev-node lists of next CC nodes and manips, required actions set, PCD locks taken and released). On errors from invalid MURAM handle (E_INVALID_HANDLE), allocation failure (E_NO_MEMORY), invalid parameters (E_INVALID_VALUE/E_INVALID_STATE/E_INVALID_SELECTION), or any error from a parameter check, shadow calculation, stats allocation, manip check or SetRequiredAction, it returns that error. Except for the invalid-MURAM-handle case, failures delete the node with DeleteNode, or FM_PCD_MatchTableDelete in the late paths. If FmPcdLockTryLockAll fails it deletes the node and returns E_BUSY. On SetRequiredAction failure it unlocks all PCD locks before returning the error.

functions.name: BuildSchemeRegs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_Scheme (with a valid h_FmPcd), p_SchemeParams and p_SchemeRegs are valid non-NULL pointers, and p_SchemeParams holds a fully filled scheme description. Postcondition: p_SchemeRegs is zeroed and then filled with the scheme registers (mode, match vector, policer profile command, CC base/bits, storage profile, hash/extract/default-value, generic extract, fqid base registers); p_Scheme is updated (matchVector, netEnvId, ccUnits, directPlcr, relativeProfileId, nextRelativePlcrProfile, numOfProfiles, vspe, extractedOrs, bitOffsetInPlcrProfile, orderedArray, nextEngine, doneAction); and E_OK is returned. On validation failure it returns an error and stops early: E_INVALID_VALUE for out-of-range or malformed values such as distinction units, baseFqid, shifts, numOfProfiles, hash parameters or masks, E_INVALID_STATE for an invalid next engine, a failed unit-vector lookup, shared or indirect profile misuse, an invalid shared profile or bypass conflicts, E_NOT_SUPPORTED for an unsupported next engine or extraction, E_INVALID_SELECTION for bad extract or default types, E_FULL when generic registers run out, E_NO_MEMORY when the temporary extract array cannot be allocated, or the error code propagated from FmPcdCcGetGrpParams or FmPcdPlcrGetAbsoluteIdByProfileParams. The temporary extract array is freed on most error paths after it is allocated, but not on every one (e.g. the invalid-selection default of the extract switch and the later extracted-OR checks), and no locks or references are taken for the caller.

functions.name: BuildSchemeRegs
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_Scheme, p_SchemeParams and p_SchemeRegs are valid pointers, and p_Scheme->h_FmPcd is a valid PCD handle. Postcondition: p_SchemeRegs is zeroed and then filled with the scheme registers (mode, NIA, policer-profile command, CC base, match vector, storage profile, hash/extract/mask/default/generic-extract registers, extracted-OR generic registers and base FQID), and p_Scheme (netEnvId, matchVector, ccUnits, profile fields, orderedArray, extractedOrs, nextEngine, doneAction) is updated. It returns E_OK on success. Otherwise it returns an error: E_INVALID_VALUE, E_INVALID_STATE, E_NOT_SUPPORTED, E_INVALID_SELECTION, E_NO_MEMORY, E_FULL, or the error from FmPcdCcGetGrpParams or FmPcdPlcrGetAbsoluteIdByProfileParams. The temporary extracts array allocated for the hash path is freed on success and on most errors, but not on the early E_INVALID_SELECTION returns in the extract-type default case or the dflts switch default, and not on later errors after it is freed.

functions.name: BuildHmct
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_Manip, p_FmPcdManipParams (header-manipulation union) and p_DestHmct must be valid, p_DestHmct must be large enough for the command table, p_DestData must point to sufficient MURAM scratch space whenever an L2 insert, IP insert, VLAN DSCP table, IPv4 ID update or IP replace command is used, and the user data pointers must be valid. Postcondition: the remove, insert, field-update and custom commands requested in the params are written in that order into the HMCD table at p_DestHmct (auxiliary data is copied into p_DestData and referenced by MURAM-relative pointers), and E_OK is returned. The HMCD_LAST bit is set on the last command word, unless a next header manip exists, is of header type and does not require reparsing, in which case no last bit is set and, if new is true, the next manip is marked via MANIP_UPDATE_UNIFIED_POSITION and this manip's unifiedPosition becomes e_MANIP_UNIFIED_FIRST. Errors: E_NOT_SUPPORTED for an unsupported remove-by-header type or L2 option, an unsupported insert-by-header type or L2 insert option, or an invalid IP-replace type. E_INVALID_SELECTION for an unknown fieldUpdateParams.type or customParams.type. On an error return, command words already written remain written. For generic insert with size not a multiple of 4, a temporary zero-padded buffer is allocated and freed before return.

functions.name: fman_kg_build_scheme
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: params points to a valid fman_kg_scheme_params and scheme_regs to writable storage for a fman_kg_scheme_regs; params->extract_params.gen_extract points to at least gen_extract_num entries and masks has at least masks_num entries. Postcondition: scheme_regs is zeroed and then filled progressively (mode, match vector, default values, known-field command and defaults, generic extract registers, mask select/bit-mask registers, FQB, hash config, policer profile, and the CC bit-select and packet counter registers if applicable) and 0 is returned; it returns -EINVAL, leaving scheme_regs only partially filled, if the NIA for next_engine/action is invalid, gen_extract_num exceeds FM_KG_NUM_OF_GENERIC_REGS, a hash-type generic extract has size 0 or above FMAN_KG_SCH_GEN_SIZE_MAX, masks_num exceeds FM_KG_EXTRACT_MASKS_NUM, base_fqid does not fit in 24 bits, the hash is used and its mask exceeds 24 bits or its shift_r exceeds FMAN_KG_SCH_HASH_HSHIFT_MAX, or policer profile generation is not bypassed and its shift exceeds FMAN_KG_SCH_PP_SHIFT_MAX.

functions.name: FM_PORT_Config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_FmPortParams points to a valid parameter structure (baseAddr, portType, portId, h_Fm, liodnBase, independentModeEnable and the type-specific rx/nonRx params filled in) and the BMI registers at baseAddr are readable. Postcondition: allocates a t_FmPort and its t_FmPortDriverParam, fills them with defaults, resource counts and register-derived FIFO settings, sets the name and creates a spinlock, then returns the port as a handle owned by the caller; returns NULL (reporting E_NO_MEMORY if either allocation fails) when allocation fails, the port type is invalid (in either type switch), Sprint of the name returns 0, or XX_InitSpinlock returns NULL, and in all failure cases after the allocations frees both the driver parameters and the port structure.

functions.name: FmHandleIpcMsgCB
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h_Fm is a valid t_Fm handle, p_Msg points to a t_FmIpcMsg of msgLength bytes (at least sizeof(uint32_t)) whose body matches the command in msgId, p_Reply has room for FM_IPC_MAX_REPLY_SIZE bytes, and p_ReplyLength is writable. Postcondition: the reply buffer is zeroed and *p_ReplyLength set to 0, then the command in msgId is dispatched and the reply body, reply error field and *p_ReplyLength are filled for commands that return data (a length of 0 for those that do not). The function returns E_OK for handled commands, including ones whose failure is only carried in p_IpcReply->error or merely reported (SET_MAC_MAX_FRAME, ECC enable/disable, SET_NUM_OF_FMAN_CTRL). FM_VSP_SET_PORT_WINDOW (SetVSPWindow) and FM_SET_CONG_GRP_PFC_PRIO (FmSetCongestionGroupPFCpriority) return that call's error directly without setting a reply length, when DPAA_VERSION >= 11. FM_MASTER_IS_ALIVE returns E_INVALID_STATE if the module name Sprint gives the wrong length, or E_NOT_AVAILABLE if the IPC session cannot be created. A NULL h_Fm returns E_INVALID_HANDLE, msgLength < 4 returns E_INVALID_VALUE, and an unknown msgId returns E_INVALID_SELECTION with *p_ReplyLength 0.

functions.name: FmSetNumOfOpenDmas
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: h_Fm is a valid t_Fm handle, hardwarePortId is in 1..63, and p_NumOfOpenDmas and p_NumOfExtraOpenDmas point to valid bytes holding the requested values. Postcondition: a guest with no mapped registers but an IPC session sends the request to the master and returns the transport error if sending fails, E_INVALID_VALUE if the reply length is not sizeof(uint32_t), otherwise the master's reply error; without IPC, a guest returns E_NOT_SUPPORTED (always when FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS is defined, else when registers are not mapped or majorRev < 6); a guest with mapped registers and majorRev >= 6 (non FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS build) reads or writes the port DMA registers (on zero request it stores the register values into *p_NumOfOpenDmas and *p_NumOfExtraOpenDmas) and then continues with the common path below. The common path, for the master and for that guest, reads the current values when !initialConfig, raises extraOpenDmasPoolSize if the requested extra count exceeds the current one, and returns E_NOT_AVAILABLE when the accumulated open-DMA total would exceed the limit (the FM max when FM_HAS_TOTAL_DMAS and majorRev < 6; DMA_THRESH_MAX_COMMQ+1 for majorRev >= 6 otherwise), leaving accumulatedNumOfOpenDmas unchanged. Otherwise it updates accumulatedNumOfOpenDmas, writes the port's DMA registers and returns E_OK; under FM_NO_GUARANTEED_RESET_VALUES a zero request reads the registers, records them in the pool and accumulated totals, outputs them via the pointers and returns E_OK. The caller keeps ownership of all memory.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the process command-line arguments of a zdb invocation (options followed by a pool or dataset target and optional arguments), and the process runs in a state where the libzpool kernel emulation can be initialised. Postcondition: it parses options, initialises the kernel emulation, opens the target pool, objset or bookmark, dumps what was requested (or copies an object with -r, or reads blocks with -R), then releases the objset or spa, the DDT and the FUID table, flushes the debug buffer and calls kernel_fini if initialised, and returns the error code: 0 on success, 2 for a non-numeric objset ID with -N, the error from dump_label or dump_path (-O), a copy error from zdb_copy_object, or 3 if corruption was found and error was 0. Many failures (usage errors, open failures, bad ranges) never return because they call usage(), fatal() or zdb_exit().

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv form a valid argument vector for zdb (options followed by a pool, dataset or path target and any further arguments), and the ZFS userland library can be initialised. Postcondition: after parsing the options (bad option values or missing arguments call usage(), a failing -o tunable calls zdb_exit(1); fatal() is used for internal and open errors), main initialises the kernel emulation, opens the pool, dataset or objset (or dumps a label, cachefile, embedded block, path, bookmark or backup), performs the requested dump, copy or block-read action, then at the fini label cleans up the DDT, closes the objset or spa, destroys the FUID table, dumps the debug buffer and calls kernel_fini if kernel_init was done. It returns 0 on success, an error code (for example 2 when -N is given with a non-numeric objset ID, or the error from dump_label or dump_path), or 3 if corruption was found and the error was 0.

functions.name: zfs_for_each
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: g_zfs is a valid libzfs handle, callback is a valid function, argv holds argc dataset names or paths when argc > 0, and sortcol/proplist describe the sort columns and properties to keep. Postcondition: it collects matching datasets into an AVL tree (all datasets when argc == 0, otherwise those named in argv, setting the result to 1 for each argument that cannot be opened and OR-ing in zfs_callback results), calls callback(handle, data) on each collected node in sorted order and OR-s the return values into the result, then removes every node, closes its handle, frees the node, destroys the AVL tree and pool, and returns the OR-accumulated result (0 if all steps succeeded, nonzero otherwise); allocation failures for the pool, tree or walk call nomem() and do not return normally here.

functions.name: zfs_do_change_key
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command-line arguments of the 'zfs change-key' subcommand and the global g_zfs library handle is initialized. Postcondition: returns 0 after freeing the property list and closing the dataset handle if the key rewrap succeeds (after optionally loading the key with -l when it is not yet available); returns 1 (freeing props) if an -o property fails to parse; returns -1 after freeing props and closing the handle if zfs_crypto_load_key or zfs_crypto_rewrap fails; for an invalid option, -i combined with -o properties, a missing or extra dataset argument, or a dataset that cannot be opened, it calls usage(B_FALSE), which does not return, so props (and in the last case nothing else) is not freed by the function.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process arguments of zinject and libzfs and /dev/zfs are usable. Postcondition: opens libzfs and the ZFS device (returning 1 if either fails); with no arguments it prints all registered handlers and returns 0; otherwise it parses the options and returns 0 for -h, 1 for invalid option values, a missing option operand, an option combination that is incompatible with logical or device errors, or a failed translate/open/unmount step, and 2 for an unknown option or wrong argument counts and incompatible-option combinations. With -c it returns the result of cancel_all_handlers() or cancel_handler(id) directly, and with -d plus -A it returns the result of perform_action() directly. Otherwise it optionally unmounts the dataset (-m), registers the injection handler, remounts the dataset if it was unmounted, and returns register_handler's result or 1 if the remount fails. libzfs_fini is called on every path except the -c and -A direct returns, which skip it.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the zinject command line, and libzfs and the ZFS device are usable. Postcondition: it opens libzfs and /dev/zfs (returns 1 if either fails); with no arguments it prints the registered handlers and returns 0; it parses the options and returns 1 for an invalid option value or an incompatible/invalid combination, 2 for usage errors (unknown option, extraneous or missing arguments, incompatible options), and 0 for -h. For -c it returns the result of cancel_all_handlers or cancel_handler, and for -d with -A it returns the result of perform_action, without calling libzfs_fini. Otherwise it fills the injection record from the device, raw, panic, import/export delay, ignored-writes, null or object mode, optionally unmounts the dataset when -m is given (returning 1 on failure), calls register_handler, remounts the dataset if it was unmounted, and returns that result (the register_handler status, or 1 if the remount fails, 0 if it succeeds). On every return path except the -c and -A cases it calls libzfs_fini(g_zfs) first.

functions.name: show_import
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: config is a pool config nvlist from an import scan containing pool name, guid, state and a vdev tree with vdev stats (the code verify()s these lookups); report_error says whether errors may be reported. Postcondition: if the import status is not ZPOOL_STATUS_OK and report_error is false, nothing is printed and the status code (reason) is returned; otherwise the function prints the pool name, id, state, status text, an action message depending on vdev state and reason, the optional comment, a see-also message, and the vdev config (including a note for a bad GUID sum), then returns 0.

functions.name: zstream_do_dump
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv describe the command line (options -v, -C, -d, optionally followed by a send-stream file name) and, when no file is named, standard input is a redirected non-terminal ZFS send stream. Postcondition: it parses the options, opens the file or uses stdin as send_stream, then reads and prints every record of the stream (with optional checksum verification, byte-swapping and block dumps), frees its buffer, prints a summary of record counts, payload sizes, header overhead and stream length, and returns 0 when the stream ends; it calls exit(1) instead if the file cannot be opened, stdin is a terminal, the first record has a bad magic number, a record type is >= DRR_NUMTYPES, or DRR_NUMTYPES is reached; a bad option calls zstream_usage().

functions.name: zstream_do_recompress
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds options (optional -l level) followed by exactly one operand naming a compression type ("off" or a zio_compress_table name with a compress function), and stdin is a redirected (non-terminal) ZFS send stream. Postcondition: each record is read from stdin, WRITE payloads that are not encrypted are decompressed and recompressed with the chosen type (stored uncompressed if the rounded compressed size is not smaller than the logical size), checksums are recomputed, and records are written to stdout via dump_record; the loop ends at end of input or when dump_record returns nonzero, then buffers and the abd, zio, zstd and fletcher subsystems are released and 0 is returned. It exits the process with status 1 on a wrong argument count (via zstream_usage), a terminal stdin, deduplicated (WRITE_BYREF) records or stdout EOF/error, 2 for an invalid compression type, 3 for an invalid stream compression type and 4 for a decompression failure; VERIFY failures abort on malformed record ordering and an unknown record type trips an assert.

functions.name: ztest_split_pool
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global ztest state (ztest_shared, ztest_spa) is initialised and the caller holds neither ztest_vdev_lock nor the SCL_VDEV config lock. Postcondition: returns nothing; it returns early without changes if zo_mmp_test is set, or if zs_mirrors < 3 or zo_raid_children > 1 (releasing ztest_vdev_lock). Otherwise it destroys any old "splitp" pool and builds a split config from the first child of each mirror top-level vdev, with log and hole vdevs replaced by hole entries. It then calls spa_vdev_split_mirror under ztest_name_lock and frees all temporary nvlists and the schild array. The SCL_VDEV lock is released before the split. If the split returns 0, it prints the pool stats, increments zs_splits and decrements zs_mirrors; any error is ignored. ztest_vdev_lock is always released before return.

functions.name: ztest_fault_inject
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ztest is set up with a valid open pool (ztest_spa), and the caller does NOT hold ztest_vdev_lock; the function takes it itself, and zd and id are unused. Postcondition: returns nothing, with ztest_vdev_lock released and both path buffers freed; it does nothing if device removal is active, raidz expansion is in progress, the pool is not yet scrubbed, or (for l2cache) there are no cache devices. Otherwise it may mark a random data, slog or cache vdev unreadable, unwritable or close its fd, may offline or online it, and, if maxfaults is non-zero and the target file opens, writes a bad 8-byte word at many random offsets in a random leaf device file, stopping early if zs_mirrors changes. A failed pwrite calls fatal(). If any corruption was injected and raid expansion testing is enabled, it starts a scrub and, if that starts without error, waits until scrubbing finishes.

functions.name: htonll
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; this inline definition is compiled only for little-endian, non-LP64, non-_STANDALONE builds, and n may be any 64-bit unsigned value. Postcondition: the function returns htonl applied to the low 32 bits of n, shifted into the high 32 bits, plus htonl applied to the high 32 bits of n, which is n with its 8 bytes in reverse order; it has no side effects, allocates no memory and takes no locks.

functions.name: ntohll
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; this inline definition is compiled only for little-endian, non-LP64, non-_STANDALONE builds, and n may be any 64-bit unsigned value. Postcondition: the function returns ntohl applied to the low 32 bits of n, shifted into the high 32 bits, plus ntohl applied to the high 32 bits of n, which is n with its 8 bytes in reverse order; it has no side effects, allocates no memory and takes no locks.

functions.name: zfs_crypto_rewrap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: zhp is a valid open dataset handle and raw_props is either NULL or an nvlist of key-change properties (used only when inheritkey is B_FALSE); the caller keeps ownership of zhp and raw_props. Postcondition: returns 0 on success; otherwise returns a nonzero errno-style value (EINVAL if encryption is not enabled, the dataset is unencrypted, it is a clone, the properties are invalid, a keyformat is missing for a new encryption root, inheritkey is requested on a non-encryption root or on a root dataset, or the parent is unencrypted; ENOENT if the parent handle cannot be opened; EACCES if the parent's key (inherit case) or the dataset's own key is not loaded; or the error from a failed helper call or lzc_change_key). Every failure calls zfs_error with EZFS_CRYPTOFAILED and the errbuf message, with auxiliary messages for the specific cases (and for EPERM, EINVAL and EACCES from the ioctl). On every path it closes the parent handle, frees the internally built props nvlist and frees the wrapping key data, when each is non-NULL.

functions.name: check_status
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: config is a valid pool config nvlist that contains the version, vdev tree (with vdev stats) and pool state entries (the fnvlist lookups abort otherwise), plus the load-info, feature or enabled-feature entries when the paths below need them; erratap is writable whenever errata is present; compat may be NULL; isimport selects import or status semantics. Postcondition: returns the first matching zpool_status_t in a fixed priority order: RESILVERING, REBUILDING, REBUILD_SCRUB, the HOSTID_* codes, VERSION_NEWER, UNSUP_FEAT_WRITE/READ, BAD_GUID_SUM, IO_FAILURE_MMP/CONTINUE/WAIT, BAD_LOG, FAULTED/MISSING/CORRUPT_LABEL_NR, CORRUPT_POOL, CORRUPT_DATA, FAULTED/MISSING/CORRUPT_LABEL_R, FAILING_DEV, OFFLINE_DEV, REMOVED_DEV, NON_NATIVE_ASHIFT, ERRATA (and only then *erratap is set to the errata value), VERSION_OLDER, COMPATIBILITY_ERR, FEAT_DISABLED, INCOMPATIBLE_FEAT; it returns ZPOOL_STATUS_OK if nothing applies, including when the version is older but compat is "legacy". It acquires or releases no locks or references and does not free or take ownership of the config.

functions.name: zfs_setproctitle
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fmt is NULL or a printf-style format string with matching variadic arguments; zfs_setproctitle_init() should have been called so SPT.base is set. Postcondition: returns no value; if SPT.base is NULL it prints a one-time warning (setting SPT.warned) and does nothing else; otherwise it formats the title into a local buffer ("progname: " plus the formatted text, the formatted text alone if fmt starts with '-' (that '-' is skipped), or SPT.arg0 if fmt is NULL); if the resulting length is <= 0 it stores errno in SPT.error and returns without touching the title area; otherwise it zeroes the title area (all of SPT.base..SPT.end on the first call and sets SPT.reset, afterwards only min(sizeof buf, SPT.end - SPT.base) bytes), copies min(len, min(sizeof buf, SPT.end - SPT.base) - 1) bytes of the title to SPT.base (the zeroing leaves it NUL-terminated), and then writes '.' at SPT.nul if the title ends before SPT.nul, or, if it ends exactly at SPT.nul with at least one byte of room left before SPT.end, writes ' ' at SPT.nul and a NUL after it.

functions.name: dmu_read_pages
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ma holds count (>=1) consecutive pages of one VM object, the requested pages being exbusied and invalid (or bogus_page), last_size <= PAGE_SIZE, and rbehind and rahead point to valid ints. Postcondition: if dmu_buf_hold_array fails it returns that error code with nothing else done (*rbehind and *rahead unchanged); otherwise it fills the optional read-behind pages before ma[0], copies the DMU buffer data into each non-bogus page of ma (zero-filling the tail of a partial last page, marking pages valid), fills the optional read-ahead pages after ma[count-1], stops each read-around loop at the first page that cannot be grabbed or is already valid, sets *rbehind and *rahead to the number of pages actually filled, releases the buffer array held under FTAG, and returns 0.

functions.name: zfs_setattr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: zp is a znode with a vnode, vap points to a vattr_t (possibly the head of an xvattr_t) whose va_mask selects the attributes to change, cr is the caller's credential, and the caller holds no ZFS teardown lock on zp's filesystem. Postcondition: returns 0 immediately without doing anything if va_mask is 0; otherwise returns EINVAL (AT_NOSET set, ephemeral ids or xvattr on a filesystem without fuids, size change on a non-regular non-FIFO file, invalid project id, or a failed rename-style lookup), EISDIR (size change on a directory), EPERM (immutable file with a forbidden change, XAT_REPARSE requested, or restricted ACL mode on a non-trivial ACL), EOVERFLOW (timestamp too large), EOPNOTSUPP (project quota unsupported or wrong file type), EROFS (read-only filesystem), EDQUOT (new owner, group or project over quota), or any error from zfs_enter_verify_zp, zfs_freesp, the secpolicy checks, sa_lookup, zfs_zget, vn_lock, zfs_acl_chmod_setattr, dmu_tx_assign, sa_add_projid, zfs_setattr_dir or zil_commit. On success the requested attributes are applied to zp, and to its xattr directory znode where uid, gid or project id change, in one committed transaction and logged to the ZIL, with a final zil_commit when the objset sync is ZFS_SYNC_ALWAYS. On the error paths after the transaction is created it is aborted, the ACL and fuid info are freed, and the locked xattr znode reference is released with vput; the ZFS enter lock is released on every return after it was taken.

functions.name: define_ddi_strtox(
functions.prose_contract: Generated functions ddi_strtol, ddi_strtoull and ddi_strtoll(str, endptr, base, result) come from this macro. Precondition: str is a valid NUL-terminated string, result is a valid writable pointer, and endptr is either NULL or writable. Postcondition: leading whitespace (space, tab, newline, CR, formfeed) is skipped; if the remaining string is empty it returns EINVAL. An optional '-' or '+' sign is consumed. With base 0, the base is detected from str[0..2] (not from the position after whitespace or sign): '0x' followed by a hex digit gives base 16, '0' followed by an octal digit gives base 8, and any other string starting with '0' returns EINVAL; otherwise base 10. Digits valid in the base are accumulated, and the first overflow detected by value wrapping returns ERANGE, leaving *result and *endptr unchanged. Otherwise *result is set to the value, negated if a minus sign was seen (using the wrapping arithmetic of the value type), *endptr (if non-NULL) is set to the first unparsed character, and 0 is returned. It does not check that any digit was consumed, and the overflow check is unreliable for signed types.

functions.name: zfsctl_snapshot_mount
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path points to a valid automount trigger dentry on a ZFS ctldir snapshot directory, and the caller may sleep. Postcondition: returns EISDIR if the dentry has no inode; returns the error from zfs_enter if the filesystem cannot be entered; returns the error from zfsctl_snapshot_name or get_root_path if either fails (zfs_teardown released first). Otherwise it releases the zfsvfs teardown lock (zfs_exit) and looks for an existing snapshot entry by name. If one exists, it waits until that entry's pending mount finishes and returns the first attempt's recorded mount error (0 on success), dropping its reference. If none exists, it creates a pending entry and runs the mount helper. If the helper fails with the MOUNT_BUSY bit, it returns 0; if it fails otherwise, it logs the error and returns EISDIR. In both failure cases the entry is removed, the recorded error is stored and waiters are woken. If the helper succeeds, it follows down into the mounted snapshot; if that succeeds it sets z_parent, marks the mount MNT_SHRINKABLE, fills the entry and schedules the expiry timer, else it removes the entry; the function then returns 0. Waiters are woken and the entry reference released. On every path after allocation, the three local buffers full_name, full_path and options are freed, and zfs_snapshot_lock is not held at return.

functions.name: arc_read
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: spa, bp (non-hole, non-redacted; embedded only of data type), zb and arc_flags are valid, arc_flags includes ARC_FLAG_WAIT or ARC_FLAG_NOWAIT unless ARC_FLAG_CACHED_ONLY applies or the block is served from the cache, and the caller holds no ARC hash lock. Postcondition: returns 0 or an errno. On a cache hit with done set and no NO_BUF it allocates a buf, sets ARC_FLAG_CACHED and returns 0, or EIO (an ECKSUM from buf allocation is converted to EIO, with an error log and ereport unless speculative) or another buf-allocation error, destroying the buf and dropping the reference on failure. In every such case done, if set, is called once with that buf (NULL on error), and the hash lock is released. On a hit on a block with I/O in progress it returns 0 for non-waiting callers, or the shared I/O's error for ARC_FLAG_WAIT callers, after queueing or waiting on a callback. ENOENT is returned for ARC_FLAG_CACHED_ONLY on a miss or in-progress I/O. ECKSUM is returned if the blkptr fails verification. On a miss it issues an L2ARC or normal read, returning 0 for NOWAIT or the zio_wait result for WAIT. If pio is set and rc is nonzero on the done path, an error null zio is attached to pio. Except on the restart path, it adds to the read history for non-embedded bps and unmarks fstrans before returning.

functions.name: dmu_redact_snap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: snapname names a snapshot in a pool that can be held, redactnvl is an nvlist whose pair names are the snapshots to redact with, and redactbook is a bookmark short name. Postcondition: it returns 0 when the redaction list was created or resumed and perform_redaction succeeded, otherwise perform_redaction's error; other errors are the dsl_pool_hold error (returned immediately, nothing to release), the dsl_dataset_hold_flags error, EINVAL (target is not a snapshot, cannot open its objset, or a listed snapshot is not before it), EALREADY (target or a listed snapshot already has the redacted-datasets feature active), ENAMETOOLONG (bookmark name too long; pool hold, name buffer and args are released and it returns at once), EEXIST (existing bookmark without a redaction list, or an already complete one), EIO (cannot hold the existing redaction list), ESRCH (existing list does not match the snapshot set), or the dsl_bookmark_create_redacted error. On every path after the pool hold, it frees the name buffer and args, releases the redaction list and dataset holds, releases the pool hold if still held, and releases the target dataset; on the main path it starts traverse and merge threads and destroys the merge queue after perform_redaction.

functions.name: dnode_free_range
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dn is a valid dnode and tx a valid assigned transaction; the caller does not hold dn_struct_rwlock (it is taken as writer internally) or dn_mtx; len may be DMU_OBJECT_END, meaning free from off to the end of the object (truncate). Postcondition: returns nothing; partial head and tail blocks of the range are zeroed via dnode_partial_zero (only if dirty or on disk), and the level-1 indirect blocks covering the range are dirtied when dn_nlevels > 1. The whole-block range [blkid, blkid+nblks) is then recorded in dn_free_ranges for the tx's txg (created if absent), in-core dbufs in that range are freed via dbuf_free_range, and the dnode is marked dirty. It returns early without recording anything when the start is past dn_maxblkid, when a non-power-of-two block size has off >= blksz (and not a whole-block free), or when after head/tail zeroing no whole block remains (len == 0) or the remaining range starts past dn_maxblkid.

functions.name: spa_vdev_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: spa is a writeable pool, the caller holds the namespace lock, guid names the vdev to attach to (or matches none), and nvroot describes the new device tree. Postcondition: it enters the vdev config transaction and returns 0 after attaching the single new leaf vdev to oldvd (mirror, replacing or spare parent, or the raidz vdev for expansion), dirtying the config and DTLs, scheduling a resilver/rebuild or raidz expansion, notifying events, committing via spa_vdev_exit and logging history. Otherwise it returns, via spa_vdev_exit (which frees newrootvd where one exists), one of: ZFS_ERR_CHECKPOINT_EXISTS, ZFS_ERR_DISCARDING_CHECKPOINT, ENOTSUP, ZFS_ERR_RESILVER_IN_PROGRESS, ZFS_ERR_REBUILD_IN_PROGRESS, ZFS_ERR_DEVRM_IN_PROGRESS, ENODEV (guid not found), ZFS_ERR_RAIDZ_EXPAND_IN_PROGRESS, EINVAL (bad nvroot), the vdev_create error, EEXIST, EOVERFLOW (new device too small), ZFS_ERR_ASHIFT_MISMATCH, ENXIO, or EADDRINUSE; on these failure paths the tree is not modified.

functions.name: vdev_prop_get
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vd is a valid vdev with a valid spa and meta objset, innvl is a valid nvlist, outnvl is a valid nvlist for output, and the caller does not hold spa_props_lock (the function takes and releases it). Postcondition: returns EINVAL, without taking the lock, if innvl lacks the vdev GUID or the vdev has no property object; otherwise it takes spa_props_lock, adds each requested property (or, when no property list is given, each string property in the vdev's MOS property ZAP) to outnvl, releases the lock, and returns 0. In the requested-list mode an unknown property name gives ENOENT, which stops the loop and is converted to 0 on return. Any other error stops processing and is returned: a zap_length/zap_lookup/vdev_prop_get_* failure other than ENOENT, EINVAL for an integer-valued user property, or the error that ended the ZAP cursor iteration in all-properties mode. The ENOENT that normally ends the cursor iteration becomes 0. Temporary string buffers are freed.

functions.name: MUL_x2_DEFINE(x)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function mul_x2_<x>(void), defined by the MUL_x2_DEFINE(x) macro for a constant byte x. Precondition: AVX512 is usable, MUL2_SETUP() has loaded the constants into zmm29, zmm30 and zmm31, and zmm21 and zmm22 hold the two input vectors. Postcondition: zmm23 and zmm24 hold the GF(2^8) product (reduction polynomial 0x11d) of each byte of zmm21 and zmm22 by the constant x, computed as a sum of doubled copies. zmm21, zmm22 and the scratch registers zmm25 to zmm28 are clobbered. It returns nothing and touches no memory.

functions.name: get_special_prop
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: state is a valid lua state, ds is a held dataset, dsname is its name, and zfs_prop is a property handled by special-case lookup or by the dsl_dir fallback. Postcondition: on success it pushes two values on the lua stack (the property value as number, string or index string depending on the property type, then the source via get_prop_src) and returns 0; for ZFS_PROP_CLONES it pushes the clones table and nil instead and returns 0 on success. On failure it returns the non-zero error from the underlying lookup (e.g. ENOENT for a missing ivset guid or resume token, or the error from zfs_prop_index_to_string for an index property) and pushes nothing. In every path the temporary strval buffer is freed.

functions.name: zfs_ioc_recv_impl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tofs, tosnap, begin_record, read_bytes, errflags and errors point to valid storage, input_fd is a descriptor number, and recvprops, localprops, hidden_args and origin are each either NULL or valid. Postcondition: it zeroes *read_bytes and *errflags, sets *errors to a newly allocated nvlist and takes a reference on the input file; if the file cannot be obtained it returns EBADF. If dmu_recv_begin fails it releases the file, frees the saved property lists and returns that error. Otherwise it sets the received, local and inherited properties and receives the stream, then ends the receive (suspending and resuming or ending the filesystem or zvol), applies delayed properties on success, merges the delayed properties back into the input lists and sets *read_bytes to the bytes consumed. On any receive error it restores the original received and local properties where it can, setting ZPROP_ERR_NOCLEAR or ZPROP_ERR_NORESTORE in *errflags on failures. It always releases the file reference and frees origrecvd and origprops, and returns 0 on success, or the first nonzero error from the receive or end step, or props_error (from dsl_prop_set_hasrecvd) if the receive succeeded. In ZFS_DEBUG builds an injected error forces the result to 1.

functions.name: load_tests
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: filepath is a valid C string and algp points to writable storage. Postcondition: the file is read line by line (a header of 'algorithm' and 'tests' keys, then blank-line separated tests of key:value lines); on success it returns the head of a linked list of calloc'd tests in file order, sets *algp to the header algorithm, and frees the line buffer and closes the file. If the file has no tests it still returns NULL and prints 'no tests' but also sets *algp. On any error (open failure, incomplete header or test, malformed line, unknown or duplicate key, bad number, bad hex or odd-length value, unknown algorithm or result, read error) it prints a message to stderr, frees the line buffer, closes the file, leaves *algp unset, and returns NULL; already-parsed tests and the partial current test are leaked, and the caller owns the returned list.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv[1] is a writable comma-separated list of field names from the fields table and argv[2] is a path (argc >= 3 is checked). Postcondition: returns usage() if argc < 3 or a field name is unknown; returns 1 if open(O_PATH) or statx fails (closing fd on statx failure); returns 2 after printing a 'kernel did not return field' message for each requested field the kernel did not report; otherwise prints one line per requested field in table order and returns 0. The fd opened by open is not closed on the unknown-field-free success path or on the rc == 2 return.

functions.name: vchiq_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cdev, cmd, arg, fflag and td come from the devfs ioctl path, devfs_get_cdevpriv can supply the per-open VCHIQ instance, and arg points to a kernel-accessible argument struct of the type the command expects. Postcondition: if devfs_get_cdevpriv fails, its error is returned unchanged. Otherwise the command is dispatched; a held service reference is released with unlock_service. If the command left ret at 0, a VCHIQ_ERROR status becomes EIO and VCHIQ_RETRY becomes EINTR. A negative ret is negated, so the function returns 0 on success or a positive errno such as ENOMEM, ENOTCONN, EINVAL, EEXIST, EINTR, EIO, EFAULT, ESRCH, EMSGSIZE, EWOULDBLOCK, or ENOTTY for an unknown cmd. On success some commands write results back through arg: the new handle for CREATE_SERVICE, the updated mode for a saved bulk waiter, the counts for AWAIT_COMPLETION, and the dequeued-message size for DEQUEUE_MESSAGE. GET_CLIENT_ID returns the client id as the result, passed through unchanged if it is positive. Some commands can also change the instance state, for example by connecting it or setting its closing flag.

functions.name: vchiq_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cdev private data yields a valid vchiq instance, cmd is a VCHIQ ioctl command and arg points to the matching kernel-accessible argument structure. Postcondition: the function returns a non-negative errno value (0 on success), obtained by negating the internal negative code, and it unlocks any service it looked up. For the AWAIT_COMPLETION case, it returns ENOTCONN if the instance is not connected. Otherwise it waits under completion_mutex for a completion, and EINTR if the wait is interrupted. Otherwise it copies up to args.count completion records (plus their messages into user msgbufs) to args.buf, advances completion_remove for each fully copied record, and writes back updated count and msgbufcount to arg. EMSGSIZE or EFAULT is set only if the first record fails; EFAULT is also set if the completion copy fails. It signals remove_event if count != 0, returns ENOTCONN if ret is 0 and the instance is closing, and releases completion_mutex. For the DEQUEUE_MESSAGE case, see the separate dequeue behaviour in the same function.

functions.name: vchiq_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cdev private data yields a valid vchiq instance, cmd is a VCHIQ ioctl command and arg points to the matching argument structure. Postcondition: the function returns a non-negative errno value (0 on success) and unlocks any looked-up service. For the DEQUEUE_MESSAGE case, it returns EINVAL if the handle is not found for the instance or the service is not VCHI-style. If the queue is empty and non-blocking it returns EWOULDBLOCK, and if blocking and the wait is interrupted it returns EINTR. Otherwise it removes one header from msg_queue (advancing msg_remove) and signals remove_event. A NULL header gives ENOTCONN, a header larger than args.bufsize gives EMSGSIZE, and a failed copy_to_user gives EFAULT. On success it copies the payload to args.buf if non-NULL, writes back args with bufsize set to the message size, and releases the message. Other cases of the function handle other ioctl commands, and an unknown cmd gives ENOTTY.

functions.name: parse_rx_slots
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: state is a valid initialised VCHIQ state whose remote shared state is mapped, and the caller is the slot handler that owns the rx side; no service reference is held on entry. Postcondition: returns nothing; processes each message from state->rx_pos up to the remote tx_pos snapshot, dispatching by message type (open, openack, close, data, connect, bulk, bulk done, padding, pause, resume, remote use/release and invalid ids), taking and releasing a service reference per message where one is looked up. After a message is handled, or skipped because no service matched, it advances rx_pos by calc_stride(size) and releases the slot when the end of a slot is reached. If parse_open, a close or data callback, a bulk mutex lock, or the queue_message in PAUSE handling fails with RETRY or interruption, it jumps to bail_not_ready, stops without advancing rx_pos past the current message, and drops any held service reference so the message can be retried later.

functions.name: name##_mask
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none for safety; the result is only a valid ring offset when ring_size is a power of two. Postcondition: returns idx & (ring_size - 1), i.e. idx reduced modulo ring_size when ring_size is a power of two.

functions.name: name##_get_ring_ptr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: buf points to a ring buffer of ring_size bytes and ring_size is a power of two. Postcondition: returns buf + (idx & (ring_size - 1)); nothing is read or written.

functions.name: name##_read_packet
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: opaque has room for size bytes, buf is a ring of ring_size bytes (a power of two), *masked_cons is a masked index and the packet of size bytes is available. Postcondition: copies size bytes from the ring starting at *masked_cons into opaque, wrapping around the end of the ring when needed (using masked_prod to decide), then sets *masked_cons to (*masked_cons + size) & (ring_size - 1); returns nothing.

functions.name: name##_write_packet
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: buf is a ring of ring_size bytes (a power of two), opaque points to size readable bytes, *masked_prod is a masked index and there is enough free space for size bytes. Postcondition: copies size bytes from opaque into the ring starting at *masked_prod, wrapping around the end of the ring when needed (using masked_cons to decide), then sets *masked_prod to (*masked_prod + size) & (ring_size - 1); returns nothing.

functions.name: name##_queued
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ring_size is a power of two. Postcondition: returns 0 if prod == cons; otherwise, with masked indices p and c, returns ring_size if p == c, p - c if p > c, and ring_size - (c - p) if p < c.
functions.contract: /*@ requires prod >= 0 && cons >= 0 && ring_size > 0 && (ring_size & (ring_size - 1)) == 0; ensures (prod == cons) ? result == 0 : (((prod & (ring_size - 1)) == (cons & (ring_size - 1))) ? result == ring_size : (((prod & (ring_size - 1)) > (cons & (ring_size - 1))) ? result == (prod & (ring_size - 1)) - (cons & (ring_size - 1)) : result == ring_size - ((cons & (ring_size - 1)) - (prod & (ring_size - 1))))); */

functions.name: inflateBack
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: strm and strm->state are expected to be non-null (state initialized by inflateBackInit_, window allocated), and in and out are valid callbacks (in is called to supply input and returns the number of bytes available, 0 meaning no more input; out is called to consume output and returns nonzero on failure). Postcondition: returns Z_STREAM_ERROR if strm or strm->state is null, or if the decoder mode is unexpected; otherwise it decodes the deflate stream, delivering output only through out, and returns Z_STREAM_END on proper termination, Z_DATA_ERROR for invalid data (strm->msg is set), Z_BUF_ERROR if the in callback supplies no input when more is needed or if out reports failure on the final flush after a proper end; Z_BUF_ERROR can also come from the input-exhaustion path (PULL), and an out failure during a ROOM flush returns Z_BUF_ERROR. On every path except the initial Z_STREAM_ERROR check, any pending window output is flushed through out before returning, strm->next_in and strm->avail_in are set to the unconsumed input, strm->msg is reset to null at start, and the state remains allocated.

functions.name: XXH_FORCE_INLINE XXH_TARGET_AVX512 XXH3_ACCUMULATE_TEMPLATE(avx512)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function XXH3_accumulate_avx512(acc, input, secret, nbStripes), returning void. Precondition: acc points to 8 writable xxh_u64 lanes aligned to 64 bytes, input holds at least nbStripes*64 readable bytes, and secret holds at least (nbStripes-1)*8+64 readable bytes (nothing is required when nbStripes is 0). Postcondition: for each stripe n from 0 to nbStripes-1 in order, it prefetches input+n*64+XXH_PREFETCH_DIST (a hint that never faults) and calls XXH3_accumulate_512_avx512 on acc, input+n*64 and secret+n*8, so acc is updated in place; it does nothing when nbStripes is 0, and it returns no value, acquires no lock and holds no reference.

functions.name: db_lex
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the debugger lexer input (db_read_char/db_unread_char) is usable and db_tok_string is writable; flags selects the radix mode (DRT_RADIX_MASK), whether whitespace is returned as a token (DRT_WSPACE) and whether a-f/A-F start hex numbers (DRT_HEX). Postcondition: it skips non-printable and blank characters and returns tEOL if it hits newline or end of input while skipping, or tWSPACE (with the next character pushed back) if whitespace was skipped and DRT_WSPACE is set. A numeric token sets db_tok_number, pushes back the terminating character and returns tNUMBER. If a letter, digit, or underscore immediately follows the number it calls db_error and db_flush_lex and returns tEOF. An identifier token (starting with a letter, '_' or '\') is stored NUL-terminated in db_tok_string, the terminating character is pushed back, and it returns tIDENT. A backslash escape followed by newline or end of input calls db_error("Bad escape") but lexing continues. An identifier that fills db_tok_string calls db_error and db_flush_lex and returns tEOF. Otherwise it returns the operator token for the punctuation: tPLUS, tMINUS, tDOT/tDOTDOT, tSTAR, tSLASH, tEQ/tLOG_EQ, tPCT, tHASH, tLPAREN, tRPAREN, tCOMMA, tDITTO, tDOLLAR, tEXCL/tLOG_NOT_EQ, tCOLON/tCOLONCOLON, tSEMI, tBIT_AND/tLOG_AND, tBIT_OR/tLOG_OR, tLESS/tSHIFT_L/tLESS_EQ, tGREATER/tSHIFT_R/tGREATER_EQ, tQUESTION, tBIT_NOT. Two-character operators consume the second character, otherwise it is pushed back. A '-1' (end of input) returns tEOF, and any other character prints "Bad character", calls db_flush_lex and returns tEOF.

functions.name: aac_reset_adapter
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds sc->aac_io_lock (asserted with mtx_assert). Postcondition: if AAC_STATE_RESET is already set, it prints a message and returns EINVAL without changing anything else; otherwise it sets AAC_STATE_RESET, disables interrupts, completes every busy and ready command with AAC_CMD_RESET (calling cm_complete or waking the sleeper), shuts down drives if the adapter is healthy (dropping and retaking the io lock around the shutdown), then resets the IOP via the MU reset or sync commands and doorbell. If the older-firmware IOP_RESET fails, it sends a pause-IO unwind FIB and skips re-initialisation. If aac_check_firmware fails, it also skips re-initialisation; otherwise it calls aac_init (with the io lock dropped and retaken) unless in sync mode. On every non-EINVAL path it then clears AAC_STATE_RESET, re-enables interrupts, calls aacraid_startio and returns 0, with the io lock held again.

functions.name: ahd_handle_target_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahd and cmd are valid, ahd->black_hole is a valid lun state, and cmd->scsiid and cmd->identify index validly into ahd->enabled_targets and the tstate's enabled_luns. Postcondition: the lun state is the enabled one for the target and lun, or ahd->black_hole if none is enabled; if its accept_tios list is empty it sets AHD_TQINFIFO_BLOCKED in ahd->flags and returns 1 with nothing consumed. Otherwise it clears AHD_TQINFIFO_BLOCKED, removes the first ATIO from the list, fills in its init_id, tag info, cdb_len (6, 10, 12 or 16, or 1 with a printed warning for reserved or vendor-unique group codes), cdb bytes and CAM_CDB_RECVD, and for the black hole also fills in target_id and target_lun. If the identify byte lacks the disconnect flag it also sets ahd->pending_device to the lun state, freezes the ccb and sets CAM_DIS_DISCONNECT, otherwise it clears CAM_DIS_DISCONNECT. It then passes the ATIO to xpt_done, which takes ownership of it, and returns 0.

functions.name: ahd_handle_message_phase
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahd points to a valid softc whose msg_type is one of the four MSG_TYPE_* states (INITIATOR_MSGOUT/MSGIN, TARGET_MSGIN/MSGOUT) and, for the states that need it, an active message (msgout_len != 0, or send_msg_perror set for initiator MSGOUT). Postcondition: returns void after fetching device info and reading LASTPHASE, handling one REQ of the message phase for the current msg_type by driving the bus registers (RETURN_1/RETURN_2, SCSISIGO, SXFRCTL0, SCSIDAT, CLRSINT1) and updating msgin/msgout indices and msg_type (it may switch between initiator MSGOUT and MSGIN states); it panics on an unknown msg_type or on missing active message, returns early with no end-of-session processing when a target-side parsed message reports MSGLOOP_TERMINATED, and otherwise if the session ended it clears the message state and either (packetized) resets the sequencer to bus free/idle or sets RETURN_1 to EXIT_MSG_LOOP.

functions.name: ahd_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahd points to a softc whose parent_dmat, features, bugs, flags, unit and related fields were set by earlier probe/attach stages, with the controller in SCSI mode. Postcondition: it returns ENOMEM if allocating saved_stack, creating the buffer DMA tag, creating the shared-data DMA tag, allocating the shared DMA memory, or ahd_init_scbdata fails (earlier completed stages stay allocated, with init_level incremented once per completed stage, so a later ahd_free can unwind them); otherwise it returns 0 after setting up the qoutfifo, targetcmds (target mode only), overrun_buf (bitbucket bug only) and next_queued_hscb pointers, initializing the chip, optionally checking termination by current sensing (a flexport timeout or failure only skips the check with a printed message), calling ahd_restart and arming the stat timer. It panics if sizeof(struct hardware_scb) != 64. The result of aic_dmamap_load is not checked. The softc and the allocated resources remain owned by the caller.

functions.name: ahd_chip_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahd is a valid ahd_softc whose probe is complete, whose shared data DMA memory is allocated and mapped (shared_data_map, qoutfifo, qinfifo, next_queued_hscb valid, targetcmds valid if target mode is enabled), and whose our_id, flags, bugs and features are set. Postcondition: returns nothing; the chip is programmed with IOCELL, LQI/LQO interrupt modes, sequencer interrupt vectors, SCB offset registers and the negotiation table, the software qoutfifo/qinfifo/target command arrays and scratch RAM are reset to empty, the freeze count is 0, the queue offsets and shared-memory addresses are given to the sequencer, coalescing is disabled, the sequencer program is loaded, and the chip is left in SCSI mode; no value or error code is returned and no lock or reference is taken or released.

functions.name: ahd_action
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sim is a registered CAM SIM whose softc is an ahd_softc and ccb is a valid CCB with func_code, target_id and path set. Postcondition: returns nothing and dispatches on ccb->ccb_h.func_code. XPT_SCSI_IO and XPT_RESET_DEV (and XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO in target mode) complete with CAM_PROVIDE_FAIL via xpt_done if the initiator role is off for SCSI_IO or RESET_DEV. If no SCB is available they freeze the simq, set AHD_RESOURCE_SHORTAGE, and complete with CAM_REQUEUE_REQ. Otherwise they bind an SCB to the ccb and start it through ahd_execute_scb (reset) or ahd_setup_data (I/O). With AHD_TARGET_MODE, XPT_ACCEPT_TARGET_IO queues the ccb on the lstate accept_tios list with CAM_REQ_INPROG, or completes it with the lookup status on error. XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO falls through to the SCB path, using the black hole lstate if the lookup fails. XPT_NOTIFY_ACKNOWLEDGE and XPT_IMMEDIATE_NOTIFY queue on immed_notifies with CAM_REQ_INPROG, or complete with the error status. XPT_EN_LUN calls ahd_handle_en_lun then xpt_done. XPT_ABORT delegates to ahd_abort_ccb. XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS, XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS and XPT_CALC_GEOMETRY call their handlers then xpt_done. XPT_RESET_BUS resets channel A and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_TERM_IO completes with CAM_REQ_INVALID. XPT_PATH_INQ fills in the pathinq fields and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. Any other func_code completes with CAM_PROVIDE_FAIL.

functions.name: ahd_aic790X_setup
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahd points to a valid ahd_softc whose dev_softc is a readable and writable PCI device handle. Postcondition: if the PCI revision is below ID_AIC7902_PCI_REV_A4, it prints a message, clears the PCI command register and returns ENXIO; otherwise it sets ahd->channel from the PCI function ('A' + function), then applies revision-specific bug flags and IO cell settings (for revisions >= B0 it also adds feature flags and sets the PREQDIS bit in DEVCONFIG1), and returns 0.

functions.name: ahc_handle_scsiint
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahc is a valid controller softc whose sequencer is paused because a SCSI interrupt is pending (intstat is passed but not used). Postcondition: returns nothing; it reads SSTAT0/SSTAT1 (on a twin-channel controller it may toggle SBLKCTL SELBUSB to the other channel), and if no cause is found it prints a spurious-interrupt message, clears CLRSCSIINT, unpauses and returns. Otherwise it clears the critical section and handles exactly one cause, in priority order: (1) Ultra2 transceiver IOERR, which resets the channel; (2) SCSIRSTI, which resets the channel without initiating a reset; (3) SCSIPERR, which logs the parity error, queues or flags a parity-error message, forces renegotiation, clears CLRSCSIINT and unpauses; (4) SELTO, which stops the selection, clears message state and interrupt state, completes the waiting SCB with CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT via device reset handling (or dumps card state if the SCB lookup fails), clears CLRSCSIINT and restarts the sequencer; (5) BUSFREE with ENBUSFREE enabled, which handles the expected or unexpected bus free (abort, bus device reset, PPR/WDTR/SDTR rejection requeue, or CAM_UNEXP_BUSFREE aborts with diagnostics), clears CLRSCSIINT and restarts the sequencer; (6) otherwise it prints a missing-case message and clears CLRSCSIINT. In the P_MESGOUT abort cases it dereferences scb, which may be NULL if the connection was not identified.

functions.name: ahc_parse_msg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ahc and devinfo are valid, and ahc->msgin_buf holds the first ahc->msgin_index bytes of an incoming SCSI message with the transfer settings of devinfo's target fetchable. Postcondition: returns MSGLOOP_TERMINATED for sequencer-handled messages (disconnect, save/restore pointers, command complete, ignore wide residue), and also for bus device reset and abort/clear-queue in target mode after restarting the controller; returns MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE for message-reject, no-op, and for a fully received SDTR/WDTR/PPR (after applying the validated width/sync settings and optionally building a reply in msgout), and also whenever the message is rejected; returns MSGLOOP_IN_PROG when more bytes are needed (extended message too short or incomplete). Unsupported or malformed messages (bad extended length, unknown extended type, terminate-I/O-process, unknown codes, target-mode messages when not in target role, or an SDTR/WDTR/PPR where we initiated and the target negotiated lower) are rejected by setting msgout to a single MESSAGE_REJECT byte at index 0, and the function returns MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE, except that it returns MSGLOOP_IN_PROG if the rejecting case broke out before completion and sets done only via the reject path (reject always forces MSGLOOP_MSGCOMPLETE). When the result is not IN_PROG and no response was generated, msgout_len is cleared to 0.

functions.name: asmc_wol_sysctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 is a valid asmc device_t and oidp and req describe a valid sysctl request. Postcondition: if reading the AUPO key fails, EIO is returned and nothing is written; otherwise the current value is exposed as 0 or 1 through sysctl_handle_int, and if that call returns an error or the request carries no new value (req->newptr is NULL) its result (error, or 0 for a read-only request) is returned without writing; otherwise the new value is clamped to 0 or 1 (1 iff nonzero), written to the AUPO key, and 0 is returned, or EIO if the write fails.

functions.name: readEepromCTLInfo
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ah is a valid HAL handle and ee points to a HAL_EEPROM whose ee_version, ee_numCtls, ee_ctl[] and (for version 4.0 and later) ee_targetPowersStart are already set. Postcondition: for each CTL index whose ee_ctl entry is nonzero, the function reads the band-edge frequencies and powers from the EEPROM, fills the matching ee_rdEdgesPower entries (rdEdge, twice_rdEdgePower, and flag for version 3.3 and later), and converts each rdEdge whose edge or power is nonzero to a frequency with fbin2freq (11A/Turbo CTL modes) or fbin2freq_2p4 (other modes); CTL entries equal to zero are skipped, leaving their edge entries untouched. It returns AH_FALSE immediately if any EEPROM read fails, leaving earlier entries already written, and otherwise returns AH_TRUE.

functions.name: ar5211Reset
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ah is a valid AR5211 HAL handle, chan points to a valid writable channel, opmode is a HAL operating mode, and status is either AH_NULL or points to writable storage. Postcondition: returns AH_TRUE after resetting the chip, reprogramming the registers for the channel, running noise floor calibration, setting up the interrupt masks and TX queues and recording opmode in ah_opmode; on failure it returns AH_FALSE and, if status is non-null, stores the error code in *status: HAL_EINVAL for a channel that does not map to a private channel, an invalid operating mode, or a channel that is neither A/TURBO nor B/PureG, and HAL_EIO for a chip reset, transmit power, set channel or noise floor calibration failure. On a failed noise floor calibration it also sets IEEE80211_CHANSTATE_CWINT in chan->ic_state if the channel is not CCK. On channel change it clears CWINT for non-DFS channels and restores the saved TSF and frame sequence counts. A failure after the chip reset leaves the hardware partly programmed.

functions.name: ar5212Reset
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ah is an attached AR5212 HAL handle (magic AR5212_MAGIC, EEPROM version at least 3), chan is a public channel, opmode is a HAL_OPMODE, and status is either AH_NULL or points to writable HAL_STATUS storage. Postcondition: the function returns AH_TRUE after the chip is woken, reset and fully reprogrammed for chan and opmode (INI, RF, power, MAC/BSSID/LED/antenna restore, PHY activate, calibration start, TX queue and interrupt setup, TPC, user settings), ah_opmode is recorded, and the CWINT channel state is cleared when bChannelChange is set and chan is not DFS; *status is not written on success. It returns AH_FALSE and stores the error code in *status (only if status is non-NULL) when it fails: HAL_EIO if wakeup, chip reset, transmit power setup, RF register setup, board values or channel set fails; HAL_EINVAL if the channel does not map to a private channel, opmode is not STA/IBSS/HOSTAP/MONITOR, or the channel is not a valid A/B/G/108G/turbo mode. CCK state is restored on both paths.

functions.name: ath_rx_pkt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc, rs and m are valid, m is an mbuf owned by the caller holding the received descriptor data, and qtype selects a valid sc_rxedma entry; the caller must hold whatever locking the RX path requires. Postcondition: the function takes ownership of m and either frees it (error frames, runt frames, frames dropped after phy/crc/MIC errors), stores it as the pending first part of a multi-descriptor frame in re->m_rxpending, chains it onto a pending mbuf (jumbogram) and passes it to net80211, or passes it up via ieee80211_input_mimo or ieee80211_input_mimo_all; any previously pending partial frame is freed on error or when a new more-fragment arrives; it updates statistics, antenna, RSSI, diversity and LED state, and returns 1 only when the frame went to a known node in station mode with a valid rx key index (so the last rx timestamp may be updated), and 0 in all other cases.

functions.name: proc_synaptics
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc, pb, ms, x, y and z are valid pointers and pb->ipacket holds a complete 6-byte Synaptics absolute-mode packet. Postcondition: returns 0 without touching anything if synaptics_support is off, returns -1 if the packet fails the sync-bit check (ipacket[0]&0xc8 != 0x80 or ipacket[3]&0xc8 != 0xc0), and otherwise returns 0 after setting *x, *y, *z and ms->button; guest (w==3) packets yield relative x/y and guest buttons, extended-W packets (w==2) only update the secondary finger or finger count, and normal packets update finger state, touchpad and extended buttons, run palm detection, gestures and smoothing, and if a palm is detected zero *x, *y, *z and restore ms->button to ms->obutton and return 0 early. Otherwise *z is set to -1, 1, -2 or 2 from the button 4, 5, 6 or 7 bit (else 0) and those four button bits are cleared from ms->button. The function also updates static state and, with evdev, pushes events.

functions.name: axgbe_isc_rxd_pkt_get
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg is the axgbe_if_softc and ri->iri_qsidx names a valid channel whose RX ring is initialised; the caller (iflib) holds whatever serialisation it normally provides for the RX queue. Postcondition: the function clears the ring's packet_data, then repeatedly calls dev_read and consumes descriptors, advancing ring->cur modulo rdesc_count, until dev_read reports the OWN bit (no more ready descriptors) or a descriptor marked last without context_next is consumed; for each consumed descriptor it adds one fragment for buffer 1 (and a second for buffer 2 when sph_enable is set), with zero lengths for context descriptors; it then ORs CSUM_IP_CHECKED and CSUM_IP_VALID into ri->iri_csum_flags if CSUM_DONE is set, sets M_VLANTAG in iri_flags and iri_vtag if VLAN_CTAG is set, sets iri_flowid and iri_rsstype if RSS_HASH is set, sets ri->iri_len to the total data length and ri->iri_nfrags to the fragment count, and always returns 0 (a zero-length or errored packet is only logged). It takes no lock or reference.

functions.name: bce_nvram_write
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc with bce_flash_info set, data_buf points to buf_size readable bytes, and the caller does not hold the NVRAM lock (the function acquires and releases it for each flash page). Postcondition: returns 0 after writing all bytes at offset (rounding the range out to 4-byte boundaries by read-modify-write of the edge dwords); returns ENOMEM if the temporary alignment buffer cannot be allocated, or the nonzero error from a failed NVRAM read, lock acquire, write enable, page erase or dword read/write, stopping at the first failure; on a failure after the lock was acquired it disables NVRAM write and access and releases the lock, on success each page iteration does the same, and the temporary buffer is freed whenever it was allocated.

functions.name: bce_rx_intr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the softc lock (BCE_LOCK) and the RX chain, page chain and DMA maps are set up, with an mbuf in each rx_mbuf_ptr slot the hardware has completed (and in the page chain slots needed when header split is on). Postcondition: returns nothing; every RX descriptor from sc->rx_cons up to the hardware consumer index (re-read after each packet) is consumed, its mbuf unmapped and removed from the chain. A frame with a CRC, PHY decode, alignment, too-short or giant error is counted in l2fhdr_error_count and freed with m_freem. Any other frame has its FCS stripped and rcvif, checksum flags and VLAN tag set (hardware tag, or the tag reinserted into the data), IPACKETS is incremented, and it is passed to if_input with the lock dropped and retaken. With header split, page-chain mbufs are concatenated onto the frame and sw_pg_cons advances. At the end sc->rx_cons (and sc->pg_cons if header split is on) is updated, the page and RX chains are refilled, and the chain DMA maps are synced for the device.

functions.name: bge_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a probed bge PCI device whose softc is allocated and the PCI bus is ready for driver attach. Postcondition: returns 0 after the whole device is set up (BAR0 and optional BAR2 mapped, chip identified, interrupt allocated, chip reset and initialized, station address read, DMA allocated, ifnet and PHY or TBI media attached, ether_ifattach done, interrupt handler hooked); on any failure (BAR0, BAR2 or IRQ mapping, chip reset, chipinit, station address, DMA allocation, EEPROM read, or bus_setup_intr failure) it returns ENXIO or the error from the failing call (mii_attach after up to five tries, taskqueue_start_threads, bus_setup_intr), after calling bge_detach(dev) to release what was acquired.

functions.name: BHNDB_IO_MISC(
functions.prose_contract: Macro template generating void functions bhndb_bus_<op>_<size>(dev, child, r, offset, datap, count) for the read/write/set multi and region operations, including the stream variants, at 1, 2 and 4 byte sizes. Precondition: r is a bhnd_resource that the common setup can translate, and the region of sizeof(type)*count bytes at offset can be accessed through a mapped window. Postcondition: the bridge lock is held during the access, the matching bus_<op>_<size> operation is performed on count elements through the translated resource and offset, any dynamic window stolen for the access is returned, the lock is released, and nothing is returned.

functions.name: bhnd_pmu_spuravoid_pllupdate
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc points to a valid PMU softc with chip id and revision set (BCM6362 rev 0 is treated as BCM43224; BCM6362 with a non-zero revision asserts via KASSERT only in the kernel build with assertions), and PMU register access is usable. Postcondition: for a recognised chip and a spuravoid mode it supports (NONE, M1, and M2 only on BCM4331 and the 6362/5357/4749/4323x/53572 group), it writes the chip-specific PLL registers via BHND_PMU_PLL_WRITE, then ORs the chosen pmuctrl bits into BHND_PMU_CTRL if they are non-zero (BCM4319 writes no PLL registers and sets nothing), and returns 0; for an unsupported mode or an unknown chip it returns ENODEV (the unknown chip case also logs), and for unsupported modes on chips that write PLL registers first (BCM4322 family, BCM4336) the common PLL registers have already been written before ENODEV is returned and BHND_PMU_CTRL is not modified.

functions.name: bhnd_nvram_val_vprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: value is a valid bhnd_nvram_val, fmt is a NUL-terminated format string, olen points to a size_t holding the output capacity when outp is non-NULL, and ap supplies the arguments required by the format (repeat count and delimiter for '%[...]', '*' width and precision ints). Postcondition: the formatted elements are written to outp as far as capacity allows, with a terminating NUL if space remains, and *olen is set to the total bytes required including the NUL (not updated on early error returns); returns 0 on success, ENOMEM if outp is non-NULL and the output did not fit, EINVAL on a malformed repeat, width, precision or length modifier, an invalid bit size, or when the format consumes more elements than the value has, EFTYPE if a byte count would overflow SIZE_MAX, or the error from bhnd_nvram_val_encode_elem if an element cannot be encoded.

functions.name: bhnd_nvram_val_vprintf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: value is a valid NVRAM value, fmt is a NUL-terminated printf-style format string, ap supplies the arguments the format consumes, olen is writable, and if outp is non-NULL it points to a buffer of at least *olen bytes. Postcondition: the formatted string is written to outp as far as it fits, with a terminating NUL if space remains; *olen is set to the total required size including the NUL on the paths that reach the end of the function; returns 0 on success, ENOMEM if outp is non-NULL and the buffer is smaller than the required size, EINVAL for a malformed format (bad repeat count, width, precision, length modifier or specifier) or if the format consumes more elements than the value has, EFTYPE if the byte count would overflow size_t, or the error returned by element encoding (other than ENOMEM when encoding strings). *olen is not updated on early error returns.

functions.name: bnxt_rdma_aux_device_add
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bp is a valid bnxt_softc whose aux_dev (bnxt_adev) is allocated, with bnxt_adev->edev either NULL or a previously allocated edev. Postcondition: returns -1 if bnxt_populate_irq(bp) fails (nothing changed), -ENOMEM if edev was NULL and allocation failed, 0 on success with the edev stored in bnxt_adev->edev and bp->edev and the auxiliary device initialized and added; if auxiliary_device_init or auxiliary_device_add fails it returns that error, calls auxiliary_device_uninit when add failed, frees edev with kfree and sets bnxt_adev->edev and bp->edev to NULL.

functions.name: bnxt_attach_pre
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctx is a valid iflib context whose softc is a bnxt_softc with a valid PCI device. Postcondition: it returns rc, which is 0 on success, after it has populated the softc, registered it on pf_list, mapped the PCI BARs, allocated the HWRM DMA memory and version info, queried the firmware (version, queues, capabilities, function config), filled in the iflib softc context and created the sysctls. On failure it returns a nonzero errno (positive such as ENXIO or ENOMEM, or negative such as -ENOMEM) from the failing step. Most failures unwind the allocations made so far (sysctls, driver registration, nvm_info, short command request, version info, HWRM DMA memory, HWRM lock, Linux pdev, PCI mapping, busmaster) via the cleanup labels. The two early returns (qportcfg rx failure and alloc_ctx_mem failure) return rc without any cleanup. The softc stays on pf_list in every case, and the results of bnxt_hwrm_func_reset, bnxt_hwrm_nvm_get_dev_info and iflib_dma_alloc are overwritten or ignored.

functions.name: bnxt_re_mmap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ib_uctx is a valid bnxt_re user context and vma is a valid vm_area_struct whose vm_pgoff selects the mapping. Postcondition: for BNXT_RE_MAP_SH_PAGE it returns directly the result of rdma_user_mmap_io on the shared page (the code after that return is unreachable), with no -EAGAIN conversion and no vma data set. For BNXT_RE_MAP_WC (write-combine), BNXT_RE_DBR_PAGE and BNXT_RE_MAP_DB_RECOVERY_PAGE it returns -EFAULT when the computed pfn is 0, and for DBR_PAGE also when vma->vm_flags has VM_WRITE (checked before the pfn). For a CQ page (default case, is_bnxt_re_cq_page finds a CQ) it maps that page and returns 0 on success or -EAGAIN on mapping failure, without setting vma data. Otherwise (default non-CQ case, noncached with pfn = vm_pgoff, or the other cases above) it calls rdma_user_mmap_io on one page, returns -EAGAIN if that fails, else returns the result of __bnxt_re_set_vma_data (0 on success or its error).

functions.name: bxe_tx_encap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is a valid fastpath and *m_head is a valid mbuf chain with a packet header, to be transmitted on the TX ring at the current producer indexes. Postcondition: it returns 0 on success, after the mbuf is DMA-mapped and stored in the tx_mbuf_chain slot, the start BD, parsing BD and data BDs are written, the producer indexes advance, the doorbell is rung and tx_pkts is incremented. It returns ENOMEM (mbuf left intact, *m_head unchanged for a retry, DMA map unloaded if it was loaded) when the first mapping reports ENOMEM or the send queue lacks nsegs+2 free BDs. Otherwise it returns a nonzero error: ENOBUFS when m_defrag fails, ENODEV when the segment count still exceeds the limit after defrag, or the bus_dmamap_load_mbuf_sg error. For every such non-ENOMEM return it frees the mbuf chain with m_freem, sets *m_head to NULL and updates the soft-error and mbuf_alloc_tx counters. A defrag followed by a failed remap that itself returns ENOMEM also leaves the mbuf intact.

functions.name: cas_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a softc whose sc_dev, sc_mtx, sc_enaddr, sc_flags and sc_variant are set up by the probe/attach caller; the ifnet, taskqueue, DMA tags, control-data memory, TX/RX DMA maps and RX buffers are all created inside this function. Postcondition: allocates the ifnet, creates the taskqueue, resets the chip, creates the DMA tags, allocates and loads the control data, creates the TX maps, and allocates and loads the RX buffers. It then attaches a PHY through MII (external, internal fallback, or SERDES), registers the interface with ether_ifattach and sets its capabilities, and returns 0. On any failure (taskqueue start, DMA tag creation, DMA alloc/load/create, or PHY attach, which gives ENXIO or the mii_attach error) it releases everything acquired so far in reverse order, frees the taskqueue and ifnet, and returns the nonzero errno. A load that succeeds but leaves the DMA address 0 can return 0 from the failure path since error is 0.

functions.name: aw_clk_mipi_register
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: clkdom is a valid clock domain and clkdef points to a valid, fully initialised aw_clk_mipi_def whose k, m and n widths and shifts are small enough that ((1 << width) - 1) << shift does not overflow an int. Postcondition: if clknode_create fails (returns NULL) the function returns 1 and nothing is registered; otherwise the new node's softc is filled from clkdef (offset, k/m/n shift, width, value, flags and min_value, with each mask set to ((1 << width) - 1) << shift, plus min_freq, max_freq, gate_shift, lock_shift, lock_retries and flags), the node is registered in clkdom with clknode_register (whose result is ignored), and the function returns 0.

functions.name: write_wr_hdr_sgl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: txd points at the tx descriptor slot for the current producer index, txqs holds the current pidx and gen for the txq, sgl holds sgl_flits 64-bit flits, ndesc is the number of descriptors the work request spans, and flits is the number of flits already used in the first descriptor.
