Postcondition: returns nothing; if ndesc == 1 it writes a single SOP|EOP work request header (length flits + sgl_flits, generation txqs->gen) and calls wr_gen2 on txd; otherwise it copies the SGL flits across consecutive descriptors, advancing txqs->pidx and flipping txqs->gen and wrapping to the start of txq->desc whenever pidx reaches txq->size, writes a continuation header with the current gen in each later descriptor, sets EOP on the last one, issues wmb(), and only then writes the first descriptor's length/generation word with the original generation (ogen) and calls wr_gen2 on it so the hardware sees the whole request as valid last.

functions.name: t4_cim_read_la
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: adap points to a valid adapter, la_buf is a writable buffer large enough for the CIM logic analyzer capture, and wrptr is a valid output location. Postcondition: forwards to t4_cim_read_la_core(adap, 0, la_buf, wrptr) and returns its result unchanged, with the capture and write pointer stored through la_buf and wrptr as that core function defines.

functions.name: ktls_write_tls_wr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: txq is the TLS connection's transmit queue (tlsp->txq), dst points to the ring slot at index pidx, m_tls is an unmapped (EXTPG) mbuf with a TLS record header, m is the chain head, and 'available' is the number of free descriptors, which must cover the work requests built. Postcondition: if only the TLS header (tlen <= m_epg_hdrlen) would be sent, it returns the result of ktls_write_tunnel_packet() and builds nothing else. Otherwise it updates the tlspcb tracking state (prev_seq, and prev_ack, prev_win, prev_tsecr and prev_mss when they change), and writes the TCB field updates, either combined with the TLS work request or as a separate FW_ULPTX_WR that consumes ring descriptors (raw_wrs is incremented and the sdesc is set with m=NULL). It then builds the TLS work request (ULP_TXPKT, IDATA, CPL_TX_SEC_PDU, key context or MEMRD, CPL_TX_DATA, TLS header if offset==0, IV for short records, padding, payload SGL), copying it from scratch space to the ring if scratch was used. It updates the kern_tls counters, records m in the sdesc at the final pidx only when this is the last work request (otherwise NULL), and returns ndesc, the number of ring descriptors consumed. The caller advances pidx and retains the mbufs; no locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: ktls_write_tls_wr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: txq is the transmit queue owned by tlsp, m_tls is an unmapped (extpg) TLS-record mbuf following the packet-header mbuf m, dst points to the ring slot at index pidx, and available is at least the number of descriptors the work request needs. Postcondition: if the request covers only the TLS header, or only part or all of the GHASH trailer in partial-GHASH mode, a tunnelled immediate-data packet is written and the result of ktls_write_tunnel_packet is returned. Otherwise a full, short or partial-GHASH TLS crypto work request is built at dst (or in the txq scratch area and copied into the ring when it would wrap), including the SGL, the copied and modified packet headers, and an optional hash-request ULP_TXPKT. In that case tlsp ghash state is updated, a send-tag reference is taken via m_snd_tag_ref when a hash is requested, and the txq counters and the sdesc at pidx are updated (m is stored there only for the last work request in the chain). The number of descriptors used is returned.

functions.name: t4_sysctls
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc points to an attached adapter whose device has a sysctl tree and whose sysctl context sc->ctx is initialized. Postcondition: returns nothing; it initializes some adapter fields (sc_do_rxcopy = 1, lro_timeout = 100, and in TCP_OFFLOAD builds with offload enabled the sc->tt defaults) and registers the dev.t4nex.X sysctl entries; for a VF adapter it returns right after the common entries (do_rx_copy through firmware_version), otherwise it also registers the VPD/capability/temperature/reset entries, a misc node (plus wcwr_stats on T5 and later), a tls node when KERN_TLS is built in and active, and a toe node with timers and backoffs when TCP_OFFLOAD is built in and offload is enabled; no errors are reported and no locks or references are taken.

functions.name: ar40xx_hw_port_setup
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc points to a valid ar40xx softc whose sc_vlan.pvid[port] indexes a valid sc_vlan.vlan_id entry, and port is a valid port number for the register macros. Postcondition: the port's VLAN0 (default SVID/CVID from the masked VLAN id), VLAN1 (egress mode UNMOD if VLAN mode is enabled, else UNTOUCH) and LOOKUP (members, learn, ingress mode SECURE or PORT_ONLY, forward state) registers are each written followed by a write barrier, and the function always returns 0.

functions.name: fxp_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is an fxp PCI device whose softc is allocated by the bus and is not yet attached. Postcondition: it initialises the softc, locks and media, maps the registers, resets the chip, reads the EEPROM, and sets up the DMA tags, memory and maps and the RX buffers; it attaches the PHYs (or manual serial media), configures and attaches the ifnet, and installs the interrupt handler. If WOL is supported it also briefly initialises and stops the chip under the softc lock. It returns 0 on success. If resource allocation fails it returns ENXIO. If an RX buffer allocation fails it returns ENOMEM. If any other step fails (DMA tag, memory or map creation, mii_attach, bus_setup_intr) it returns that step's nonzero error. If bus_setup_intr fails it first calls ether_ifdetach. On every nonzero return it calls fxp_release(sc), which frees all resources including the mutex and ifnet.

functions.name: fDeviceSendCommand
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pCmd is a valid Command whose pVDevice refers to a disk device with a valid Marvell SATA channel and adapter, and any scatter-gather list is terminated by an SG_FLAG_EOT entry. Postcondition: returns nothing; the command is dispatched in one of these ways. If the device is offline, pCmd->Result is RETURN_BAD_DEVICE and completion is called. If the LBA range exceeds the device capacity, or the command is not READ/WRITE/VERIFY, Result is RETURN_INVALID_REQUEST and completion is called. For READ/WRITE with device mode below 8, or with no usable physical SG, DMA is disabled and the queue flushed, and the data is transferred by PIO. Result is then RETURN_SUCCESS, RETURN_NEED_LOGICAL_SG, RETURN_INVALID_REQUEST (size not a multiple of 512) or RETURN_IDE_ERROR. DMA is re-enabled and completion is called. For UDMA, a PRD table is allocated, or Result is RETURN_DEVICE_BUSY and completion is called if allocation fails. The PRD table is filled from the SG list and the command is queued with mvSataQueueCommand. On queue failure Result is RETURN_IDE_ERROR (or RETURN_DEVICE_BUSY if the queue is full), the PRD table is freed and completion is called. On the UDMA path pDevice->QueueLength is incremented after the queue attempt, even after a failure. For VERIFY, a non-UDMA verify command (EXT if lba48) is queued, and on queue failure the same queue_failed handling runs with no PRD table to free. On success the completion callback is invoked later.

functions.name: Kernel_DeviceIoControl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dwIoControlCode selects an ioctl; lpInBuffer and lpOutBuffer point to valid buffers of at least nInBufferSize and nOutBufferSize bytes, and lpBytesReturned is either NULL or writable. Postcondition: the function returns -1 for an unknown ioctl code, for a wrong buffer size, for a failing helper call, or when the vbus or controller lookup fails; for the cases visible here this means: SET_DEVICE_INFO needs an input size exactly equal to the struct and an output size of 0, SET_DEVICE_INFO_V2 needs an input size of at least the struct and an output size of 0, SET_BOOT_MARK needs an input size of sizeof(DEVICEID) and returns -1 if a top-level device belongs to a different vbus, ADD_SPARE_DISK and REMOVE_SPARE_DISK need an input size of sizeof(DEVICEID) and an output size of 0, ADD_DISK_TO_ARRAY needs an exact input size and an output size of 0 (the input buffer is read before the size check), GET_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES needs an output size of at least sizeof(DRIVER_CAPABILITIES) and fills the output buffer. SET_BOOT_MARK also updates the boot mark of top-level devices and calls SyncArrayInfo on them. GET_CONTROLLER_VENID returns -1 if the adapter index is not found or the output size is under 4; otherwise it writes (pciConfigDeviceId<<16)|0x11AB to the output buffer and returns 0 without setting *lpBytesReturned. EPROM_IO returns -1 if the adapter is not found or the buffer sizes are too small; otherwise it reads flash into the output buffer or writes flash from the input buffer at offset 16 and returns 0 without setting *lpBytesReturned. All other successful cases set *lpBytesReturned = nOutBufferSize if lpBytesReturned is non-NULL and return 0.

functions.name: pmc_syscall_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td is the current thread and syscall_args points to a pmc_syscall_args giving the operation code and user data pointer. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise an errno, and bumps the syscall and syscall-error counters. The pmc_sx lock is taken exclusive (or downgraded to shared by some ops) and released before return. If pmc_hook is NULL it returns EINVAL at once; if the exclusive lock cannot be taken it returns ENOSYS. For the PMC_OP_PMCADMIN case, the caller needs PRIV_PMC_MANAGE (otherwise the priv_check error is returned) and the user pmcadmin struct must be copyable in (otherwise the copyin error is returned). EINVAL is returned if the cpu is out of range, the state is neither DISABLED nor FREE, or the row index is out of range; ENXIO if the cpu is inactive; EBUSY if disabling a thread-disposition row, or if a PMC is allocated on that hardware slot. Otherwise, with the thread bound to that cpu, DISABLED clears the enabled flag and marks the row standalone if it was enabled, and FREE sets the flag and unmarks the row if it was disabled; other cases are no-ops. The PMCALLOCATE, PMCATTACH, PMCDETACH, PMCGETMSR and PMCRELEASE cases are other branches of the same function. PMCALLOCATE copies the struct in, calls pmc_do_op_pmcallocate, and copies it back out on success. PMCGETMSR returns EINVAL for a non-virtual, inherited, or not exactly owner-attached PMC, and ENOSYS if the class has no get_msr. Otherwise it copies out the MSR, flags the owner process with PMC_PP_ENABLE_MSR_ACCESS and forces a context switch. PMCRELEASE copies in the id and calls pmc_do_op_pmcrelease.

functions.name: pmc_syscall_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td is the current thread and syscall_args points to a pmc_syscall_args giving the operation code and user data pointer. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise an errno, and bumps the syscall and syscall-error counters. The pmc_sx lock is taken exclusive (or downgraded to shared by some ops) and released before return. If pmc_hook is NULL it returns EINVAL at once; if the exclusive lock cannot be taken it returns ENOSYS. The PMC_OP_PMCALLOCATE case copies a pmc_op_pmcallocate struct in from arg (copyin error returned on failure), calls pmc_do_op_pmcallocate (its error returned on failure), and on success copies the updated struct back out, returning the copyout result. The PMCADMIN, PMCATTACH, PMCDETACH, PMCGETMSR and PMCRELEASE cases are other branches of the same function.

functions.name: pmc_syscall_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td is the current thread and syscall_args points to a pmc_syscall_args giving the operation code and user data pointer. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise an errno, and bumps the syscall and syscall-error counters. The pmc_sx lock is taken exclusive (or downgraded to shared by some ops) and released before return. If pmc_hook is NULL it returns EINVAL at once; if the exclusive lock cannot be taken it returns ENOSYS. The PMC_OP_PMCGETMSR case downgrades the lock, copies in the request, and looks up the PMC (errors returned). It returns EINVAL if the PMC is not virtual-mode, has descendants, or does not have exactly one target equal to its owner, and ENOSYS if the class has no get_msr. It returns the get_msr error if negative, or the copyout error if negative. Otherwise it copies the MSR out, sets PMC_PP_ENABLE_MSR_ACCESS on the target process and forces a context switch. The other ops are other branches of the same function.

functions.name: pmc_syscall_handler
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td is the current thread and syscall_args points to a pmc_syscall_args giving the operation code and user data pointer. Postcondition: returns 0 on success, otherwise an errno, and bumps the syscall and syscall-error counters. The pmc_sx lock is taken exclusive (or downgraded to shared by some ops) and released before return. If pmc_hook is NULL it returns EINVAL at once; if the exclusive lock cannot be taken it returns ENOSYS. The PMC_OP_PMCRELEASE case copies a pmc_op_simple in from arg (copyin error returned on failure) and returns the result of pmc_do_op_pmcrelease on its pm_pmcid. The other ops are other branches of the same function.

functions.name: hv_flush_tlb_others_ex
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid vmbus softc and pmap a valid pmap; the current CPU's per-CPU cpu_mem buffer, if allocated, is large enough to hold a struct hv_tlb_flush_ex plus the VP set banks and GVA list (about PAGE_SIZE). Postcondition: returns EINVAL without issuing a hypercall if the current CPU's cpu_mem pointer is NULL, if hyperv_recommends lacks HYPERV_X64_EX_PROCESSOR_MASKS_RECOMMENDED, or if hv_cpumask_to_vpset returns a negative value; otherwise it fills the per-CPU flush descriptor (address space 0 and flush-all-address-spaces flag for INVL_OP_TLB, else the pmap's CR3 with the PCID bits cleared and flags 0; sparse-4K VP set built from mask), issues exactly one rep hypercall and returns its status. That hypercall is HVCALL_FLUSH_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_SPACE_EX with count 0 (adding the non-global-mappings-only flag) when addr2 is 0, the same space-wide call without that flag when (addr2-addr1)/HV_TLB_FLUSH_UNIT exceeds max_gvas, and otherwise HVCALL_FLUSH_VIRTUAL_ADDRESS_LIST_EX with the GVA list built by fill_gva_list.

functions.name: iavf_asq_send_command
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid iavf_hw, desc points to a valid descriptor in non-DMA memory, buff is NULL or points to at least buff_size bytes, and cmd_details is NULL or valid; the function takes hw->aq.asq_spinlock itself. Postcondition: it sets asq_last_status to IAVF_AQ_RC_OK and returns IAVF_ERR_QUEUE_EMPTY if the queue is uninitialized (count==0) or the head register is >= num_asq_entries, IAVF_ERR_INVALID_SIZE if buff_size > asq_buf_size, IAVF_ERR_PARAM if postpone is set without async, or IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_FULL if no descriptor could be reclaimed; in all these cases nothing is queued. Otherwise it copies desc (and buff, with its DMA address and datalen) to the ring, advances next_to_use modulo count, writes the tail register unless postponed, and polls for completion in 50 us steps up to asq_cmd_timeout unless async or postpone is set. If the command completed, desc and buff are copied back from the ring, asq_last_status is set to the firmware return code (low 8 bits when nonzero), and it returns IAVF_SUCCESS for IAVF_AQ_RC_OK, IAVF_ERR_NOT_READY for IAVF_AQ_RC_EBUSY, or IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_ERROR otherwise. If not completed and neither async nor postpone is set, it returns IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_CRITICAL_ERROR if the ATQCRIT bit is set in the len register, else IAVF_ERR_ADMIN_QUEUE_TIMEOUT. If not completed and async or postpone is set, it returns IAVF_SUCCESS. If wb_desc is given, the ring descriptor is copied there on the queued paths. The spinlock is released before returning.

functions.name: ice_clean_rq_elem
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw, cq and e are valid, cq->rq_lock is not held by the caller (the function takes and releases it), e->msg_buf if non-NULL has room for e->buf_len bytes, and pending is either NULL or points to a writable u16. Postcondition: e->desc is zeroed first; it returns ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY if cq->rq.count is 0 (the queue is uninitialized; pending is not written), ICE_ERR_AQ_NO_WORK if the hardware head equals next_to_clean (ring state unchanged, *pending set if pending is non-NULL), otherwise it processes one descriptor: it copies the descriptor into e->desc, sets e->msg_len to min(datalen, e->buf_len), copies that many bytes into e->msg_buf if msg_buf is non-NULL and msg_len is nonzero, resets the descriptor to its original buffer address and size, writes the cleaned index to the tail register, advances cq->rq.next_to_clean modulo cq->num_rq_entries, sets cq->rq.next_to_use to the head value read, and returns 0, or ICE_ERR_AQ_ERROR if the descriptor carried the error flag (processing still completes). Except for ICE_ERR_AQ_EMPTY, *pending is set to the recomputed number of pending messages when pending is non-NULL; cq->rq_lock is always released before returning.

functions.name: virtchnl_vc_validate_vf_msg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ver points to a valid version info, and msg points to at least msglen readable bytes (the opcode-specific header is read only when msglen is at least that header's size). Postcondition: returns VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_PARAM for VIRTCHNL_OP_EVENT, VIRTCHNL_OP_UNKNOWN or any unrecognised opcode; otherwise computes the expected length for the opcode (a fixed struct size, or for variable-length messages the header size plus the element-count-dependent extra bytes once msglen covers the header) and returns VIRTCHNL_STATUS_ERR_OPCODE_MISMATCH if an embedded count is zero or above its opcode-specific maximum (RSS key/LUT lengths of zero are allowed, and quanta requires nonzero quanta_size and num_queues) or if the expected length differs from msglen; otherwise returns 0. Nothing is modified and no references or locks are taken.

functions.name: irdma_create_qp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ibpd is a valid irdma PD, init_attr is a valid QP init attribute with valid send_cq and recv_cq, and udata is either NULL (kernel QP) or a valid user-data descriptor. Postcondition: on success it returns &iwqp->ibqp for a newly allocated QP with refcnt 1, stored in rf->qp_table[qp_num], with the QP created in hardware (for RoCE also a workload-scheduler add, QoS registration and, for UD QPs, an entry on the PD's udqp_list) and, if udata was given, the response copied to udata; on failure it returns ERR_PTR of a negative errno: the error from irdma_validate_qp_attrs, -EINVAL if udata is too short or if dev->ws_add fails (after irdma_cqp_qp_destroy_cmd), -ENOMEM if the QP, sg_list or Q2/context DMA allocation fails, the error from irdma_alloc_rsrc, irdma_setup_umode_qp/irdma_setup_kmode_qp or irdma_cqp_create_qp_cmd, -EPROTO if irdma_sc_qp_init fails, or the error from ib_copy_to_udata. Early failures free the allocations directly, later ones call irdma_free_qp_rsrc, and the copy_to_udata failure calls irdma_destroy_qp on the new QP instead.

functions.name: sati_log_sense_translate_response
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sequence, scsi_io and ata_io are valid, and the ATA command's D2H register FIS and data buffer addresses can be obtained from ata_io. Postcondition: if the ATA status has the error bit set, it builds CHECK CONDITION / ABORTED COMMAND sense data and returns SATI_FAILURE_CHECK_RESPONSE_DATA; otherwise if the ATA data address is NULL it returns SATI_FAILURE with no sense data built; otherwise, for the extended self-test, self-test or information-exceptions log page sequence types, it builds that log page in the SCSI response and returns SATI_COMPLETE; for any other sequence type it builds CHECK CONDITION / ABORTED COMMAND sense data and returns SATI_FAILURE_CHECK_RESPONSE_DATA.

functions.name: sati_read_capacity_16_translate_data
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sequence points to a valid translator sequence whose device pointer is valid, ata_input_data points to a valid ATA identify device data structure, and scsi_io is a valid SCSI IO whose response data buffer can take 16 bytes. Postcondition: the function returns nothing and writes response bytes 0-15 via sati_set_data_byte: bytes 0-7 hold the last LBA as a big-endian 64-bit value built from lba_high and lba_low, each reduced by one (lba_low always decremented with wrap, lba_high decremented only when both were 0); bytes 8-11 hold the sector size; byte 12 is 0; byte 13 is the physical-per-logical sector exponent if the enable bit in word 106 is set, otherwise 0; bytes 14-15 hold the lowest aligned LBA (0 if logical_sector_alignment is 0, else (physical_per_logical_sector - alignment) % physical_per_logical_sector, masked to 14 bits in byte 14) with byte 14 also ORed with 0x80 (tpe) when the device supports DSM trim and deterministic read after trim, plus 0x40 (tprz) when it also reads zero after trim; no locks or references are taken or released and the caller keeps ownership of all buffers.

functions.name: scic_sds_io_tag_construct
functions.prose_contract: Function-like macro (no function is defined). Precondition: sequence and task_index are integers; the macro does not mask them, so sequence should fit in 4 bits and task_index in 12 bits for a valid tag. Postcondition: the expansion is the value (sequence << 12) | task_index, with sequence in bits 12 and up and task_index in the low bits.
functions.contract: /*@ requires 0 <= sequence && sequence <= 15 && 0 <= task_index && task_index <= 4095; ensures result == ((sequence << 12) | task_index); */

functions.name: scic_sds_io_tag_get_index
functions.prose_contract: Function-like macro (no function is defined). Precondition: io_tag is an integer expression. Postcondition: the expansion is the low 12 bits of io_tag, (io_tag & 0x0FFF).

functions.name: scic_sds_io_sequence_increment
functions.prose_contract: Function-like macro (no function is defined). Precondition: value is an assignable integer lvalue, evaluated twice. Postcondition: value is assigned ((value + 1) & 0x000F), so it wraps from 15 to 0, and the assignment expression has that same value.

functions.name: iwx_run
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the softc lock is held (IWX_ASSERT_LOCKED) and vap->iv_bss is a valid iwx_node with a PHY context in the vap. Postcondition: it updates the PHY context (only for HT nodes), the firmware STA entry, the MAC context (with associd), smart-FIFO full-on, multicast permission, device power and MAC power mode, and for non-monitor opmode initialises rate scaling; it returns 0 on success, or the first nonzero error from any of these steps (printing a message) without running the later steps, and monitor mode returns 0 right after the power update, skipping rate scaling.

functions.name: i40e_parse_discover_capabilities
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw is a valid i40e_hw and buff points to at least cap_count capability elements returned by the firmware discover-capabilities command. Postcondition: if list_type_opc is neither the device nor the function list opcode, the function returns without changing anything; otherwise it fills hw->dev_caps or hw->func_caps (chosen by the opcode) from each element according to its id (and sets hw->num_wol_proxy_filters and hw->wol_proxy_vsi_seid for the WOL/proxy id), unknown ids being ignored. It then forces fcoe to FALSE, recounts hw->num_ports as the number of the 4 PRTGEN_CNF registers (read through the admin queue) whose port-disable bit is clear, and on X722 sets num_ports to 4 if the NVM OCP config word has the OCP-enabled bit (when the NVM was acquired for reading and the read succeeded, releasing the NVM afterwards). If num_ports is nonzero it sets hw->partition_id = pf_id/num_ports + 1 and hw->num_partitions = (count of set bits in valid_functions)/num_ports, and finally sets rx_buf_chain_len to I40E_MAX_CHAINED_RX_BUFFERS. It returns nothing and reports no errors.

functions.name: genkbd_keyaction
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: kbd has a valid keymap and kb_lastact array, keycode is a valid key index (also valid after adding ALTGR_OFFSET for the keymap lookup), and shiftstate and accents point to valid ints holding the current modifier state and pending accent state. Postcondition: on key release (up) it takes the last recorded action for the key, resets it to NOP, and if that was NOP it clears SHIFTAON in *shiftstate and returns NOKEY; otherwise it clears the matching modifier or lock-down bits (calling set_lockkey_state for ALK when an auto-shift key was released with SHIFTAON set), stores state without SHIFTAON in *shiftstate and returns SPCLKEY | RELKEY | action. On key press for a special key it records the action in kb_lastact if none is pending, treats a differing recorded action as NOP, and then: lock keys call set_lockkey_state; non-locking system keys clear *accents; BTAB clears *accents and returns with BKEY; modifier keys set their state bits, store state in *shiftstate and return SPCLKEY | action; NOP stores state and returns NOKEY; for any other action it stores state, and an accent key goes through save_accent_key returning NOKEY or ERRKEY unchanged, or the accent action (with MKEY if META is active); any other special key returns ERRKEY (clearing *accents) if an accent was pending, else SPCLKEY | action (with FKEY added for function keys). For a regular key it resets kb_lastact to NOP, stores state in *shiftstate, composes an accented character via make_accent_char if *accents > 0 (returning ERRKEY on failure), and returns the character with MKEY added if META is active.

functions.name: lio_get_set_intr_coalesce
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg1 points to a valid struct lio with a valid oct_dev, arg2 selects one of the LIO_* coalescing parameters, and oidp/req describe a sysctl request. Postcondition: for an unknown arg2 it returns EINVAL; it returns the sysctl_handle_64 error if that fails, and returns 0 without changes if the request is a read (newptr NULL) or the new value equals the old value shown; otherwise it stores the new value (adaptive enables as 0/1, the thresholds and rate fields only when the relevant rx/tx adaptive flag is set, the non-adaptive rx usecs, rx frames and tx frames values are held in locals), refreshes rx_usecs, rx_frames and tx_frames in intrmod_cfg from the device config, and pushes the config to firmware (a failure there is only logged). Then, if rx adaptive is off, it programs rx interrupt time and count (using the oct defaults for zero values) and returns the first nonzero error; if rx adaptive is on, it copies the config values into oct. The same follows for tx (tx interrupt count when tx adaptive is off, otherwise copies into oct). It returns 0 on success, with no locks or references taken or released.

functions.name: MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE(name, index)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function mfi_enqueue_<name>(cm), a static inline template inside MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE. Precondition: cm is a valid command with a valid cm_sc, and the caller holds whatever lock protects the queue. Postcondition: if any MFI_ON_MFIQ_MASK bit is set in cm->cm_flags it panics; otherwise cm is inserted at the tail of cm->cm_sc->mfi_<name>, MFI_ON_<index> is set in cm_flags, and the queue's q_length is incremented (q_max is raised if exceeded). Returns nothing.

functions.name: MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE(name, index)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function mfi_requeue_<name>(cm), a static inline template inside MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE. Precondition: cm is a valid command with a valid cm_sc, and the caller holds whatever lock protects the queue. Postcondition: if any MFI_ON_MFIQ_MASK bit is set in cm->cm_flags it panics; otherwise cm is inserted at the head of cm->cm_sc->mfi_<name>, MFI_ON_<index> is set in cm_flags, and the queue's q_length is incremented (q_max is raised if exceeded). Returns nothing.

functions.name: MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE(name, index)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function mfi_dequeue_<name>(sc), a static inline template inside MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE. Precondition: sc is a valid softc and the caller holds whatever lock protects the queue. Postcondition: if the queue mfi_<name> is empty it returns NULL and changes nothing; otherwise, if the first command lacks the MFI_ON_<index> flag it panics; else that command is removed from the queue, its MFI_ON_<index> flag is cleared, q_length is decremented, and it is returned.

functions.name: MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE(name, index)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function mfi_remove_<name>(cm), a static inline template inside MFIQ_COMMAND_QUEUE. Precondition: cm is a valid command with a valid cm_sc, and the caller holds whatever lock protects the queue. Postcondition: if MFI_ON_<index> is not set in cm->cm_flags it panics; otherwise cm is unlinked from cm->cm_sc->mfi_<name>, the flag is cleared, and q_length is decremented. Returns nothing.

functions.name: lxtphy_set_tp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc points to a valid mii_softc for an LXT PHY whose register accessors can be called. Postcondition: reads the PHY's MII_LXTPHY_CONFIG register, clears the CONFIG_100BASEFX bit and writes the value back, so the PHY is configured for twisted-pair; returns nothing and takes or releases no locks or references.

functions.name: mlx4_init_cmpt_table
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a valid mlx4 device whose caps (num_qps, num_srqs, num_cqs, reserved counts) and phys_caps.num_phys_eqs are set, and cmpt_base and cmpt_entry_sz describe the firmware cMPT layout. Postcondition: the function initializes the cMPT ICM tables for QP, SRQ, CQ and EQ in that order and returns 0 on success; if any mlx4_init_icm_table call fails, it cleans up (mlx4_cleanup_icm_table) only the cMPT tables already initialized, in reverse order, and returns that call's error code unchanged.

functions.name: mlx4_ib_post_send
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ibqp is a valid mlx4 QP, wr is a non-NULL chain of send work requests, bad_wr is writable, and the caller does not already hold the send queue lock. Postcondition: for a GSI QP with a RoCEv2 GSI companion the QP used may be switched to the companion according to the AH's GID type; the function takes qp->sq.lock (irqsave) and releases it before returning; if the device is in internal error state it sets *bad_wr = wr and returns -EIO with nothing posted; otherwise it builds WQEs for each request in order, and on the first failure sets *bad_wr to that request and returns -ENOMEM (send queue overflow), -EINVAL (too many SGEs or opcode out of range of mlx4_ib_opcode), or the error returned by build_sriov_qp0_header, build_lso_seg or build_mlx_header; requests before the failing one stay posted; if at least one request was posted it advances qp->sq.head by the count, rings the send doorbell, stamps the last WQE, and updates qp->sq_next_wqe; it returns 0 if all requests were posted.

functions.name: create_qp_common
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, pd, init_attr and caller_qp are valid, and *caller_qp is either NULL (the function allocates the QP) or points to a preallocated QP; for a user PD, udata holds a valid create-QP command. Postcondition: returns 0 after the QP has its resources, is registered with the hardware by mlx4_qp_alloc, and is added to the device and send/recv CQ reset-flow lists, with *caller_qp set to the QP if it was NULL; otherwise it returns a negative errno (-EINVAL for a bad tunnel QP request, -ENOMEM, -EFAULT, PTR_ERR of ib_umem_get, or an error from a helper such as set_rq_size, set_user_sq_size, set_kernel_sq_size, MTT, doorbell or QPN allocation). On failure the resources acquired so far are released in reverse order, and a QP allocated here is freed. The NETIF-unsupported path jumps to err with err still 0 (set by the earlier set_rq_size), so the function returns 0 without creating the QP and a QP allocated here is freed while *caller_qp stays NULL.

functions.name: mlx5e_sq_xmit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sq is a valid initialised send queue and mbp points to a non-NULL mbuf pointer owning a valid packet mbuf. Postcondition: if the queue lacks room for 2*MLX5_SEND_WQE_MAX_WQEBBS WQEBBs it returns ENOBUFS (enobuf counted), and if after padding with a NOP there is still not enough contiguous room before the ring end it returns ENOMEM (enobuf counted), in both cases leaving the mbuf untouched and owned by the caller; with KERN_TLS a deferred TLS packet returns 0 without posting a WQE here, and a TLS failure drops the mbuf with ENOMEM. Otherwise it builds the WQE (checksum/LSO/VXLAN flags, inlined headers with VLAN tag insertion, DMA segments) and on success returns 0: the WQE is posted by advancing sq->pc, the doorbell copy is stored, sq->mbuf[pi].mbuf holds the mbuf (or NULL if all data was inlined and the mbuf was freed), a reference to args.mst is taken when it is non-NULL, packet and byte statistics are updated, and *mbp is set to NULL. On failure it increments sq->stats.dropped, sets *mbp to NULL, frees the mbuf and returns EINVAL (zero or invalid header size, or inline header too big for a TSO/VXLAN packet or too small for VLAN insertion), the error from bus_dmamap_load_mbuf_sg, or, when m_defrag fails after EFBIG, the EFBIG error; no WQE is submitted.

functions.name: create_raw_packet_qp
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, qp, in and pd are valid, pd->uobject is non-NULL with a ucontext, and qp->sq.wqe_cnt / qp->rq.wqe_cnt say which of the send and receive queues to build. Postcondition: if qp->sq.wqe_cnt is nonzero it creates the TIS and then the SQ, and sets sq->base.container_mibqp = qp; if qp->rq.wqe_cnt is nonzero it sets rq->base.container_mibqp = qp, creates the RQ and then the TIR; on success it sets qp->trans_qp.base.mqp.qpn to the SQ's qpn if the SQ exists, otherwise to the RQ's qpn, and returns 0; on failure it returns the negative errno from the failing create helper and destroys the objects it created earlier (the RQ, SQ and TIS as applicable, in reverse order), so nothing is left allocated by this call.

functions.name: mpi3mr_app_mptcmds
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, cmd, td are unused; uarg points to a valid struct mpi3mr_ioctl_mptcmd (kernel copy) whose user pointers (mpi_msg_buf, buf_entry_list and each buffer entry's buffer) are user addresses, and the call is in a context that may sleep waiting for completion. Postcondition: the function validates the request, copies in the MPI request and buffer list, maps or uses preallocated DMA buffers, builds SGL/PRP, submits the admin command, waits up to karg->timeout (raised to at least MPI3MR_IOCTL_DEFAULT_TIMEOUT), then copies the MPI reply, sense data and data-in buffers back to user space, and returns 0 on success. Error returns: ENODEV if no adapter matches mrioc_id (or the SCSI task-management target is not found); ENOMEM if DMA memory was not allocated, or any kernel allocation, DMA mapping, reply buffer or NVMe PRP build fails; EINVAL (the initial rval, returned directly with nothing allocated) if mpi_msg_size or buf_entry_list_size is zero or mpi_msg_size*4 exceeds MPI3MR_AREQ_FRAME_SZ; EINVAL also for zero buffer entries, invalid buffer entries, excessive transfer sizes, bad NVMe format or NVMe SGL build failure; EFAULT on any copyin/copyout failure or an unrecoverable controller; EAGAIN if a command is pending, reset in progress, ioctls blocked, SGL build fails, or the command times out (a soft reset is requested unless the command was already reset); or the nonzero error from mpi3mr_submit_admin_cmd. On every path after the allocation of mpi_request it frees mpi_request, buffer_list, dma_buffers with their descriptors, kern_erb and the reply buffer; after the command was issued it also clears the ioctl command state, drops any target block_io count taken, and resets the sense state. The early-return paths before mpi_request is allocated free nothing.

functions.name: mpr_user_pass_thru
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid initialized mpr_softc whose lock is not held by the caller, and data points to a kernel-resident mpr_pass_thru_t whose user pointers are meant for copyin/copyout. Postcondition: returns EBUSY at once (touching nothing else) if another passthru is in progress (MPR_FLAGS_BUSY set); otherwise it sets BUSY, and returns EINVAL if the DataSize/DataDirection/DataOutSize combination is invalid (BOTH is rewritten to READ, otherwise DataOutSize is zeroed), if RequestSize exceeds sc->reqframesz, if no TM command can be allocated, if the SCSI IO DevHandle matches no target or is 0; returns the copyin error if copying the request from user space fails; for a task-management request returns EIO if the target is unknown or the TM command fails, else the copyout result of the reply; returns ENOMEM if no command can be allocated; otherwise submits the command and returns the wait error or the first copyout error (data, reply, SCSI sense or NVMe error response) or 0 on success; a NULL NVMe error-response buffer ends with the current err value. On every path after the BUSY check the BUSY flag is cleared, the command and its data buffer are freed or released, the request copy is freed, and the softc lock is released on return.

functions.name: mpssas_ir_shutdown
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid, attached mps softc with initialized mapping_table, sassc and targets arrays (max_devices entries), and howto holds the reboot flags; the caller does not hold the mps lock, because the function takes and releases it around the wait. Postcondition: if IR firmware is loaded and a volume with nonzero physical_id and zero missing_count is found among the volume-mapping indices, a RAID_ACTION SYSTEM_SHUTDOWN_INITIATED request is sent with a 5-second sleepable wait (the reply is ignored) and the command is freed if it is still held; if the command allocation fails it prints a message and skips the request. In every case it then sets stop_at_shutdown on each target with nonzero handle and supports_SSU according to enable_ssu (0: FALSE; 1 or any other value: TRUE only for non-SATA-SSD; 2: TRUE only for non-SSD... see code: 2 gives TRUE except SATA SSD becomes FALSE; 3: TRUE) and finally calls mpssas_SSU_to_SATA_devices(sc, howto). It returns nothing.

functions.name: mps_user_pass_thru
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc and data points to a kernel copy of a passthru descriptor whose user pointers refer to user memory; the caller holds no mps lock. Postcondition: returns EBUSY at once if another passthru is in progress (the busy flag is left alone); otherwise sets the busy flag for the duration and returns EINVAL for an invalid DataSize/DataDirection/DataOutSize combination, for RequestSize larger than sc->reqframesz, for a failed TM command allocation, or for a SCSI IO request with DevHandle 0; returns the copyin error if copying the request or data-out fails (a data-out copyin error is only logged and may be overwritten by later steps), ENOMEM if no command is available, EIO if a task-management request fails or has an unknown target handle, the mps_wait_command error if the command fails, or the copyout error for the data-in, reply or sense copy; returns 0 on success, with data-in, reply and autosense data copied to user space. On every path other than EBUSY the command (and its data buffer) is freed, the busy flag is cleared, the request buffer is freed and the lock is released.

functions.name: mpt_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev->si_drv1 is the mpt_softc and arg points to a kernel copy of the ioctl argument structure matching cmd (the 32-bit layout for the *32 commands on amd64). Postcondition: the command is dispatched (config header/page read, extended config header/page read, config page write, RAID action) with the softc lock held only around the mpt_user_* calls, any allocated page buffer is always freed, and unknown commands give ENOIOCTL; an error from the length check (EINVAL), from buffer allocation, from copyin/copyout or from the mpt_user_* helper is returned unchanged and the 32-bit struct is not updated. On success on amd64, for a *32 command the results are converted back into the caller's 32-bit structure, and the function returns 0.

functions.name: mrsas_init_fw
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid, attached mrsas softc whose registers are accessible. Postcondition: returns the error from mrsas_transition_to_ready if the firmware does not become ready; returns 1 if mrsas_init_adapter, mrsas_alloc_mfi_cmds, the ctrl_info malloc, mrsas_get_ctrl_info, mrsas_get_pd_list, mrsas_get_ld_list or a stream-detection allocation fails (in the last case the partially allocated streamDetectByLD is freed and set to NULL; other earlier allocations are not released); returns 0 on success, after configuring MSI-X (msix_enable set from mrsas_allocate_msix), allocating ctrl_info, setting up the RAID map and JBOD map (a RAID-map setup failure is only logged), initializing target_list, pd_list and ld_ids, and computing max_sectors_per_req (clamped to the controller limit when non-zero) and fast_path_io when uneven spans are supported.

functions.name: mthca_multicast_detach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ibqp is a valid QP of an mthca device and gid points to a valid GID; the caller does not hold dev->mcg_table.mutex. Postcondition: returns 0 after removing the QP from the multicast group MGM entry identified by gid; if that was the group's last QP, the MGM/AMGM entry is also unlinked and, when it was an AMGM entry, freed to the allocator. Returns PTR_ERR of the failure if the mailbox allocation fails (nothing else is done), the error from find_mgm, -EINVAL if the MGID or the QP is not found in the MGM, or the first error from a failed WRITE_MGM or READ_MGM firmware command (later steps are skipped, so the entry may be partially updated). The mutex is taken and released and the mailbox is freed on every path after the mailbox was allocated.

functions.name: mthca_alloc_srq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, pd, attr and srq are valid; attr->max_wr and attr->max_sge are the requested sizes; udata is non-NULL for a userspace SRQ and NULL for a kernel SRQ. Postcondition: returns -EINVAL if attr->max_wr or attr->max_sge exceeds the device limits, or (non-memfree only) if the descriptor size exceeds max_desc_sz; returns -ENOMEM if no SRQ number is available (or, on memfree, if the doorbell allocation fails); otherwise returns the error from mthca_table_get, mailbox allocation, mthca_alloc_srq_buf or mthca_SW2HW_SRQ. If mthca_array_set fails it unwinds and returns the status of mthca_HW2SW_SRQ, which can be 0 even though the call failed. On success it returns 0, the SRQ is in the SRQ table with refcount 1, first_free = 0 and last_free = max-1, attr->max_wr and attr->max_sge are updated to the actual values, and the mailbox is freed. On any failure the acquired resources (SRQ number, ICM entry, doorbell, mailbox, buffer) are released in reverse order, and the SRQ is no longer in the hardware.

functions.name: mvneta_update_mib
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc points to a valid attached mvneta softc whose MIB and drop-counter registers are readable and whose ifp is valid; the TX queue locks are not required. Postcondition: returns nothing; every nonzero hardware MIB counter is added to the matching sysctl_mib counter and to the matching ifnet counter (IBYTES, IERRORS, IPACKETS, IMCASTS, OBYTES, OPACKETS, OMCASTS, COLLISIONS, or OERRORS) according to its register number; the PDFC and POFC register values are added to counter_pdfc and counter_pofc and each to IFCOUNTER_IQDROPS; a positive counter_watchdog_mib is added to IFCOUNTER_OERRORS and reset to 0; for each TX ring a positive drv_error is added to IFCOUNTER_OERRORS and reset to 0.

functions.name: nm_vale_flush
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ft points to a work area holding n packet fragment descriptors (the first fragment of each packet carrying its ft_frags count), followed by the dst_ents queue array and dsts index array, all queues empty (bq_head == NM_FT_NULL); na is a VALE port attached to a bridge. Postcondition: each packet is looked up in the first pass and dropped if the virtio header placement is invalid, the lookup returns a port >= NM_BDG_NOPORT, or the destination is the source port or an inactive port; the remaining packets are queued per destination and, in the second pass, copied (or passed to the mismatch datapath when virtio header lengths differ) into slots leased on the destination RX ring, with unusable destinations (NULL, NAF_SW_ONLY, not in netmap mode, ring not open, kring stopped) skipped and packets dropped if space is lacking, unused leased slots rolled back or zeroed, hwtail advanced and the destination notified when this lease is the oldest one (with possible retries), all destination and broadcast queues reset to empty, and the function always returns 0.

functions.name: linux_ntsync_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td is the calling thread and args holds a file descriptor, a Linux ntsync ioctl command and a user-space pointer to the command's argument. Postcondition: returns the errno from fget_cap (with no fdrop) if the descriptor cannot be obtained; otherwise it dispatches on the command, copying arguments in and results out with copyin/copyout, and returns 0 on success. Non-create commands (semaphore, mutex, event operations other than create and wait) return ENOTTY when the file is not DTYPE_NTSYNC, and an unknown command returns ENOTTY. Any copyin, copyout or helper error is returned, and copyout is skipped after an earlier failure except that WAIT_ANY/WAIT_ALL still copy out on EOWNERDEAD (returning EOWNERDEAD unless the copyout itself fails, in which case that error is lost) and MUTEX_READ copies out whenever the helper set doco, even if the helper returned an error. The file reference taken by fget_cap is dropped with fdrop on every path after a successful fget_cap.

functions.name: ocs_action
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sim is a CAM SIM whose softc is an initialized ocs_softc and ccb is a valid CCB whose func_code selects the request. Postcondition: the function dispatches on ccb_h->func_code and sets the CCB status; in most cases it completes the CCB with xpt_done(ccb). XPT_SCSI_IO: a CDB pointer that is also physical gives CAM_REQ_INVALID with xpt_done. Otherwise ocs_initiator_io is called. A return of 0 sets CAM_REQ_INPROG|CAM_SIM_QUEUED with no xpt_done (the CCB stays queued). CAM_REQUEUE_REQ freezes and releases the devq with a 100 ms timeout, sets CAM_REQUEUE_REQ, and calls xpt_done. Any other return clears CAM_SIM_QUEUED and sets status rc if rc > 0, else CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT, then calls xpt_done. XPT_PATH_INQ fills the pathinq fields and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS gives CAM_REQ_INVALID if the transport is not FC, CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE if target_id > OCS_MAX_TARGETS or the target state is OCS_TGT_STATE_NONE, else fills the settings and gives CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS gives CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_CALC_GEOMETRY computes the geometry and completes. XPT_GET_SIM_KNOB gives CAM_REQ_INVALID if the transport is not FC, else fills the WWNN/WWPN, role and valid fields and gives CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_SET_SIM_KNOB gives CAM_REQ_INVALID if the transport is not FC; otherwise it may change the port role via ocs_fcp_change_role and gives CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_ABORT dispatches on the function code of the aborted CCB: ATIO and INOT go to ocs_abort_atio and ocs_abort_inot, SCSI_IO gives CAM_UA_ABORT if ocs_abort_initiator_io returns nonzero, else CAM_REQ_CMP, and any other code gives CAM_REQ_INVALID. XPT_ABORT never calls xpt_done in this function. XPT_RESET_BUS takes the port offline and then online, and gives CAM_REQ_CMP, or CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR if going offline fails; the online result is only logged. XPT_RESET_DEV gives CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE if there is no node, CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR if IO allocation or the send of the LUN-reset TMF fails, else CAM_REQ_CMP. It resets the CRN for fcp2 devices. XPT_EN_LUN enables or disables the LUN resource and gives CAM_REQ_CMP, or the status from ocs_tgt_resource_get on failure. XPT_ACCEPT_TARGET_IO and XPT_IMMEDIATE_NOTIFY queue the CCB on the resource list with CAM_REQ_INPROG and no xpt_done, or give CAM_DEV_NOT_THERE if no resource exists. XPT_NOTIFY_ACKNOWLEDGE gives CAM_REQ_CMP_ERR if no IO is found for the tag, else sends a TMF response or clears the abort-notify flag and gives CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_CONT_TARGET_IO calls ocs_target_io and calls xpt_done only if it returns nonzero. Any unknown func_code gives CAM_REQ_INVALID with xpt_done. There is no return value.

functions.name: ocs_dump_to_host
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ocs is a valid initialized device; buf is a user buffer writable for buflen bytes. Postcondition: returns -1 immediately if buflen is 0 or the array of ocs_dma_t descriptors cannot be allocated; otherwise it allocates ceil(buflen/OCS_MAX_DMA_ALLOC) DMA buffers, registers them as the dump location (function-specific flag 0), generates the dump, and copies each buffer to the user buffer in order. It returns the nonzero rc from ocs_dma_alloc, ocs_hw_set_dump_location or ocs_gen_dump if one fails, and -1 if any ocs_copy_to_user fails (copying continues for the remaining buffers), else 0. Every DMA buffer and the descriptor array are freed on all paths after allocation; nothing is left owned by the caller.

functions.name: ocs_hw_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hw points to a set-up ocs_hw_t (ocs_hw_setup has been done, or a reset has cleaned up) whose cmd_head and cmd_pending lists are empty; otherwise the function returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR immediately. Postcondition: returns OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS after SLI init, queue init, RQ buffer and sequence pool allocation, rpi_ref setup, FCFI registration, IO setup, queue arming, hash setup and hw->state = OCS_HW_STATE_ACTIVE, and after allocating domain_dmem and fcf_dmem (and loop_map if not yet allocated, whose failure is only logged). It returns OCS_HW_RTN_ERROR if the command lists are non-empty, sli_init fails or a configured queue count exceeds the SLI maximum; OCS_HW_RTN_NO_MEMORY if an allocation (rnode_mem, seq_pool, rpi_ref, domain_dmem or fcf_dmem) fails; or the nonzero error code from a failing sub-step (auto xfer rdy config, health check, queue init, header template registration, rx_allocate, REG_FCFI/MRQ config, reqtag/setup_io/init_io, DIF mode). A failed DIF seed setting logs and returns the current rc, which may be success. Failures of ocs_hw_rx_post, ethernet license, rqpair init, send_frame IO allocation, watchdog config and loop_map allocation are only logged. On failure earlier-allocated resources are not released.

functions.name: ocs_hw_wq_process_io
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg points to a valid ocs_hw_io_t whose hw pointer is valid, cqe points to the WQ completion entry for it, and for an OCS_HW_IO_TARGET_RSP with io->is_port_owned set, io->axr_buf is valid and the caller does not hold io->axr_lock. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it updates io->quarantine, io->quarantine_first_phase, the secondary IO's quarantine flag and io->xbusy from the CQE, removes the IO's timed WQE, and derives len (and ext for ELS requests) from the CQE according to io->type. If status is nonzero it reads the extended status. It may then call ocs_hw_io_abort, either for an initiator IO with config.i_only_aab or for a non-originator IO with XB set. If that abort returns OCS_HW_RTN_SUCCESS, it latches status, ext and len in io->saved_* with io->status_saved set and jumps to the exit, so the secondary IO is not freed, io->done is not called and the out-of-order unsolicited callbacks are skipped. Any other abort result (including ABORT_IN_PROGRESS) is only logged and processing continues. Otherwise it frees io->sec_hio if present and clears it. If io->done is non-NULL it clears it, substitutes the saved status, len and ext if status_saved was set (clearing the flag), restores the default SGL, and calls done once. Then, if an out-of-order AXR command was flagged, it passes the command sequence to the bounce callback (if set) or the unsolicited callback, and likewise the data sequence if an out-of-order AXR data was flagged. On every exit, io->axr_lock is released if it was taken for a port-owned target response.

functions.name: pci_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, cmd, data (a kernel pointer to the structure matching cmd), flag and td are as passed by the ioctl layer, and the caller does not hold the bus topology lock. Postcondition: returns EPERM without taking the lock if the descriptor is not opened for writing and cmd is not one of the read-only commands (GETCONF variants, GETBAR, LISTVPD); otherwise it takes the bus topology lock, dispatches on cmd, releases the lock and returns 0 or an errno. For GETCONF it allocates and frees a temporary pci_conf_io and pattern buffer, returns 0 for list-changed, past-end, and normal walks (status, offset, generation and num_matches updated, matches copied out), EINVAL for bad pattern sizes or a failed pattern copyin, or the copyout error if copying a match fails. For READ/WRITE it returns EINVAL for a bad width, a negative or misaligned register, or ENODEV if the device is not found (except the FreeBSD6 read compat case, which sets pi_data to -1 and returns 0), and otherwise 0 after reading or writing config space. GETBAR returns ENODEV if the device is missing, EINVAL if there is no such BAR, else 0 with base, length and enabled filled in. ATTACHED returns 0 with pi_data set, or ENODEV. LISTVPD returns ENODEV or the result of pci_list_vpd. BARMMAP returns EPERM for an RW mapping on a read-only descriptor, ENODEV if the device is missing, else the result of pci_bar_mmap. BARIO returns ENODEV or the result of pci_bar_io. Any other cmd returns ENOTTY.

functions.name: pci_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, data and td are valid for the given ioctl cmd, with data pointing to the command-specific structure, and the caller does not hold the bus topology lock. Postcondition: if the descriptor was not opened for writing and cmd is not one of the read-only commands (PCIOCGETCONF and its compat variants, PCIOCGETBAR, PCIOCLISTVPD), it returns EPERM without taking the lock; otherwise it takes the bus topology lock, dispatches on cmd, releases the lock on every path and returns the result. The result is 0 on success. PCIOCGETCONF may return EINVAL (bad pattern sizes or a failed copyin of patterns) or the copyout error. PCIOCREAD and PCIOCWRITE return EINVAL for a bad width, a negative or misaligned register, and ENODEV when no device is found (the FreeBSD6 read compat case returns 0 with pi_data set to -1). PCIOCGETBAR returns ENODEV or EINVAL (no such BAR). PCIOCATTACHED returns ENODEV if no device is found. PCIOCLISTVPD returns ENODEV or the pci_list_vpd error. PCIOCBARMMAP returns EPERM when a read-write mapping is requested without write access, ENODEV, or the pci_bar_mmap error. PCIOCBARIO returns ENODEV or the pci_bar_io error. Unknown commands return ENOTTY.

functions.name: tiCOMMgntIOCTL
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tiRoot and agIOCTLPayload are valid non-null pointers, with tiRoot->tdData pointing to the driver root and agIOCTLPayload->FunctionSpecificArea large enough for the requested major/minor function. Postcondition: if the payload signature is not PMC_IOCTL_SIGNATURE it returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE and does nothing else; otherwise it dispatches on MajorFunction and returns the handler's status, which is IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS, IOCTL_CALL_PENDING, IOCTL_CALL_FAIL or whatever the delegated helper (SMP, FW control, NVMD, TMF, etc.) returns. IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE is returned for unhandled minor functions, and IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS from the PHY_DETAILS case. Within the tail shown, PORT_START/PORT_STOP (only when PHY_RESTART_TEST is defined) set payload Status to OK or INTERNAL_ERROR and return IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS. SEND_TMF delegates to tdsaSendTMFIoctl for the device-reset and LUN-reset minors, and otherwise returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE. GET_DRIVER_VERSION writes the version string into FunctionSpecificArea, sets Status OK and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS. An unknown major function sets Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED and returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE. The event-log and FW-info cases can return IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS early with NO_MORE_DATA.

functions.name: tiCOMMgntIOCTL
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tiRoot and agIOCTLPayload are valid, and tiRoot->tdData is an initialised tdsaRoot_t; agParam1..agParam3 are valid for the requested major/minor function (for IOCTL_MJ_MODE_CTL_PAGE agParam2 points to a bit32 mode operation). Postcondition: if the payload Signature is not PMC_IOCTL_SIGNATURE it returns IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE; otherwise it dispatches on MajorFunction/MinorFunction and returns the value set by the handler: IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS (for example IOCTL_MJ_PHY_DETAILS always returns it after filling the PhyDetails array, the event log, FW info, FW revision and driver version cases return it after writing Status and Length, and the out-of-range or no-data cases return it with Status NO_MORE_DATA or EVENTLOG_DISABLED), IOCTL_CALL_PENDING (IOCTL_MJ_GET_DEVICE_LUN on success, IOCTL_MJ_PHY_GENERAL_STATUS when the request was started), IOCTL_CALL_FAIL (IOCTL_MJ_PHY_GENERAL_STATUS when Length is too small or the query fails, in which case the pending FW control state is cleared on query failure), or the status code from a delegated handler or saSet/GetControllerConfig. Unknown major functions set Status to IOCTL_ERR_STATUS_NOT_SUPPORTED and return IOCTL_CALL_INVALID_CODE, as do unmatched minor functions without a status assignment. For IOCTL_MJ_PHY_GENERAL_STATUS a successful start records param1, param2 and the payload in tdFWControlEx with inProgress set to 1, and a NOT_SUPPORTED result sets Status NOT_SUPPORTED and returns IOCTL_CALL_SUCCESS.

functions.name: agtiapi_MapDek
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pCard and dek_map are valid, and pCard's mapping tables and map_cache/map_mempool are initialised; the caller serialises access to the per-device mapping list. Postcondition: returns -E_CHANNEL_INDEX, -E_DEVICE_INDEX, -E_LUN_INDEX, -E_DEK_INDEX, -E_DEK_TABLE or -E_LBA_RANGE if the channel, device, lun, dek index, dek table or LBA range (min >= max) check fails, with nothing changed; otherwise, if the CLEAR flag is set in dekMapEntry[0], every entry on the (chan,device,lun) list matching lba range, dek table, dek index and the looked-up kek index is unlinked and passed to mempool_free, and it returns 0 if at least one was removed or -E_NOT_FOUND if none; otherwise if the VALID flag is set, a new entry is allocated from map_cache, filled from the request, an overlap warning is printed per overlapping existing entry, the entry is linked at the list head and it returns 0, or -E_MEMPOOL_ALLOC if allocation returned NULL; if neither flag is set it returns -E_FLAGS with the list unchanged.

functions.name: puc_bfe_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a puc device whose softc is valid and whose configuration callbacks (puc_config) work. Postcondition: it initialises the ioport, iomem and irq resource managers (returning the rman_init error with nothing else allocated if one fails), allocates the port array, reserves per-port resources and adds child devices, allocates and sets up the shared interrupt (falling back to polled mode if unavailable), probes and attaches the children (deleting those that fail), tears down the interrupt handler if no serdev children attached, and returns 0. If rman_manage_region, any puc_config step, puc_get_bar (ENXIO) or the per-port interrupt reservation (ENXIO) fails, it deletes the children, releases port and BAR resources, finalises the rmans, frees their descriptions and the port array, and returns that error.

functions.name: PWMBUS_ACCESSOR(channel, CHANNEL, u_int)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pwmbus_get_channel(dev, t). Precondition: dev is a valid device_t with a parent bus and t points to writable storage for a u_int (it is cast to uintptr_t *, so it must be large enough for a uintptr_t write). Postcondition: it returns the result of BUS_READ_IVAR on the parent of dev for PWMBUS_IVAR_CHANNEL, which is 0 on success with the channel value written through t, or an errno value from the parent bus on failure; it takes no locks or references.

functions.name: PWMBUS_ACCESSOR(channel, CHANNEL, u_int)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function pwmbus_set_channel(dev, t). Precondition: dev is a valid device_t with a parent bus. Postcondition: it returns the result of BUS_WRITE_IVAR on the parent of dev for PWMBUS_IVAR_CHANNEL with value t cast to uintptr_t, which is 0 on success or an errno value from the parent bus on failure; it takes no locks or references.

functions.name: qat_ocf_session_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev, crp, qat_instance and qat_ssession are valid pointers, and crp->crp_session refers to a live cryptodev session. Postcondition: returns CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS after storing the new contiguous session context and its size in qat_ssession (also setting aadLen and, unless the mode is cipher-only, authLen); returns CPA_STATUS_FAIL if crp_session or its params are NULL or the csp mode is unhandled; CPA_STATUS_UNSUPPORTED for an unsupported cipher or auth algorithm, or if no hash definition is found when csp_auth_mlen is 0; CPA_STATUS_RESOURCE if contigmalloc fails; or the error status from cpaCySymSessionCtxGetSize or cpaCySymDpInitSession. On every failure after allocation the session memory is freed, and qat_ssession->sessionCtx and sessionCtxSize are left unset on failure.

functions.name: dcCreateRequest
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the service, session descriptor, cookie, source and destination buffer lists, results and optional opData are valid, and buffer lengths were already checked by the caller. Postcondition: if writing either buffer list descriptor fails, that error status is returned at once and the cookie is not populated; otherwise the cookie is filled, the request template is copied into the cookie's message, checksum seeds and CRC mode are set, session request-type, SOP and consumed-bytes state is updated, the compression request parameters are populated, and the request parameter flags (SOP/EOP/BFINAL/CNV/CRC mode) are computed; the remainder of the function after that point is not visible here.

functions.name: LacSymKey_KeyGenSslTls_GenCommon
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: instanceHandle is a valid crypto service instance, pKeyGenSslTlsOpData points to the op-data structure matching lacCmdId (SSL3, TLS v1.1, v1.2 or HKDF), and pKeyGenOutputData is a valid flat buffer. Postcondition: if pKeyGenCb is NULL it returns the result of LacSymKey_SslTlsSync and does nothing else. Otherwise it allocates a cookie from the sym cookie pool; if the pool is empty it returns CPA_STATUS_RESOURCE, and if the pool says retry it returns CPA_STATUS_RETRY. Next it builds the nested-hash content descriptor and request for the command, computing a hash of the secret when it is too long. It returns CPA_STATUS_FAIL if the physical address of a user label or of the output buffer is 0. It then writes the request and sends it with icp_adf_transPutMsg, returning that call's status. On success the request-count statistic is incremented and the cookie is owned by the in-flight request, to be released later by the response handler. On any failure after cookie allocation, the request-error statistic is incremented and the cookie is returned to the pool. The function returns CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS on success, otherwise the error status.

functions.name: LacSymKey_CheckParamSslTls
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pKeyGenOpData points to an operation-data structure matching cmdId (CpaCyKeyGenSslOpData for SSL3, CpaCyKeyGenTlsOpData for TLS 1.1/1.2, CpaCyKeyGenHKDFOpData for the HKDF commands), pGeneratedKeyBuffer points to a flat buffer, and hashAlgCipher is a hash algorithm or HKDF cipher suite valid for cmdId. Postcondition: the function only reads its inputs and returns CPA_STATUS_SUCCESS if every check passes. It returns CPA_STATUS_INVALID_PARAM if cmdId is not a supported SSL/TLS/HKDF command, or if any of the following is violated: secret length, seed length, output length, op code, user label length, hash algorithm (TLS1.2), number of labels, HKDF seed/info/label length or sublabel flags, or the generated-key buffer being smaller than the required output length. It also returns the status produced by LAC_CHECK_NULL_PARAM (an error status) if pKeyGenOpData, pGeneratedKeyBuffer, its pData, the secret/seed pData, or the user label pData (when the user-defined op is selected) is NULL.

functions.name: LacSymQat_UseSymConstantsTable
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pSession points to a valid session descriptor (with a valid pInstance) and pCipherOffset and pHashOffset point to writable Cpa8U storage. Postcondition: both offsets are first set to 0; for chaining commands (CIPHER_HASH or HASH_CIPHER) the optimised content descriptor is queried, which currently always yields CPA_FALSE. For a CIPHER command (or optimised chaining) it returns CPA_FALSE if the cipher key length exceeds sizeof(icp_qat_fw_comn_req_hdr_cd_pars_t), otherwise it looks up the cipher config offset, stores it in *pCipherOffset and sets the result to CPA_TRUE iff that offset is > 0. For an AUTH command (or optimised chaining with SHRAM constants) it returns CPA_FALSE if digestVerify is set, or if the optimised path is not in use and qatHashMode is ICP_QAT_HW_AUTH_MODE1; otherwise it looks up the auth config offset, stores it in *pHashOffset and sets the result to CPA_TRUE iff that offset is > 0. For other commands, or when no branch applies, it returns CPA_FALSE. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: check_accel_unit_config
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: accel_dev and accel_dev->hw_device are valid and the general configuration section is readable; num_cy_au, num_dc_au and num_inline_au are the accel-unit counts configured for each service. Postcondition: returns EFAULT if the services-enabled parameter cannot be read, if any listed service is unsupported by the hardware capabilities, if DC/CY/inline units are configured while their service is not enabled, if the three unit counts do not sum to the total number of accel units, or if an enabled cy/dc/inline service has zero units; otherwise returns 0. hw_data->service_mask is overwritten with the parsed service mask once the service-vs-unit checks up to and including the inline check pass, so it may already be updated when the later sum or zero-count checks return EFAULT; it is not modified on the earlier error returns. Error paths print diagnostics via device_printf.

functions.name: qat_crypto_sym_rxintr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: msg is a completed firmware response whose opaque field holds a valid in-flight symmetric cookie, with its session still active and its crypto request and DMA buffers loaded. Postcondition: the DMA buffers (AAD, main and, when present, output) are unloaded; if the session's auth_mlen is non-zero, the digest is compared with the hardware result on VERIFY_DIGEST requests (setting error to EBADMSG on mismatch) and otherwise copied back into the request; the cookie is freed; the session's inflight count is decremented under qs_session_mtx and, if a wakeup was needed and inflight reached zero, qs_need_wakeup is cleared; crp_etype is set to 0 or EBADMSG, crypto_done is called on the request, crypto_unblock is called for CRYPTO_SYMQ if the wakeup was pending, and the function always returns 1.

functions.name: ecore_hw_lock
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_hwfn and p_ptt are valid and p_ptt can be used for register access; block says whether the caller may sleep and wait. Postcondition: if the resource bit is already set in this PF's lock register it returns ECORE_BUSY without registering a request. Otherwise it writes a lock request for the resource and polls the register up to HW_LOCK_MAX_RETRIES times, sleeping 5 ms between polls when block is true; if the resource bit becomes set it returns ECORE_SUCCESS and the hardware lock is held (the request is not cleared). If block is false and the first poll does not show the bit, it clears the pending request and returns ECORE_BUSY. If all retries are used up it logs a notice, clears the pending request and returns ECORE_TIMEOUT.

functions.name: ecore_mfw_get_fcoe_tlv_value
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p_tlv, p_drv_buf and p_buf are valid pointers, and for indexed TLV types the computed idx is within the bounds of the corresponding array in p_drv_buf. Postcondition: for a TLV type whose value field has its *_set flag true, p_buf->p_val is set to point at that field inside p_drv_buf and the field size in bytes is returned; for timestamp TLV types (CRC error, FLOGI, FLOGI ACC, FLOGI RJT, PLOGI, PLOGI ACC, LOGO, ABTS and SCSI check timestamps) the result of ecore_mfw_get_tlv_time_value on the corresponding timestamp field and p_buf is returned unconditionally; for a known type whose *_set flag is false, or for an unknown tlv_type, -1 is returned and p_buf->p_val is not modified. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: qlnx_pci_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a PCI device for the qlnx driver; its softc is zeroed and initialised by this function, so no prior setup is required. Postcondition: returns ENOMEM if device_get_softc yields NULL, and ENXIO without calling qlnx_release if qlnx_valid_device fails. Otherwise it maps the BARs, allocates the DMA tags, initialises the hardware, allocates the MSI-X vectors, interrupts and taskqueues, and, for a non-VF device, the grcdump and idle-check buffers and the error-recovery taskqueue. It then starts the slowpath, reads the flash size and MFW version (a PF failure there triggers a dump and skips ahead to the cdev creation step), initialises the ifnet, adds the sysctls, creates the ioctl cdev for a non-VF device, optionally registers RDMA and initialises SR-IOV, and returns 0. Any later failure (resource mapping, DMA tag, hardware init, insufficient MSI-X, pci_alloc_msix, interrupt or taskqueue setup, buffer allocation, slowpath start, cdev creation) calls qlnx_release(ha) and returns ENXIO.

functions.name: ql_rcv_isr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ha is a valid host structure and sds_idx indexes an initialised status descriptor ring of ha whose ring base is mapped; count is the maximum number of descriptors batches to process. Postcondition: it sets rcv_active to 1 and, if ha->stop_rcv is already set, clears it and returns 0 at once; otherwise it processes up to count completion entries starting at sdsr_next (RCV_PKT, SGL_RCV and SGL_LRO entries are passed to qla_rx_intr or qla_lro_intr; an unknown opcode, an invalid continuation descriptor or a qla_rcv_cont_sds failure ends the loop), zeroes consumed descriptors, advances comp_idx and periodically updates the consumer index and sdsr_next when the threshold sds_cidx_thres is exceeded, flushes soft LRO if enabled, and if stop_rcv became set skips the rest and returns 0; else it updates the consumer index and sdsr_next if comp_idx changed, otherwise replenishes normal rx buffers when rx_free exceeds std_replenish; it returns (uint32_t)-1 if the descriptor at the final comp_idx has a nonzero opcode (more work pending), else 0; rcv_active is cleared to 0 on every return path and the caller keeps ownership of ha.

functions.name: qls_mbx_get_mgmt_ctrl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ha and t_status are valid pointers and ha->mbox points to a usable mailbox array of Q81_NUM_MBX_REGISTERS words. Postcondition: *t_status is first set to 0; the mailbox is zeroed and Q81_MBX_GET_MGMT_CTL is sent via qls_mbx_cmd (1 word out, 2 words in); if the command fails it prints a message and returns -1 with *t_status still 0; otherwise *t_status = mbox[1] and 0 is returned.

functions.name: r88e_ratectl_tx_complete_periodic
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: buf points to len readable bytes holding a struct r92c_rx_stat descriptor followed by packed r88e_fw_c2h_txreport2_entry records, and sc is a valid softc with node_list covering indices below min(64, macid_rpt2_max_num). Postcondition: returns void; if len is smaller than the Rx descriptor it returns without doing anything; otherwise it skips the descriptor, builds a 64-bit macid bitmap from tsf_low (high half) and rxdw4 (low half), and walks entries for macid = 0 up to min(64, macid_rpt2_max_num) while enough bytes remain for a full entry, consuming one entry per macid; for each macid whose bitmap bit is clear it skips the entry, and for each set bit it computes nframes (total including drops), nsuccess (total minus drops) and nretries (retry1..4 plus drops), logs a debug message, and if sc->node_list[macid] is non-NULL calls ieee80211_ratectl_tx_update on that node's vap with these stats; no references, locks or memory are acquired or released by the caller.

functions.name: safe_process
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a safe device with a valid softc and crp is a crypto request with a valid session, and the caller does not hold sc_ringmtx. Postcondition: if the ring is full while requests are queued on the chip, it sets CRYPTO_SYMQ in sc_needwakeup and returns ERESTART without queuing; otherwise it builds the SA, DMA maps and particle descriptors in the front ring entry, advances the front, calls safe_feed, and returns 0 with the request queued. On a setup error (EINVAL for AAD/payload gap, misaligned or too-big coffset, bypass over 96, or non-aligned or non-uniform uio; ENOMEM for DMA map or mbuf failures) it frees the destination mbufs and maps and unloads the source map. If the error is ERESTART (mbuf allocation failure while requests are queued on the chip) it sets CRYPTO_SYMQ in sc_needwakeup and returns ERESTART. Otherwise it sets crp_etype to the error, calls crypto_done(crp) and returns 0. sc_ringmtx is released on every return.

functions.name: efx_build_signed_image_write_buffer
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: bufferp points to a writable buffer of buffer_size bytes, infop describes a signed image (eii_imagep, eii_headerp inside the image, eii_image_size) and headerpp is a valid pointer. Postcondition: returns EINVAL if any argument is NULL or buffer_size is 0, if the image info is not a valid signed image, or if a located chunk (CMS header, image header, code, trailer, signature) does not fit within buffer_size; otherwise it fills the buffer with 0xFF and writes the chunk headers and payload copies for the CMS header, reflash header, code, reflash trailer and signature. In that case it sets *headerpp to the copied image header inside the buffer and returns 0, but it returns ENOSPC if any chunk header or chunk data would not fit in the buffer, in which case the buffer may be partly written and *headerpp may or may not have been set. The function takes no locks or references.

functions.name: ef10_get_datapath_caps
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: enp is a valid EF10 NIC whose en_nic_cfg is writable and whose MCDI interface can be used. Postcondition: it queries the PF count and executes MC_CMD_GET_CAPABILITIES, fills the datapath capability fields of en_nic_cfg from the response, and returns 0. Capability fields newer than the response version are set to defaults (fixed 8K or invalid VI window by family, legacy MAC stats count, mark max 0). On failure it returns a nonzero error and the fields after the failing step are not updated: the error from ef10_mcdi_get_pf_count or from the MCDI command (emr_rc), EMSGSIZE if the response is shorter than MC_CMD_GET_CAPABILITIES_OUT_LEN, ENOTSUP if the firmware does not report the 14-byte RX prefix, or (with EFSYS_OPT_RX_SCALE) EINVAL if the RSS-limited flag is set on a family other than Medford2, Medford or Huntington. It acquires no locks or references.

functions.name: efx_hash_bytes
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: input points to at least length readable bytes (it may be unused when length is 0), and length is a size_t. Postcondition: returns the 32-bit Jenkins-style hash c, computed from the seed EFX_HASH_INITIAL_VALUE + (uint32_t)length + init, with the input read as little-endian 32-bit words in 12-byte blocks, mixed after each block longer than 12 and finalised over the remaining 1..12 bytes; when length is 0 no input is read and the seed value is returned unchanged. The function has no error return, does not modify the input, and acquires or releases no locks or references.

functions.name: sfxge_tx_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid SFXGE softc whose efx NIC config and interrupt state (intr.state is SFXGE_INTR_INITIALIZED, intr.n_alloc set) are already initialized and whose device sysctl tree exists. Postcondition: returns EINVAL (after logging) if sfxge_tx_dpl_get_max <= 0, sfxge_tx_dpl_get_non_tcp_max <= 0 or sfxge_tx_dpl_put_max < 0, leaving sc->txq_count unchanged on those early checks except that it is reset to 0 only on later failures; otherwise it sets sc->txq_count, sc->tso_fw_assisted (FATSOV1/FATSOV2 bits cleared when the NIC lacks or has disabled that firmware-assisted TSO) and creates the sysctl node sc->txqs_node, returning ENOMEM if that node is NULL; then, when sc->txq_dynamic_cksum_toggle_supported is B_FALSE, it initializes the non-checksum and IP-checksum queues, and it initializes one IP/TCP/UDP-checksum queue per index in 0..txq_count-SFXGE_EVQ0_N_TXQ(sc); on success it initializes the Tx statistics and returns 0. If any sfxge_tx_qinit fails, the queues already initialized are finalized in reverse order, sc->txq_count is set to 0, and that call's nonzero error code is returned; the sysctl node is not removed explicitly.

functions.name: siisaction
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sim is a valid CAM SIM whose softc is a siis_channel, ccb is a valid CCB, and the caller holds the channel mutex ch->mtx (asserted). Postcondition: depending on func_code, XPT_ATA_IO/XPT_SCSI_IO either returns without completing the ccb (when siis_check_ids fails, when the command is begun via siis_begin_transaction, or when a command collision freezes the ccb in ch->frozen and freezes the simq), or sets CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT when there are no devices or the target id is invalid for a channel without port multiplier; XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS and XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS return early without completion if siis_check_ids fails, otherwise update or report the device settings (set pm control bits for PM) and set CAM_REQ_CMP; XPT_RESET_BUS/XPT_RESET_DEV call siis_reset and set CAM_REQ_CMP; XPT_PATH_INQ fills the path inquiry structure and sets CAM_REQ_CMP; XPT_ABORT, XPT_TERM_IO and any unknown func_code set CAM_REQ_INVALID. In all paths that do not return early, the ccb is completed with xpt_done; nothing is returned.

functions.name: smartpqi_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a smartpqi PCI device whose softc may be obtained via device_get_softc.
