Postcondition: if the softc is NULL it returns EINVAL; otherwise the softc is zeroed and set up, and it returns 0 (BSD_SUCCESS) only after the library init, device scan, CAM SIM registration, character device creation and debug_level sysctl all succeeded; it returns ENXIO if memory decoding is disabled, the device ident or hardware type is unknown, pqisrc_init fails or pqisrc_scan_devices fails; ENOMEM if the register window or the parent DMA tag cannot be allocated; ENOMEM directly if the buffer DMA tag cannot be created (with no cleanup); the bus_dmamap_create error if a datamap creation fails; and the register_sim or create_char_dev error otherwise. The register window resource is released only on the parent-DMA-tag and datamap failure paths; other failure paths leave acquired resources (including after pqisrc_init) for the caller to clean up.

functions.name: smbioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a smb cdev with a valid softc, data points to a writable struct smbcmd (or smbcmd32 for the 32-bit compat commands), and the calling thread may sleep for the bus. Postcondition: returns EINVAL without acquiring the bus if the slave address has its low bit set (after being overridden by the minor number when unit & 0x0400 is set); otherwise returns the error from smbus_request_bus if it fails (the bus is then not held); otherwise runs the requested SMB command and returns 0 on success, the mapped smbus_error code on bus failure, ENOTTY for an unknown command, EINVAL for a negative wcount (SMB_BWRITE) or negative rcount (SMB_BREAD), or the copyin/copyout error; read commands update rcount, rdata and cmd in the request (copied back to the 32-bit struct for compat commands), wcount and rcount are clamped to SMB_MAXBLOCKSIZE, and the bus is released on every path after it was acquired.

functions.name: davbus_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: self is a DAVbus device whose OpenFirmware node and bus resources can be queried; it is called once during attach. Postcondition: it allocates a zeroed softc (M_WAITOK) and returns 0 on success, with the register, DBDMA and interrupt resources mapped, the softc kept by the sound layer, and the codec mixer initialised for "screamer" or "burgundy" (no mixer for other codecs). If mapping the register space, the DBDMA space or the DBDMA IRQ fails it returns ENXIO, and if powerpc_config_intr fails it returns that error; in each case it releases the resources acquired so far in reverse order and frees the softc. If aoa_attach fails it returns its error and deliberately keeps the softc and the resources (they are already shared with the sound layer and the interrupt handler). The optional control interrupt is set up only if it can be allocated, and its absence is not an error.

functions.name: feeder_chain
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the channel lock of c (CHN_LOCKASSERT) and c is a valid pcm_channel with its device, buffers, matrix and parent channel (for virtual passthrough) set up. Postcondition: all existing feeders are removed and a new feeder chain is built; the matrices, c->format and c->speed may be updated, c->feederflags is reset, and on success the soft and hard buffer formats and the soft speed are set, the channel state is synced and 0 is returned. It returns ENODEV if channel caps or their format list are unavailable, a passthrough format is not in the list, no valid hardware format is found, or the origin or target format is not convertible. It returns ENOTSUP if the direction/vchan combination is neither non-vchan or record nor play with vchan. It returns the non-zero error of the first failing feeder_build_* step, in which case the chain is left partly built.

functions.name: Z_DECLARE_SINC(SIGN, BIT, ENDIAN)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function z_feed_sinc_<SIGN><BIT><ENDIAN>(info, dst) (e.g. z_feed_sinc_S16LE). Precondition: info points to a valid z_info whose z_delay ring buffer, z_coeff and z_dcoeff tables, z_size, z_start, z_alpha, z_dx, z_dy and z_scale are consistent, and dst has room for one output frame of channels*PCM_<BIT>_BPS bytes. Postcondition: for each channel (written from the last channel to the first) it accumulates the delay-line samples against the interpolated sinc coefficients, once forward from the sample after center with phase z_alpha*z_dx and once subtracting from center with phase z_dy-z_alpha*z_dx, scales the sum (by z_scale if not Z_ONE, otherwise by a shift), clips it, and writes the clamped sample into dst. Nothing is returned and no locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: Z_DECLARE_SINC_POLYPHASE(SIGN, BIT, ENDIAN)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function z_feed_sinc_polyphase_<SIGN><BIT><ENDIAN>(info, dst) (e.g. z_feed_sinc_polyphase_S16LE). Precondition: info points to a valid z_info whose z_delay ring buffer holds 2*z_size frames from the start position computed from z_start, z_pcoeff holds at least 2*z_size coefficients for phase z_alpha, and dst has room for one output frame of channels*PCM_<BIT>_BPS bytes. Postcondition: for each channel (written from the last channel to the first) it sums the products of 2*z_size consecutive samples with the phase's coefficients, scales the sum (by z_scale if not Z_ONE, otherwise by a shift), clips it, and writes the clamped sample into dst. Nothing is returned and no locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: umidi_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a probed uaudio device whose softc holds an initialised MIDI channel (interface index, alternate index, mutex) and whose ivars are the USB attach arg. Postcondition: returns 0 after setting the alternate interface, setting up the transfers, attaching one FIFO per embedded jack (max_emb_jack, forced to UMIDI_EMB_JACK_MAX if 0 or too large) and starting the RX transfer under the channel mutex; returns ENXIO if setting the alternate interface fails, transfer setup fails, neither TX nor RX transfer exists, or any usb_fifo_attach fails. It may set single_command (from the quirk or a clamped TX maxp). On failure it does not undo earlier setup (no transfers are unset and no FIFOs are detached here).

functions.name: ufshci_dev_config_write_booster
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ctrlr points to a controller whose device descriptor and geometry descriptor have already been read. Postcondition: returns 0 without changes if the device lacks WriteBooster support, and returns 0 if ufshci_dev_enable_write_booster fails (nothing more is configured). Otherwise it records the buffer type and user-space option, determines the allocation units (shared or from the first LU with nonzero units), computes wb_buffer_size_mb, sets the flush threshold to 40%, and returns 0 with WriteBooster left enabled if the buffer lifetime check succeeds and life remains. If the buffer type is unsupported, the allocation units are zero, the lifetime query returns an error, or no lifetime is left, it calls ufshci_dev_disable_write_booster; it returns the lifetime query's error in that case, and 0 in the other three cases (the local error is only set by the lifetime query).

functions.name: atmegadci_roothub_exec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the USB bus lock (asserted), udev belongs to an atmegadci bus, and req, pptr and plength point to valid memory. Postcondition: the root-hub control request is handled; *plength and *pptr are always set (default length 0 and pointer to sc_hub_temp, or a static descriptor or status reply with its length), and the return value is 0 on success, USB_ERR_STALLED for unsupported or malformed requests (bad request type or code, nonzero descriptor index, address with high byte set, config value >= 2, port index != 1, unknown descriptor or string), or USB_ERR_IOERROR for an unknown port feature in set/clear port feature; port feature requests update the softc flags and may touch the hardware registers and clocks/pull-ups, and get-port-status refreshes clocks and pull-up according to VBUS and fills the port status and change words.

functions.name: avr32dci_roothub_exec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the USB bus lock (asserted), udev is a valid device whose bus maps to an initialized avr32dci softc, req points to a valid decoded setup request, and pptr and plength are writable. Postcondition: always stores the response length in *plength and the response data pointer in *pptr (by default the softc's sc_hub_temp buffer with length 0, or a static descriptor for descriptor requests, or sc_hub_temp filled with 1 or 2 bytes of config, status, interface or port status data); returns 0 for handled or no-op requests (including unforwarded class/vendor interface requests and set-descriptor/set-feature class-device requests), USB_ERR_STALLED for unsupported or invalid requests (bad descriptor type or index, nonzero low byte for device/config/class descriptors, set address with value above 0xFF, set config with value >= 2, port index other than 1, unknown request), and USB_ERR_IOERROR for an unknown port feature selector in clear/set port feature. Side effects: updates sc_conf, sc_rt_addr, the port flags (enabled, powered, change_connect, change_suspend), may wake the peer, pull the bus up or down, switch clocks on or off, and reconfigure endpoint 0 hardware registers (clearing connect change), and reads the interrupt status register for port status; no locks or references are acquired or released.

functions.name: dwc_otg_roothub_exec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the bus lock (checked with USB_BUS_LOCK_ASSERT), udev is a valid device on a dwc_otg bus, req points to a valid control request, and pptr and plength are writable. Postcondition: the request is decoded by bmRequestType and bRequest, and on every path *plength is set to the reply length and *pptr to the reply data (the descriptor, or sc_hub_temp for status replies; the buffer pointer is unchanged and the length is 0 when there is no data). The function returns 0 on success, including no-op requests and unhandled class or vendor interface requests; it returns USB_ERR_STALLED for unsupported requests, bad descriptor or value arguments, or a port index other than 1; it returns USB_ERR_IOERROR for an unknown port feature, or for a PORT_RESET set while in device mode. Port requests may change softc flags, write the HPRT register, pause with the bus mutex, start or stop the timer, switch clocks and pull-ups, and reinitialize the FIFOs. A set-address request stores the address in sc_rt_addr and a set-config request stores the value in sc_conf.

functions.name: ehci_roothub_exec
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the USB bus lock (asserted), udev is a valid device on an EHCI bus, req points to a valid root-hub control request, and pptr and plength are writable. Postcondition: the request is dispatched on (bRequest, bmRequestType) and the reply pointer and length are always stored in *pptr and *plength (by default the sc_hub_desc buffer and length 0, or a static descriptor, or data staged in sc_hub_desc with its length); the function returns 0 on success, USB_ERR_IOERROR for an unsupported request or bad argument (wrong descriptor index, bad descriptor type, address >= EHCI_MAX_DEVICES, config not 0 or 1, port index outside 1..sc_noport, unknown port feature, set-feature on device/interface/endpoint, set-descriptor on the hub), and USB_ERR_TIMEOUT if a port reset does not complete. Side effects include updating sc_addr, sc_conf and sc_isreset, writing port status registers, sleeping with the bus mutex during suspend-resume and reset, and possibly handing a port to a companion controller via ehci_disown.

functions.name: wmt_hid_parse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc points to a valid wmt_softc (its cont_max_rid, caps, buttons, max_button and similar fields are expected to be initially zero) and d_ptr/d_len describe a readable HID report descriptor. Postcondition: it scans the feature items and then the input items of the descriptor, recording report IDs, usage locations, buttons, caps bits and absinfo in sc. It returns WMT_TYPE_UNSUPPORTED if no touchscreen or touchpad top-level collection was found, if no Contact Count Maximum feature report ID was found (sc->cont_max_rid == 0), if the contact count or scan time usage is missing, if no finger collection was completed (cont == 0), if a required usage in wmt_hid_map is not in sc->caps, or if it is a touchpad with no buttons and no integrated button. Otherwise it defaults cont_count_max to cont when it is below 1, adds the orientation cap when width and height are both present, stores the report sizes, report_id, nconts_per_report, has_int_button and cont_count_max in sc, and returns the detected type (WMT_TYPE_TOUCHSCREEN or WMT_TYPE_TOUCHPAD). It may already have modified sc fields before returning UNSUPPORTED. It acquires no locks and keeps no references; the hid_data parse handles are released.

functions.name: uhso_ifnet_write_callback
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called by the USB stack with the softc's mutex held, with xfer a valid transfer of the uhso interface write endpoint and error the transfer's error code. Postcondition: returns nothing; on USB_ST_TRANSFERRED it increments the OPACKETS counter and clears IFF_DRV_OACTIVE, then (also on USB_ST_SETUP) it dequeues one mbuf from the interface send queue; if the queue is empty it stops with IFF_DRV_OACTIVE left as is, otherwise it sets IFF_DRV_OACTIVE, clamps the packet length to MCLBYTES, copies the mbuf into frame 0, submits the transfer, passes the mbuf to BPF and frees it. In any other state it logs the error; if error is USB_ERR_CANCELLED it does nothing more, otherwise it sets the stall flag on the transfer and retries the dequeue/submit path once.

functions.name: umass_cam_action
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sim and ccb are valid CAM pointers supplied by CAM; sim's softc is either NULL or a valid umass_softc. Postcondition: if the softc is NULL, ccb status is set to CAM_SEL_TIMEOUT and xpt_done is called. Otherwise it switches on ccb_h.func_code. XPT_SCSI_IO: if a transfer is already in progress the ccb gets CAM_SCSI_BUSY and is completed. Otherwise the status is set to CAM_REQ_INPROG|CAM_SIM_QUEUED and the command is transformed by umass_std_transform. If the transform succeeds, quirk-driven INQUIRY (emulated serial-number VPD page, EVPD rejection, fake inquiry data), PREVENT_ALLOW, SYNCHRONIZE_CACHE and START_STOP_UNIT commands are completed immediately via xpt_done, either as CAM_REQ_CMP with SCSI_STATUS_OK or as an illegal request (check condition, devq frozen). Otherwise FORCE_SHORT_INQUIRY may shorten dxfer_len and umass_command_start is called with umass_cam_cb as callback, so the ccb is completed later. If the transform fails, this function does not complete the ccb itself. XPT_PATH_INQ fills in the path inquiry data (transfer speed by quirk or USB speed, max_lun) and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_RESET_DEV calls umass_reset and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_GET_TRAN_SETTINGS fills in the SCSI/USB transport settings and completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. XPT_SET_TRAN_SETTINGS completes with CAM_FUNC_NOTAVAIL. XPT_CALC_GEOMETRY calls cam_calc_geometry and completes. XPT_NOOP completes with CAM_REQ_CMP. Any other func_code completes with CAM_FUNC_NOTAVAIL. Returns nothing.

functions.name: ustorage_fs_do_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid softc whose sc_cbw, sc_csw, sc_qdata and the current LUN pointer are usable and sc_cbw->CBWCDB holds the SCSI command. Postcondition: sets sc_transfer.data_ptr to sc_qdata, dispatches on CBWCDB[0] (setting cmd_dir where the command transfers data), validates length via ustorage_fs_min_len and the CDB via ustorage_fs_check_cmd, and runs the matching handler, returning that handler's uint8_t result (0 on success, nonzero on failure); it returns 1 if any check fails, for the READ_12 (temp >= 2^23) or WRITE_12 (temp > mask9>>9) overflow cases (which also set bCSWStatus to CSWSTATUS_FAILED), and for unimplemented or unknown commands (FORMAT_UNIT, RELEASE, RESERVE, SEND_DIAGNOSTIC, default), which also set the current LUN's sense_data to SS_INVALID_COMMAND once checks pass. TEST_UNIT_READY returns the result of its checks only.

functions.name: usb_handle_request
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: xfer is a valid control transfer whose frame 0 buffer holds the setup request and whose xroot->udev is valid; it is called from the control-endpoint transfer callback. Postcondition: returns 0 when the request is accepted in the NOT_COMPLETE state, after setting force_short_xfer and nframes (1 or 2) and staging frame 1 (copied data, zero-copy data, or a zero-length status frame with manual_status cleared); returns USB_ERR_STALLED if the setup state has no active control transfer, the transfer is in a completed (OK or error) state, the request is unsupported or its handler fails; returns USB_ERR_BAD_CONTEXT (after setting udev->address to wValue & 0x7F) for SET_ADDRESS in a completed state. It resets frame 0 length and offsets, reads the request from frame 0, and may change the device configuration, halt or wakeup state via handlers.

functions.name: uhub_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev has a valid uhub_softc and usb_attach_arg whose device is a valid usb_device for a hub; the sc mutex is not yet initialised. Postcondition: it initialises sc_mtx and reads the hub descriptor (USB 2.0 or 3.0 by speed, or assumes one port), and rejects a hub that is too deep, bus-powered under a bus-powered parent, fails MTT enable or descriptor reads, changes its port count, has zero ports, more than 127 (2.0) or 15 (3.0 non-root) ports, or more than USB_MAX_PORTS. On success it allocates the hub structure (unless fixed ports), sets udev->hub, sets up the interrupt transfer (except for the root hub), powers each port on or off (errors are logged only), prints the port summary, starts the interrupt transfer under sc_mtx, sets the power mode to save and returns 0. On any failure it unsets up the transfers, frees udev->hub if dynamically allocated, sets udev->hub to NULL, destroys sc_mtx and returns ENXIO.

functions.name: usbd_transfer_setup_sub
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: parm points to a usb_setup_params whose curr_xfer, curr_setup, udev, speed and hc_max_packet_size/hc_max_packet_count/hc_max_frame_size are initialized, and curr_xfer->endpoint has a valid edesc (ecomp may be NULL). Postcondition: it returns nothing; it fills in the transfer's flags, nframes, timeout, callback, interval, endpointno, clamped max_packet_size/count, max_frame_size, fps_shift, max_data_length, max_hc_frame_size, frlengths, frbuffers and max_frame_count, and advances parm's xfer_length_ptr and xfer_page_cache_ptr. Where applicable it also sets up the local buffer, dma_page_ptr and DMA maps, and updates parm->bufsize and bufsize_max. On any failure it sets parm->err and skips the rest of the setup. The error values are USB_ERR_INVAL (zero HC limits, too many isochronous frames, bufsize wrap, control buffer smaller than the 8-byte request, zero max_hc_frame_size), USB_ERR_ZERO_NFRAMES, USB_ERR_ZERO_MAXP and USB_ERR_NOMEM (buffer or DMA-map allocation). Whenever parm->err is nonzero at exit, including an err set earlier, it sets max_hc_frame_size, max_frame_size and max_packet_size to 1, and max_data_length, nframes and max_frame_count to 0.

functions.name: uath_bulk_tx_callback
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the uath softc lock (UATH_ASSERT_LOCKED) and xfer is the bulk TX USB transfer of that softc. Postcondition: returns nothing. On USB_ST_TRANSFERRED, the head of sc_tx_active (if any) is removed, passed to uath_data_txeof and appended to sc_tx_inactive; then (or directly on USB_ST_SETUP) the head of sc_tx_pending is moved to sc_tx_active, set as frame 0 data of xfer, the transfer is submitted and uath_start is called; if the pending queue is empty it returns without submitting. On any other state (error), if sc_tx_active is empty it goes to the setup path; otherwise the head's node (if any) gets its vap's OERRORS counter incremented, is freed via ieee80211_free_node only when UATH_FLAG_INVALID is not set, and is cleared to NULL; then if error is not USB_ERR_CANCELLED the transfer is stalled and the setup path runs (resubmit the next pending item), while for USB_ERR_CANCELLED nothing is resubmitted. The active-queue head is not removed in the error path.

functions.name: edid_parse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: data points to a 128-byte EDID base block and edid points to writable struct edid_info storage. Postcondition: if edid_is_valid(data) is nonzero it returns -1 and leaves edid untouched; otherwise it fills edid with vendor, product, serial, date, version, chroma, feature and extension-count data, rebuilds edid_nmodes and edid_modes from established timings, standard timings (skipping duplicates) and the descriptor blocks, sets edid_preferred_mode to NULL before the descriptor blocks are processed, trims trailing whitespace from the name, serial and comment strings, raises the range er_max_clock to the highest mode dot clock in MHz (or sets it when no range was given), and returns 0. The code does not check that edid_modes has room for all added modes.

functions.name: vesagtf_mode_params
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: params points to a valid struct vesagtf_params and vmp to a writable struct videomode; freq is nonzero and the parameters are such that the intermediate divisors (including v_field_rqd, the line count term, h_period_est, total_v_lines, h_period, 100*256000 minus ideal_duty_cycle, and h_period/1000) are nonzero, because DIVIDE is not guarded here. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it rounds h_pixels to a multiple of CELL_GRAN, halves v_lines if VESAGTF_FLAG_ILACE is set, computes the GTF timing (margins when VESAGTF_FLAG_MARGINS is set, h_period, duty cycle, h_blank, total pixels, pixel clock, h_sync, front porches) in integer fixed-point arithmetic, and stores hdisplay, hsync_start, hsync_end, htotal, vdisplay, vsync_start, vsync_end, vtotal and dot_clock into *vmp; it takes no locks and touches no other memory except optional debug printing.

functions.name: virtio_scmi_message_poll
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a virtio SCMI device whose softc and A2P virtqueue (with its spin mutex) are initialized, and rx_len points to writable storage for a uint32_t. Postcondition: under the A2P queue spin mutex it dequeues one used PDU from the virtqueue without waiting (virtqueue_dequeue fills *rx_len); if one was available it returns that PDU's buf pointer and releases the PDU back via virtio_scmi_pdu_put, otherwise it returns NULL; the mutex is released on both paths and no error codes are produced.

functions.name: vmmdev_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cdev is a vmm device, cmd is an ioctl command, data points to a kernel copy of the argument structure for cmd (its first int is the vcpu id for commands that take one), and td is the calling thread. Postcondition: returns ENXIO if the device has no softc, ENOTTY if cmd is not in the generic or machine-dependent ioctl tables, EPERM if a passthrough ioctl is attempted by a jailed process without permission, or the priv_check error; it takes the memseg lock (exclusive or shared) and the single or all vcpu locks as required by the flags, and returns EINVAL for a missing vcpu id (-1 when not allowed) or an unallocatable vcpu, or the error from a lock attempt, releasing the memseg lock before returning on those failures. Otherwise it dispatches to the handler for cmd (or vmmdev_machdep_ioctl for unlisted commands), which can return 0, ERANGE, EINVAL or any other non-negative errno or ERESTART, with output fields in data filled by the handler; temporary buffers are freed, all locks taken are released, and the handler's error is returned.

functions.name: mdionexus_ofw_bus_attach
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is a newbus device whose softc is a simplebus_softc and which has an FDT node. Postcondition: it initializes the simplebus state and fills the ranges; if filling the ranges fails it prints a message and returns ENXIO; otherwise, for each child node of the device's node it allocates a zeroed devinfo, skips the node (freeing the devinfo) if devinfo setup fails, builds the resource list from reg and interrupts, adds a newbus child and sets the devinfo as its ivars, or if adding the child fails frees the resource list, the devinfo contents and the devinfo and skips that node; it returns 0 after enumerating all children.

functions.name: vt_parse_rgb_triplet
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: rgb points to a NUL-terminated string and r, g and b each point to one writable unsigned char. Postcondition: the function returns 0 in exactly two cases, and returns -1 for every other input: (a) the first character is '#', strlen of the whole string is exactly 7, and base-16 strtoul applied to the six characters after '#' consumes all of them; strtoul also accepts leading whitespace, a '+' or '-' sign (a '-' wraps the value) and a 0x prefix within those six characters, so a seven-character string such as "#0x1234", "#+12345", "# 12345" or "#-10000" also succeeds, and *r, *g and *b receive bits 16-23, 8-15 and 0-7 of the resulting unsigned long; (b) otherwise, the string is consumed by three successive base-10 strtoul conversions, each converting at least one digit and each yielding a value of at most 255, in which case *r, *g and *b receive the three values; strtoul skips leading whitespace and an optional sign before each number, and a '-' sign wraps, so only "-0" passes; between conversions any run, possibly empty, of ',' and ' ' characters is skipped; after the last number only ' ' characters may follow. In case (a) a -1 return leaves *r, *g and *b unchanged, while in case (b) a -1 return may leave *r, or *r and *g, already set from components parsed earlier; the function allocates and frees no memory.

functions.name: ofwfb_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vd points to a valid vt_device and the Open Firmware device tree is available. Postcondition: the function sets vd->vd_softc to the static console softc and fills it in. It returns CN_DEAD if the selected node's device_type is not "display", if the height, width or depth property is not exactly one cell, if the depth is neither 8 nor 32, if the address property has a length other than 4 or 8, if no PCI assigned-address candidate can be found or resolved (powerpc only), if there is no address property on a non-powerpc build, or if the resulting physical base is zero. These early returns can leave the softc partly filled in, and the stdout instance may already have been opened. Otherwise it maps the framebuffer with bus_space_map, sets FB_FLAG_NOWRITE on powerpc real-mode non-BookE, calls ofwfb_initialize and vt_fb_init, and returns CN_INTERNAL.

functions.name: vtterm_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tm is a valid terminal whose tm_softc is a vt_window with a valid vt_device, data points to a buffer of the size cmd requires (for the old compat command numbers it is replaced by a pointer to a local int taken from the ioctl argument), and td is the calling thread. Postcondition: it dispatches on cmd and returns 0 on success, or ENOIOCTL if cmd is not handled (also when an FBIO_* command is given and the driver has no vd_fb_ioctl); keyboard commands (KDSETRAD, GIO/PIO_KEYMAP, deadkeymap, FKEY, KDGKBINFO, KDGKBTYPE, KDGETREPEAT, KDSETREPEAT, KBADDKBD, KBRELKBD) go through the keyboard driver under Giant, returning its error, except ENOIOCTL becomes ENODEV (for KDGKBTYPE it instead stores 0 and returns 0); EINVAL is returned for KDSETRAD with bits outside 0x7f, bad KDSKBSTATE/KDSETLED/KDSKBMODE values, CONS_HISTORY out of range, CONS_GETINFO with wrong size, bad CONS_MOUSECTL operation, CONS_SETKBD with an unknown keyboard, VT_ACTIVATE or VT_LOCKSWITCH or VT_SETMODE with bad values, VT_OPENQRY with no unopened window, VT_WAITACTIVE with too large index, and some VT_RELDISP cases; other errors come from the keyboard, font, priv_check/securelevel, window-switch or finish_vt_* helpers (ENOTSUP for PIO_VFONT in text mode, EPERM for VT_SETMODE or VT_RELDISP by a non-controlling process or a failed kbd_allocate in CONS_SETKBD); get-type commands write their result through data (e.g. KDGKBSTATE, KDGETLED, KDGETMODE, KDGKBMODE, CONS_GET, CONS_GETVERS, VT_GETACTIVE, VT_GETINDEX, VT_GETMODE, GIO_SCRNMAP), and set commands update window or device state; Giant and the device lock are always released before returning, VT_WAITACTIVE may sleep interruptibly, no reference is retained (a loaded font is unreferenced after use), and the caller keeps ownership of data.

functions.name: vtterm_ioctl
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tm is a vt terminal whose softc is a valid vt_window with a valid device, td is the calling thread, and data points to a buffer of the type the command cmd expects (with COMPAT_FREEBSD* thunking, some old commands have their integer argument copied out of data first). Postcondition: it dispatches on cmd, performs the requested keyboard, LED, font, screen-map, mode, console-info, mouse show/hide, I/O privilege, bell, or virtual-terminal switching operation, and returns 0 on success; it returns EINVAL for bad arguments (for example out-of-range values, wrong vid_info size, unknown mouse operation or VT_SETMODE mode, no free window in VT_OPENQRY, VT_RELDISP in the wrong state), EPERM for a non-controlling process or a failed keyboard allocation, ENOTSUP for PIO_VFONT in text mode, ENODEV when a keyboard command gets ENOIOCTL (except KDGKBTYPE, which then stores 0 and returns ENOIOCTL's replacement, i.e. the code falls through to return the error value ENOIOCTL), any error from the called helpers, priv_check, securelevel_gt, cv_wait_sig or kbd functions, and ENOIOCTL for unknown commands or framebuffer commands the driver has no vd_fb_ioctl for. Giant is taken and released around keyboard accesses and the VT lock around its critical sections, so no lock is held on return.

functions.name: xl_setmode
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller holds the softc lock (XL_LOCK_ASSERT) and sc is a valid xl_softc; media is an ifmedia word. Postcondition: returns nothing; it reads the media-status register (window 4) and internal config (window 3), and for each media option present in sc->xl_media whose subtype matches media (10baseT, 100baseFX, AUI/10baseFL, BNC) sets sc->xl_xcvr and edits the connector bits of icfg and the link-beat, jabber-guard and SQE bits of mediastat; if no subtype matches, only the duplex part, the COAX start/stop command and the register write-back below are done and the message strings stay empty. It sets the MAC duplex bit for full duplex (or 100baseFX) and clears it otherwise, issues COAX_START for 10base2 or COAX_STOP otherwise, writes icfg and mediastat back, waits 800us, selects window 7, and prints a 'selecting <media>, <full|half> duplex' message.

functions.name: pax_enforce_tpe
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: td, vn and path should be non-NULL; vn must be a vnode the caller has referenced and not hold locked, because the function locks it itself (shared), and path should be a kernel-space path string. Postcondition: returns EDOOFUS if any argument is NULL or path has no '/'; returns 0 if TPE is disabled in the thread's prison, TPE is not active for the thread, or the part after the last '/' is shorter than 2 characters (a bare '/' or trailing '/'); otherwise returns the error from VOP_LOCK or VOP_GETATTR on vn, or EPERM if vn's attributes fail the TPE check (root/user ownership, owner-write or group/other-write bits), or the namei error for the parent directory path, or the VOP_GETATTR error or EPERM from the same TPE check on the parent directory, and 0 if all checks pass. The temporary parent path buffer is always freed and vn is left unlocked, except that when VOP_GETATTR on vn fails vn remains locked; the parent vnode is unlocked after a successful namei, and the namei path buffer is freed on all paths.

functions.name: in_cksum_skip
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: m is a valid mbuf chain (or NULL) whose data covers the bytes to be summed, len is the total length counted from the start of the chain, and skip is the number of leading bytes to ignore. Postcondition: returns the 16-bit Internet ones-complement checksum (~sum & 0xffff) of the len-skip bytes that follow the skipped prefix; a trailing odd byte is treated as the high byte of a final word padded with a zero byte; if the chain runs out before the requested length is consumed it prints an 'out of data' message via printf; it never fails with an error code, and it does not modify the mbufs or take or release any lock or reference.

functions.name: cpu_minidumpsys
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: di is a dump device and state supplies a valid dump bitset and msgbuf, with kernel page tables readable. Postcondition: it marks dumpable pages from the kernel page tables in the dump bitmap, drops undumpable pages from it, computes the dump size, and writes the header, msgbuf, dump_avail, bitmap, kernel page table pages and dumped memory pages, then flushes and finishes the dump. On success it prints "Dump complete" and returns 0. If dump_start, any blk_write or blk_flush, or dump_finish fails, it takes the error (negated if negative) and prints a message: "Dump aborted" for ECANCELED, a partition-too-small message for E2BIG or ENOSPC, otherwise "DUMP FAILED" with the error code. It then returns that nonnegative error value.

functions.name: __CONCAT(PMTYPE, protect)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: prot contains only VM_PROT_ALL bits, and pmap is not already locked by the caller (the function takes the pmap lock itself). Postcondition: if prot is VM_PROT_NONE it calls pmap_remove on [sva,eva) and returns; if the request would leave write access (PAE: both write and execute requested; non-PAE: write requested) it returns without changes; otherwise, for each valid mapping in [sva,eva), large pages wholly covered are protected via pmap_protect_pde, partially covered large pages are demoted (skipped if the demotion destroyed them), and 4KB PTEs have PG_RW and PG_M cleared (dirtying managed modified pages first) and, under PAE, pg_nx set when execute is not requested; the PTEs are updated with an atomic compare-and-set retried on failure; global PTEs get a single-page TLB invalidation and others a full invalidation at the end if anything changed. The pmap lock is taken and released; pvh_global_lock is write-locked (possibly after dropping the pmap lock and retrying) and released before return. Nothing is returned.

functions.name: vm86_emulate
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vmf points to a valid vm86 trap frame for the current thread, whose faulting instruction bytes at cs:ip can be read with vm86_fubyte. Postcondition: returns SIGBUS if curpcb->pcb_ext is null, or if the opcode is not handled (in VME mode: any opcode other than the operand-size-prefixed PUSHF/POPF, STI, INTn, POPF or IRET; in non-VME mode: any other than CLI, STI, PUSHF, INTn, IRET, POPF or the prefixed PUSHF/POPF), or when a case breaks out of the switch (VME INTn; VME prefixed POPF, POPF or IRET with VIF set and VIP pending; non-VME STI, POPF, IRET or prefixed POPF with VIP pending; non-VME INTn whose vector is set in the intmap). In VME mode, STI sets VIF and advances IP, then returns SIGKILL after printing 'fatal sti' if VIP is clear, else SIGBUS. Otherwise the instruction is emulated: the stack, flags, VIF and IP/CS are updated in the frame or vm86 state, and the function returns retcode, which is SIGTRAP if PSL_T was set in vmf_eflags on entry, else 0. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sysnum is a syscall number, params points to the matching linux_*_args structure for that number (not dereferenced for argument-less cases), uarg points to a writable uint64_t array large enough for the case's arguments (uarg doubles as the int64_t array iarg), and n_args is writable. Postcondition: for a recognised sysnum, each argument field is stored in order into uarg[0..] (pointers and unsigned values cast to intptr_t or assigned as unsigned, signed or integer-typed ones through the int64_t view) and *n_args is set to the argument count (0 for cases with no arguments listed). For an unrecognised sysnum, the visible part of the switch shows no default, so nothing is written there. The function returns nothing, acquires no locks or references, and allocates no memory.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to a writable array of 64-bit slots large enough for the arguments of the syscall, n_args is writable, and if sysnum is a syscall number handled by the switch then params points to that syscall's argument struct (for example struct linux_clone3_args for 435). Postcondition: for a handled sysnum that takes arguments, each field is stored in order into the next slot of uarg: integer-typed fields are sign-converted into the int64_t view, pointer fields are cast to intptr_t, and unsigned fields such as uint32_t, u_int and size_t are stored through the unsigned slot. *n_args is set to the argument count, and it is 0 for handled syscalls that are not implemented, which store nothing. For a sysnum with no case in the switch, nothing is written and *n_args is left unchanged. The function returns nothing and does not modify params.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes (the code does not check this); sysnum is a syscall number and ndx an argument index, and any values are accepted. Postcondition: a switch on sysnum and then ndx selects a constant type-name string such as "int", "l_uint" or "userland char *" for that argument. If sysnum is unlisted, the syscall takes no described arguments, or ndx is out of range for it, no string is selected. The tail of the function is not shown in the source given, so the final copy cannot be confirmed. By the generator's usual convention it copies the selected string into desc with strlcpy when one is selected and leaves desc untouched otherwise. The function returns nothing, takes no locks and acquires no references.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes, and sysnum and ndx are any integers (no validity is required). Postcondition: returns nothing; a switch on sysnum and ndx selects a constant type-description string for that syscall argument (for example "int", "l_int" or "userland char *"), or leaves it NULL when sysnum has no case, the syscall has no described arguments, or ndx is out of range. If a string was selected it is copied into desc with strlcpy (truncated to descsz). If no string was selected, desc is left unmodified. The code after the switch lies outside the visible part of the function and is assumed from the usual generated pattern.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sysnum is a Linux syscall number, ndx is an argument index, and desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it selects a static type-description string p for argument ndx of syscall sysnum (for example "l_int" or "userland char *"), and p stays NULL when sysnum has no case, the syscall has no arguments, or ndx is out of range for it. The visible slice shows no code after the switch that uses p, so what is written to desc is not shown here and may depend on that unseen tail.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc points to a writable buffer of at least descsz bytes (descsz > 0 is needed for the copy to be meaningful); sysnum is the Linux syscall number and ndx the zero-based argument index, and any values are accepted. Postcondition: returns nothing; looks up the C type-name string for argument ndx of syscall sysnum in a nested switch, and if one exists (valid argument index of a known syscall) copies it into desc with strlcpy, truncated to descsz; for unknown syscall numbers, syscalls with no described arguments, or out-of-range indexes it leaves desc untouched.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: desc must point to a writable buffer of descsz bytes (descsz > 0 is needed for any string to be stored); sysnum and ndx may be any ints. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it looks up the argument type name for syscall sysnum and argument index ndx in a static switch table, with p left NULL for unknown syscalls, indices beyond the argument count, and syscalls listed with no arguments or no description. Any name found is a static string, which the code (after the switch, beyond the visible part) copies into desc, so desc is otherwise unchanged. It takes no locks and allocates no memory.

functions.name: systrace_entry_setargdesc
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sysnum is a syscall number, ndx is an argument index, and desc points to a writable buffer of descsz bytes. Postcondition: the function selects a type-description string for argument ndx of syscall sysnum (for example 'l_int' or 'userland struct l_timespec64 *'); for syscalls with no described arguments, or an out-of-range ndx, or an unknown sysnum, no string is selected, and otherwise the selected string is copied into desc (truncated to descsz); nothing is returned.

functions.name: systrace_args
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: uarg points to an array of uint64_t large enough for the argument count of sysnum, n_args points to a writable int, and for a sysnum with a case below params points to the matching syscall argument struct (params is not read for no-argument cases). Postcondition: for a sysnum handled by a case, the arguments are stored in order into slots 0.. of uarg (integer arguments as int64_t via iarg, pointer and unsigned arguments as uint64_t via uarg), and *n_args is set to the number of arguments (0 for no-argument syscalls); for a sysnum without a case, or after the cases cut off in the shown source, behaviour is whatever the remaining code does (the default is not visible in the slice), and nothing is returned since the function is void.

functions.name: ieee80211_crypto_init_aad
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: wh points to a readable 802.11 frame header (including addr4 and QoS control when the frame type indicates them), aad points to a writable buffer of len bytes with len at least 32, and the two buffers do not overlap. Postcondition: the first len bytes of aad are zeroed and then filled with the CCMP AAD (masked frame control bytes in aad[2] and aad[3], addr1..addr3 at aad+4, masked fragment number in aad[22], aad[23]=0, then addr4 and/or masked QoS priority bits when present, rest zero), aad[1] is set to the AAD length, and the function returns that length: 22 for a 3-address non-QoS frame, 24 for a 3-address QoS frame, 28 for a 4-address non-QoS frame, 30 for a 4-address QoS frame; it has no error return and takes no locks or references.

functions.name: hostap_recv_mgmt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node of a hostap-mode VAP, m0 is an mbuf whose first mbuf holds a complete 802.11 management frame header plus body, and subtype is that frame's management subtype. Postcondition: returns void; it dispatches on subtype (beacon/probe response go to the scan module or update ERP/HT protection state; probe request may trigger a probe response; auth goes to the open/shared handlers or is rejected with an error frame; assoc/reassoc request validates the IEs and rates, may free and clear ni->ni_challenge, updates the node's rate, HT, VHT, QoS and IE state, then joins the node and delivers the L2 update frame; deauth/disassoc makes the node leave unless it is the BSS node; action frames are passed to ic_recv_action when valid). Malformed, disallowed or unsupported frames are discarded early with a statistics counter incremented, and in several cases an error, deauth or auth-reject frame is sent. The caller keeps ownership of ni and m0.

functions.name: ieee80211_recv_pspoll
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node with a valid vap and ic, and m0 is an mbuf holding a PS-Poll frame whose header is readable; the caller's ownership of m0 is not changed (this function neither frees it nor uses it beyond reading the header). Postcondition: returns nothing; if the node is unassociated (ni_associd == 0) it counts is_ps_unassoc and sends a DEAUTH with reason NOT_ASSOCED; else if the poll AID differs from ni_associd it only counts is_ps_badaid and returns; else if the power-save queue is empty it sends a null-data frame (on a new node reference), counts is_ps_qempty and calls iv_set_tim(ni, 0) if set; otherwise it dequeues the first queued packet, sets M_MORE_DATA if more packets remain (else calls iv_set_tim(ni, 0) if set), sets M_PWR_SAV, and transmits it via ieee80211_parent_xmitpkt if M_ENCAP is set or else ieee80211_vap_xmitpkt, ignoring the transmit result.

functions.name: hostap_input
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node with valid vap and ic, and m is an mbuf holding a received 802.11 frame; rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns the frame type (IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_*) from the header, or -1 cast to uint8_t (255) if the frame was dropped before the type was read (too short, or A-MPDU resubmit paths return DATA); the mbuf is consumed in every case: delivered up the stack (data), passed to iv_recv_mgmt or iv_recv_ctl (mgmt/ctl, which then fall to the common exit), queued by A-MPDU reorder, handed to the WDS discover, defrag or decap paths, or freed with m_freem after an optional radiotap tap. Error paths (bad version, wrong direction, unassociated source, decap failure, unauthorized port, bad frame type, management wrong direction) also increment the interface input-error counter; the corresponding vap statistics are incremented on each drop.

functions.name: ieee80211_check_rxseq
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node with a valid vap, wh points to a readable 802.11 frame header, and rxs is either NULL or a valid rx-stats pointer (bssid is used only for the discard log message). Postcondition: returns 1 (frame accepted) for frame types without a sequence number, for multicast destinations, for HT nodes with a running RX A-MPDU on the TID, when the last seen sequence number for the TID is 4095 and the frame is not a retry with the identical seq/frag value, and when the frame is not a retry with rxseq less than or equal to ni_rxseqs[tid]; on accepted frames that reach the ok path it sets ni_rxseqs[tid]=rxseq only if ieee80211_check_rxseq_amsdu_more(rxs) is true and otherwise only bumps A-MPDU statistics; returns 0 (duplicate) in the retry cases below the current number or equal to a last-seen 4095, logging the discard, incrementing vap->iv_stats.is_rx_dup and the node rx_dup statistic, and leaving ni_rxseqs unchanged.

functions.name: ieee80211_ioctl_set80211
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: vap is a valid vap, ireq points to a valid ieee80211req whose i_type selects the setting and whose i_val, i_len and i_data carry the value, and the caller is in a context that permits copyin and driver reset callbacks. Postcondition: it dispatches on ireq->i_type, updating the corresponding vap/ic setting or calling the delegated handler (for example setkey, setmlme, setchannel or setdefault) and taking its error code; it returns EINVAL for out-of-range or invalid values, EOPNOTSUPP for a missing capability, or the copyin error, and some early-return cases (such as EINVAL for a bad length or key id and EOPNOTSUPP for a missing capability) leave state unchanged, although some paths update state before they fail. After the switch, a result of ERESTART is replaced by the iv_reset callback's result if the interface is up and running, or by 0 otherwise, and a result of ENETRESET calls ieee80211_init when IS_UP_AUTO(vap) holds and becomes 0, so the final return is 0 or an error code from a handler, copyin or iv_reset.

functions.name: mesh_recv_mgmt
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a valid node of a mesh VAP, m0 is a management frame whose first mbuf holds the 802.11 header and the elements up to m_len, and rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns nothing and does not free m0 or release ni. Beacons and probe responses that fail parsing are ignored. While scanning they are passed to the scan module, and a probe request is sent first if the channel is marked passive. Otherwise, in RUN state, valid beacons from mesh STAs of our mesh and permitted by the ACL add the neighbor if its address differs from ni. If the mesh AP flag is set and the node is idle, the function starts peering and sends an Open action, unless the hold count is at its limit or the id generated is 0. If the node is established, the function refreshes the route lifetime. Non-mesh, wrong-mesh or ACL-denied frames increment the matching stat and are dropped. A probe request that is valid, unicast, and received in RUN state triggers a probe response. Action frames from known nodes, addressed to us or multicast, in RUN state are parsed and passed to ic_recv_action. Other action frames, and unhandled subtypes, are discarded with is_rx_mgtdiscard or is_rx_badsubtype incremented.

functions.name: ieee80211_phy_vht_get_mcs_kbit
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none beyond a valid enum value for bw; any nss, mcs and is_shortgi are accepted, and mcs_entries is only indexed after mcs has been checked to be at most 9. Postcondition: returns 0 if mcs > 9, if nss is 0 or above 8, or if bw is not one of NET80211_STA_RX_BW_20, _40, _80 or _160; otherwise returns (n_carriers * mcs_entries[mcs].n_sym * mcs_entries[mcs].cod_n * nss * 10000) / (mcs_entries[mcs].cod_d * sym_len) with unsigned integer division, where n_carriers is 52, 108, 234 or 468 for 20, 40, 80 or 160 MHz and sym_len is 36 for short GI and 40 for long GI; no locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: sta_input
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ni is a non-NULL node with valid ni_vap and ni_ic, m is a valid mbuf chain holding a received 802.11 frame whose ownership passes to this function, and rxs may be NULL. Postcondition: returns the frame type (IEEE80211_FC0_TYPE_DATA for data frames delivered, passed to the A-MPDU reorder queue or A-MSDU/fast-frame decap, the masked type for mgmt/ctl frames, or -1 converted to uint8_t when the frame was too short or had a bad version), and the mbuf is consumed in every path: delivered upward, handed to the reorder queue, defragmentation, decap, management or control handlers, or freed with m_freem after the matching drop statistic is incremented (radiotap tap is made first if not yet tapped); the error paths via err also increment the IFCOUNTER_IERRORS counter of the interface.

functions.name: nga_rcv_async
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: sc is a valid node private state and item is a netgraph item carrying an mbuf chain of raw async-PPP bytes. Postcondition: if async is not enabled on the node, the item is forwarded unchanged to the sync hook and that forwarding error code is returned; otherwise every byte is run through the HDLC-like deframer (flag, escape, CRC, runt, bad-checksum and overflow handling update the stats and reset the parser state), each valid frame is copied with m_devget (address/control bytes stripped when present, dropped if longer than cfg.amru) and sent to the sync hook (consuming the item for the first frame, via NG_SEND_DATA_ONLY afterwards), the mbuf chain is freed, any item not consumed is freed, and 0 is returned (errors from sending frames are ignored).

functions.name: ng_ksocket_rcvmsg
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: node is a ksocket node with private data (priv->so may be NULL) and item carries a netgraph message. Postcondition: for NGM_KSOCKET_COOKIE it dispatches on the command (BIND, LISTEN, ACCEPT, CONNECT, GETNAME/GETPEERNAME, GETOPT, SETOPT) and returns EINVAL for a bad arglen, an unknown command or an unknown typecookie, ENXIO if so is NULL, EALREADY for ACCEPT while accepting or CONNECT while connecting, ENOTCONN for GETPEERNAME on an unconnected socket, ENOMEM if a response cannot be allocated, EINPROGRESS if CONNECT is still pending (response token/address saved and KSF_CONNECTING set), or the error from the underlying socket call, otherwise 0; GETNAME/GETPEERNAME/GETOPT attach a response with the address or option value. In every case it passes the error and any response to NG_RESPOND_MSG (which consumes the item), frees msg, and returns the error.

functions.name: nglmi_checkdata
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hook belongs to a node whose private data is a valid sc, and m is a valid mbuf whose first m_len bytes hold an LMI frame. Postcondition: returns 1 if the frame is accepted (it begins with 0x03, a matching or auto-detected protocol ID, a zero call reference, a Status message type 0x7D, any locking shift consistent with the Annex D/Group4 mode, and well-formed information elements ending with a response type and a matching sequence number seen), leaving the mbuf owned by the caller; the same 1 is returned after logging a hex dump of the packet when extra bytes remain at the end, or when an element is longer than the remaining packet. In the auto-detect mode it also updates the LMI type and protoID in sc. Returns 0 after logging a hex dump and freeing the mbuf with NG_FREE_M on any rejection: bad header bytes, Status enquiry or unknown message type, locking shift wrong, bad or duplicate-order IE sizes, unexpected sequence or report type, a DLCI above 1023, or missing response type or sequence number.

functions.name: ng_pptpgre_rcvdata_lower
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hook is a node's lower (IP/GRE) hook and item carries an mbuf whose data starts with an IP header; no session lock is held by the caller. Postcondition: the item is always consumed. Returns EINVAL for runt packets, bad GRE length or bits, unknown, unhooked or disabled session (bad CID), and for late or duplicate sequence numbers (including a duplicate already in the reorder queue). Returns ENOBUFS if m_pullup fails (the item's mbuf is set to NULL, then the item is freed). Returns 0 for a lone ack with no data. For a data packet: in-order packets, and packets that become deliverable after the reorder queue is drained, are acked and delivered through ng_pptpgre_sendq (the session lock is dropped by ng_pptpgre_ack); early packets are queued in the reorder queue (up to reorder_max) with the lock released, and the function returns 0. When the queue is full, the queue head is moved to the send queue to make room. If malloc fails, preceding queued packets are flushed and delivered, the current packet is forwarded, memoryFailures is incremented and ENOMEM is returned. Otherwise it returns 0. Items that were queued or delivered are not freed here; error paths via done free the item. Statistics counters are updated and the session lock is held during the work and released before returning.

functions.name: genl_unregister_group
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: group_id satisfies MIN_GROUP_NUM < group_id < MIN_GROUP_NUM + MAX_GROUPS, family_id names a registered generic netlink family, the group slot groups[group_id - MIN_GROUP_NUM] is currently owned by that family, and the family has family_num_groups > 0; the caller must not already hold the GENL lock. Postcondition: returns nothing; first calls nl_clear_group(group_id), then under the GENL lock decrements the family's family_num_groups and sets that group slot's group_family and group_name to NULL, and releases the lock before returning.

functions.name: bootpc_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called once during early boot from a thread context (curthread) with the network stack and vnet initialised; nfsv3_diskless and nfs_diskless_valid are accessible. Postcondition: returns nothing; it returns immediately, touching nothing, if nfs_diskless_valid is already nonzero, or if vfs.root.mountfrom is set to a value not starting with "nfs:" (after printing a message and freeing the env string). Otherwise it allocates a global context and per-interface contexts, finds Ethernet broadcast interfaces (retrying with pauses until a timeout, then panicking if none is found), creates the BOOTP socket, runs the BOOTP exchange, decodes replies and adjusts interfaces, and closes the socket. If no interface got a root path or resolved reply, or there are no eligible interfaces, it skips to cleanup. If a root path was obtained it sets boot.netif.name, adds and removes a default route around md_mount of the root; on mount failure it panics unless root overrides exist, in which case it skips to cleanup; on success it sets rootdevnames[0]="nfs:" and nfs_diskless_valid=3. It then fills nd->myif (name, address, broadcast, mask) and nd->mygateway from the chosen interface. On every path past the allocations it frees all interface contexts and the global context. It panics if no HW address is found, no suitable interface appears before the timeout, or socreate fails.

functions.name: swcr_ccm
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ses holds valid auth and encdec state for an AES-CCM session and crp is a valid request whose session params are retrievable. Postcondition: returns EMSGSIZE if the payload length exceeds the CCM maximum for the session, or EINVAL if CRYPTO_F_IV_SEPARATE is not set, in both cases before any processing. Otherwise it MACs the b0 block, the AAD and the payload. On encrypt it writes the ciphertext to the output (or in place) and stores the tag at crp_digest_start, returning 0. On decrypt it compares the computed tag with the one read from the digest location. If they differ it returns EBADMSG without decrypting the output. If they match it decrypts the payload to the output and returns 0. After processing, the stack cipher context and the scratch buffers are zeroed before returning; the early EMSGSIZE and EINVAL returns happen before they are set up. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: RMD160Transform
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: state points to five valid, writable 32-bit words holding the current RIPEMD-160 chaining value, and block points to 64 readable bytes. Postcondition: the 64 bytes are loaded as 16 little-endian 32-bit words, both the main line and the parallel line of 80 steps are computed from the original state, and state[0..4] are replaced by the standard RIPEMD-160 combination of the old state with both line results; the block is not modified and nothing is returned.

functions.name: DB_SHOW_COMMAND(tlb0, tlb0_print_tlbentries)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called as the kernel debugger 'show tlb0' command on a PowerPC Book-E CPU, in a context where the MAS special-purpose registers and the tlbre instruction can be used. Postcondition: prints the header 'TLB0 entries:', then for every way (0..TLB0_WAYS-1) and every entry index (0..TLB0_ENTRIES_PER_WAY-1) selects that TLB0 entry via MAS0/MAS2, reads it with tlbre, and calls tlb_print_entry with the computed table index (tlb0_tableidx(mas2, way)) and the MAS1, MAS2, MAS3, MAS7 values; it returns nothing, and modifies MAS0 and MAS2 as a side effect.

functions.name: atomic_load_acq_long
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: addr points to a readable, suitably aligned u_long. Postcondition: it returns the value of atomic_load_acq_int applied to addr cast to a u_int pointer, converted to u_long (a plain load of *addr followed by powerpc_lwsync()). It cannot fail and takes no lock.

functions.name: atomic_store_rel_long
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: addr points to a writable, suitably aligned u_long. Postcondition: it calls atomic_store_rel_int on addr cast to a u_int pointer with val cast to u_int, so powerpc_lwsync() runs and then the (truncated) value is stored. It returns nothing and takes no lock.

functions.name: ofwfb_configure
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called once during early console setup with a flags argument that is not used; the Open Firmware /chosen, stdout and screen nodes may or may not describe a display. Postcondition: always returns 0; it returns early without doing anything if hw.syscons.disable is nonzero, if it already ran once, if the node's device_type is not "display", if the depth is not 8 or 32, if the height/width/linebytes properties do not have the expected size, or if no framebuffer region can be found among the assigned PCI addresses when there is no "address" property. Otherwise it fills in the global softc (blank/putc/putm/border functions, depth, node, console flag, geometry, PCI addresses), maps or decodes the framebuffer address, and calls ofwfb_init to initialise and register the adapter. For depth 8 or 32 the blank, putc, putm and set_border function pointers are set before the later checks, so they stay set even if the function then returns early.

functions.name: smuiic_transfer
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: dev is an smuiic device with a valid softc, msgs points to nmsgs valid iic_msg entries whose lengths fit the SMU command data buffer (a message with IIC_M_NOSTOP must be followed by another message and has len < 4), and the caller does not hold sc->sc_mtx. Postcondition: the function takes sc->sc_mtx, sleeps until no other transfer is in use, marks the bus in use, and runs each message (a NOSTOP message is combined with the next one) as an SMU_I2C command, polling up to 10 times with 10-tick sleeps for completion while dropping the mutex around each smu_run_cmd; it returns 0 if all complete, with each processed message's buf overwritten by the response data (including write messages) and its len set to the response length minus 1, or returns EIO if a polled status still has bit 0x80 set, in which case that message's len is set to 0 and later messages are not processed; in every case it clears sc->sc_iic_inuse, releases sc->sc_mtx, and calls wakeup(sc) before returning.

functions.name: cpu_minidumpsys
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: di is a valid dumper device and state holds a valid dump bitset and message buffer pointer, with the kernel page tables readable. Postcondition: the function walks the kernel page tables to mark dumpable pages in the bitset, computes the dump size, and writes the header, msgbuf, dump_avail, bitmap, kernel page-directory pages and memory chunks, then flushes and finishes the dump, printing "Dump complete" and returning 0. If any step fails, the error is made positive and a message is printed. On ENOSPC it restarts the whole dump if fewer than 5 attempts have been made, otherwise it prints "Dump failed." and returns ENOSPC. Other errors, including ECANCELED and E2BIG, are returned as positive errno values.

functions.name: clnt_bck_call
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the caller passes a valid backchannel client handle, transport and request arguments; the function itself allocates the request structure cr (and the xid and mreq), and ct_threads has already been incremented for this call; ct_lock is not held by the caller on entry. Postcondition: returns an enum clnt_stat: RPC_SUCCESS with the reply mbuf chain stored in *resultsp after the reply was decoded and AUTH_VALIDATE accepted it; RPC_CANTENCODEARGS if the procedure number or arguments could not be marshalled; RPC_CANTRECV (if the connection is closing, the upcall reported cr_error, or msleep failed with an error other than EINTR/EWOULDBLOCK); RPC_CANTSEND if sosend failed (other than EMSGSIZE, which waits for send buffer space and retries); RPC_TIMEDOUT (zero timeout without a ready reply, or msleep gave EWOULDBLOCK); RPC_INTR (msleep gave EINTR); RPC_CANTDECODERES if the reply could not be decoded; RPC_AUTHERROR with re_why = AUTH_INVALIDRESP if validation of the reply fails, or the status from _seterr_reply (including RPC_AUTHERROR after a failed or exhausted credential refresh) otherwise. A successful AUTH_REFRESH restarts the call at call_again with a decremented refresh count. Details are recorded in *errp. On the exit path ct_lock is released, any unsent mreq and any leftover cr->cr_mrep are freed, ct_threads is decremented, ct is woken if ct_closing, cr is freed, and AUTH_VALIDATE(NULL) is called on failure if auth is set; cr is removed from ct_pending on every path that inserted it.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(lpathconf_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global path must not already exist, so that symlink("symlink", path) can create it, and the audit pipe/class globals (fds, auclass, successreg) are set up. Postcondition: the test creates the symlink (aborting if that fails), enables auditing, requires lpathconf(path, _PC_SYMLINK_MAX) to return other than -1, then checks that an audit record matching successreg appears; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(lpathconf_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: errpath names a nonexistent symbolic link, and the audit globals (fds, auclass, failurereg) are set up. Postcondition: the test enables auditing, requires lpathconf(errpath, _PC_SYMLINK_MAX) to return -1 with errno ENOENT, then checks that an audit record matching failurereg appears; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fpathconf_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path can be created with open(O_CREAT, mode), and the audit globals are set up. Postcondition: the test records the pid, builds extregex "fpathconf.*<pid>.*success", opens/creates the file (aborting on failure), enables auditing, requires fpathconf(filedesc, _PC_NAME_MAX) to return other than -1, checks that an audit record matching extregex appears, then closes filedesc; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(fpathconf_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the audit globals (fds, auclass) are set up. Postcondition: the test enables auditing, requires fpathconf(-1, _PC_NAME_MAX) to return -1 with errno EBADF, then checks that an audit record matching "fpathconf.*return,failure : Bad file descriptor" appears; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(extattr_get_file_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path can be created and its file system supports extended attributes (otherwise the test is skipped), and the audit globals are set up. Postcondition: the test creates the file, sets a user extended attribute of sizeof(buff) bytes on it, builds a regex naming path and attribute with return,success, enables auditing, requires extattr_get_file to return sizeof(buff), checks that a matching audit record appears, and closes filedesc; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(extattr_get_file_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path does not exist, and the audit globals are set up. Postcondition: the test builds a regex naming path and name with failure, enables auditing, requires extattr_get_file(path, USER, name, NULL, 0) to return -1 with errno ENOENT, then checks that a matching audit record appears; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(extattr_get_fd_success, tc)

Postcondition: the test creates the file, sets a user extended attribute of sizeof(buff) bytes via extattr_set_file, builds a regex naming the attribute with return,success, enables auditing, requires extattr_get_fd(filedesc, ...) to return sizeof(buff), checks that a matching audit record appears, and closes filedesc; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(extattr_get_fd_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the audit globals are set up. Postcondition: the test builds a regex naming the attribute with "return,failure : Bad file descriptor", enables auditing, requires extattr_get_fd(-1, USER, name, NULL, 0) to return -1 with errno EBADF, then checks that a matching audit record appears; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(extattr_get_link_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: path does not already exist so the symlink can be created, the current directory supports extended attributes (otherwise the test is skipped), and the audit globals are set up. Postcondition: the test creates the symlink, sets a user extended attribute of sizeof(buff) bytes on it via extattr_set_link, builds a regex naming path and attribute with return,success, enables auditing, requires extattr_get_link to return sizeof(buff), then checks that a matching audit record appears; it returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(extattr_delete_link_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated cleanup function for the ATF test case extattr_delete_link_failure (ATF_TC_CLEANUP expansion, named extattr_delete_link_failure_cleanup). functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(lchown_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function lchown_failure_cleanup(tc) is the ATF cleanup routine for the lchown_failure test case. Precondition: it is called by the ATF framework after the test case body has run, with a valid tc. functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(munmap_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function munmap_success_body(tc). Precondition: the audit test harness is available (setup/check_audit work). Postcondition: it builds a regex from the pid, maps one byte with mmap, enables auditing, requires munmap of that mapping to return 0 (the ATF requirement fails the test otherwise), then calls check_audit to verify a munmap success record for the pid appears in the audit pipe; returns void.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(munmap_failure, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function munmap_failure_body(tc). Precondition: the audit harness is available. Postcondition: it requires munmap((void *)SIZE_MAX, -1) to return -1 (ATF requirement fails the test otherwise), then calls check_audit to verify an audit record matching 'munmap.*return,failure : Invalid argument'; returns void.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(close_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function close_success_body(tc). Precondition: the current directory is writable and the audit harness is available. Postcondition: it creates/opens the file 'fileforaudit' (required to succeed), stats it for its inode, enables auditing, requires close(fd) to return 0, builds a regex with the inode number, then calls check_audit to verify a close success record containing that inode; returns void.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(close_failure, tc)

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(closefrom_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function closefrom_success_body(tc). Precondition: the audit harness is available. Postcondition: it enables auditing, calls closefrom(INT_MAX) (returns void), then calls check_audit to verify a close_range record with lowfd 0x7fffffff, highfd 0xffffffff and return,success; returns void.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(revoke_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function revoke_success_body(tc). Precondition: a pseudo-terminal can be opened and the audit harness is available. Postcondition: it builds a regex from the pid, requires posix_openpt and ptsname to succeed, enables auditing, requires revoke(ptyname) to return 0, calls check_audit to verify a revoke success record for the pid, then closes the master descriptor; returns void.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(revoke_failure, tc)

Postcondition: it requires revoke on the nonexistent path to return -1 (ATF requirement fails the test otherwise), then calls check_audit to verify a record matching 'fileforaudit.*return,failure'; returns void.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(mkdir_success, tc)

Postcondition: sets up audit pipe, requires mkdir(path, 0777) to return 0 (test fails otherwise), then calls check_audit with the success regex; returns nothing.

Postcondition: requires the first mkdir to return 0, sets up the audit pipe, requires the second mkdir to return -1 (already exists), then calls check_audit with the failure regex; returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(mkfifo_success, tc)

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(recvfrom_success, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function atfu_recvfrom_success_body(tc). Precondition: the audit test globals are initialised and the UNIX socket address can be assigned and bound. Postcondition: it creates and binds a datagram server socket, sends a message to it from a second socket, starts audit capture, requires recvfrom to return non-zero, builds a regex containing the socket fd and byte count, calls check_audit, then closes both sockets; any failed ATF_REQUIRE aborts the test; it returns nothing.

functions.name: OPEN_AT_TC_DEFINE(read, "read", O_RDONLY, "fr")

Precondition: the working directory allows creating 'fileforaudit' and the audit pipe can be set up for class "fr". Returns nothing.
