functions.name: ATF_TC_CLEANUP(auditpipe_set_qlimit, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function auditpipe_set_qlimit_cleanup(tc), the cleanup routine of the ATF test case auditpipe_set_qlimit. Precondition: it runs in the test's working directory after the test body; if the file qlimit_store does not exist it does nothing. Postcondition: when qlimit_store exists it opens it for reading into the global fileptr, reads one integer with fscanf, opens /dev/auditpipe read-only, and sets the queue limit to that integer with AUDITPIPE_SET_QLIMIT, then closes the device descriptor and the file. It returns nothing; each ATF_REQUIRE (fopen non-NULL, fscanf result non-zero, open != -1, ioctl == 0) fails the test and aborts the cleanup if violated, in which case the files opened so far are not closed. The qlimit_store file is not removed.

functions.name: TEST(CapabilityPair, sendfile)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the process can create and write the temp file cap_sendfile_in and create an AF_UNIX stream socketpair. Postcondition: it writes 4 bytes to the file, makes capability dups of the file (read+seek, write+seek) and of the socket (read+seek, write+seek), and checks that sendfile_ fails with NOTCAPABLE for a read-only output or a write-only input, and succeeds for a write-capable output with a read-capable input. It then closes all descriptors, unlinks the temp file and returns nothing; failures are recorded as gtest expectation failures.

functions.name: TEST(CapabilityPair, tee)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: HAVE_TEE is defined and two nonblocking pipes can be created. Postcondition: it writes 4 bytes into pipe1, creates capability dups of pipe1's read end (write-only, read+write) and pipe2's write end (read-only, read+write), and checks that tee fails with NOTCAPABLE if the input lacks CAP_READ or the output lacks CAP_WRITE, and succeeds when the input has read and the output has write. It then closes all descriptors and returns nothing; failures are recorded as gtest expectation failures.

functions.name: TEST(CapabilityPair, splice)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: HAVE_SPLICE is defined and two nonblocking pipes can be created. Postcondition: it writes 4 bytes into pipe1, creates capability dups of pipe1's read end and pipe2's write end with various rights, and checks that splice fails with NOTCAPABLE unless the input has read+seek and the output has write+seek, and succeeds in that case. It then closes all descriptors and returns nothing; failures are recorded as gtest expectation failures.

functions.name: TEST(CapabilityPair, vmsplice)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: HAVE_VMSPLICE is defined and a nonblocking pipe can be created. Postcondition: it creates capability dups of the pipe's write end (read-only, read+write), and checks that vmsplice of a 4-byte iovec fails with NOTCAPABLE using the read-only one and succeeds with the read+write one. It then closes all descriptors and returns nothing; failures are recorded as gtest expectation failures.

functions.name: FORK_TEST_ON(Capability, SocketTransfer, TmpFile("cap_fd_transfer"))
functions.prose_contract: Generated test body Capability_SocketTransfer_Test::TestBody (the slice labels it FdTransfer). Precondition: it runs in a forked test process and can create sockets, fork and open the temp file cap_fd_transfer. Postcondition: it returns void; it creates a socketpair and forks a child that enters capability mode, announces startup, receives a capability fd over the socket, checks its rights equal read+seek and tries read/write on it, then acknowledges and exits on request. The parent opens the temp file (returning early if open fails), dups it, limits the dup to read+seek rights, enters capability mode, tests read/write, waits for the child's startup message, sends the fd via SCM_RIGHTS, waits for the acknowledgement, and sends the exit request. Failures are recorded as gtest expectation failures, and nothing is returned.

functions.name: FORK_TEST(Capmode, AllowedIdentifierSyscalls)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none beyond running as a forked test process. Postcondition: it records gid, pid, ppid, uid and sid, enters capability mode, then expects getegid/geteuid/getgid/getpid/getppid/getuid/getsid to return the recorded values, expects getgroups, getresuid and getresgid to succeed (and getlogin to be non-NULL when HAVE_GETLOGIN is defined), and expects the set*gid/set*uid calls (setfsgid/setfsuid only if defined) with the existing values and setsid to succeed; it returns nothing and failures are only recorded as test expectation failures.

functions.name: FORK_TEST(Fcntl, Basic)
functions.prose_contract: Test body generated by FORK_TEST(Fcntl, Basic), run in a forked child; precondition: /etc/passwd is readable and the process is not yet in capability mode. Postcondition: it opens a file, a local stream socket and a shared-memory object (SHM skipped if shm_open gives ENOSYS), makes capability dups limited to CAP_READ|CAP_FCNTL, enters capability mode, then expects fcntl(F_GETFL) to succeed on every raw fd and to fail with -1/ENOTCAPABLE on a dup limited to CAP_READ only; it then closes all fds and unlinks the shm name, reporting failures through gtest expectations and returning nothing.

functions.name: TEST(Fcntl, Commands)
functions.prose_contract: Test body generated by TEST(Fcntl, Commands); precondition: a temp file can be created and InitRights is callable. Postcondition: it calls InitRights, creates a file and a socket plus dups limited to each of the nine fcntl_rights sets, checks that F_DUPFD on caps[0] yields an fd with identical rights, F_GETFD and F_SETFD work, that F_GETFL/F_SETFL/F_GETOWN/F_SETOWN (CAP_FCNTL) and F_GETLK (CAP_FLOCK) succeed only on caps whose rights contain the required right and fail with ENOTCAPABLE on others, then closes all fds and unlinks the temp file; failures are reported via gtest expectations and nothing is returned.

functions.name: FORK_TEST(Linux, ProcessClocks)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as a forked test process. Postcondition: it records its pid, forks a child which records its pid, sleeps 100ms and exits with 0; the slice is cut off before the rest of the body, so what the parent does with the clocks afterwards is not visible here; returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST(Linux, fstatat)
functions.prose_contract: Test body generated by TEST(Linux, fstatat) (class Linux_fstatat). Precondition: the temp directory is writable. Postcondition: it creates a file, makes dups limited to CAP_READ or CAP_READ|CAP_FSTAT, and asserts that fstatat with AT_EMPTY_PATH succeeds on the plain fd and the CAP_FSTAT dup but fails with ENOTCAPABLE on the read-only dup. It repeats the check for a directory fd (the dir_ro dup is taken from the already closed fd, so that check is flawed), closes the fds, unlinks the file and returns nothing.

functions.name: FORK_TEST_ON_MQ(PosixMqueue, CapModeIfMqOpenAvailable, "/cap_mq")
functions.prose_contract: Generated function PosixMqueue_CapModeIfMqOpenAvailable_ForkTest(), a void test body run in a forked child by the FORK_TEST_ON_MQ macro. Precondition: it runs inside a forked test process, and the caller may have message queue support available or not. Postcondition: if mq_open("/cap_mq") fails with ENOSYS the test is skipped (GTEST_SKIP) and the function returns early. Otherwise it creates the queue, makes three dup'd descriptors limited to read, write and event rights, closes the original, installs a SIGUSR2 handler and enters capability mode. It then expects mq_open to fail with a capability-mode error, mq_notify to succeed only with the event descriptor, mq_timedsend only with the write descriptor, mq_getattr and mq_setattr to succeed with the event descriptor, and mq_timedreceive only with the read descriptor. It expects the signal to have been delivered, and the received message and priority to equal the sent ones ("xyzzy", 10). It frees the malloc'd buffer and closes the three limited descriptors. It returns nothing, and failures are recorded as gtest expectation failures. The queue is not unlinked in this function; the outer TEST wrapper unlinks "/cap_mq".

functions.name: FORK_TEST(Openat, Relative)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test runs in a forked child with a readable /etc/ directory containing a readable passwd file, and the Capsicum capability APIs are available. Postcondition: the test opens /etc, makes capability fds with limited rights (plus fcntl/ioctl limits when supported), and checks that openat succeeds outside capability mode (including absolute paths and '..' paths with plain fds), that '..' lookups relative to capabilities fail with a traversal error, and that files opened relative to a capability carry the same rights. It then calls cap_enter and checks that relative lookups succeed for fds with CAP_LOOKUP, that lookups relative to a capability without CAP_LOOKUP fail as not-capable, that absolute-path and '..' lookups fail in capability mode, and that resulting fds from capabilities have the expected limited rights; it records failures through gtest EXPECT macros and returns nothing.

functions.name: FORK_TEST(Pdfork, OtherUserIfRoot)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test runs as root (otherwise skipped) and other_uid is set to a non-zero uid via the -u flag. Postcondition: the test pdforks a looping child and calls setuid(other_uid). It expects kill(pid, SIGKILL) to fail with EPERM and the child to stay alive. On FreeBSD it expects pdkill to fail with EBADF, the child to still be alive, and closing pd to kill it, after which pdwait4 fails with EBADF. Elsewhere it expects pdkill to succeed and the child to become a zombie, and pdwait4 to return the pid with a signaled status. It returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST(Socket, UnixDomain)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a Capsicum test environment where a Unix stream socket and a pipe can be created. Postcondition: the test creates a pipe and forks; the child waits for the parent's message, then checks that connect on the rw-limited socket fails with ENOTCAPABLE and succeeds on the all-rights socket, and exits with HasFailure(). The parent returns early if socket creation fails. Otherwise it checks that bind, listen, getsockname, setsockopt, getsockopt and accept fail with ENOTCAPABLE on the rw-limited socket and succeed on the all-rights socket, then signals the child, waits for it, expects exit status 0, closes its descriptors and unlinks the socket path. It returns nothing; failures are recorded through gtest expectations.

functions.name: TEST(Socket, TCP)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a Capsicum test environment where an AF_INET stream socket can be created. Postcondition: the test returns early if socket creation fails. Otherwise it binds the all-rights socket to an ephemeral port (bind on the rw-limited socket fails with ENOTCAPABLE) and reads the port. It forks a child that, after the parent's message, checks that connect to 127.0.0.1:port fails with ENOTCAPABLE on the rw-limited socket and succeeds on the all-rights socket, then exits with HasFailure(). The parent checks that listen, getsockname, setsockopt, getsockopt and accept fail with ENOTCAPABLE on the rw-limited socket and succeed on the all-rights socket, waits for the child, expects exit status 0, and closes its descriptors. It returns nothing; failures are recorded through gtest expectations.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv[1] names a file path that can be created and written, and the program is run with exactly one argument (argc == 2). Postcondition: if argc != 2 it calls usage(); otherwise, for every repetition, pattern and phase it creates and truncates the file, zero-fills it, optionally mmaps it and runs leader and follower (as threads with semaphores, or sequentially), unmaps, verifies the file contents and closes it; it returns 0 if everything succeeds, and any failure of open, ftruncate, write, mmap, sem_init, pthread_create or pthread_join, sem_destroy, msync, munmap, verify_file or close prints an error (where perror is used) and calls exit(1), while a failed lseek only prints a message and continues.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uint128_inc, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Test-case body for uint128_inc (the generated function name is derived from the ATF_TC_BODY macro). Precondition: called by the ATF runner with a valid test-case pointer. Postcondition: for each entry of a fixed 6-entry table, it encodes the input and expected vectors as little-endian 128-bit values, decodes the input, applies uint128_increment, and calls u128_check_equality against the expected value. A mismatch is recorded as a non-fatal ATF_CHECK_MSG failure; the function returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uint128_add64, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Test-case body for uint128_add64 (the generated function name is derived from the ATF_TC_BODY macro). Precondition: called by the ATF runner with a valid test-case pointer. Postcondition: for each entry of a fixed 5-entry table, it decodes the little-endian input to a uint128_t, calls uint128_add64 with the 64-bit addend, and calls u128_check_equality against the expected decoded value. A mismatch is recorded as a non-fatal ATF_CHECK_MSG failure; the function returns nothing.

functions.name: ATF_TC_BODY(uint128_chacha_ctr, tc)
functions.prose_contract: Test-case body for uint128_chacha_ctr (the generated function name is derived from the ATF_TC_BODY macro). Precondition: called by the ATF runner with a valid test-case pointer. Postcondition: the visible part defines a 6-entry table of counter vectors with expected incremented values, and declares a randomdev_key context, a zeroed RANDOM_KEYSIZE key, a trash block buffer and the loop locals. The loop that checks the ChaCha counter advance is cut off in the given slice, so nothing beyond these declarations is stated. The function returns nothing.

functions.name: test9
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fd is an open file descriptor on a file that the process may lock. Postcondition: the function creates a pipe and forks a child that takes a whole-file shared (F_RDLCK) lock and signals through the pipe; the parent waits for that byte, prints a header, tries a non-blocking F_SETLK for an exclusive (F_WRLCK) lock, then sends SIGTERM to the child, reaps it, and closes both pipe ends. The FAIL checks then cause failure if the exclusive lock succeeded (res == 0) or if errno is not EACCES or EAGAIN; otherwise SUCCEED is returned. pipe, fork, child-side fcntl/write and parent-side read errors terminate the process via err(1, ...).

functions.name: NoAllowOther_setextattr_Test::TestBody
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test fixture NoAllowOther is set up with a FUSE mount lacking allow_other and the test runs with privilege to fork. Postcondition: a forked child registers a lookup expectation returning a regular file (mode 0644, inode 42, infinite validity) and calls access() on FULLPATH to cache it, asserting success; a second, unprivileged child calls extattr_set_file on FULLPATH in the user namespace and returns 0 only if the call fails with errno EPERM, otherwise prints a message and returns 1; the test then asserts that the exit status of that child is 0. Nothing is returned (void).

functions.name: TEST_P(BmapEof, eof)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the BmapEof fixture is set up with a running mock FUSE server and m_maxbcachebuf set, and GetParam's second element (ngetattrs) is 1, 2 or 3. Postcondition: it registers mock expectations (lookup of RELPATH as inode 42 with size 2*m_maxbcachebuf and attr_valid 0, an open, one FUSE_READ at offset 0 of size 2*m_maxbcachebuf or m_maxbcachebuf answered with zeroes, and between ngetattrs-1 and ngetattrs FUSE_GETATTRs in sequence answered with size 2*m_maxbcachebuf, with any later GETATTRs answered with size m_maxbcachebuf); it then opens FULLPATH with O_RDWR (ASSERT_LE aborts the test with a failure and returns if open fails, leaking the buffer), reads 2*m_maxbcachebuf bytes into a heap buffer ignoring the read result, deletes the buffer and leaks the fd; it returns no value, and unmet expectations are reported as test failures.

functions.name: TEST_F(CopyFileRangeRlimitFsize, truncate)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function CopyFileRangeRlimitFsize_truncate_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: RLIMIT_FSIZE is set to start2 + len/2, and the mock FUSE server expects one FUSE_COPY_FILE_RANGE with off_out start2 and len len/2, which it answers with size len/2. Postcondition: it asserts that copy_file_range with len requested returns len/2, so the copy is truncated at the limit rather than failing; it returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(CopyFileRange, clear_sgid)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the mock FUSE server is scripted with root getattr, lookup and open of in.txt and out.txt (both mode 02777, size 16), one copy_file_range and one chmod to 0777. The test opens both files, asserts copy_file_range(off_in 0, off_out 8, len 8) returns 8, then expects fstat of the output fd to show S_IFREG|0777 (SGID cleared) and of the input fd to show S_IFREG|02777. Both fds are leaked at the end and the function returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(CopyFileRange, clear_suid)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the mock FUSE server is scripted with root getattr, lookup and open of in.txt and out.txt (both mode 04777, size 16), one copy_file_range and one chmod to 0777. The test opens both files, asserts copy_file_range(off_in 0, off_out 8, len 8) returns 8, then expects fstat of the output fd to show S_IFREG|0777 (SUID cleared) and of the input fd to show S_IFREG|04777. Both fds are leaked at the end and the function returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Create, ok)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the root directory has mode 0777 and the lookup of some_file.txt returns ENOENT, and the mock expects a create. The test calls open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL and asserts it returns a nonnegative fd, which is then leaked; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Create, eacces)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the root directory has mode 0755 and the lookup of some_file.txt returns ENOENT, with no create expected. The test asserts that open with O_CREAT|O_EXCL returns -1 and errno is EACCES; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Deleteextattr, eacces)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0644 and its lookup uid is 0, with no removexattr expected. The test asserts that extattr_delete_file in the user namespace returns -1 with errno EACCES; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Deleteextattr, ok)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0644 and is owned by geteuid(), and the mock expects a removexattr. The test asserts that extattr_delete_file in the user namespace returns 0; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Deleteextattr, system)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0666 and is owned by geteuid(), with no removexattr expected. The test asserts that extattr_delete_file in the system namespace returns -1 with errno EPERM; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Utimensat, utime_now)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0666 and owner 0, and the mock expects a FUSE_SETATTR with the ATIME and MTIME valid bits, which it answers with the attributes. The test asserts that utimensat with both times UTIME_NOW returns 0; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Utimensat, utime_omit)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0444 and owner 0, and no setattr is expected. The test asserts that utimensat with both times UTIME_OMIT returns 0; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Deleteextattr, user)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0666 and owner 0, and the mock expects a removexattr. The test asserts that extattr_delete_file in the user namespace returns 0; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Getextattr, eacces)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0600 and owner 0, with no getxattr expected. The test asserts that extattr_get_file in the user namespace returns -1 with errno EACCES; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Getextattr, ok)
functions.prose_contract: Test: the file has mode 0444 and owner 0, and the mock answers getxattr with the string "whatever" (length 9 including the NUL). The slice is cut off before the end of the test, so the final assertions are not visible; it sets up the lookup and getxattr expectations that the rest of the test then checks.

functions.name: TEST_P(FspacectlCache, clears_cache)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a mock FUSE daemon is mounted with a 26-byte file, with LIFO expectations (a read returning zeros, a read returning the contents, a punch-hole FUSE_FALLOCATE returning 0). Postcondition: the test opens the file, reads and caches the contents, runs fspacectl(SPACECTL_DEALLOC) over the whole file expecting success, rmsr.r_len 0 and rmsr.r_offset equal to offset+length, then re-reads and expects the daemon-supplied zeros; it asserts these with gtest and leaks the fd.

functions.name: TEST_F(PosixFallocate, enosys)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a mock FUSE daemon replies ENOSYS to the first FUSE_FALLOCATE on a 500-byte file. Postcondition: the test expects posix_fallocate to return EINVAL, a second call to return EINVAL without querying the daemon again, and fspacectl(SPACECTL_DEALLOC) to return 0 via the VOP_DEALLOCATE fallback without a daemon FUSE_FALLOCATE; the fd is leaked.

functions.name: TEST_F(Fsync, two_handles)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest function Fsync_two_handles (TEST_F(Fsync, two_handles)): precondition is a mounted mock FUSE filesystem in the Fsync fixture; it sets expectations for one lookup of some_file.txt (inode 42, twice), two opens, one write of "abcdefgh", and an fsync on the inode that must be issued for both open file handles. It opens the file write-only (fd1) and read-only (fd2), writes 8 bytes through fd1, and fsyncs fd1; each step is asserted (open returns >= 0, write returns the byte count, fsync returns 0) and a failed assertion aborts the test with a failure. On completion both descriptors are passed to leak() and not closed; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Intr, enosys)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a FUSE mock filesystem is mounted and the test fixture is set up. Postcondition: the test passes only if the first mkdir succeeds synchronously and the daemon answers FUSE_INTERRUPT with ENOSYS while completing the first mkdir. Signalling the blocked second mkdir thread then sends no further FUSE_INTERRUPT, and that thread returns 0. Failed expectations are reported as gtest failures; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Intr, ignore)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a FUSE mock filesystem is mounted and the test fixture is set up. Postcondition: the lookup of the directory returns ENOENT, and the daemon ignores the FUSE_INTERRUPT for the mkdir and replies only to the mkdir with a directory entry. The test passes only if the interrupted mkdir returns 0. Failed expectations are reported as gtest failures; nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Intr, in_kernel_restartable)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a FUSE mock filesystem is mounted and the test fixture is set up. The test opens a file for reading and starts a mkdir thread and a read thread, with the daemon stalled in the mkdir. Postcondition: a signal arrives while the read is still queued in the kernel. The test passes only if no FUSE_INTERRUPT is sent, the read is automatically restarted, and both threads return 0. The semaphores are destroyed and the fd is leaked deliberately. Nothing is returned.

functions.name: TEST_F(Intr, in_kernel_nonrestartable)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a FUSE mock filesystem is mounted and the test fixture is set up. A lookup and open for the target file are mocked, and the daemon stalls in a mkdir. Postcondition: a non-restartable operation (write or setextattr) still queued in the kernel is interrupted by a signal without any FUSE_INTERRUPT being sent, and it returns EINTR. Failed expectations are reported as gtest failures; nothing is returned. The slice is cut off, so the exact remaining steps are not shown.

functions.name: TEST_P(LastLocalModify, vfs_vget)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a mock FUSE filesystem is mounted at mountpoint and the parameter names a mutator (VOP_ALLOCATE, VOP_COPY_FILE_RANGE, VOP_SETATTR or VOP_WRITE); the test is skipped without effect if the effective user is not root. Postcondition: the test sets up lookup and mutator expectations, gets a file handle with getfh, runs the mutator in a thread, calls fhstat while the FUSE_LOOKUP reply is delayed, and asserts that fhstat succeeds and reports the new size (15), so the stale old size from the lookup is not cached. It then joins the thread and expects the mutator to return 0; failed assertions fail the test, and it returns void.

functions.name: Setlk_unlock_Test::TestBody
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the test fixture is set up so a mock FUSE filesystem is mounted. Postcondition: this is the body of TEST_F(Setlk, clear) (the Setlk_clear_Test::TestBody generated function). It queues lookup, open and setlk(F_UNLCK, range 10..1009) expectations, opens the file, calls fcntl(F_SETLK) with F_UNLCK, asserts it does not return -1, and leaks the descriptor; it returns void and reports failures via gtest assertions.

functions.name: TEST_F(Lookup, dotdot_no_parent_nid)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function Lookup_dotdot_no_parent_nid_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: the mock daemon answers LOOKUP of foo and foo/bar (both valid indefinitely) and an OPENDIR, and the test expects a FORGET of foo_ino with count 1; the file system is not exportable. Postcondition: the slice shown stops after setting up the FORGET expectation, so the remainder of the body, which exercises lookup of ".." on a vnode with no valid parent nid, is not visible; returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Lookup, vtype_conflict)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the mock daemon answers LOOKUP of 'foo' with a directory entry (nodeid 42, nlink 1, mode 0644) and LOOKUP of 'bar' with a regular-file entry of the same nodeid 42 with an infinite entry timeout; one FUSE_FORGET for node 42 with nlookup 1 may arrive asynchronously (at most once). Postcondition: the visible setup only registers these expectations; the test's final assertions are cut off in the slice.

functions.name: TEST_F(LookupExportable, dotdot_entry_cache_timeout)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a LookupExportable fixture is mounted and the mock answers LOOKUP of foo (nodeid 42, directory, attr_valid max, entry_valid 0) in the root, LOOKUP of bar (nodeid 43, directory, both validities max) in foo, OPENDIR for bar, and LOOKUP of ".." in foo with the root (both validities max). Postcondition: the test opens mountpoint/foo/bar with O_EXEC|O_DIRECTORY (asserting fd >= 0) and then expects faccessat(fd, "../..", F_OK, 0) to return 0.

functions.name: TEST_F(LookupExportable, dotdot_no_parent_nid)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: a LookupExportable fixture is mounted and the mock answers LOOKUP of foo (nodeid 42) and bar (nodeid 43) as directories with max validity, OPENDIR with an empty open reply, expects a FORGET of foo, and answers LOOKUP of ".." in bar with foo and LOOKUP of ".." in foo with the root. Postcondition: the test opens mountpoint/foo/bar (asserting fd >= 0), asserts that unmount("mountpoint", 0) fails with errno EBUSY, naps so asynchronous vnode reclamation can occur, and then expects faccessat(fd, "../..", F_OK, 0) to return 0.

functions.name: TEST_P(Notify, notify_after_unmount)
functions.prose_contract: Test body: precondition is a mock FUSE filesystem expecting a DESTROY. It unmounts the mock, then calls notify_inval_entry on the root with name foo and the expected error ENODEV; the test only requires that nothing crashes. It returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Open, o_rdonly)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest function Open_o_rdonly_Test::TestBody(); it needs the Open fixture with its mock FUSE server set up. It calls test_ok(O_RDONLY, O_RDONLY), which checks that opening a file with O_RDONLY succeeds and that the FUSE_OPEN request carries O_RDONLY flags; it returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Open, DISABLED_o_trunc)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest function Open_DISABLED_o_trunc_Test::TestBody(); it needs the Open fixture with its mock FUSE server set up. It is disabled by default (DISABLED_ prefix, FreeBSD bug 236340). When run, it calls test_ok(O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC, O_WRONLY | O_TRUNC), which checks that the open succeeds and the FUSE_OPEN request carries those flags; it returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Open, o_wronly)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest function Open_o_wronly_Test::TestBody(); it needs the Open fixture with its mock FUSE server set up. It calls test_ok(O_WRONLY, O_WRONLY), which checks that opening with O_WRONLY succeeds and the FUSE_OPEN request carries O_WRONLY flags; it returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Open, o_rdwr)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest function Open_o_rdwr_Test::TestBody(); it needs the Open fixture with its mock FUSE server set up. It calls test_ok(O_RDWR, O_RDWR), which checks that opening with O_RDWR succeeds and the FUSE_OPEN request carries O_RDWR flags; it returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Open, enosys)
functions.prose_contract: Generated gtest function Open_enosys_Test::TestBody(); it needs the Open fixture with its mock FUSE server set up. It expects a lookup of some_file.txt (ino 42), exactly one FUSE_OPEN for O_RDONLY that the server answers with ENOSYS, and one FUSE_FLUSH answered with ENOSYS. It then opens the file twice with O_RDONLY, asserting each open returns fd >= 0, closes the first fd, and leaks the second one with leak(fd); the second open succeeds without being sent to the server. It returns nothing.

functions.name: ReadSigbus::mmap_getblksz_fail
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the FUSE mock answers lookup, open and two GETATTRs successfully, then fails further GETATTRs with EIO, and expects no FUSE_READ. Postcondition: the test opens the file, mmaps one page, and reading the page raises SIGBUS, which is caught via the handler and longjmp. It then asserts the faulting address equals the mapped pointer, unmaps the page and leaks the fd; any failed assertion fails the test.

functions.name: TEST_F(RofsRead, atime_during_close)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: runs as a gtest test of fixture RofsRead with a read-only mock FUSE mount. Postcondition: it expects lookup, open, a read, flush and release, and no FUSE_SETATTR request. It opens the file read-only, sleeps via nap(), asserts that read returns the full 8 bytes, and closes the fd; the mock verifies that no atime update occurs during close.

functions.name: AioRead.async_read_disabled
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the fusefs test fixture is mounted without FUSE_ASYNC_READ and the mock daemon never answers FUSE_READ requests. Postcondition: after submitting two AIO reads at offsets 0 and m_maxbcachebuf and napping, the test expects only one FUSE_READ to have reached the daemon (read_count == 1); it then kills the daemon, waits for AIO completion ignoring errors, and leaks the fd. Returns nothing.

functions.name: AsyncReadNoAttrCache.read_sizechange
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the fixture is mounted with async reads and a zero-validity attribute cache; the mock daemon is set up to expect, in sequence, two GETATTRs returning size bufsize-1, a READ of size bufsize-1, a GETATTR returning bufsize, and a READ of size bufsize. Postcondition: this part of the test only sets up those sequenced expectations; the slice is cut off before the code that performs the reads. Returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Read, atime_during_close)
functions.prose_contract: Test body: requires a mocked daemon expecting lookup, open, read, one FUSE_SETATTR with only FATTR_ATIME equal to the atime from fstat, then flush and release; it reads the file, fstats it, and closes the fd (return value of close is not checked), so the dirty atime is flushed to the daemon during close.

functions.name: TEST_F(Read, direct_io_pread)
functions.prose_contract: Test body (the slice is cut off after the declarations): sets up a mocked daemon with a direct_io open of a file, opens it and preads CONTENTS at offset 100 straight from the daemon without filling the cache; only the setup declarations are visible in the slice, the rest is not shown.

functions.name: TEST_F(Rename, einval)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function Rename_einval_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: a mounted mock FUSE filesystem exists where lookup of "src" returns a directory with inode 42 and lookup of "dst" inside it returns ENOENT. Postcondition: renaming mountpoint/src to mountpoint/src/dst must fail with a nonzero return and errno EINVAL; gtest assertions fail otherwise, and the function returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Rename, enoent)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function Rename_enoent_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: a mounted mock FUSE filesystem exists where lookup of "src" in the root inode returns ENOENT. Postcondition: renaming mountpoint/src to mountpoint/dst must fail with a nonzero return and errno ENOENT; gtest assertions fail otherwise, and the function returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Rename, entry_cache_negative)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function Rename_entry_cache_negative_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: a mounted mock FUSE filesystem exists where "src" is a regular file with inode 42 and lookup of "dst" in the root returns a negative cache entry with zero validity; the daemon accepts a FUSE_RENAME of src to dst in the root and replies with success. Postcondition: rename(mountpoint/src, mountpoint/dst) returns 0, otherwise a gtest assertion fails; the function returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Rename, entry_cache_negative_purge)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function Rename_entry_cache_negative_purge_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: a mounted mock FUSE filesystem exists where "src" is a regular file with inode 42 and lookup of "dst" returns a negative cache entry that never expires, once; the daemon accepts FUSE_RENAME with success. Postcondition: rename succeeds (returns 0), and a later access(mountpoint/dst, F_OK) must succeed, which requires the negative entry to have been purged so the daemon is queried again; gtest assertions fail otherwise, and the function returns nothing.

functions.name: TEST_F(Rename, erelookup)
functions.prose_contract: Generated function Rename_erelookup_Test::TestBody(). Precondition: a mounted mock FUSE filesystem exists with src (directory, inode 42), dstdir (inode 43) and no dst inside it, where the daemon answers FUSE_SETATTR and FUSE_RENAME with EIO. Postcondition: it starts a thread that repeatedly chmods src, then repeatedly calls rename(mountpoint/src, mountpoint/dstdir/dst) for about NAP_NS nanoseconds, each of which must return -1 with errno EIO (the kernel restarts on ERELOOKUP internally); then it sets stopit, joins the thread, and returns nothing; gtest assertions fail otherwise.

functions.name: TEST_F(Setattr, eperm)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the mock FUSE daemon answers LOOKUP of some_file.txt with a regular file (mode 0777, owned by the caller) and answers FUSE_SETATTR on that inode with EPERM. Postcondition: the test passes only if truncate("mountpoint/some_file.txt", 10) returns nonzero and errno is EPERM; it returns nothing and takes no locks.

functions.name: TEST_F(Setattr, fchmod)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the mock daemon answers LOOKUP with a regular file (mode 0755, infinite attr validity), FUSE_OPEN with an empty open reply, and a FUSE_SETATTR with valid==FATTR_MODE and mode==0644 with matching attributes. Postcondition: the test asserts that open(O_RDONLY) yields fd>=0 and that fchmod(fd, 0644) returns 0; the fd is deliberately leaked via leak(fd) rather than closed.

functions.name: TEST_F(Setattr, ftruncate)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the mock daemon answers LOOKUP with a regular file (mode 0755, size 99, infinite attr validity), FUSE_OPEN with file handle 0xdeadbeef1a7ebabe, and a FUSE_SETATTR whose valid==FATTR_SIZE|FATTR_FH and fh equals that handle with new attributes of size 12345. Postcondition: the test asserts that open(O_RDWR) yields fd>=0 and that ftruncate(fd, 12345) returns 0; the fd is deliberately leaked via leak(fd).

functions.name: TEST_F(Setattr, truncate)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the mock daemon answers LOOKUP with a regular file (mode 0644, size 100000000) and answers a FUSE_SETATTR with valid==FATTR_SIZE and size==20000000 with attributes of that size.
