If the LUN is not attached and the command is not INQUIRY, REPORT_LUNS or REQUEST_SENSE, it fills ILLEGAL_REQUEST sense (asc 0x25) and returns. MODE_SENSE and MODE_SENSE_10 with an unsupported page fill ILLEGAL_REQUEST sense (asc 0x24) and return, and with a supported page copy up to min(allocation length, dxfer_len, built length) bytes of generated mode data into data_ptr and set resid. READ and WRITE commands with bad parameters from vhba_rwparm fill ILLEGAL_REQUEST sense (asc 0x24); otherwise they copy data_len bytes between data_ptr and the in-memory disk and set resid. READ_CAPACITY with nonzero reserved CDB bytes fills UNIT_ATTENTION sense, otherwise it writes the 8-byte capacity data. Other commands go to vhba_default_cmd. On the paths that fall through the switch, the CAM status is cleared and then set to CAM_SCSI_STATUS_ERROR (plus CAM_AUTOSNS_VALID on CHECK CONDITION) if scsi_status is not OK, else scsi_status is set OK and the status is CAM_REQ_CMP.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the usual process arguments (argv[0] non-NULL, argv[argc] NULL). Postcondition: main never returns; it calls exit. In ranlib mode (program name ends in "ranlib") it parses -t/-D/-U/-V, requires at least one archive and exits EXIT_FAILURE if any ar_write_archive(...,'s') call fails, else EXIT_SUCCESS (-V prints the version and exits EXIT_SUCCESS; bad options or no archive give usage and EXIT_FAILURE). In ar mode it requires argc >= 2 (prefixing '-' to argv[1] if missing, via malloc, erroring on failure), parses options and sets the mode; -V exits EXIT_SUCCESS; invalid usage, conflicting options (-a with -b/-i, -j with -z, -s with -S), a missing position operand, options not allowed in the mode, or two different modes cause a usage message or error exit via bsdar_errc/bsdar_usage. Mode 'M' runs ar_mode_script and exits EXIT_SUCCESS. Otherwise the archive name is required (else usage); if -s is set with no mode or mode p/t/x the archive is written with 's' (exit with its code if no mode). Modes d/m/q/r call ar_write_archive and p/t/x call ar_read_archive to stdout; any other mode gives usage. Each remaining file operand not found in the archive produces a warning and forces EXIT_FAILURE; the process exits with the accumulated exit code. The malloc'd argv[1] is not freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv form a valid argument vector with argv[0] non-NULL, as passed by the C runtime. Postcondition: the program mode is chosen from the basename of argv[0] (atq, atrm, batch, otherwise at) and then possibly changed by options (-r/-d, -l, -b, -c, -t, -q, -f, -m, -v); invalid options, an invalid queue or a mode option given when the mode is not at call usage(); a failed permission check calls errx(EXIT_FAILURE); otherwise the matching handler runs (list jobs for atq with privileges reduced, remove jobs for atrm with privileges reduced, print jobs for cat, writefile for at and batch, with the time parsed or taken from -t or now), an unknown mode calls panic(), and every path ends with the process terminating via exit(EXIT_SUCCESS) or through usage/errx/panic; main never returns normally.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process's command-line arguments. Postcondition: main never returns; it parses options (calling usage(), which exits with EX_USAGE, on invalid options or on more than one of -a/-d/-s, and exiting with EX_USAGE if xo_parse_args fails), defaults the path list to "." when none is given, walks the trees with fts, prints sizes (and a total with -c), and then calls exit(rval) with rval 0 if no FTS_DNR/FTS_ERR/FTS_NS entry was seen and 1 otherwise; fts_open, fts_read or xo_finish failures terminate with xo_err(1, ...).

functions.name: do_printf
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: plan points to a valid PLAN whose c_data is a NUL-terminated format string, entry points to a valid FTSENT with fts_statp, fts_path, fts_name and fts_accpath set, and fout is an open FILE stream. Postcondition: the escaped format is expanded to fout, with literal characters copied and each %-specifier (path, name, directory, ids, mode, sizes, link target, file type, times and so on) printed from entry; %Z prints nothing; the F_HAS_WARNED flag of plan is set if escaping warned; fout is flushed if the escape processing requested a flush; the escaped copy is freed; nothing is returned; the unimplemented specifiers %P, %H, %F, the numeric modifiers and '.', and unknown specifiers terminate the process through errx(1, ...) without returning.

functions.name: MCWriteCat
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fd is a descriptor open for writing, the global set list and each set's message list are well-formed, and every msg->str is a valid NUL-terminated string. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it builds in a newly allocated zeroed buffer the catalog (header with magic, set count and offsets, one set header per set, one message header per message in list order, then the concatenated NUL-terminated strings, all numeric fields in network byte order) and calls write(fd, buffer, size) once, ignoring the write result and any short write; the buffer is never freed, and xmalloc handles allocation failure.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv points to an argv-style array of NUL-terminated strings with argc entries (argc >= 0), and the iscsi device (ISCSI_PATH) and any config file named by -c are available as needed. Postcondition: the function never returns; it parses the options and exits with status 1 via xo_errx/xo_err/usage on any invalid or conflicting option, on a failure to open or close the iscsi device (after trying kldload when it is missing), on a missing nickname target or invalid target name, or on a stdout flush failure. Otherwise it runs the selected -A/-M/-R/-L operation against the kernel, optionally waits for -w timeout, closes the device and the xo container, and exits with status 1 if any kernel operation failed, else 0.

functions.name: ktrsyscall_freebsd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: ktr points to a valid struct ktr_syscall whose ktr_args array holds ktr_narg register_t values, resc, resip and resnarg are valid writable pointers, and *resc holds the current separator character. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it writes the decoded, symbolic form of the syscall arguments selected by ktr_code (at-fd, flags, modes, signals and similar) to stdout, consuming arguments by advancing a local cursor and decrementing a local count, with the ILP32 flag sv_flags determining quad slot sizes. For SYS_wait4 and SYS_kill it first overwrites the first argument in ktr_args with its pid_t-truncated value. Finally it stores the updated separator in *resc, the updated argument cursor in *resip and the remaining argument count in *resnarg; it takes no locks and holds no references.

functions.name: yyparse
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the lexer (YYLEX) and the flex grammar globals (scset, scbol, scon_stk, nmstr and so on) are initialised so the parser can run over the flex input. Postcondition: the function parses the whole input, running each rule's semantic action on reduction and calling the error routine on syntax errors. It returns 0 when the parse accepts (EOF is reached in the final state), and returns 1 when it aborts (error recovery exhausts the stack or hits EOF) or the parser stack cannot grow (stack overflow, after reporting "yacc stack overflow"). In both cases the parser stack is freed before it returns.

functions.name: yylex
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the flex scanner globals (yyin, start state, buffers, linenum, infilename, nmstr and the other parser state) are valid for scanning section 1 of the input. Postcondition: yylex matches the longest rule at the current position and runs its action: the actions in this slice return SCDECL, XSCDECL, SECTEND or TOK_OPTION (via BEGIN(OPTION)), or return a name token through RETURNNAME. The other actions return nothing: they update linenum, yytext_is_array, sectnum, bracelevel, brace_depth, infilename or the action buffer, push or pop start states, report errors through synerr, or discard the text, after which scanning continues. A definition name of MAXLINE characters or more triggers synerr and FLEX_EXIT(EXIT_FAILURE). The caller gets the token value or the end-of-input value; no reference or lock is passed to the caller.

functions.name: yylex
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the flex scanner's input source is available (yylex sets up the buffer and start state itself on its first call). Postcondition: it matches input rules until one returns a token, then returns that token code (e.g. '<', '^', '"', '$', '\n', BEGIN_REPEAT_POSIX/BEGIN_REPEAT_FLEX, EOF_OP) or 0 at end of input (yyterminate); in the slice's rules it updates linenum, bracelevel, sectnum, start conditions, action state and the pushed-back input, and it exits the process with EXIT_FAILURE on an over-long input line.

functions.name: yylex
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the flex scanner globals (input file, buffer, start-condition stack, nmstr, lex_compat/posix_compat flags) are set up so that yylex may be called. Postcondition: yylex scans input and runs the action of the matched rule. In the rules shown, an action either returns a token code (for example '[', CCL_OP_DIFF, CCL_OP_UNION, '(', ')', '/', '>', '^', '"', a literal character via RETURNCHAR or a name via RETURNNAME) or returns nothing and the scan continues with the next match. The actions also change the start condition (BEGIN), push or pop the start-condition stack or the sf_ flag stack, and push text back with yyless/unput. Error cases call synerr or format_synerr and keep scanning, except for an over-long definition name in rule 156, which calls synerr and FLEX_EXIT(EXIT_FAILURE) and does not return. At end of input the generated code (outside this slice) returns the EOF token.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the msgs command line, and the process can run setuid(getuid()), read the _PATH_MSGS directory and its bounds file (which is required unless send mode), and, to display messages, HOME must be set to a non-empty value. Postcondition: it never returns; it exits the process. It exits with err/errx status on failure (setuid failure, bad flag via usage, c flag by a non-superuser/daemon, missing bounds file unless -f where it exits 1, opendir or fopen failure, or no usable HOME which exits 1). In clean mode (-c) or when the bounds file is missing it rescans _PATH_MSGS, unlinking old writable messages when cleaning, and rewrites the bounds file unless in send mode; clean mode then exits 0. In send mode (-s) it writes the bounds file, creates message number lastmsg+1 from stdin and exits with ferror(stdin) (or 1 if OBJECT is defined and no Subject was seen). Otherwise it updates the user's .msgsrc file, shows the headers and bodies of messages from firstmsg to lastmsg as the user commands (query mode prints 'There are new messages.' and exits 0, 'x' and 'q' exit 0), updates the .rc next-message number, prints 'No new messages.' if nothing was shown and not hush or query, and exits 0. Open files are closed only through process exit.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv form a valid program argument vector, the netstat global flags are in their initial state and xo_parse_args can parse the libxo options. Postcondition: main never returns; it parses the options, optionally attaches to a jail, loads kvm symbols for non-live use, then prints exactly one report (bpf stats for -B, mbuf for -m, netisr for -Q, interfaces for -i without -s, routes or route stats for -r, nexthops for -o, nexthop groups for -O, multicast routing for -g, one protocol for -p, or all protocols for the selected address family plus unix sockets), and finishes the xo output and calls exit(EX_OK), or exits with EXIT_FAILURE if xo_parse_args fails, or with EX_IOERR if xo_finish fails, or with the EX_DATAERR, EX_USAGE or EX_UNAVAILABLE codes (or via usage()) on invalid options, invalid fib, unknown family or protocol, incompatible -x and -T, -B without a live system, a jail that is not found or cannot be attached, or setfib failure.

functions.name: another_hunk
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the global patch state is initialised (pfp open on the patch, diff_type set, buf, hunkmax and the p_line/p_char/p_len arrays allocated); any lines left in p_line from the previous hunk are still owned by the arrays. Postcondition: the previous hunk's lines are freed (except the fake-copied range p_bfake..p_efake); then the next hunk of the given diff type (context, new context, unified or normal) is read and converted to the context-diff layout in p_line/p_char/p_len, with p_first, p_newfirst, p_ptrn_lines, p_repl_lines, p_context, p_hunk_beg and p_end set, omitted context lines filled in, and a stopper '^' stored in p_char[p_end+1] if room allows; the hunk is swapped if reverse is set (a swap failure only prints a message), and the function returns true. It returns false without consuming the hunk when the next line is not a hunk header (len == 0 or no hunk marker), after calling next_intuit_at to reposition the input, or when savestr runs out of memory, after trimming p_end and freeing partially built lines. Malformed input or premature end of file calls malformed() or fatal() and does not return normally.

functions.name: setup
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the program's command-line arguments and the pr global option state is initialised so egetopt can parse them. Postcondition: returns 1 on any failure and 0 on success. Failures are: tmpfile() cannot be created while stdout is a tty (this also sets err to stderr), an invalid option value, an unknown option, or a combination or width that is invalid (-a with one column, -a with -m, -m with multiple columns, or a column width below 1). Each failure except the unknown option and the tmpfile case writes a diagnostic to err. On success it sets the option globals (page, column, gap, width and line counts, with defaults filled in). It reduces lines by the header and trailer length, or increments nohead if lines is too short. It halves lines for double spacing, or clears dspace when lines is 1. It sets the LC_TIME locale from -L (or the environment) and sets timefrmt to a strdup'd date format string chosen from the locale's day/month order.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the program's command-line arguments (options -h, -f, -, -x, -n, -sN, -lLANG, -d FILE, or input file names), and a vgrindefs language database is available. Postcondition: for each file argument (or stdin when none or '-' is given) it loads the language definition, emits the troff setup, then copies each stdin line to stdout, passing '.' lines through verbatim (toggling pass on .vS/.vE) and running other lines through putScp (or echoing them verbatim when filtering and not in a pass region); it calls err(1) if a file cannot be reopened, prints a message and exits with status 0 if the language entry or vgrindefs file is missing or has a reference loop, and otherwise exits with status 0 after all arguments are processed; it never returns normally.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the program's command-line arguments; the options are parsed and default directories set up by scanopts() and defaults(), with at least one of the man, bin or source directory lists non-empty. Postcondition: for each query name (after stripping the path, the SCCS/RCS prefix and suffix, and compression suffixes) it searches the binary, man and source locations enabled by the options, and unless -u is given and nothing unusual was found it prints the name and the matches to stdout. It returns 0 at the end. It exits via errx(EX_DATAERR) if no directories are left to search and via errx(EX_UNAVAILABLE) if a regex fails to compile. It calls abort() on allocation failure. It frees the temporary strings and the regex it compiled, but the bin, man and src result strings are not freed.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process arguments, with argv[0] the program name and the remaining words options and file operands. Postcondition: the function never returns; it parses the options (an invalid option, an invalid -l/-m/-N/-f value, an unknown group, user or digest, a -s combined with -d or -l, or a wrong operand count calls usage() or errx/err and exits with nonzero status), and then installs the operands with install() or creates directories with install_dir() and calls exit(EX_OK). A failed open of the metafile only produces a warning. Operands are handled in one of three ways: with -d each operand becomes a directory; if the last operand is an existing directory (or, with a symbolic link, a symlink to one) every other operand is installed into it; otherwise exactly two operands are installed as file to file. Further nonzero exits occur when stat/lstat fails, the target is not a regular file, the source and target are the same file, or more than two operands are given with a symlinked target. It frees the parsed mode set, and sets the globals gid, uid, digesttype and metafp as a side effect.

functions.name: defined_init
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none beyond the program being able to call uname(); any previous contents of the global defined_values list are discarded without being freed, since the list head is simply reinitialised. Postcondition: defined_values is an empty tail queue that then receives, via defined_add, the entries ARCH and CPU (both the uname machine), DOLLAR ("$"), HOST (nodename), OSNAME (sysname), OSREL (release) and OSVERS (version); if uname() returns nonzero, log_err(1, "uname") is called, which does not return, so the entries are not added; the function returns nothing.

functions.name: mevent_dispatch
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: called once by the thread that will run the event loop, with no other mevent_dispatch loop running; mevent_init (run via pthread_once) must be able to set up the kqueue descriptor mfd. Postcondition: it records the calling thread as mevent_tid and names it, creates the wake-up pipe mevent_pipefd (calling exit(0) if pipe() fails, and errx(EX_OSERR) if Capsicum rights cannot be applied), registers the pipe read end as an internal EVF_READ event (asserting that registration succeeds), then loops forever: building and submitting the change list through kevent, blocking in kevent for events (printing an error on failure other than EINTR), and passing the result to mevent_handle; it never returns and has no return value.

functions.name: umouse_request
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: scarg points to a valid umouse_softc and xfer to a valid usb_data_xfer whose data blocks (and ureq, if non-NULL) are valid, with the first usable data block's buf large enough for the requested reply. Postcondition: every data block in the ring gets bdone=0 and processed=1; the first usable block is filled according to the setup request (descriptors, status, config, interface, idle, protocol or report), and SET_FEATURE/CLEAR_FEATURE/SET_IDLE/SET_PROTOCOL update the softc state; it returns USB_ERR_NORMAL_COMPLETION on success or when ureq is NULL, USB_ERR_STALLED for an invalid descriptor, index or report request, any feature request on an interface or endpoint, or an unhandled request, and USB_ERR_SHORT_XFER if a read reply left remaining bytes (blen > 0) and the error was not already set; for a successful write request with a data block, blen is set to 0. No locks or references are taken or released.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are a valid command line, and the -d option must give a ugen device name as bus.dev. Postcondition: the function exits the process on any failure, and returns normally without an explicit value only after the firmware init attempt. Details: exit(127) if libusb_init fails; usage() if -d is missing or unparseable, or for -h or an unknown option; exit(1) if the device is not found, its descriptor cannot be read, libusb_open fails, or ath3k_get_state or ath3k_get_version returns 0; exit(0) if it is an AR3012 with bcdDevice > 1. Otherwise it uses -f as the firmware path, defaulting to _DEFAULT_ATH3K_FIRMWARE_PATH, calls ath3k_init_ar3012 or ath3k_init_firmware with the result ignored, then closes the handle, unrefs the device and exits the libusb context. The strdup'd firmware_path is never freed. No explicit return statement ends main.

functions.name: kbd_status_changed
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: s is non-NULL, len equals sizeof(vkbd_status_t), data points to a buffer of at least max(len,3) bytes holding a vkbd_status_t, and get_hid_device(&s->bdaddr) returns non-NULL (these are asserted). Postcondition: always returns 0; data is overwritten with an HID output report (data[0]=0xa2, then LED bits, and the report ID in data[1] with the LED byte in data[2] when a report ID was found); if any HUP_LEDS output items were found it writes 3 bytes (when a report ID was found) or 2 bytes to s->intr (write result ignored) and, if s->srv->uinput and the device is a keyboard, calls uinput_rep_leds(s->ukbd, st.leds, leds_mask); a warning is logged for each LED item whose report ID differs from the first one; the HID parse context is ended with hid_end_parse.

functions.name: server_send_service_attribute_response
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: srv is valid, fd indexes a valid srv->fdidx entry whose rsp buffer holds rsp_size bytes with rsp_cs <= rsp_size and a rsp_limit large enough (at least 3) to hold the continuation state, and srv->req points to a valid request PDU. Postcondition: it sends one chunk of the pending response (the PDU header, byte count, response bytes, and continuation state of 1 or 3 bytes) to fd with a single writev, retried while it fails with EINTR; rsp_cs is advanced past the bytes in this chunk (if the remainder does not fit within rsp_limit, the chunk is shortened and a 2-byte continuation state carrying the new rsp_cs is appended, otherwise a single zero byte is appended); if rsp_cs then equals rsp_size, rsp_cs, rsp_size and rsp_limit are reset to 0 even if the write failed; returns 0 if the write succeeded, or errno if writev failed with an error other than EINTR.

functions.name: server_prepare_service_search_attribute_response
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: srv->req holds an SDP PDU whose header len gives the parameter length, fd indexes a valid srv->fdidx entry with a response buffer of at least NG_L2CAP_MTU_MAXIMUM bytes. Postcondition: returns SDP_ERROR_CODE_INVALID_REQUEST_SYNTAX if the request is shorter than 13 bytes or if the ServiceSearchPattern, MaximumAttributeByteCount (must be > 0), AttributeIDList or ContinuationState fields are malformed or truncated, or a UUID type is unknown or truncated; returns SDP_ERROR_CODE_INVALID_CONTINUATION_STATE if the request's continuation state differs from fdidx[fd].rsp_cs; returns 0 without changing the response if a response is already pending (rsp_size > 0); returns SDP_ERROR_CODE_INSUFFICIENT_RESOURCES if building an attribute list fails (a partly built response may remain in the buffer but rsp_size is not set); otherwise builds the AttributeLists sequence in the response buffer for each matching provider and each searched UUID, sets rsp_limit to min(omtu - sizeof(sdp_pdu_t) - 2, requested max byte count), sets rsp_size to the total length and rsp_cs to 0, writes the seq16 header, and returns 0.

functions.name: server_send_service_search_response
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: srv is a valid server whose fdidx[fd] holds a pending response buffer (rsp, rsp_size, rsp_cs <= rsp_size, rsp_limit large enough for the splitting loop to terminate) and srv->req points to the request PDU, and fd is a connected socket. Postcondition: it builds a ServiceSearchResponse PDU from the unsent part of the buffer, advancing rsp_cs and, if the remainder does not fit in rsp_limit, trimming the chunk in steps of 4 bytes and appending a 2-byte continuation state (otherwise a zero-length one); it writes the PDU with writev, retrying on EINTR; if rsp_cs then equals rsp_size (the last chunk was sent or failed) it resets rsp_cs, rsp_size and rsp_limit to 0; it returns 0 if writev did not fail, otherwise the errno value of the failure.

functions.name: op_hrSWInstalled
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: curr_op is SNMP_OP_GET or SNMP_OP_SET to return normally, and for GET value must be non-null with sub >= 1 and value->var.subs[sub - 1] equal to LEAF_hrSWInstalledLastChange or LEAF_hrSWInstalledLastUpdateTime. Postcondition: for SNMP_OP_SET it returns SNMP_ERR_NOT_WRITEABLE and changes nothing; for SNMP_OP_GET it calls refresh_swins_tbl(), sets value->v.uint32 to 0 if swins_tick <= start_tick and otherwise to swins_tick - start_tick clamped to UINT_MAX, and returns SNMP_ERR_NOERROR; for SNMP_OP_ROLLBACK, SNMP_OP_COMMIT, SNMP_OP_GETNEXT, any other operation, or an unsupported leaf, the function calls abort() and does not return.

functions.name: wlan_hwmp_config_set
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: wif points to a valid wlan_iface whose wname and the hwmp_root_mode / hwmp_max_hops fields are readable, and which is one of the LEAF_wlanHWMPRootMode or LEAF_wlanHWMPMaxHops values. Postcondition: returns -1 without issuing an ioctl if which is neither LEAF_wlanHWMPRootMode nor LEAF_wlanHWMPMaxHops, or if which is LEAF_wlanHWMPRootMode and hwmp_root_mode is not one of the four known modes; otherwise it maps the setting to an ioctl value (root mode translated, max hops copied) and calls wlan_ioctl in set mode, returning -1 if that call returns a negative value and 0 on success.

functions.name: env_get
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: name is a valid NUL-terminated string and envp is a NULL-terminated array of valid NUL-terminated strings. Postcondition: scans envp in order, skipping entries without '=', and returns a pointer to the character just after the '=' in the first entry whose text before its first '=' has exactly the same length and bytes as name; returns NULL if no entry matches; nothing is allocated or modified, and the returned pointer points into the matching entry string.

functions.name: ELFNAMEEND(hide)
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fd is an open, readable and writable file descriptor for an ELF object of this class and fn is a NUL-terminated file name used in messages and in the new symbol names. Postcondition: returns 0 if the file has no symbol table (file untouched) or if every symbol was renamed and the rewrite succeeded; in the success case each symbol that is not in the keep list and not SHN_UNDEF is renamed "_$$hide$$ <fn> <name>", the string table, the symbol table, later sections and the section header table are written back at recomputed offsets (e_shoff updated in the header if it moved); returns 1 on any failure: header read failure, e_shentsize not equal to sizeof(Elf_Shdr), allocation, read or write failure, multiple symbol tables, missing strtab or shstrtab, combined strtab and shstrtab, zero-sized or unterminated string tables, or a needed buffer being NULL. Failures can leave the file partially rewritten. On every path the layout table, the per-section buffers it owns and the new string table are freed; the caller keeps fd and fn.

functions.name: iscsi_connection::login
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the connection has a freshly accepted iSCSI socket with no initiator name or session type yet set, and a Login Request PDU can be received. Postcondition: it reads the first Login PDU and, on any error (non-zero TSIH, missing or invalid InitiatorName, invalid SessionType, missing TargetName, unknown target, deny or unknown auth-type, initiator name or portal not permitted, or CHAP required but the initiator skipped authentication), it sends a login error response and exits the process via log_errx(1); on redirect it exits with 0. If the initiator's current stage is operational negotiation and no authentication is needed, it deletes the request keys and calls login_negotiate(request) and returns, without sending an auth response. Otherwise it sends one response PDU carrying AuthMethod (None, CHAP or Reject) plus TargetAlias and TargetPortalGroupTag for normal sessions, frees the response, request and key objects, and exits with status 1 if AuthMethod was rejected under CHAP. Otherwise it runs login_chap then login_negotiate(nullptr) when authentication is required, login_negotiate(nullptr) if the transit flag is set, or else login_wait_transition(); it returns void.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the program name followed by exactly one floppy device path, with optional flags -F, -f, -n, -q, -s, -v and -y; the device must open and answer the floppy ioctls. Postcondition: it formats and/or verifies every track of the device and returns 0 if no verification errors were recorded, or 1 if at least one verify error with EIO was recorded (errs != 0). It returns EX_UNAVAILABLE if the user does not confirm the format prompt. Bad options, a wrong argument count, an unknown format, or failed open, ioctl or fcntl calls end the program through usage(), err() or errx() with an exit code and do not return. The device descriptor is never closed and the path buffer is not freed on the success path.

functions.name: dvsend
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: d is an open FireWire device descriptor, filename names a DV file to read, ich encodes the channel in its low 6 bits and the tag in bits 6-7, and count is the frame limit (a value <= 0 means no limit). Postcondition: returns nothing; it opens the file (exiting via err(EX_NOINPUT) if that fails), allocates a read buffer that it never frees, sets the tx buffers and the stream channel by ioctl (exiting via err(1) on failure), then repeatedly reads DV data and sends it with writev as isochronous packets with CIP headers, retrying on EAGAIN and exiting via err(1) on any other write error. It stops at end of file, at a read error (which prints a warning), or when the frame count is exceeded, then prints the frame count and timing statistics to stderr and closes the input file.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the standard program arguments, and exactly one of -a, -i, -r or -s is given (usage() is called otherwise, as for -h, a missing mode, a bad option argument, or leftover non-option arguments). Postcondition: with -i it returns instruct_bus's result without opening a device; if encode_offset fails it prints the message and returns EX_USAGE; if open of the device fails it prints an error and returns EX_NOINPUT; otherwise it runs access_bus (-a), scan_bus (-s) or reset_bus (-r), closes the descriptor (asserting close succeeds) and returns that operation's error value.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the standard program arguments. Postcondition: the function never returns; it parses the options -i (interface name), -f (inet, inet6 or link), -v, and with KVM also -K, -M and -N. An unknown interface exits with EX_NOHOST. An unknown address family exits with EX_USAGE. Any other option, or family link combined with -v, calls usage(). It then runs the KVM backend if -K was given. It runs the getifmaddrs backend if -K was not given, or if the KVM backend failed and neither a core nor a kernel was specified. If the last backend run returned nonzero it exits with EX_OSERR, otherwise it exits with EX_OK.

functions.name: getconfigent
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: the config file stream fconfig is open and the global settings (euid, egid, bind_sa4/bind_sa6, v4bind_ok/v6bind_ok, maxchild, maxcpm, maxperip, biltins) are initialised. Postcondition: it reads lines via nextline, skipping comments and blank lines, and for each line fills the static servtab 'serv' (zeroed first); a line that is invalid or ignored (bad user/group/mode, faith, bad RPC version or IP version, ignored IPv4/IPv6 bind, too-long unix path, bad wait/nowait, bad max-child, bad tcpmux protocol/socktype, unknown internal service, too many arguments) is logged and skipped by restarting at 'more' with the next line (in some of these cases the partially built entry is freed with freeconfig, in others not); on the first valid line it returns a pointer to the static servtab with all fields (service, socktype, proto, family, ctladdr, accept, child limits with defaults, user, group, server, bi, argv, empty children and connection lists) set; at end of file it returns NULL; an invalid IPsec policy line terminates the process with exit(EX_CONFIG).

functions.name: run_command
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: j points to a valid cfjail whose comparam, comstring, flags and intparams are initialised as run_command expects (e.g. KP_JID must be set for IP_ZFS_DATASET). Postcondition: IP_STOP_TIMEOUT returns term_procs(j); IP__OP removes or creates the jail and returns 0, or -1 if jail_remove fails with EPERM or create_jail fails; otherwise argv is built per comparam, and it returns -1 after a warning on a mount parse error, missing information, a missing KP_PATH for the devfs/fdescfs/procfs mounts, a failed check_path, or a failed open of the console log; it returns 0 if the command is empty (a mount with no arguments or argv[0] NULL); in the parent after fork it sets j->comline and returns 0 (freeing and NULLing j->comline) when the command is backgrounded or add_proc fails, else decrements paralimit and returns 1 with j->comline kept; the forked child never returns (it execs the command or exits with 1 on error); fork failure and ZFS buffer overflow exit the process with status 1.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the command-line arguments, with at least one path operand after the options (-R, -d, -f file, -v), otherwise usage() is called and the program exits. Postcondition: it exits with status 1 on a usage error, if the first path cannot be stat'ed, if it is not a directory and -d is not given (ENOTDIR), if libelf is unsupported, if fts_open fails, or if a hint temp file cannot be created. Otherwise it walks the tree and calls read_kld on every regular file whose name has no dot or ends in ".ko". Unless -d is given, each visited directory gets a temp hint file, which is renamed to the hint file if any entries were recorded and otherwise removed along with any existing hint file. Finally it closes the traversal and returns 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the usual command-line arguments of lpr (argv[0] is the program name). Postcondition: bad options or arguments, an unknown or unusable printer, a copy-count violation, an unprivileged -U, an unknown user, a restricted-group failure or a disabled queue make it exit via usage() or errx(1, ...). Otherwise it creates the temporary control file, writes the header cards and spools each named file (or stdin) by hard-link move or copy. If at least one file was queued (nact > 0), it links the control file to its final name, removes the temporary name, starts the printer daemon unless -q was given (printing a message if that fails) and calls exit(0). If a failure while touching or renaming the control file occurs, it calls cleanup(0). If nothing was queued, it calls cleanup(0) and, should that return, returns 1.

functions.name: ffs_cg_swap
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: o and n point to valid cylinder-group buffers (o readable, n writable, large enough for every offset and array the function touches) and fs points to a valid superblock. Postcondition: all fixed header fields of n (including cg_frsum entries and cg_time) are set to the byte-swapped values from o; if fs_magic is FS_UFS2_MAGIC the function returns there, otherwise it also copies, byte-swapped, the fs_old_cpg 32-bit words at the btotoff offset, the fs_old_cpg*fs_old_nrpos 16-bit words at the boff offset, and cluster summary words 1..fs_contigsumsize at clustersumoff, using offsets taken from n (swapped back again if n->cg_magic is not CG_MAGIC); it returns nothing and acquires or releases no locks or references.

functions.name: read_mtree
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fname names a readable mtree manifest file, or is "-" for stdin, and node must be NULL (asserted; nesting is unsupported). Postcondition: opens the file (exiting via err if it cannot be opened), parses it line by line until EOF or an error, and closes it unless it is stdin. It exits with status 1 if a read error (error > 0) occurs, or if any parse errors were counted. Otherwise it returns the root of the parsed fsnode tree (mtree_root), or, if the manifest produced no nodes, a newly created '.' directory node whose first field points to itself. Warnings alone only print a message. If mtree_file_push fails it skips parsing and goes to the error exit.

functions.name: read_mtree_keywords
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is an open stream positioned at the keywords of an mtree spec line, and node is a valid fsnode whose inode (and its stat) is valid. Postcondition: it reads keywords from fp until an empty keyword, applying each to node and its stat (possibly allocating node->symlink or node->contents, and flags, mode, size, times, uid/gid, type), and the loop continues after a bad keyword, printing a diagnostic for EINVAL, ENOATTR, ENOSYS or ENXIO; the error code of the last keyword processed is overwritten by the next one, so an error is returned only if it is the last one set, or if skip_over or read_word fails (their error code is returned immediately). After the loop it returns that nonzero error if any. Otherwise it sets the file type in st_mode, applies the default timestamp if present, and returns 0 for global defaults (node->name NULL). It also returns 0 after printing a diagnostic when link and contents are both given, a link type lacks a link keyword, the file type mismatches the keywords, or the contents file cannot be stat'ed (freeing the resolved name). If mtree_resolve fails it returns errno. Otherwise it may merge hardlinked inodes (freeing node->inode and bumping the link count), replaces node->contents with the resolved path (freeing the old one), sets st_size from the contents file, and returns 0.

functions.name: r_gestures
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: tp points to a valid touchpad state with hw caps and info configured, time points to a valid timestamp, and ms points to a mouse status that may be modified. Postcondition: if the pressure is high enough (z >= min_pressure_hi, or a finger is already down and z >= min_pressure_lo), it ignores a palm single-touch packet (returns GEST_IGNORE without further changes), otherwise clamps coordinates to the margins, starts a new action if none was in progress, records the position and finger count, maps clickpad softbuttons, adds the tap-hold button, updates the peak pressure, finger count and virtual-scroll state, and returns GEST_IGNORE on a finger-count change, GEST_VSCROLL or GEST_HSCROLL for vertical or horizontal scrolling, GEST_IGNORE (more than one finger) or GEST_ACCUMULATE (one finger) while within the tap timeout, else GEST_MOVE. When the pressure is too low, it clears BUTTON1 on clickpads with softbuttons, resets prev_nfingers, and ends any action in progress: a qualifying tap (no vscroll, zmax >= tap_threshold, within the tap timeout) either completes a double tap (clears in_taphold, sets fingerdown, idletimeout = 0) or starts tap-hold (sets in_taphold, idletimeout, a new taptimeout, the tap_button chosen by finger count 3/2/other, and ORs it into ms->button), while a non-tap clears in_taphold. With no action in progress and in_taphold set, it keeps the tap button pressed until the tap timeout passes and then clears in_taphold. The low-pressure path always returns GEST_IGNORE.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the standard program arguments and the moused globals (portname, config_file, pidfile, etc.) are initialised. Postcondition: main never returns; it parses options (calling usage() on invalid ones), opens /dev/consolectl and a kqueue (exiting with status 1 on failure), installs signal handlers, initialises quirks and the rodent devices (exiting 1 if a named device cannot be initialised), and in identify mode prints device info and exits 0; otherwise it optionally opens a pidfile (exiting 1 if moused is already running) and daemonizes (exiting 1 on failure), then runs moused(). On SIGHUP it unrefs quirks, deinitialises the devices and restarts; on SIGINT/SIGQUIT/SIGTERM it exits 0 directly; on other longjmp values or after moused() returns it unrefs quirks, deinitialises all rodents, closes dfd, kfd and cfd if open, and exits 0.

functions.name: r_protocol
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: rBuf is the next byte read from the mouse device, act points to a valid writable mousestatus_t holding the previous button state, and the globals rodent and cur_proto describe the current protocol. Postcondition: for KIDSPAD and GTCO_DIGIPAD it returns the result of kidspad()/gtco_digipad(); otherwise it accumulates rBuf into a static packet buffer, resynchronising (discarding the partial packet) on a bad header or data byte, and returns 0 when the byte is skipped, the packet is still incomplete, an optional fourth byte fails its check, the protocol is unknown, or an X10 MouseRemote button packet was handled (forwarded to rodent.mremcfd if >= 0). On an optional extra byte after a full packet it updates dx/dy/dz/obutton/button, resets the buffer and returns act->flags. On a newly completed packet it sets dz, obutton, button, dx and dy per the protocol (PS/2 model-specific handling included), updates static VersaPad state, and returns act->flags, which is MOUSE_POSCHANGED if dx, dy or dz is nonzero, ORed with the XOR of the old and new buttons. The buffer index is not reset after a full packet, since an extra byte may follow.

functions.name: apic_probe
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: paddr and where are valid writable pointers, and the global verbose and grope flags are set and the memory-access helpers seekEntry/readEntry can read the probed physical memory areas. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it searches in order the EBDA (only if its pointer is nonzero), the CMOS top-of-memory last 1K, the default 639K last 1K (only if that differs from the CMOS target), the BIOS, the extended BIOS, and, only if grope is set, two extra areas, for the MP signature on 4-byte boundaries, and at the first hit sets *where to 1..7 respectively (1 EBDA, 2 CMOS top of mem, 3 default top of mem, 4 BIOS, 5 extended BIOS, 6 grope area 1, 7 grope area 2) and *paddr to the physical address of the signature; if nothing is found it sets *where to 0 and *paddr to 0. It may print progress when verbose is set.

functions.name: process_cmd
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cmd points to a writable NUL-terminated command line with at least one character after the command letter (the code reads cmd[1] and skips blanks after it), fp is an open stream (read for further source lines by 'i'/'e'), and s and s6 are IPv4/IPv6 socket descriptors, either of which may be negative when that family is unavailable. Postcondition: returns nothing and dispatches on *cmd. '?' calls usage(); 'q' closes s and exits the process with status 0 and never returns; 's' prints "-1" if no integer >= 1 is parsed, else sleeps that many seconds and prints "ok"; 'j'/'l' (join/leave), 'i'/'e' (set include/exclude filter, reading n further address lines from fp), 't'/'b' (allow/block source) and 'g' (get source filter, printing mode, count, sorted sources, then "ok") print "ok" on success and "-1" on parse or lookup or setsockopt failure, while some failures (unsupported protocol family, getsourcefilter failure in 't'/'b') only emit a warning and print nothing; 'a'/'d' add or delete a link-layer multicast address by ioctl and print "ok" or "-1" (or only warn on parse errors); 'm' warns and prints "-1"; 'p' toggles IFF_PPROMISC via ioctl and prints "changed to 0x..." or only warns on failure, printing "-1" if arguments do not parse; a newline does nothing; any other command prints "invalid command". It does not return a value and keeps no resources acquired, except that exit for 'q' terminates the process.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the nfsuserd command line (optional -domain NAME, -verbose, -force, -manage-gids, -usermax N, -usertimeout N, and at most one positional server count), and the process has privileges to load or use the nfscommon kernel module and call nfssvc. Postcondition: main never returns normally; it calls usage() or exits with status 1 (errx/err/exit) on any failure: module missing, no inet/inet6 socket, bad arguments, domain name empty or all dots or containing a non-ASCII character, nfssvc delete-port failure when -force is given, udp socket, svcudp_create or svc_register failure, nfssvc port registration failure (with a jail or already-running message), or an nfssvc idname failure for initialize, group or user entries. On success it lowercases the domain name with leading and trailing dots stripped, registers the default ids, then up to nid_usermax groups and then unique-uid users with the kernel, frees aip if mustfreeai is set, blocks SIGUSR1 and SIGCHLD, daemonizes, installs signal handlers, and forks nfsuserdcnt children. Each child sets im_a_server, unblocks SIGUSR1, runs svc_run() and exits with status 1 if it returns; a failed fork is only logged. The master renames itself and loops forever in sigsuspend, so it ends only via a signal handler (cleanup_term).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: none; the function takes no meaningful inputs beyond the standard program entry. Postcondition: it prints to stdout the sizeof of the NTP request/response structures and unions (req_data_u_tag, req_pkt, req_pkt_tail, resp_pkt_u_tag, resp_pkt, info_peer_list, info_peer_summary, info_peer, info_peer_stats) together with the offsetof of their fields, separated by blank lines. The visible slice ends before the function's return statement, so the return value is not shown there; it acquires or releases no locks, references or memory.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the program name followed by options [-a] [-h] [-l limit] [-m raw|global|block] [-k kernelfile] and exactly two operands (pmcstat log file, then binary file), all readable; the pmcstat tool must be runnable via system(). Postcondition: it creates temporary files in TMPDIR or _PATH_TMP, runs pmcstat to produce a map file, reads it into entries (skipping lines starting with whitespace, counting samples and acquiring references for known pcs), removes the map file, builds and compacts the function queue, writes the binary file output, parses it as assembly (if -a) or C and then removes it, and returns 0; any bad option, wrong operand count, inaccessible file, allocation, system, I/O, scan or parse failure ends the process via usage(), errx or FATAL instead of returning.

functions.name: contested_has
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: cpu is a counter list in which find_counter locates both CPU_CLK_UNHALTED.THREAD_P and MEM_LOAD_UOPS_LLC_HIT_RETIRED.XSNP_HITM (non-NULL results), and pos is either -1 or a valid index into the vals arrays of both counters. Postcondition: prints (XSNP_HITM * 84.0) / CPU_CLK_UNHALTED.THREAD_P with format "%1.3f", using vals[pos] of each counter when pos != -1 and the sum fields when pos == -1 (a zero denominator gives inf or NaN in floating point, not a trap), and returns the printf result (the number of characters printed, or a negative value on output error); it allocates nothing and takes or releases no locks.

functions.name: arp_EtherAddr
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: hwaddr points to writable memory large enough for the link-level sockaddr_dl found (dl->sdl_len bytes), and ipaddr is an IPv4 address. Postcondition: it fetches the interface list via sysctl(NET_RT_IFLIST) and returns 1 when it finds an interface that is up and broadcast-capable (and not point-to-point, noarp or loopback) with an AF_INET address and netmask whose masked address equals ipaddr's masked address, after copying that interface's sockaddr_dl into hwaddr and freeing the buffer; it returns 0 if the sysctl size estimate fails (logging an error), if malloc fails, if the second sysctl fails, or if no interface matches, in which case hwaddr is untouched; the temporary buffer is always freed before return.

functions.name: SetVariable
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: arg points to a valid cmdargs structure whose cmd->args holds a VAR_* selector, with argv/argc/argn consistent, a valid bundle, and a datalink cx or link wherever the selected variable needs one. Postcondition: it dispatches on the selector and updates the matching configuration field (auth key/name, autoload, scripts, window size, MPPE, device list, accmap, mode, MRRU/MRU/MTU, openmode, phone, queue, idle timeout, RADIUS settings, LQR period, retry values, DNS/NBNS, callback, CBCP, choked, pipes, CD, parity, RTS/CTS, urgent ports, PPPoE, port id); it returns 1 immediately, with a warning, if the command needs a context and none is given. Otherwise it returns 0 on success, 1 for invalid or missing values (a warning is logged and the field is usually left unchanged), -1 for syntax errors or invalid values (MPPE, mode, MRU/MTU forms, callback option, DNS/NBNS address that does not parse as IPv4; for DNS/NBNS the addresses have already been reset), or whatever SetRetry or physical_SetParity returns for those cases; the caller gets no reference or lock.

functions.name: ether_Create
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p is a valid initialized physical link whose name.full and fd are set (fd < 0 with a name of the form "PPPoE:<iface>[:<provider>]" selects the PPPoE path, otherwise fd is treated as an already open descriptor). Postcondition: on the PPPoE path it decrements p->fd, loads the netgraph modules, creates a netgraph socket node and a PPPoE connection, and on success sets the descriptor callbacks and returns a newly allocated ether device with carrier pending; if malloc fails it returns NULL, if socket node creation fails it frees the device, sets p->fd to -2 and returns NULL, and on any later netgraph failure it returns the result of ether_Abandon(dev, p). On the other path, if p->fd is a netgraph socket it returns a newly allocated device with carrier OK, no hook and slot taken from the SESSIONID environment variable (hex, else 0), returns NULL if allocation fails, and if getsockname fails it closes p->fd, sets it to -1 and returns NULL; if p->fd is not a netgraph socket it returns NULL. When a device is returned, the physical stack is set up with PHYSICAL_FORCE_SYNCNOACF and the caller owns the device.

functions.name: exec_Create
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p points to a valid initialized struct physical. Postcondition: if p->fd < 0 and p->name.full starts with '!', it mallocs an exec device (NULL is returned if malloc fails), decrements p->fd, creates a socketpair and a pipe and forks a child that runs the command through a vfork'd grandchild with fids[1] as stdin/stdout/stderr; on socketpair, pipe or fork failure it closes the descriptors it opened, and on socketpair or pipe failure it frees the device and leaves dev NULL. In the parent, p->session_owner is read from the pidpipe (set to -1 if the read is short) and the child is waited for; on waitpid error, a signalled child or a nonzero exit status it closes fids[0], sets p->session_owner to -1 and p->fd stays negative, while on success or a stopped child p->fd is set to fids[0]. If p->fd >= 0 and fstat shows a FIFO, it mallocs a device (logging a warning and returning NULL if that fails) with fd_out = dup(STDOUT_FILENO) when p->fd is stdin (also installing exec_UpdateSet/exec_IsSet on p->desc) and -1 otherwise. If a device exists at the end, it copies baseexecdevice into it, calls physical_SetupStack, warns if carrier necessity is not CD_DEFAULT, and returns a pointer to the embedded struct device; otherwise it returns NULL. The caller owns the returned device. In the fork-failure case the device is not freed, yet it is still returned.

functions.name: FilterCheck
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: packet points to a complete IP (or IPv6 when family is AF_INET6) packet header with its payload, filter points to an initialised filter with MAXFILTERS rules, and psecs is NULL or points to an unsigned the caller owns. Postcondition: returns 0 (permit) if the first rule has action A_NONE (empty filter), if an IPv4 packet is a non-first fragment with offset of at least 3 units and filter->fragok is set, or if the first matching rule (following jumps for rule actions below A_NONE) has action A_PERMIT, in which case *psecs is set to that rule's timeout when psecs is not NULL; returns 1 (deny) for an IPv4 fragment with offset 1 or 2, a non-first fragment when fragok is not set, a TCP datagram shorter than 20 octets or shorter than its declared header length, a payload shorter than the protocol minimum, a matching rule with a non-permit action, or when no rule matches (implicit deny). It only logs, and does not modify the packet or the filter, and the caller gains no references or locks.

functions.name: LcpDecodeConfig
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: fp is an LCP fsm, cp..end is a buffer of received LCP configuration options, mode_type is MODE_REQ, MODE_NAK, MODE_REJ or MODE_NOP, and dec is a valid decode context; for a callback option in a REQ, p (the physical link) must be non-NULL. Postcondition: returns nothing; it reads options until the buffer is exhausted or fsm_readopt returns NULL. Each option is handled according to its type and mode_type: in REQ mode it is normally answered with fsm_ack, fsm_nak or fsm_rej (unknown options are rejected), and my_reject is set for rejected options. In NAK/REJ mode the want_*/his_* fields of lcp are updated and his_reject bits are set, and fsm_Close is called when a required callback is NAKed or rejected. After the loop, unless mode_type is MODE_NOP, a REQ on a direct physical link that requires callback but received no callback option gets a callback NAK. A REQ with no MRU option may get an MRU NAK when the limited MRU is below DEF_MRU, which sets his_mru and mru_req. Finally fsm_opt_normalise(dec) is called. A matching magic number in a REQ makes the function sleep in sigsuspend.

functions.name: tty_Create
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: p points to a valid struct physical whose fd is either negative or an open descriptor. Postcondition: returns NULL without touching the fd if p->fd is negative or not a tty; returns NULL after closing p->fd and setting it to -1 if malloc fails; otherwise allocates a ttydevice, saves the current termios, sets the line to raw mode with the configured flow control, parity and speed (a failure of tcsetattr or cfsetspeed is only logged), and, if F_GETFL fails, logs a warning, calls tty_Cooked, closes the fd, sets it to -1, frees the device and returns NULL. On success it clears O_NONBLOCK on the fd, calls physical_SetupStack and returns a pointer to the embedded struct device, which the caller owns. If p->name.full is empty, the device name is set from ttyname.

functions.name: pw_user_mod
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the command-line arguments for the 'usermod' operation and arg1 is either NULL, a numeric uid string, or a user name; unless -N (dry run) is given the process must be root (pw_check_root). Postcondition: the function parses options, finds the user by name or uid, applies the requested changes (rename, uid, group, times, shell, class, home, password, gecos) in memory, and if -N is given returns the value of print_user without writing anything; otherwise it writes the passwd entry if edited, updates group memberships for -G and for a rename, re-reads the user, logs the change, optionally creates and populates the home directory (when -m and the home path is absolute and not altdir), runs the NIS update if -Y (logging on success), and returns EXIT_SUCCESS. On usage errors, a missing user or uid, non-local or NIS user that cannot be modified, renaming root, changing root's uid, a bad skeleton, bad -h/-H options, or the user vanishing after the update, it does not return but exits via errx/usage (EX_USAGE, EX_DATAERR, EX_NOUSER, EX_OSFILE), possibly after earlier edits were already written.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process command line, and the file-level globals (hosts, nhosts, sock_fd, sock_fdcnt, svcport_str, mallocd_svcport, debug) are in their initial state. Postcondition: main never returns normally. It parses -d, -F, -h host and -p port (an invalid port or unknown option calls usage()), unsets and re-registers the statd RPC service, and builds the host list ("*" if none given, else the given hosts plus ::1 if IPv6 exists plus 127.0.0.1). It then creates and binds sockets for every visible netconfig transport via create_service, retrying with a new dynamic port up to GETPORT_MAXTRY times on EADDRINUSE. On the last attempt it keeps one port per transport in port_list. It calls complete_service for each visible transport and frees sock_fd and port_list. It then runs init_file, daemonizes unless -F was given, opens the syslog, installs the SIGCHLD handler, calls notify_hosts and svc_run. It exits with status 1 on out-of-memory, a persistent bind failure, too many port numbers, a fork failure, or if svc_run returns.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv hold the command line (options -p dir, -h), and the process is either started by inetd with an AF_INET socket on fd 0 or started standalone. Postcondition: main never returns; it parses options (an unknown option calls usage()), loads securenets, and either uses fd 0 (inetd: exit(1) if the socket is not AF_INET or SO_TYPE cannot be read) or, standalone, forks (err(1) on fork failure, the parent exits 0), closes all descriptors, reopens console/tty and unregisters old portmap mappings. It then creates and registers UDP and/or TCP RPC services as selected by _rpcfdtype, calling exit(1) after a message if creation or registration fails or no handle exists, installs signal handlers (plus an alarm closedown timer when started by inetd), runs ypxfrd_svc_run(), and if that ever returns logs 'svc_run returned' and calls exit(1).

functions.name: make_packet
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: rai points to a valid struct rainfo whose rai_ifinfo is valid and whose prefix, route, rdnss and dnssl lists and option flags are consistent. Postcondition: the function returns nothing; it computes the total Router Advertisement length, allocates a zeroed buffer (logging and calling exit(1) if malloc fails), frees any previous rai_ra_data, and stores the new buffer in rai_ra_data and its length in rai_ra_datalen. It fills in the RA header, then the optional link-layer address option, MTU option and PREF64 option, then one prefix-information option per prefix (valid/preferred lifetimes are 0 if the prefix timer is set, otherwise the remaining time, with preferred lifetime clamped to valid lifetime), then route-information, RDNSS and DNSSL options with lengths in 8-octet units (DNSSL entries are zero-terminated and padded to 8 octets). If the link-layer option has zero length, rai_advlinkopt is cleared and an info message is logged. The caller owns the buffer via rai.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv describe the process's command-line arguments in the standard way (argv is a NULL-terminated array of argc strings). Postcondition: it parses the options, and on an invalid option or argument, a repeated -C, a bad -C byte string, a negative count without a write direction, or no action requested it prints usage or an error and returns 1, or 0 for -h; if the device cannot be opened it returns 1; with -i it returns get_info's result (0 or the ioctl's -1); otherwise it sets mode and speed and returns the nonzero result of the failing set_mode or set_speed ioctl (-1), or the result of perform_read, perform_write or perform_readwrite for the chosen direction (or 0 if no direction applies). Before returning in every case it closes the device if it was opened and frees opt.pcmd.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the process command-line arguments of syslogd, with no non-option operands (argc minus optind must be 0). Postcondition: main never returns; it parses the options, and on bad options or operands calls usage() or errx(1, ...), on a failed open of /dev/null, kqueue creation, kevent registration or sigaction it removes the pid file and calls exit(1), and on an already-running instance it calls errx(1, ...). A failure to open the pid file with any other error only produces a warning. Otherwise it registers the sockets, /dev/klog and the signals with a kqueue (SIGCHLD and others in sigcatch are set to be ignored), writes the pid file, calls init(false), and loops forever dispatching read events to socket handlers, SIGHUP to init(true), SIGTERM (and SIGINT/SIGQUIT only with -F or -d) to die(), SIGALRM to markit(), and process-exit events by logging the dead child, closing its process descriptor and freeing the filed entry if it is unused.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process command-line arguments, and the program is started so the raw ICMP and raw send sockets can be opened before privileges are dropped. Postcondition: main never returns; it exits with status 1 after printing a diagnostic on any setup error (cannot open /dev/null, setuid failure, sysctl failure, bad option or arguments, usage, malloc failure, missing protocol or socket, interface/source/bind/connect/capsicum errors). Otherwise it sends probes for each TTL from first_ttl to max_ttl, printing replies, times and annotations (loss, ECN, unreachable flags), stops early once the destination is reached or nearly all probes got unreachable replies, shuts down the AS lookup if enabled, and calls exit(0).

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the process command-line arguments and the last non-option argument names a network interface. Postcondition: it parses the options and exits early without returning (usage and exit(EXIT_SUCCESS) for -h/-?/unknown options, errx(1) when no interface is given, setitimer fails, no control port can be opened or no uhso tty list is found, and send_disconnect then exit(EXIT_SUCCESS) in disconnect mode). Otherwise it installs signal handlers, starts a watchdog timer, opens the control tty, optionally daemonizes, and loops in select on the tty, handling AT events and reconnecting after a watchdog expiry. When select fails or at_async returns nonzero, it prints a newline if not daemon and an IP is assigned, resets the signal handlers (SIGALRM to ignore), disconnects, removes the pidfile and closes syslog if daemonized, and returns 0.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc/argv are the usbdump command line; on the normal path /dev/bpf can be opened and used and the bus interface exists or can be created. Postcondition: options are parsed (bad options call usage(), and the program exits through err/errx with EXIT_FAILURE or EX_SOFTWARE on any setup failure); if -r is given the file is read and the process exits with EXIT_SUCCESS without capturing; otherwise it captures packets until the loop ends, prints capture statistics, destroys the usbusN interface only if it created it, closes the socket, closes each of p->fd, p->rfd, p->wfd, p->bfd that is greater than zero, and returns EXIT_SUCCESS.

functions.name: voss_httpd_start
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: pvp points to a valid vprofile_t whose http fields (host, port, nstate, rtp_ifname) are initialised. Postcondition: if host or port is NULL or nstate is 0, it does nothing and returns NULL (HTTP disabled). Otherwise it allocates pvp->http.state with nstate entries (fd=-1, ts=0) and allocates a client. It returns an error string if the state allocation fails, the client allocation fails, the RTP channel count exceeds 2, the RTP bind fails (that function's error string), buffer setup fails (the client is freed first), or either pthread_create fails. On those errors the state array stays allocated, and the client is leaked or already registered, except in the buffer-setup failure, where it is freed. On success it sets rx_enabled=1 and type=VTYPE_OSS_DAT, appends the client to pvp->head under the atomic lock, starts the server and streamer threads, and returns NULL. In RTP mode it sets http.rtp_fd from the bind; otherwise it sets rtp_fd to -1.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argv holds the yp_mkdb command line; with -u a map name is given, otherwise an input file name (or "-" for stdin) and a map name are given. Postcondition: with -u it unwinds the map and exits 0; if the input file or map is missing it jumps to the optional -c clear step, otherwise it calls usage(); otherwise it opens the input and creates the map database (calling err(1) and exiting with status 1 on gethostname, fopen or open_db failure), stores the YP_* bookkeeping records, then inserts each valid 'key<whitespace>data' line (backslash continuations joined) and warns and skips lines that have no whitespace, start with +/- when -f is set, have no key, or have a key or data longer than YPMAXRECORD. A duplicate key (YP_FALSE) only warns and skips; any other put failure calls err(1) and exits with status 1. It then closes the database, with -c sends a 'clear' RPC to the local ypserv (warning on failure), and exits with status 0. It never returns.

functions.name: main
functions.prose_contract: Precondition: argc and argv are the usual program arguments; the options -c (zone command) and -d (device path) are required, while -a, -l, -o, -P and -h are optional. Postcondition: main never returns; it always ends in exit(error) after freeing the entries buffer (if one was allocated) and closing the device (if it was opened). The exit status is 0 if the chosen action completed (open/close/finish/reset-write-pointer ioctl succeeded, all report-zones chunks were printed, or the disk parameters were printed). The status is 1 if any option value is invalid, an unknown option was given, -d or -c is missing, the action is unknown, the entries malloc fails, the device cannot be opened, the DIOCZONECMD ioctl fails, or zonectl_print_rz returns ZONE_PRINT_ERROR. With -h, usage(0) is called and the process exits with status 0 (unless a prior error was set). Option-parse failures and usage errors jump to bailout before the device is opened. A strdup failure for the filename calls err(1, ...), which exits immediately without the cleanup.
